notes: The findings, verdicts and directions below are unchanged: the historical review of 281af6e (main ecbb79a, the reviewed tree plus this record).

Each status is the final verifiers' verdict on the integrated tree; the fix rounds after it only closed residual issues. 4aeaee7 took the 40 issues the verifiers and the docs, bug and design reviewers raised: 38 fixed and 2 partly, both by decision and recorded under U5 and U12. Its re-check raised one more, the delete dialog's raw red, fixed in 9ec6783, and the re-check after that found none open.
U61 is partial: part A (the edit Example's note, Check's heuristic note, the dropped-file guard) is in; part B, importing one's own picture as a reference, is not built.
not_done names a part of a fixed finding's recommendation left undone by decision, mostly optional extras; alternative names a documented way round the recommendation's letter.

findings.title: Sticky settings panel runs past the viewport bottom, so Generate, progress, Run grid and Resume can't be reached; the media queries meant to unpin it are overridden by the later .panel rule

findings.recommendation: 1) Move the two @media blocks (style.css:65-73) below the .panel rule (after l.92), so max-width:900px really unpins the one-column layout. 2) Replace the 900px height guess with a measured sticky-bottom top in app.js: `const panelEl = document.querySelector('.panel'); const fitPanel = () => { panelEl.style.top = Math.min(68, innerHeight - panelEl.offsetHeight - 18) + 'px'; }; new ResizeObserver(fitPanel).observe(panelEl); addEventListener('resize', fitPanel); fitPanel();`. Where the panel fits it stays pinned at 68 exactly as now. Where it does not, it scrolls with the page until its bottom meets the viewport and holds there. Simulated at QHD with the grid open: top -184px, and Run grid stays at y=1227-1270 at every scroll position. The max-height:900px rule can be dropped, or kept below .panel as the no-JS fallback. 3) When the fold toggles open, call `els.gridRun.scrollIntoView({block:'nearest', behavior: reduce ? 'auto' : 'smooth'})` so opening it shows its button. 4) Do not make the panel overflow-y:auto: it clips the Examples menu, the tag menu and the right-hand tips. 5) Optional: a 'Ctrl+Enter' hint under Generate. 6) Add a smoke step at 1400x900 with the grid open: after a wheel over the stage, expect `els.gridRun.getBoundingClientRect().bottom <= innerHeight`. Known cost: while the user scrolls the gallery, the top of the panel (the prompt, about 184 px at QHD with the grid open) sits above the fold until they scroll back up. That is still more reachable than static.
findings.documented_rule: style.css:70-73, 'Sticky only where the whole panel fits ... Run grid - was simply not reachable until the very end of the gallery released it', added in commit 496bfb1 ('the sticky panel releases when it cannot fit'). style.css:85-91: the panel stays positioned at z-index 10 so its tips paint over the cards. CLAUDE.md Frontend and index.html: validation and the prompt check stay out of the sticky column so they cannot push Generate down (design-notes l.3785).
findings.rule_tension: The rule never worked. In 496bfb1 both @media blocks were placed above the equally specific .panel rule, so sticky always wins: at 1400x900 matchMedia(max-height:900px) is true and position is still sticky. The fix carries out the rule's own purpose (every control reachable) with a measurement instead of a 900px guess. Sticky-bottom keeps position:sticky and z-index 10, so tips and menus are not clipped, and it shows more of the panel than the static fallback the comment intended. overflow-y:auto (panel-1, walkthrough-8) breaks the z-index/popover constraint: the Examples menu reaches x=421 against the panel's right edge at 348, and Animagine's tag menu spans x 133-431, so both would be clipped or scroll sideways. Also, panel-1's claim that the smokes run with a static panel at 1400x900 is false: the panel is sticky there today.
findings.smokes_affected: No smoke asserts the panel's position or top. Re-run smoke-animagine.json:59-60 and :94-96, which compare #btn-generate's top before and after rendering chips or the check (both at scrollY 0, so they should hold). smoke-paging.json:20,35,49 wheel at (900,500) over the stage and are unaffected. Every 1400x900 smoke will now run with an unpinned (sticky-bottom) panel, but they drive the panel through eval, not coordinates. Add the new reachability expect.
findings.how_checked: FLUX.1 Krea [dev] fake on 7902 with a 160-image grid planted. Ran a scroll trace at 2560x1305, 1400x900 and 2048x1040@1.25: I opened Grid search with a real click on its summary, wheeled over the stage and measured the panel, Generate, the summary, Budget and Run grid with getBoundingClientRect after each wheel. I checked the computed position against matchMedia and found the commit that added the rule with git log -S. I also tried each proposed fix as in-page CSS/JS (the repo was not touched): the cascade fix, a measured sticky-bottom top, and overflow-y:auto with the Examples menu open.
findings.verifier_notes: Merged findings visual-1, panel-1, grid-1 and walkthrough-8 all reproduce. The root cause is the cascade order, which visual-1 identified. The three remedies were judged as follows: the JS measured unpin (visual-1) is compatible; sticky-bottom with a negative top (grid-1) is compatible and better; overflow-y:auto (panel-1, walkthrough-8) is rejected because it clips popovers. I did not reproduce walkthrough-8's claim that focusing an axis scrolled the page 311 px. Tab-to-Run-grid reachability was not re-measured (my Tab sequence left the panel).
findings.merge_note: panel-1 and grid-1 measure the grid fold case: the panel grows to 1387-1588 px, so Run grid, Budget, Seed list, Resume and the preview sit below the fold at any scroll. grid-1 proposes a sticky-bottom offset. walkthrough-8 adds that focusing a grid axis scrolls the page about 311 px and pushes the live viewer off-screen, and proposes a self-scrolling panel.

sources.surface: Settings panel (aside.panel): sticky positioning against the viewport height
sources.observation: style.css puts `@media (max-width: 900px) {.panel{position:static}}` (l.65-68) and `@media (max-height: 900px) {.panel{position:static}}` (l.73) BEFORE `.panel { ... position: sticky; top: 68px }` (l.75-93). The selectors are equally specific, so the later sticky rule always wins. At 1400x900, matchMedia('(max-height: 900px)').matches is true but the computed position is still 'sticky'. Measured with 157 images in the gallery: at 1400x900 Generate's top edge sits at y=915 at scrollY 0 and at y=905-907 at scrollY 600, 1939, 3439, 4939 and 5874 (all 4 pages loaded). The viewport is 900 tall, so Generate never appears; the panel is cut off after the Seed row. At 2048x1040 DPR 1.25 (QHD at 125%) the panel is 1089px tall from y=76, bottom at 1165. The last-run box (y=995-1083) is cut off and the Grid search summary (y=1112) stays off-screen while the gallery scrolls. At 2560x1305 with Grid search open the panel is 1489px tall. Run grid sits at y=1497 while the panel is pinned (scrollY 0 and 1018). It only came into view (y=1227) at scrollY 1804, the document end, after the scroll watcher had auto-loaded every page of the gallery. Ctrl+Enter generates from anywhere (app.js:255-262), but nothing on the page mentions it; only the Refine button's title says Ctrl+Enter.
sources.why_it_matters: Generate, Cancel/Pause, the error line and Run grid are the panel's main actions. The comment at style.css:69-72 describes exactly this failure ('was simply not reachable until the very end of the gallery released it'), and it is back. The gallery pages itself as you scroll near the bottom, so the end keeps moving away: with a few hundred images the user has to load every page before Run grid appears. At 125% scaling this hits every session; at 100% it hits whenever the grid is open. The smokes run at 1400x900 but click through eval(), so they never see it.

findings.recommendation: In showSheetScope (web/panel.js:241-249), keep setSheet(true)'s promise and read galleryEpoch right after the call. When the promise resolves, if sheetMode is still on and the epoch is unchanged, call document.querySelector('.gallery-head').scrollIntoView({block:'start'}). Also route the last-run banner's job branch (app.js:224, which calls setSheet directly) through showJob. Leave the Sheet toggle alone: the user is already at the gallery head. findings.documented_rule: CLAUDE.md Frontend: the comparison 'opens its submission (job:<id>) as the sheet when done - Favorites unticked first', and the gallery's filters are the sheet's. On a two-column page the prompt check sits above the results (placeTagValidation). Design notes 'The running batch on wide screens' and 'The live preview' say the viewer is where a running job lands. 'The morning after: runs and finished jobs' says a pick from the Runs picker is a run:<id> search plus the sheet.
findings.rule_tension: No rule requires the sheet to stay below the fold. Two of the proposed fixes do conflict with rules. Hiding the viewer in sheet mode would hide a running job and its live preview. Folding the check panel works against the deliberate placement of the check above the results. Scrolling alone avoids both. scrollIntoView does not move focus, so the focus rules (Check focuses the heading, the critic's answer takes focus) are untouched. Scroll after setSheet's promise resolves: it resolves only after learnSheetOrder and renderSheet (gallery.js:63).

It is high severity because, in the comparison flow, nothing in view changes on success except the cell note and an unlabelled strip that looks like the result. The Refine sweep, part of the new feature the user called clunky, has the same problem. analysis-6's per-variant cell cap is the same mechanism as M18, so fix it there. Side observation, not in this cluster: the stale 'Last run finished ... 1 image' banner stayed in the panel beside the new comparison's result.
findings.merge_note: analysis-6 notes that the visible unlabelled 16-image viewer strip looks like the result. grid-5 shows the same for the Runs picker and Sheet button: the viewer still holds the last job, or an empty 380 px placeholder. It proposes hiding the viewer in sheet mode.

sources.surface: Stage: prompt check panel + viewer + sheet stacking; showJob/showRun
sources.observation: Task 6: Check + Ask the critic + Run comparison (Original vs Rewrite, 4 seeds) finished with only 'Finished 8 images in 36s. Only 4 distinct.' in the panel. The sheet opened (sheetMode=true, search job:433fe5192f48), but at y=1625 in a 1305 px viewport. Above it were the still-open prompt check panel (366,76, 2161x1039) and the viewer strip (y=1133, 380 px). The page did not scroll (scrollY=0, docH=2773), so getting from the Run comparison button to the sheet took about 1400 px of scrolling. Task 5 had the same problem: the run's sheet opened from a card's ⊞ started at y=782 under a 554 px viewer strip, and its 4x3 cells (523 px each) put the first row's bottom below the fold.
sources.why_it_matters: The comparison is the one flow whose whole answer is the sheet, and the user is left looking at an unchanged check panel. 'Where did my results go?' is the most likely reaction, and the fix today is a long blind scroll past two large panels.

sources.surface: Run comparison > showJob(fresh) > #sheet
sources.observation: Run comparison was clicked with the panel open (4 versions x 4 seeds). When the job finished, the sheet opened at y=1290 of a 1305 px viewport (page scrollY 605), so none of it was visible. What was visible was the viewer strip: 16 thumbnails, 256 px each, in 8 columns with no version labels, which looks like the result but can't be read as one. After scrolling down, the sheet is 4 rows of 512 px cells (a 2090 px grid). At most 2 of the 4 versions fit on screen together, and the Original row (y=312) and the Your version row (y=1865) are 1,553 px apart.
sources.why_it_matters: The comparison is there to put versions side by side on the same seeds. When it ends, the labelled answer is off-screen, and the strip on screen invites reading an unlabelled grid as the result. Comparing the first and last rows means scrolling back and forth.

sources.surface: Stage when sheet mode is on (viewer + gallery head + sheet)
sources.observation: Opening run c6f… from the Runs picker set scrollY to 0 with the sheet's top at y=1010. Only the column headers and the top ~290 px of row 1 were visible; the rest of the first screen was the viewer's 24-image strip of the job just finished (822 px tall), i.e. the same images again. The Sheet button gave the same result (sheet at y=1015). At 125% with an empty viewer the sheet starts at y=568 under the 380 px 'Generated images appear here.' box, and one row shows. Neither setSheet nor showSheetScope scrolls.
sources.why_it_matters: Every way into the sheet (Runs picker, a card's ⊞, Sheet, Show run) lands the user on the wrong thing. They have to scroll to find the result they asked for, and the duplicate strip above spends a full QHD screen height on images the sheet already shows.

findings.title: A refine pass can't be compared with its source: the lineage is a bare id, the two aren't adjacent, and stepping between them resets the zoom
surfaces: Lightbox after a Refine pass; gallery cards
Lightbox settings line, gallery card for a refined record, lightbox view (lbView)
Viewer strip after Refine; lightbox opened on a pass
findings.recommendation:
(1) Primary: in renderLightbox (web/lightbox.js:89), when rec.refine != null, show a 'Compare with source (S)' toggle in .lb-side. At QHD that column has about 700px free between the settings line and the zoom row (a03). On press, or on S (add 's' to app.js's lightbox key block below the input guard):
- fetch `/api/images/${rec.refine}` once and cache it by id. On 'unknown image', disable the toggle with 'source #N deleted', as reusePass handles it.
- set els.lbImg.src to the source's url with els.lbImg.style.objectFit='cover'. Cover reproduces refine.fitted's cover-and-centre-crop when the pass changed shape.
- leave lbList, lbIndex and lbView untouched, so crop and magnification stay identical.
- label the stage state in the zoom line ('source #9 · 1024×1024'). Any renderLightbox (arrow, delete) returns to the pass.
(2) Make the settings clause a button that toggles the same thing. Keep its text 'refine of 9 @ 0.1', which smoke-refine.json:55 reads.
(3) In card() (gallery.js:91), when rec.refine != null, add class 'refined' and data-badge `⤢ ${w}×${h}`, rendered with `.card.refined::before{content:attr(data-badge);position:absolute;top:4px;left:4px;font-size:11px;padding:1px 5px;border-radius:4px;background:rgba(0,0,0,.65);color:#fff;pointer-events:none}`.
(4) Optional: carry lbView across records whose aspect ratios agree within 1%. Store lbView.aspect and test |a-b|/b < 0.01, not a toFixed key. In renderLightbox, clamp lbView.scale to the new record's ceiling (oneToOneScale*8). Amend design-notes. Do not add the source to viewerRecords.
findings.documented_rule: design-notes 'The lightbox zooms': lbView is keyed on width x height and carried across records of the same size, so a sweep's cells compare the identical crop. generation.js:379-380: results replace the viewer once the first image lands. CLAUDE.md Frontend/Reproduction: a refine source is a gallery id fetched by GET /api/images/{id}, never a path, and Reuse on a pass goes through reusePass.
findings.rule_tension: A compare toggle inside the lightbox leaves the size keying and the strip alone. It fetches by id, as reusePass does, so it fits every rule. Keying lbView on aspect widens the documented carry rule. That needs a design-notes amendment, a tolerance instead of a string key (see notes) and a ceiling clamp. Putting the source in the strip as a lead record conflicts with viewerRecords meaning 'this job's images': it changes the multi/many tier and breaks several smoke expectations, so I do not recommend it.
findings.smokes_affected: smoke-refine.json:55 (expects els.lbMeta to include 'refine of <id> @ 0.1'; keep that wording in the new button). Only if a strip lead record were adopted: smoke-refine.json:51-53, :81, :105 and smoke-refine-unavailable.json:6-30, which assume viewerRecords and '#viewer img' hold only the pass. Aspect carry leaves smoke.json:53-56 alone (same-size cells). Add toggle steps after smoke-refine.json:55.
findings.how_checked: Ran the FLUX.1 Krea [dev] fake on 7906 at 2560x1305, DPR 1. I generated a 1024x1024 source (id 9, seed 78), opened it from the viewer strip, then pressed lightbox Refine, 2x and Refine. I measured the strip, the lightbox, the gallery order and the zoom carry. I also built a compare toggle with eval only (no file edits): it swaps els.lbImg.src to the source's url from GET /api/images/9 and leaves lbView alone.
findings.verifier_notes:
Severity stays high. The pass exists so the user can judge it against its source, a judgement made on fine detail at strength 0.1, and no route lets the user see both at the same crop: the view resets on every flip. This is the Refine flow the user called clunky. Corrections to the source findings:
- Adjacency is conditional. In my run the source was the newest image, so the pass (id 10) sat right before it. They are far apart only when an older image is refined.
- Both proposed aspect keys, toFixed(3) and toFixed(4), break on 16-px snapping (2048/1152 = 1.7778 vs 1360/768 = 1.7708), so use a tolerance.
- The in-lightbox toggle needs no keying change at all, because fitSize is derived from the pass record.
- The swap was checked with plain viewport shots: elshot's captureBeyondViewport re-laid out the stage and reset the pan, a driver artifact.
- 'Passes (n)' on a source would need an extra `/api/gallery?search=refine:<id>&limit=1` for the count. That is optional.
findings.merge_note: walkthrough-7 proposes a 'Compare with source (S)' button that puts the pair in lbList. refine-flow-2 adds that the pass replaces its source in the viewer strip (clearResults on the first image) and proposes keeping the source as a lead record.

sources.surface: Lightbox settings line, gallery card for a refined record, lightbox view (lbView)
sources.observation: A refined record says only "refine of 57 @ 0.1" in the 12px settings line (g10). The id 57 is shown nowhere else on the page: cards carry no ids, and the Refine dialog's title is "Refine image 147" (g27). It is plain text, not a link. The refined card looks the same as every other card: its class is just "card", with no badge, size or marker. With the search "lighthouse seed:78", the pass (id 61, 1536x1536) came first and its source (id 57) fifth, not next to it. I zoomed the pass to 335% (scale 4.06) and pressed ArrowRight to a 1024x1024 cell: the view reset to "fit · 124%" (scale 1). lbView is keyed on `${width}x${height}`, so a 1.5x pass never shares a view with its source. Nothing on the source leads to its passes either; only typing refine:57 in the search box does.
sources.why_it_matters: The only point of a refine pass is to see whether it improved the source, at the same crop and magnification. Today that takes a hand-written search, finding the two images in a list, and zooming each one by hand. The view is lost on every flip. This is the Refine flow the user called clunky.

sources.surface: Lightbox after a Refine pass; gallery cards
sources.observation: Task 3 was quick up to the render: open card, F to star, Refine, 2×, Refine = 4 clicks + 1 key, and the dialog's preview said 'about 3 of 28 steps run'. Comparing was the clunky part. The result opened from the viewer was a 1-image lightbox (no arrows); its source was named only as plain text ('refine of 6 @ 0.1'). The refined 2048 card looked identical to its 1024 source (no badge or size). From the gallery the source was 3 ArrowRights away. Zooming to 1:1 on the refined image (scale 1.61) and stepping to the source reset the view to 'fit · 124%'; stepping back gave 'fit · 62%'. lbView is keyed on width x height, so a 2x pass and its source can never be compared at the same crop. 'Keep one' then took F, 3 ArrowLeft and F, about 10 keystrokes in total.
sources.why_it_matters: The user called Refine the clunkiest part. Its only question, 'is the pass better than the source?', needs a same-crop A/B, and that is what the lightbox currently prevents.

sources.surface: Viewer strip after Refine; lightbox opened on a pass
sources.observation: Typical path: Generate, open the result in the lightbox, Refine, 2×, Refine (4 clicks). When the pass lands, streamJob's first image calls clearResults(), so the source disappears from the strip (srcInStrip=false; during the pass the live preview takes its place). The strip then shows the pass alone with no caption (d02). Opening it gives a one-image lightbox: lbList.length=1, prev/next disabled, and the settings line says only 'refine of 14 @ 0.1'. To compare against the original, the user must close it, open the pass's card in the gallery and press ArrowRight past every image between the two (3 presses in my run of 4 images, more in a real session). The view also resets on arrival: after 1:1 on the 1792×2304 pass ('1:1', scale 1.82) the 896×1152 source opened at 'fit · 110%', because lbView is keyed on exact width×height. Task count for 'make X twice as big with a light touch, compare to the original, keep the better one': at least 8 clicks, N arrow keys and 2 Escapes, and there is still no way to see the same crop at the same magnification.
sources.why_it_matters: Comparing the pass with its source is the decision Refine asks the user to make: did it keep the picture, is it sharper. The page removes the source at the moment the comparison is wanted and gives no route back. This is the core of 'clunky'.

findings.title: Examples, Reuse and the tag tools assign .value, so a half-written prompt is overwritten with no Ctrl+Z
surfaces: Examples menu, Tags helper (rating/quality buttons, 'Use the recommended negative prompt'), autocomplete accept, chip × / drag / edit
Gallery card ↻ / lightbox Reuse settings -> panel
Prompt box: Examples menu; Reuse writes into the panel
findings.recommendation: Route every programmatic whole-box write through replaceBoxText (analysis.js:315): the Examples pick (app.js:41-51), fillPanel's prompt and negative (gallery.js:342-344), writePromptTags (tags.js:545) and the recommended negative (tags.js:677-683). For applyTagSuggestion (tags.js:52), select [start,end) and call execCommand('insertText', false, suggestion.text) so undo stays granular. After each insert, do what usePromptText does (clearTimeout(tagSuggestionTimer); hideTagSuggestions()) so no suggestion popup opens over the new text. Where a chip started the write, refocus `els.tagValidation.querySelector(`[data-index="${i}"]`)` with preventScroll. For Reuse, Ctrl+Z only covers the text boxes, so also snapshot the panel (the object persistPanel builds) before fillPanel. Then show `Settings from image N loaded - your prompt was replaced.` with an inline Undo that restores the snapshot, including seed, size, steps/CFG/mu and the owned flags. When an Example replaces different non-empty text, show the same note with Undo.
findings.documented_rule: CLAUDE.md Frontend: Use and Apply write through replaceBoxText 'so Ctrl+Z restores'; validation chips: 'All mutations must go through writePromptTags'; every programmatic write goes through promptReplaced(). design-notes 'The prompt analyser' l.3830-3831: 'assigning .value emptied the undo history'. design-notes 'Per-control defaults and Reuse': Reuse owns steps/CFG/mu and shows a note only on a checkpoint mismatch.
findings.rule_tension: The fix applies the rule the analyser already follows. Do it inside writePromptTags so the 'all chip mutations go through writePromptTags' rule holds, and keep calling promptReplaced(). replaceBoxText already falls back to .value for a greyed negative box. It focuses the box, though, so chip-driven writes (Delete, Alt+Arrow, drag in the stage strip) must hand focus back to the chip, the way placeTagValidation restores focus and selection by hand. Reuse's checkpoint-mismatch note must survive: append the Undo note to it.
findings.smokes_affected: Values are unchanged and the error expectations use includes(), but re-run: smoke.json:25-27; smoke-flux.json:20 and 37-52 (Reuse mismatch note via includes); smoke-animagine.json:19-46 (chip drag/insert/remove/edit, with focus expectations at :36 and :38) and :86-90; smoke-illustrious.json:18 and 33-35; smoke-wai.json:20 and 32-34; smoke-kohaku.json:24-26; the Examples steps in smoke-anima/netayume/newbie/z-anime.json:10-12; smoke-conditioning.json:79 and 110; smoke-refine.json:121 (the reusePass path, where the prompt must stay 'panel prompt').
findings.how_checked: Copied the screenshot driver into my scratch dir and gave its keycombo real key codes; without them Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+A were no-ops in headless Edge. A control showed that typed text plus Ctrl+Z undoes normally. On a FLUX fake (7902) I typed into the prompt and tested the Examples pick (real clicks) and a card's Reuse (hover, then a real click on the 23x24 ↻), each followed by Ctrl+Z, document.execCommand('undo'), a read of the localStorage panel and a reload. On an Animagine fake (8902) I did the same for chip ×, the 'safe' rating button, an Examples pick, 'Use the recommended negative prompt' and an autocomplete accept.
findings.verifier_notes: It is worse than stated. In Chromium a .value write does not reliably empty the undo stack: a later Ctrl+Z can apply a stale entry and splice old and new text into a corrupted prompt (seen twice), which persistPanel then saves. The cost is wrong output, not only lost work. walkthrough-3's card-tool sizes match my measurement (23x24 ↻ next to the 23x24 ⤢).
findings.merge_note: tags-2 extends the cause to every tag tool: writePromptTags, applyTagSuggestion, chip edit/drag/delete and the recommended negative. It also notes that persistPanel has already saved the overwrite, so a reload can't recover it. walkthrough-3 adds that Reuse also replaces the seed, size, steps and CFG with no note shown, and proposes a panel snapshot.

sources.surface: Prompt box: Examples menu; Reuse writes into the panel
sources.observation: I typed a prompt by hand ('my carefully written prompt about a harbour at night...'), opened Examples and clicked an item. The box became 'White owl, close up portrait...' and Ctrl+Z in the box left it unchanged. Reuse (galleryRecords[0]) over a typed prompt behaved the same: replaced by 'a lighthouse on a cliff at dusk', Ctrl+Z did nothing. Both write `els.prompt.value = ...`, which wipes the textarea's undo history. The menu item is one click, with no confirmation and no 'replaced' note, and the persisted copy in localStorage is overwritten too.
sources.why_it_matters: A long prompt is the user's main work in this panel, and FLUX's guide asks for 30-80 words. One misclick in a menu that sits right over the prompt box loses that work with no way back. The codebase already fixed this exact problem for Use/Apply (analysis.js:310-320, 'Assigning .value empties a textarea's undo history'), but the two most common programmatic writes don't use that fix.

sources.surface: Examples menu, Tags helper (rating/quality buttons, 'Use the recommended negative prompt'), autocomplete accept, chip × / drag / edit
sources.observation: Control case: typed text is undone by Ctrl+Z as normal. Then I typed 'TYPED' into the prompt, opened Examples and clicked the second example. The prompt became '1boy, male focus, …'. Ctrl+Z / execCommand('undo') left the example in place, and persistPanel had already saved it, so a reload doesn't bring the text back either. I typed 'my own negative, extra fingers' into Negative and clicked 'Use the recommended negative prompt': it was overwritten, and undo did nothing. After clicking × on a chip, Ctrl+Z neither restored the tag nor removed the 'hand typed tag' I had typed before. Rating buttons and accepting a suggestion behave the same way. Each of these assigns .value, which empties the textarea's undo history.
sources.why_it_matters: A 70-tag prompt is minutes of work. One click on Examples, which people open to look at, replaces it with no confirmation and no way back. The project already found and fixed this for the prompt check: design-notes 'The prompt analyser' says 'assigning .value emptied the undo history', which is why replaceBoxText exists. The tag tools never got that fix.

sources.surface: Gallery card ↻ / lightbox Reuse settings -> panel
sources.observation: Task 4: I typed a 100-character prompt in progress, searched 'lighthouse' (4 results), hovered the first card and clicked its ↻ (a 23x24 px glyph next to ⤢). The prompt, seed (1235), size (896x1152), steps (20) and CFG (4) were replaced. The note line stayed empty (errHidden=true): no feedback, no confirmation. Two undos in the prompt did not bring the old text back, because fillPanel assigns .value, which clears the textarea's undo history. In Chromium the undo instead reverted the search box's typing: search went empty and the gallery unfiltered. persistPanel then saved the replacement, so the old prompt was gone for good.
sources.why_it_matters: Losing work. ↻ sits a few pixels from ⤢ and ❐ on a hover-only strip, and the same overwrite happens from the lightbox. Someone who reuses one setting to borrow a seed or size loses whatever they were writing.

findings.title: The prompt check and chip tray stack above the viewer and push the image just made below the fold, while the space beside the image stays empty
surfaces: Stage layout on a tag checkpoint (#tag-validation-wide host above #viewer)
Stage: #tag-validation-wide host > .prompt-analysis above #viewer
Stage: tag-validation-wide host (prompt check panel)
findings.documented_rule: CLAUDE.md Frontend: 'On a two-column page validation lives above the results ... The prompt check's panel follows it, in that order (placeTagValidation moves both ...)'. design-notes 'The prompt analyser' (The page): above the results 'so its length cannot push Generate down the sticky settings column'. design-notes 'The running batch on wide screens': eight slots across QHD. The index.html comment at lines 64-70 says the same.
findings.rule_tension: The rule exists to keep the panel out of the sticky settings column. A CSS-only side column keeps that, keeps chips-then-panel DOM order and keeps placeTagValidation unchanged. Measured: Generate stays at y=915 (FLUX) and 897 (Animagine), and focus still lands on the h2 at y=87, inside the view. Only the wording changes: 'above the results' becomes 'beside the results from 1800 px' in CLAUDE.md, design-notes and the index.html comment. Batch rule cost: while the panel is open, a .many batch keeps 8 slots per row but each shrinks to 159 px (258 px when closed) at QHD and to 113 px (192 px) at 2048@1.25. Optionally exclude that case with :not(:has(> #viewer.many)), at the price of the layout flipping when a batch starts.
findings.smokes_affected: None fail: browser.mjs fixes the viewport at 1400x900, below the 1800px query. Re-run as guards smoke-animagine.json step 93 (Generate top unchanged; panel follows the chips) and the smoke-analysis.json steps that check focus on the panel heading after Check / Check again (h2 below the topbar). Those DOM-order and parentElement expectations stay true because the fix is CSS-only. If the optional below-1800 max-height cap is added, re-run smoke-analysis's heading-focus steps, which then scroll inside the panel. A QHD-viewport smoke step would be needed to cover the new layout at all.
findings.how_checked: Ran fresh fakes on 7915 (FLUX.1 Krea [dev]) and 8915 (Animagine) with a copy of shot.mjs that clicks by selector. Generated an image, then really clicked Check and Ask the critic and pressed Ctrl+Enter with the panel open. Measured with getBoundingClientRect at 2560x1305 DPR 1 and 2048x1040 DPR 1.25. I then injected each proposed CSS through a <style> element on the live page (the repo was not touched) and measured again: analysis-1 verbatim, then a corrected variant.
findings.verifier_notes: All three source findings reproduce, and their numbers match mine within content variance: tags-8's 70-tag case put the viewer at 920 against my image top at 1175, because my tags carry a longer 'Partly checked' text. The verdict is adjusted, not confirmed, for three reasons. analysis-1's literal CSS mis-places the panel on non-tag checkpoints. tags-8's variant (host always in column 2 at 2000 px or more, .viewer.many spanning both columns) would overlap the host in row 1 and moves the chip tray into a narrow column. walkthrough-9's 680px column has the same row problem. The only way to dismiss the panel is its Close button: Escape does not close it (app.js handles Escape only for menus and the lightbox). Taking M21 and M22 with it, this is the panel's main QHD problem: a 760 px side column also removes the 825-1414 px finding-to-badge gaps (they shrink to 35 px or less).
findings.merge_note: walkthrough-9 measures the critic's answer pushing the viewer fully off-screen and finding lines about 2100 px wide. tags-8 adds the chip tray's growth on a tag checkpoint (viewer at y=920 with 70 tags plus Check). All three propose a side-by-side column at wide widths.

sources.surface: Stage: #tag-validation-wide host > .prompt-analysis above #viewer
sources.observation: At 2560x1305, before Check, the viewer image fills y=91-978. Check on a 76-word FLUX prompt opens a 2161x669 panel at y=76, which moves the image to y=778: 527 of its 887 px are visible (59%). After Ask the critic the panel grows to 1069-1136 px and the image top moves to y=1178-1245, leaving 60-127 px visible (7-14%). A Generate pressed in that state lands its image at y=1245. At 2048x1040 with 125% scaling, Check leaves 280 of 707 px visible (image top 760). After the critic answers, the panel (1118 px) is taller than the viewport and none of the image is visible (top 1227). The viewer is still 2161 px wide with the 887 px image centred in it, so about 1,274 px of width beside the image is unused at QHD (942 px at 125%). The panel only goes away when you press its 20x15 px Close.
sources.why_it_matters: The usual loop is Check, fix, Generate, look at the result. While the panel is open, every result lands off-screen, so each generation costs a scroll or a Close and then a re-Check. This fits the user's 'clunky' complaint, and the wasted width shows the layout was sized for 1400 px.

sources.surface: Stage: tag-validation-wide host (prompt check panel)
sources.observation: After Check, the panel took 2161x540-626 px at the top of the stage. After Ask the critic it grew to 1039 px. With it open, Ctrl+Enter put the result image at y=649, showing 656 of its 887 px. With the critic's answer, the viewer started at y=1133, entirely below the fold, and the gallery at y=1566. Each finding was one 12 px line up to 2135 px long, with its GUIDE source badge at x≈2480, about 1500 px from where the text starts. Check itself is a 43x19 px, 10 px-font button.
sources.why_it_matters: Check and critique are meant to be done next to generating, but at QHD they hide what the next Generate produces, and reading 2000 px lines of 12 px text is slow. The user ends up closing the panel (losing the check) or scrolling between it and the viewer.

sources.surface: Stage layout on a tag checkpoint (#tag-validation-wide host above #viewer)
sources.observation: At 2560x1305: with no tags the viewer starts at y=76. With 18 tags it starts at y=163, with 70 tags (4 rows, 144px) at y=238, and with the Check open on 70 tags at y=920, where only 385 of its 917px are on screen. The generated 1024² image is drawn 887x887 (max-height 68vh) inside a 2161px-wide viewer, which leaves 1274px (59%) of the row empty beside it. At 2048x1040 / DPR 1.25 the 70-tag tray is 6 rows (208px), and with the Check open the viewer starts at y=984, so 56px of the image is visible.
sources.why_it_matters: The user sends a prompt and immediately has to scroll to see what it made. Meanwhile the empty space beside the image is wider than the whole chip tray needs. The wide host exists so the chips don't move Generate, and it does that. But at QHD the vertical space it takes is the result's, even though spare horizontal space is right there.

findings.title: The Refine dialog opens at a size beyond what the checkpoint holds, and on FLUX the default strength repaints at that size; the only warning is 'may run tight on 16GB VRAM'
surfaces: Refine dialog: opening size (fittingRefineSize), size line, preview line
Refine dialog: scale buttons, size line, Strength, preview line
findings.recommendation: (1) Opening size (refine.js:63,119): apply the remembered scale, or 1.5x, only while refineScaled(...) stays at or under sizeIsTight (1600x1600 = 2.56 MP). Otherwise open at the largest REFINE_SCALES factor that does, else 1x. When the remembered factor was skipped, title its button '(last run at 2×)' so it remains one click away. This removes both measured traps: a recommended 1.5 MP FLUX source opening at 3.5 MP, and one 2x run making every later source open at 2x. (2) Size-dependent strength: for a single strength, /api/grid/preview returns start_sigma when a pipeline is loaded, computed as the live scheduler's sigmas at start_index after set_timesteps with the size's mu or the request's Mu, and null before a load or for an unprofiled pipeline. previewRefine (refine.js:340) appends '· starts at 65% noise', with the warn class when that is more than 0.1 above the sigma the same strength has at 1.5x of 1 MP. Until a load, show a FLUX-profile note under Strength when w*h > 2.56 MP, worded from verified.md: 'FLUX.1's shift grows with size: at 2× its 0.1 started at sigma 0.75 and repainted the subject in the measured run; Mu 1.15 at 0.2 kept it'. Keep the 8.4 MP guard as the hard limit.
findings.documented_rule: CLAUDE.md Frontend: openRefine fills the size from '1.5x the source's size or the remembered scale, else the largest factor that fits'. Design notes, 'The source is covered and cropped': 'The Refine dialog opens at the source's size times 1.5'. 'A pass has a size guard of its own': 'a typo guard, not a VRAM model ... the time estimate ... is the honest per-checkpoint answer'. 'A strength is an index into the checkpoint's schedule': each profile value 'starts the pass at about half noise for a 1.5x pass of a 1 MP image'.
findings.rule_tension: The opening-size rule in CLAUDE.md and in the design notes would need rewording to '...the largest factor that fits and is not past the tight line'. The fix stays compatible with 'typo guard, not a VRAM model': refine_max_side/refine_max_pixels and tests/test_profiles.py are untouched, explicit clicks on 1.5x/2x still work, and the cap reuses the page's existing 2.56 MP sizeIsTight line instead of new per-profile VRAM numbers. That line is also about where every profile's refine_strength is calibrated (1.5x of 1 MP = 2.36 MP). Any start_sigma the server reports must be read from the scheduler's own sigmas after set_timesteps (CLAUDE.md: assert on scheduler.sigmas), never a client-side formula.
findings.smokes_affected: smoke-refine.json step 52 expects a 1344x1728 refined source (remembered 1.5x) to open at 2016x2592 with '5.2 MP'. Under the cap it opens at 1344x1728 with '2.3 MP — 1× the source', so that step needs updating (step 53 is unaffected, and steps 55-59 set their sizes explicitly). Steps 18, 28 and 97 (2.3 MP, under the line) are unaffected. Step 24's preview check uses startsWith, so appended sigma text does not break it, and the fake has no scheduler, so it returns null anyway. smoke-refine-unavailable.json is unaffected because Reuse uses the pass's own size.
findings.how_checked: FLUX.1 Krea [dev] fake on 7910 with empty prefs. Opened ⤢ on 1664x928 (the 16:9 1.5 MP preset), 896x1152, 1024x1024 and 2048x2048 sources and read the size, size line, preview, focus and prefs. Ran one 2x pass on the 1024x1024 source, then reopened the others. Computed the start sigma with FLUX.1 dev's published dynamic shift (base 0.5 and max 1.15 over 256-4096 tokens, 28 steps, the flow start index from refine.start_index) in sigma.py. The script reproduces verified.md's measured values exactly: 0.474 at 1.5x and 0.1, 0.62 at 0.15, 0.752 at 2x and 0.1, and 0.463 for Mu 1.15 at 0.2.
findings.verifier_notes: The finding is stronger than stated. Its sigma arithmetic (3.5 MP gives mu 2.75, sigma about 0.65) is right, and the remembered-scale path is worse than the finding says: after any single 2x run, the next 1.5 MP source opens at 6.2 MP and starts at sigma 0.92, which is essentially a new picture. A 4 MP source opens at 6.6 MP and sigma 0.94 with no remembered scale at all. Severity stays high: the fastest path (⤢, Enter) on the default checkpoint gives a repainted subject after a pass that, by verified.md, spills VRAM. The original 'refine_comfort_pixels' profile key would put VRAM numbers per profile, which the design notes explicitly decline ('typo guard, not a VRAM model'). Reusing sizeIsTight gets the same effect with no new numbers. Its cost is that SDXL/WAI, which ran 8.6 MP comfortably, also opens capped, but one click on 1.5x/2x still goes there. The scale buttons' state ('1.25×*' in 'scales') confirmed the fallback logic in fittingRefineSize.
findings.merge_note: refine-flow-1 walks the user path (2× at strength 0.1) and proposes returning a size-dependent start_sigma from /api/grid/preview.

sources.surface: Refine dialog: opening size (fittingRefineSize), size line, preview line
sources.observation: The dialog opens at 1.5x of any source, or the largest factor under the 8.4 MP guard. On the FLUX.1 Krea fake, the recommended 1.5 MP 16:9 preset (1664x928) opens at 2496x1392 = 3.5 MP, and a 4 MP source (2048x2048) opens at 2560x2560 = 6.6 MP. The only signal is the size line's 11 px amber 'may run tight on 16GB VRAM'. The preview line still reads 'about 3 of 28 steps run', with no time estimate for a size never run before. docs/verified.md (2026-10-04) says FLUX.1 already fills the card at 2.4 MP; 4.2 MP spills (77 s, 16-22 s per step); 8.4 MP was stopped by hand at 20.2 GB. It also says strength 0.1 at 2x (4.2 MP) starts at sigma 0.752 and repaints the man. By the design notes' own shift arithmetic, 3.5 MP is mu ≈ 2.75, where 0.1 starts at sigma ≈ 0.65, past the 0.62 at which the face 'began to change'. Focus opens on Refine, so ⤢ then Enter runs this unchanged.
sources.why_it_matters: The fastest path through the dialog (open, Enter) on a common FLUX source both spills VRAM for minutes and, by the documented schedule, redraws the subject the user wanted to keep. That is wrong output plus wasted time, with the warning in the smallest text in the dialog.

sources.surface: Refine dialog: scale buttons, size line, Strength, preview line
sources.observation: Asked to make an image twice as big with a light touch, a user presses 2× and leaves Strength at the profile's 0.1. On the FLUX.1 Krea [dev] fake the dialog then reads: size line '4.1 MP — 2× the source — may run tight on 16GB VRAM', preview '1 image · strength 0.1 · about 3 of 28 steps run'. Nothing says what docs/verified.md:384-387 measured on the card: 'FLUX.1 at 2x and its own 0.1 starts at sigma 0.752 ... and repaints the man - another face, coat and hands', while 'Mu 1.15 at 0.2 starts at 0.463 and keeps him'. That warning exists only in the 78-word Strength ? tooltip ('FLUX.1's shift grows with the size, so 2x redraws more than 1.5x at one strength'), which shows on hover only. The dialog also remembers the scale it last ran (prefs.scale=2), so the next image opened, 1024×1024, starts at 2048×2048 with 0.1. That reproduces the repaint without the user choosing 2× again (d04: '4.2 MP — 2× the source — may run tight on 16GB VRAM').
sources.why_it_matters: Wrong output in the core Refine flow. 'Bigger, keep the picture' is the reason the feature exists (design notes: 'A refine pass keeps the picture'), and on the default checkpoint the obvious choice of 2× plus the default strength changes the subject's face. The user finds out only after the pass, and the minute it took is lost.

findings.title: The chip tray shows every tag green and never marks the 77-token CLIP cut, though about 47 of 70 tags are never read
surfaces: Tag validation tray (#tag-validation, wide host above the viewer)
findings.recommendation: Show the cut in the tray in two steps. (1) S effort, no backend: while analysisResult is fresh (not analysisStale), take the earliest prompt-field encoder `cut`, convert it with units(), and find the comma item that contains it. In renderTagValidation, give that chip and every later one a .past-cut class (opacity .55, dashed border, title 'not read: CLIP-L/CLIP-G stop at 75 tokens'). Mark the chip the cut splits as 'partly read'. (2) M effort: add POST /api/prompt/measure, which returns only prompt_encoding.measure(...) (encoders and encoders_detail) on _detached, with no rules and no tag lookup. Call it from validatePromptTags after a 600 ms debounce, with its own epoch. A tokenizer still inside LOAD_WAIT, or an encoders_detail entry, renders as 'cut unknown' and never as 'no cut'. Show the count without adding a child element: set els.tagValidation.dataset.tokens = '110/75' and change the ::before rule (style.css:258) to content: "Prompt tags · Danbooru " attr(data-tokens), with an amber variant when it is over. Then the `[...els.tagValidation.children].every(valid)` smoke steps still hold. If you add a divider, place it with CSS (a box-shadow or ::before on the first .past-cut chip), not as a sibling element. Check remains the full report.
findings.documented_rule: CLAUDE.md Prompt analyser: Check works cold. It uses CPU tokenizers on a _detached thread, never ensure_loaded or the gate, and status never loads a tokenizer. measure never raises, and a loading tokenizer is reported as still loading. Offsets are code points, converted with units(). design-notes 'Animagine XL 4.0': the chips are a round-trip editor (writePromptTags), and green means a known tag. The guide prose says 'Both CLIP tokenizers stop at 77 tokens'.
findings.rule_tension: No rule makes the cut Check-only. Calling POST /api/prompt/analyze from the tray is the weak part of the original recommendation. For a tag prompt it also runs every rule and _lookup_tags, which asks Danbooru for categories on up to 64 items (main.py:612-622). Doing that on every validation pause would double the network lookups and run the order rules unseen. A first measure on a tag checkpoint may also fetch tokenizer files without anyone pressing Check. That is allowed, since the 'never from /api/status' rule is about status, but the cost should be stated. The compatible fix is a measure-only route on the same _detached path, plus the data a Check already returned.
findings.smokes_affected: None break with the CSS-only divider and label. Steps that iterate `els.tagValidation.children` would break if a real divider or label element were inserted: smoke-animagine 10 and 14, smoke-illustrious 13, 21 and 24, smoke-kohaku 12 and 17, smoke-wai 17. smoke-animagine 120-123 (the 70-tag Check) would make one extra background request. New steps are needed for the past-cut class and the 'cut unknown' state.
findings.how_checked: Fresh Animagine fake on 7917 at 2560x1305 DPR 1. I used a realistic 39-tag prompt: identity first, detail tags, and the card's suffix last. I dispatched input, measured the tray, then pressed Check and mapped the reported cut offset (code points) onto the comma items.
findings.verifier_notes: The finding's '47 of 70' comes from its own prompt. My prompt lost 13 of 39 chips. The fake tokenizer counts a token per word or mark, and real CLIP BPE is usually denser on Danbooru names such as 'firefly (honkai: star rail)', so real cuts come at least as early. The sharpest cost: on any prompt over about 75 tokens, the guide's own 'finish with masterpiece, high score, great score, absurdres' suffix is the first thing lost, and it shows four green ticks. The same applies on Kohaku, Illustrious and WAI (SDXL, 77 tokens). Severity stays high: the output is silently wrong, the always-visible view says nothing, and Check is the only place that tells you.

sources.surface: Tag validation tray (#tag-validation, wide host above the viewer)
sources.observation: With the 70-tag prompt, the tray shows 68 green ✓ chips and 2 red ones in 4 rows (144px tall). Pressing Check then reports 'CLIP-L and CLIP-G read the first 75 of the prompt's 194 tokens and stop at "dress, detached sleeves, black gloves...": the rest never reaches them.' That cut falls at chip 23 of 70, so about 47 chips (67%) are never read, yet they look exactly like the ones that are. The tray is the prompt view that is always on screen. Nothing in it shows the cut: no divider, no dimming, no token count. The guide's own prompt hint says 'Both CLIP tokenizers stop at 77 tokens, so put identity and essential details first.'
sources.why_it_matters: On an SDXL tag checkpoint, the cut is the most important fact about a long tag list. Here the green tick reads as 'this tag is fine' on tags the model never sees. Users pile on detail tags and quality suffixes past the cut, and lose them without knowing, unless they think to press Check and read a small Encoders column.

findings.title: The grid preview hides the resolved prompt when variables collapse to one prompt, so 'size = big, small' silently renders 'a big, small fox'
surfaces: Grid preview line (#grid-preview)
findings.recommendation: In previewGrid (generation.js:331-344), list the resolved prompt whenever els.gridPrompt.value.trim() is non-empty, even when there is only one. Change promptLines' guard to `if (!prompts || !prompts.length) return []` and call it only when the variables box has text; prefix a single prompt with 'prompt: '. Add a client-side pass over the variable lines: for each line matching /^\s*([A-Za-z_]\w*)\s*=(.*)$/ whose value has no '|', add the warn class and append a line. If the value contains ',', the line reads "size has one value 'big, small' - values split on |, not commas"; otherwise it reads 'size has one value: it never varies'. Keep the | split.
findings.documented_rule: Design notes 'The prompt is an axis: variables': values split on |, not commas, because a comma belongs to the prompt. The comment at generation.js:274-277 says substitution 'goes wrong quietly', so the preview shows the finished text. 'Grid preview and the per-step estimate': the preview is the server's own expansion.
findings.rule_tension: No conflict. The | split stays, and the fix only shows the resolved text and warns. The warning is client-side and advisory (warn colour, like the duplicate-cells warning), so the server's single parser is unchanged.
findings.smokes_affected: smoke.json 151-154 (a variable used in the negative prompt, then preview): its includes() checks still pass, but a 'prompt:' line may now appear, so re-run. smoke-conditioning.json 66 has no variables box and is unaffected.
findings.how_checked: Fake on 7912. Prompt 'a {size} fox sitting in the snow', variables 'size = big, small', Steps 6-12x2, CFG 2,3.5,5. Read #grid-preview's text and its warn class, and called /api/grid/preview with gridPayload() directly. Compared against 'size = big | small', against two variables with one comma line, and against a one-value 'size = big'. Read promptLines and previewGrid in generation.js:278-344 and the design-notes section 'The prompt is an axis: variables'.
findings.verifier_notes: Reproduced exactly. High stays: the preview's one safety net for substitution switches off in exactly the case where it is needed, and a night's prompt comparison runs with no warning. The placeholder and tip both show |, which limits how often this happens but not what it costs. I widened the warning to any one-value variable, since a variable that never varies is always a mistake in a grid.

sources.surface: Grid preview line (#grid-preview)
sources.observation: Prompt 'a {size} fox sitting in the snow', variables 'size = big, small' (commas, as in every other grid box and the CFG placeholder '0,0.5,1'), Steps 6-12x2, CFG 2,3.5,5. The preview read '12 images · 4 steps x 3 CFG x 1 mu x 1 seed · about 5s', with no warn colour and no prompt line. The summary drops the prompts factor entirely, and promptLines() returns nothing for fewer than 2 prompts. Every cell would render 'a big, small fox sitting in the snow'. A direct preview call confirmed the server accepts it as one value.
sources.why_it_matters: The design note on promptLines says substitution 'is the half of a prompt grid that goes wrong quietly' and that the preview shows the finished text to catch it. That safety net switches off in the one case where the variable did not vary. A whole overnight run gets spent on a variable that never varied.

findings.title: 'Lost the generation stream. The run carries on — reload to pick it up.' is false when the server died, and reloading says nothing about the dead run
surfaces: Panel progress and #error after the SSE stream fails; the page after a reload
findings.recommendation: In source.onerror's give-up branch (generation.js:496-499), before writing the message, probe GET /api/jobs/<id> (the route exists, main.py:1226-1231). On a network error: 'Can't reach the server — it may have stopped. The N image(s) finished so far are saved. Start it again; the page will notice.' G1.3's offline state then takes over. On a 404: 'The server restarted, and this job ended with it after N of M images. They are in the gallery; Generate again for the rest (a grid: tick Resume).' N = shown.size and M = the last data.total_runs (times the batch) seen. In both cases call resetGallery() and loadRuns(), so the saved image shows up without waiting for another job. On a 200, call streamJob(jobId) again rather than asking for a reload. resumeActiveJob only finds live jobs, and events() answers done for a finished one. The original finding's 'skip the five retries when readyState is CLOSED' is already the behaviour: the condition reads readyState === CONNECTING, and the 404 gave the message 3.5 s after the kill.
findings.documented_rule: design-notes 'A job outlives the page; per-stream queues': the browser's auto-reconnect is left alone for the first few failures, and /api/jobs lets a reload reattach. design-notes 'events() opens with done'. design-notes 'The morning after: runs and finished jobs': finished jobs live in memory, so a restart loses the 'why'.
findings.rule_tension: Compatible. Keep the five auto-reconnects and the /api/jobs reattachment. The probe runs only after the stream has given up. On a 200, re-opening streamJob(jobId) is safe: events() opens with done for a job that has already finished.
findings.smokes_affected: None. No smoke breaks a stream; grep finds no step on 'Lost the generation stream' or 'reconnecting'.
findings.how_checked: Two crash runs on 7971 (--step 0.3, Runs 4, os._exit at T+12.3 s). Long outage: restart after 30 s. Fast restart: restart after 1 s, so the reconnect hits the new process's 404 for the old job id. Sampled the progress line and #error every 500 ms, then checked /api/jobs?include_finished=true, the Runs picker and #viewer, reloaded, and measured again. Read generation.js:377-525, main.py:1226-1264 and panel.js:168-194.
findings.verifier_notes: Reproduced in both variants. The copy is false when the server died: nothing carries on, and a reload shows nothing about the run. Severity stays high because it misleads about a job's state, and on an overnight grid it hides that most of the night is missing. Adjusted only in the recommendation: the 'skip retries when CLOSED' point is moot, a 200 should re-open the stream itself, and the gallery must refresh.

sources.surface: Panel progress and #error after the SSE stream fails; the page after a reload
sources.observation: Outage (server down 35 s): progress read 'reconnecting… (1)' at T+13.5 through '(5)' at T+25.5. Meanwhile the bar stayed frozen at 13/28 and the cell line at '13s elapsed · ~22s left'. At T+28.5 the red message appeared, while the server was down, so a reload would fail outright. Fast restart (server back about 3 s after the kill): the reconnect hit the new server's 404 for the old job id (main.py:1262), EventSource closed, and the same message appeared at T+16, while the topbar already said 'not loaded'. /api/jobs and /api/jobs?include_finished=true both returned []. Nothing carried on. Doing what the message says (reload) showed no banner (finished jobs live in memory) and an empty viewer. The dead 4-run job appears in the Runs picker only as '4 Oct, 04:23 pm · 1 img · a lighthouse…', with nothing saying it stopped after 1 of 4. Its saved image was in the viewer but not in the gallery until another job finished.
sources.why_it_matters: The message tells the user to wait or reload for a job that no longer exists, so the missing three images are discovered later, if at all. The one fact the user needs (the server restarted, 1 of 4 images saved, run again for the rest) is never stated.

findings.title: Delete unstarred deletes the source of a starred refine pass, and nothing before the click says the pass depends on it
surfaces: Delete unstarred dialog, card/lightbox delete confirm, lightbox lineage line
findings.recommendation: (1) storage: add one predicate under keep_favorites, used by both matching_preview and delete_matching: `id NOT IN (SELECT refine FROM images WHERE favorite = 1 AND refine IS NOT NULL)`, plus the json_each(reference) equivalent for klein references. Have matching_preview return `sources_kept`. main.py:1413 then becomes `unstarred = records - favorites - sources_kept`; clear.py:103/159 use the same field. The dialog's first line reads 'Delete 72 unstarred images ..., keeping 4 starred and 1 image a starred pass was refined from (63)?'. (2) In deleteImage, before confirm(), ask `/api/gallery?limit=1&all_models=true&search=refine:${rec.id}` (the `refine:` key exists in search.py). When total > 0, add 'Image 78 was refined from this one; once it is gone that pass cannot be made again.' (3) Have list_images LEFT JOIN the source and return `refine_missing`. Render 'refine of 63 (deleted) @ 0.1' at lightbox.js:112 and 'itself a refine of image 63, since deleted' at refine.js:112.
findings.documented_rule: design-notes 'Delete unstarred': the scope is the search box plus favorite = 0 (plus the checkpoint scope); the gate is typing the count back, and `expected` is compared under the write lock. CLAUDE.md Reproduction: the refine source is a gallery id on the row and in the PNG, and is part of the reproduction set. design-notes 'The refine pass': 'Reuse on a refined record asks GET /api/images/{id} for its source ... A source that has been deleted cannot be refined again'.
findings.rule_tension: Keeping sources inside the sweep changes what 'unstarred' selects, so the count gate has to move with it. The dialog's number comes from main.py:1413 `unstarred = records - favorites`, which has to subtract the kept sources too. Otherwise the typed number never equals the COUNT(*) delete_matching takes under the write lock, and every sweep answers 409. The CLI shares delete_matching: clear.py:103 and :159 compute kept/doomed from `favorites` alone and need the same field. With the predicate shared and the counts derived from it, the typed-count and `expected` pin still hold. Sources stay ids. A warn-only variant (count those sources in the preview and name them in the dialog, without keeping them) leaves the sweep's meaning alone if the auto-keep is felt to be too implicit.
findings.smokes_affected: None break if the wording keeps its substrings. smoke.json:174-181 expects the dialog to include 'Delete N unstarred images' and 'keeping K starred', plus `total === __k` and every remaining record starred after the sweep. Its run has no refine pass, so the new clause never appears there. smoke-refine.json:55 ('refine of ' + source + ' @ 0.1') and :60 ('itself a refine of image ' + source) only see live sources, so the '(deleted)' suffix never shows in them. smoke-refine.json:138 (the Reuse note) is unchanged.
findings.how_checked: Fresh FLUX.1 Krea [dev] fake on 7972, seeded through the API: 60 filler images, source 63 (1024², seed 400) and its pass 78 (1536², refine of 63 @ 0.1), a 3x3 steps x CFG teapot grid and a 4-image fox batch; 76 images in all. I starred pass 78 with its card star, then ran Delete unstarred with an empty search, stubbing window.prompt to capture the dialog text and type the count back. Afterwards I checked the source's status, the lightbox line, the Refine dialog line and Reuse, and logged the per-card confirm text for source 63.
findings.verifier_notes: Reproduced exactly as described. I adjusted only the recommendation: the original omitted that main.py derives the dialog's count as records - favorites, so adding the predicate without changing that formula makes every sweep a 409, and the CLI's clear.py shares delete_matching. I kept high because this happens on the documented triage path (refine, star the pass, sweep the rest): the source PNG is deleted from disk, with no undo, by a gesture whose dialog says nothing about it, and the user finds out only at a later Reuse. The kept pass itself survives, which is the one argument for medium.

sources.surface: Delete unstarred dialog, card/lightbox delete confirm, lightbox lineage line
sources.observation: Seeded gallery: refine pass 82 (1536², refine of 67 @ 0.1), with source 67 unstarred. Starred 82, then ran Delete unstarred with an empty search. The prompt() read: 'Delete 67 unstarred images in the gallery (FLUX.1-Krea-dev only), keeping 5 starred?' plus three sample prompts, 250 chars and 8 lines, and said nothing about the pass. After typing 67 the page said 'Deleted 67 images, keeping 5 starred.' Image 67 was among them. The kept, starred pass still reads 'refine of 67 @ 0.1, seed 400' in the lightbox (d06). The Refine dialog opened on it says 'itself a refine of image 67' (d07). Reuse puts the source's settings in the panel at 1024×1024 with the note 'Image 67, the source this was refined from, is no longer in the gallery, so the pass cannot be made again.' (d08). The per-card confirm for 67 doesn't warn either: 'Delete this image (seed 400)? "portrait of an old fisherman, weathered face, golden hour" The file is removed from disk.', even though search refine:67 returns [82].
sources.why_it_matters: A star means 'keep this', and the refine source is part of the pass's reproduction set (CLAUDE.md: the refine source is on the row and in the PNG). The sweep removes that PNG from disk with no undo, and the user finds out only on a later Reuse, when the pass can no longer be made again.

findings.title: At QHD the Refine dialog is 460 px wide and shows the image being refined only as a 72 px cover-cropped thumbnail
surfaces: Refine dialog (#refine-dialog)
Refine dialog layout at QHD
Refine dialog: source block (.rf-source) and overall dialog size
findings.recommendation: At @media (min-width: 1600px): .refine-dialog { width: min(1400px, calc(100vw - 64px)); max-height: calc(100vh - 64px) } .refine-dialog[open] { display: grid; grid-template-columns: minmax(0,1fr) 420px; column-gap: 24px; align-content: start } .refine-dialog > * { grid-column: 2 } .rf-source { display: contents } .rf-source img { grid-column: 1; grid-row: 1 / span 12; width: 100%; height: auto; max-height: min(calc(100vh - 140px), 1100px); object-fit: contain; align-self: start } .rf-source-text { grid-column: 2 }. Use height:auto, not the proposed fixed calc(100vh - 140px): the fixed height letterboxes a 16:9 source (about 918x512 of picture inside a 918x1100 box). In openRefine (refine.js:109), set src = rec.url when matchMedia('(min-width: 1600px)').matches, else thumb_url, and alt = `Image ${rec.id}, the source`. Below 1600 px keep the single column, but give the 72 px thumb object-fit: contain so it shows the whole picture instead of the middle 56% of a 16:9 source. The crop overlay (visual-7, refine-flow-4) belongs to M51 and builds on this.
findings.documented_rule: CLAUDE.md Frontend 'A refine pass is the Refine dialog's (web/refine.js)' with its modal contract (index.html:533-539: 'Modal like the lightbox: focus stays inside, Escape closes it'; Refine autofocused); style.css:964-966 'A dimmed rather than a near-black backdrop: the page behind it is context'. No rule fixes the 460 px width or the 72 px thumb. openRefine closing the lightbox (refine.js:98, app.js:235) is a choice, not a documented requirement.
findings.rule_tension: None, provided the DOM order (tab order), showModal, the autofocus on Refine, Escape/Ctrl+Enter and the source and prompt lines stay as they are. A CSS grid with .rf-source {display: contents} changes only the layout. The 'page behind is context' rationale is better served by the source in the dialog than by the stage behind it, which shows the strip's last image: refining image 3 showed image 6 behind it.
findings.smokes_affected: None. smoke-refine.json, smoke-refine-unavailable.json and smoke-conditioning.json run at 1400x900, below the breakpoint, and no smoke step reads refineThumb or the dialog's geometry. smoke-refine step 20 (refineSourceLine startsWith '896×1152 · seed 5') keeps working because the source line is unchanged.
findings.how_checked: Fresh FLUX.1 Krea [dev] fake on 7910. Opened ⤢ on a 1664x928 (16:9 1.5 MP) source, a 896x1152 source and a 2048x2048 source at 2560x1305 DPR 1, and again at 2048x1040 DPR 1.25. Measured the dialog and thumb rects, the natural size, object-fit and the backdrop. Injected refine-dialog-1's CSS at runtime (plus src=rec.url) and measured the two-pane layout with the fold closed and open.
findings.verifier_notes: Every measurement in the three source findings reproduced exactly: dialog [1050,372,460,561], thumb 72x72 of a 384x214 webp under object-fit cover, and the same 460 CSS px at 125%. I lowered the severity from high to medium. The cost is a clear waste of the QHD screen and recurring friction in the user's named pain point, but nothing blocks or misleads: the title, source line and prompt line do identify the image. The refine-dialog-1 grid CSS works as written, with no row spreading and no scroll even with the fold open. Only the fixed image height needs changing to height:auto with a max-height. visual-7's variant (980 px, source in a column on the left of a 420 px controls grid) is equivalent; I kept refine-dialog-1's because I prototyped and measured it. All three findings in the cluster describe one problem.
findings.merge_note: refine-flow-4 notes the backdrop behind the dialog shows an unrelated image. visual-7 adds that there is no crop preview for a reshaped W/H. All three propose a two-column dialog with a large source at min-width 1600px.

sources.surface: Refine dialog: source block (.rf-source) and overall dialog size
sources.observation: At 2560x1305 the dialog is 460x561 px at (1050,372): 18% of the width and 43% of the height, with the rest of the screen dimmed. The source appears only as a 72x72 thumbnail. Its src is the 384 px webp thumbnail (natural 384x214 for the 16:9 harbour), cropped with object-fit: cover, so a 16:9 source shows only the middle 56% of its width. The thumbnail has no click or zoom. Opening Refine from the lightbox closes the 1270 px-tall view the user was just looking at (h03 vs k01). At 2048x1040 at 125% the dialog is the same 460 CSS px with the same 72 px thumbnail. Strength and scale are chosen about the picture, but the picture is effectively absent. A CSS-only prototype injected at runtime (grid, .rf-source display:contents, img in column 1, src = rec.url) gives a 1400x1138 dialog with the source at 918x1100 and the unchanged controls in a 420 px column.
sources.why_it_matters: Refine is about detail (a face that may be repainted, the edge a reshaped size crops away). The user commits to minutes of GPU time while looking at a 72 px swatch, and has to close the dialog and open the lightbox to check anything. This is the main source of the 'clunky' feel on a 2560 px screen.

sources.surface: Refine dialog layout at QHD
sources.observation: At 2560×1305 the dialog is 460×561 px (18% of the width; 22.5% at 2048×1040 with 125% scaling) and centred over the stage. Its only picture of the source is #refine-thumb at 72×72 with object-fit: cover, so an 896×1152 portrait loses its top and bottom. Behind the 0.6 backdrop the stage shows whatever the strip last held: refining the fisherman (image 3) from a gallery card left the fox (image 5) big and dimmed behind the dialog (a04). The dialog is modal, so the user cannot look at the source at size while choosing a scale, a strength or a crop. Closing it to look costs the settings (refine-flow-5). With the fold open, or for another checkpoint's image, it grows to 832-851 px tall, and at 460 px the summary 'PROMPT AND SAMPLING' wraps to two lines beside the note 'made on Krea-2-Turbo: steps, CFG and mu are FLUX.1-Krea-dev's' (c06).
sources.why_it_matters: Strength is a judgement about this picture: how much detail to keep and where the crop falls. The page shows a different picture larger than the one being refined, which invites confusion about which image will be refined, and it wastes about 2000 px of width.

sources.surface: Refine dialog (#refine-dialog)
sources.observation: At 2560x1305 the dialog is 460x561 at (1043,372), 7.7% of the screen. Unfolded it is 460x832, with the prompt in a 3-row box. The only picture of the source is `.rf-source img`, 72x72 object-fit:cover, which crops the thumbnail too. W and H are free number boxes, and the size tip says the source 'is scaled to cover this size and cropped to its shape'. Nothing in the dialog shows which part of the picture a different aspect keeps. The rest of the screen is the page behind a 0.6 black backdrop.
sources.why_it_matters: Refine is the feature the user named as clunky. It is a decision about one specific image: how much to upscale, how much to repaint, what gets cropped. On a 2560px screen the image is shown smaller than a gallery card (171px), and a crop is only discovered after the pass has run.

findings.title: The viewer stacked above the gallery pushes the gallery down to one row, or below the fold, while one image leaves most of the viewer empty
surfaces: Results viewer above the gallery (stage column)
Results viewer, many tier, and the gallery's first rows
Stage: results viewer (#viewer) above the gallery
findings.recommendation: (1) S, in `@media (min-width: 2000px)`: `.viewer.many { grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(160px, 1fr)); max-height: min(560px, 45vh); overflow-y: auto; align-content: start }`, `.viewer.many img, .viewer.many img.preview { width: 100%; height: auto; max-height: none }`. In appendResult, if the strip was scrolled to its end before the append, scroll it to its end again. Extend #viewer-note to 'N this run, scroll the strip or open one to walk them all'. Prototype without the cap at QHD: 28 images go from 4 rows/1090px to 3 rows/554px (heading 1219→683, fully visible cards 0→36), and 48 from 1625px to 732px (heading 1756→861). At 125% auto-fill alone gives only 834→743 with 0 cards visible, which is why the cap is needed. (2) S: `.viewer:has(> .placeholder) { min-height: 120px }`. On every page load the empty box drops from 380px to 120px (heading 509→249, cards 48→60 at QHD). (3) S: outline gallery cards whose id is in viewerRecords (`.card.this-run`, 2px var(--accent-2), set in card() and cleared in clearResults), so the first gallery rows read as the same run the strip shows. Do not reverse the strip's order: the lightbox and the preview slot depend on append order. (4) Optional, L: at >=2000px a two-column stage, with #viewer and #viewer-note sticky on the left and the gallery head, grid and Load more on the right. #tag-validation-wide and the sheet span both columns, and the many tier is recomputed for the half width. This is the only option that fixes the single image's ~1270px of empty width at QHD and the 125% case, where one 1024² render leaves zero gallery cards fully visible.
findings.documented_rule: docs/design-notes.md 'The running batch on wide screens' (line 1573): at >=2000px the many tier uses eight equal columns so QHD fits more than seven per row at 100% and 125%, and the live preview shares those columns. web/panel.js:264-265: the tiers exist so a sweep does not push the gallery down. VIEWER_MAX=48 bounds DOM nodes and fetches.
findings.rule_tension: Switching from 8 fixed columns to `repeat(auto-fill, minmax(160px,1fr))` keeps the rule's purpose (12 per row at 100%, 9 at 125%, both more than 7) but changes its wording, so the design note must be updated in the same change. A height cap keeps VIEWER_MAX and the lightbox walking viewerRecords. The source findings disagree: visual-4 wants the single image larger, gallery-6 wants it at 55vh. The 55vh shrink is a trade of taste and is dropped.
findings.smokes_affected: None. Every smoke runs at 1400x900, below the 2000px query, and no smoke asserts viewer geometry, the placeholder's height or the many tier (grep of 'viewer' in tools/smoke*.json finds only a viewerRecords field check in smoke-refine.json:51).
findings.how_checked: Fake FLUX server with 144 planted images, 2560x1305 and 2048x1040@1.25. I measured the viewer, the first image, the gallery heading and the count of fully visible cards in five states: empty, after 1 image, Batch 4, 28 images and 60 images. In a 4x2 run I compared viewerRecords seeds with galleryRecords. I then injected the proposed CSS into the page (browser only, nothing in the repo) and measured again.
findings.verifier_notes: Code: web/style.css:654 (min-height 380px), 664 (68vh), 686 (repeat(8,...)), web/panel.js:257-278 (appendResult, VIEWER_MAX). This is the merged cluster's three findings reconciled into one plan, items 1-3 being S each. The results-5 two-row cap is reasonable, but 45vh/560px fits both scalings better than a calc on 20vh tiles that no longer exist once the columns auto-fill.
findings.merge_note: gallery-6 measures 12 of 145 cards visible after one render and proposes a 55vh cap. results-5 covers the many tier: a 35-48 image strip puts the gallery heading below the fold, and the gallery then repeats those images in reverse order. It proposes a two-row scroll cap.

sources.surface: Stage: results viewer (#viewer) above the gallery
sources.observation: At 2560x1305, one 1024x1024 result makes the viewer 2176x917 with the image capped at 68vh = 887x887. That is 87% of native size, though about 1180px of height is available, and roughly 1290px of the viewer's width is empty. The gallery heading lands at y=1046, so one 172px row of thumbnails shows. A 28-image batch switches the viewer to the 'many' tier: 8 columns of 256px tiles, 1090px tall. The gallery heading moves to y=1219, entirely below the fold. The same 28 images are on the page twice, at 256px in the viewer and 171px in the gallery (12 per row). VIEWER_MAX is 48, so a long run grows the viewer to 6 rows, about 1600px, more than a screen. panel.js:264-265 says the tiers exist 'so a long sweep does not push the gallery a screen further down'; at QHD the tier itself pushes it more than a screen down. At 2048x1040@1.25 the single image is 707x707 and the gallery has 9 per row at 174px.
sources.why_it_matters: Look, judge, iterate is the core loop. At QHD the user scrolls past a full screen of duplicated tiles to reach the gallery and its search, Sheet and favourites. A single result is shown smaller than native, with three-fifths of the viewer empty. The screen's main advantage, width, goes unused.

sources.surface: Results viewer above the gallery (stage column)
sources.observation: On a fresh load an empty 380px box saying 'Generated images appear here.' sits above the gallery, whose header is at y=509 (48 cards fully visible). After one 1024² generation the viewer is 917px tall (68vh image), the gallery header moves to y=1046 of 1305, and only 12 of 145 cards are fully visible. After a batch of 4 the header is at y=603 (36 visible). The 1:1 image in the viewer is 887px wide in a 2161px box, with about 620px empty on each side.
sources.why_it_matters: On the target screen the gallery, the place to compare and triage, is almost entirely below the fold after every single render. Every look back at earlier images costs a scroll down and back up.

sources.surface: Results viewer, many tier, and the gallery's first rows
sources.observation: A budgeted grid that kept 35 images grew the viewer to 2161x1357 (5 rows of 256 px tiles). The gallery heading moved to y=1486, below the 1305 px fold. At VIEWER_MAX (48) it would be 6 rows, about 1630 px. The comment at panel.js:264-265 says the tiers stop a sweep pushing the gallery down, but at 8 per row every 8 images add a 268 px row. After a 4x2 run, the 8 results appear in the viewer oldest-first (seeds 300 to 307). They appear again directly below as the gallery's first row, newest-first (galleryRecords [400, 307, 306, ...]). So the first screen shows the same 8 images twice, in opposite orders.
sources.why_it_matters: The gallery, the user's other working surface, scrolls away during a long run, and the duplicate reversed row wastes the rest of the first screen. It also makes it hard to tell which copy is which when starring or comparing.

findings.title: Card tools are six glyph-only 23-29 px buttons labelled only by native title; Refine is a '⤢' that reads as 'expand'
surfaces: Gallery card hover tools (.card .tools)
Gallery card tool row
Gallery card tools row
findings.recommendation:
(1) Instant visible names. In tool() (gallery.js:142) set b.dataset.tip to a short name: Reuse, Refine…, Reference, Sheet, Star, Delete. Render it with `.card .tools button:is(:hover,:focus-visible)::after{content:attr(data-tip);position:absolute;left:6px;bottom:100%;margin-bottom:2px;font-size:12px;padding:2px 6px;border-radius:4px;background:rgba(0,0,0,.85);color:#fff;white-space:nowrap;pointer-events:none}`. The buttons are not positioned, so the tip anchors to .tools' left edge. Placed there it is never clipped by .card's overflow:hidden; a tip centred over the right-edge ⌦ would be.
(2) Fix the overflow. Hide ❐ where it cannot work: syncConditioning toggles `#gallery.no-references`, with `#gallery.no-references .ref-tool{display:none}`. A class rather than a card rebuild, because referenceSupported can flip on a status. And/or at min-width 2000px set `.grid{grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fill,minmax(190px,1fr))}`, which gives 11 columns at 2560.
(3) Separate Delete with `.card .tools .del{margin-left:auto}`.
(4) Where !refineSupported, give ⤢ aria-disabled and opacity .45 through a class synced in status.js; its click still runs openRefine, which explains.
Inline SVG icons are optional and not needed for the fix.
findings.documented_rule: style.css:791-797: the tools are revealed on :focus-within and on coarse pointers. gallery.js:146-149: aria-label carries the name because title is not announced. CLAUDE.md Frontend: 'A ⤢ on a checkpoint without a pass says so and opens nothing', with aria-disabled rather than disabled so a press can still explain. Smoke steps find these buttons by their glyph textContent.
findings.rule_tension: Compatible if the glyph stays the textContent, aria-label stays, the label is CSS only, and ⤢ stays clickable (aria-disabled, with the click still calling openRefine to explain).
