Changing the ⤢ glyph would break two smoke steps and the lightbox's '⤢ Refine' consistency, so keep it.
findings.smokes_affected: smoke-refine.json:20 and smoke-conditioning.json:28,33 find the buttons by textContent '⤢' and '❐'; keep the glyphs. Hiding ❐ only when references are unsupported leaves smoke-conditioning, which runs on klein, unaffected. No smoke clicks ❐ on a checkpoint without references.
findings.how_checked: FLUX fake on 7906 with 60 images at 2560x1305. I hovered a card with the real mouse, measured every tool button's rect, font, opacity and attributes, took an element shot, and pressed ❐ with a real click at (1163,720). Card size and columns were also measured at 2048x1040, DPR 1.25.
findings.verifier_notes: New fact not in the source findings: at QHD the six-button row is wider than the card, so the Delete button is partly clipped. The '⤢ reads as expand' argument is partly taste. The concrete cost is a hover-only, unnamed entry point for the feature the user called clunky; a visible name fixes it without changing the glyph. Merged as given: visual-12 and refine-flow-9 are the same finding as copy-a11y-3.
findings.merge_note: visual-12 notes the glyphs come from font fallback, so their weight varies, and proposes inline SVG icons on 30 px buttons. refine-flow-9 adds that ⤢ is the usual full-screen sign while the image click already opens the lightbox. All three propose instant CSS labels on hover and focus.

sources.surface: Gallery card tool row
sources.observation: Each card's tool row is six glyph-only buttons (↻ ⤢ ❐ ⊞ ☆ ⌦), 23-29 px wide and 24 px tall (a.out T49-T54), at opacity 0 until hover or focus. Their names exist only as native titles and aria-labels. On a card, the new Refine feature is the '⤢' glyph, a generic expand arrow. The ❐ button stays live on FLUX, which takes no references: pressing it writes a refusal into the panel's error slot about 1060 px away (copy-a11y-10). The lightbox labels the same actions in words ('⤢ Refine', 'Reuse settings').
sources.why_it_matters: The user called Refine clunky. Its main entry point needs a hover, then a wait for a native tooltip, then a guess about a glyph. ❐ invites a click that can only fail on most checkpoints.

sources.surface: Gallery card hover tools (.card .tools)
sources.observation: On hover each 171px card shows ↻ ⤢ ❐ ⊞ ☆ ⌦ as buttons of 23x24, 23x24, 25x24, 26x24, 24x24 and 29x24px with 12px glyphs, labelled only by title (for example ⤢ = 'Refine: scale this image up and re-denoise it part of the way'). The glyphs come from font fallback, so their weight and size vary (⌦ is wider and lighter than ↻). The bar covers the bottom 36px, 21% of the thumbnail. The page's own CSS says native titles are 'invisible until you happen to rest on the right pixels, and plenty of setups never show one at all' (style.css:132-134).
sources.why_it_matters: The new Refine feature's main entry point is an unlabeled ⤢ that appears only on hover, beside a delete glyph (⌦) of similar size. That is slow to learn and easy to mis-click.

sources.surface: Gallery card tools row
sources.observation: Each 172px card (12 columns at QHD) has six glyph-only buttons of 23×24 px with 12px glyphs: ↻ ⤢ ❐ ⊞ ☆ ⌦. ⤢ (U+2922) is the usual 'expand / full screen' sign, and the image itself already opens the lightbox on click. The word 'Refine' appears only in the native title= and aria-label, which take about a second of hovering to show. The lightbox, which has room, labels the same action '⤢ Refine', so the card entry point depends on recall.
sources.why_it_matters: The card is the most common way in. A user who reads ⤢ as 'open bigger' either never finds Refine or opens a modal they did not expect. Six unlabelled glyphs side by side make every hover a guess.

findings.title: The panel is a fixed 330 px at every width, so at QHD the 5-row prompt box hides half of a recommended-length prompt
surfaces: #prompt textarea in the 330px settings panel
Page grid (main) and the settings panel's type scale
Panel width and prompt textarea
code_pointers: web/style.css:73 (sticky only where the panel fits)
findings.recommendation: `@media (min-width: 2000px) { main { grid-template-columns: clamp(400px, 18vw, 480px) minmax(0, 1fr); } #prompt { field-sizing: content; min-height: calc(5lh + 20px); max-height: calc(12lh + 20px); } .size-row label.sub { flex: 1; } }`. Keep resize:vertical. Simulated at QHD, this shows an 82-word prompt in full (165 px) and the panel grows only 6 px (1095 vs 1089), because the wider column also unwraps other lines. At 125% the panel grows 48 px (1137) in a 1040 px viewport, so ship it after M1's sticky-bottom fix. Cheaper interim fix: remember the textarea's dragged height in the panel store. The type-scale part of visual-3 belongs to M17, not here.
findings.documented_rule: style.css:70-73, sticky only where the whole panel fits (see M1). design-notes 'The running batch on wide screens': eight viewer columns at 2000px and wider, at 2560 and at 2048 (125%). CLAUDE.md: the 901px threshold for placeTagValidation.
findings.rule_tension: A taller prompt makes the panel taller, against the 'whole panel fits' rule. The proposals' max-height:40vh (522 px) or 30vh would add up to ~400 px to a panel that already overflows at 125% and with the grid open. Cap the growth in lines and land this after M1's measured fit. The eight-column viewer is repeat(8, minmax(0,1fr)) and still holds; cells just shrink (stage 2030 at QHD, 1579 at 125%). The 901px threshold is untouched.
findings.smokes_affected: None: every smoke runs at 1400x900 and the query starts at 2000px. If field-sizing were applied outside the query, smoke-animagine.json:59-60 and :94-96 (which compare Generate's top before and after) could move.
findings.how_checked: Measured the panel, stage, #prompt client/scroll heights and the input widths at 2560x1305 and at 2048x1040@1.25 on the FLUX fake, using a 92-word guide-style prompt cut to 50, 71 and 82 words. Measured a 70-tag prompt on the Animagine fake. Then simulated the proposed wide tier as in-page CSS (main clamp(400px,18vw,480px); #prompt field-sizing:content, 5 to 12 lines) and re-measured, with the grid fold closed and open.
findings.verifier_notes: Real and recurring, but the reviewers' numbers depend on the prompt: half hidden is the top of FLUX's 30-80 word range; a 50-word prompt shows 75%. Two mitigations go unmentioned: the box can be dragged taller (not remembered), and on tag checkpoints the chip strip shows the whole prompt in the stage. The proposals' 30-40vh caps conflict with M1 and are replaced with a 12-line cap.
findings.merge_note: tags-9 measures a 70-tag prompt (73% hidden) and notes that Check findings select words scrolled out of view. visual-3 frames it as a page sized for 1400 px and stretched, and also covers the 10-12 px type scale (see M17).

sources.surface: Panel width and prompt textarea
sources.observation: main's grid is `330px minmax(0,1fr)` at every width. At 2560 the panel is 330 of 2560 px (12.9%) and the stage gets 2176. At 1400 (the smoke size) the same panel is 23.6%. The prompt textarea is 296x123 px (rows=5, 14px/21px), about 40 characters a line. A 50-word prompt (inside FLUX's 30-80 word recommendation) had scrollHeight 186 against clientHeight 123. A 71-word prompt had 249 against 123, so only 49% was visible (j02). The four sampling inputs get 68 px each, and W/H get 93 px with about 110 px empty to their right.
sources.why_it_matters: The prompt is edited every session, and on QHD most of the screen is idle stage (an empty viewer placeholder before the first image). The user scrolls inside a five-line box to edit their own sentence, while the guide in its ? tip says long, detailed prompts give the best results.

sources.surface: #prompt textarea in the 330px settings panel
sources.observation: The panel is a fixed 330px (12.9% of 2560), and the textarea is 296px wide with rows=5 (123px). The 18-tag example exactly fills it. The 70-tag prompt has scrollHeight 459px against clientHeight 123px, so 73% is hidden behind an inner scrollbar. Clicking a Check finding selects words that are often scrolled out of view. Meanwhile the chip view of the same prompt has the stage's full 2176px.
sources.why_it_matters: Tag prompts are long by nature, and the textarea is where the caret, autocomplete, the Tags helper and the Check's span selection all work. Editing through a 5-line slot means constant inner scrolling, at the resolution with the most room to spare.

sources.surface: Page grid (main) and the settings panel's type scale
sources.observation: `main` is `grid-template-columns: 330px minmax(0,1fr)` at every width. The panel is 23.6% of the window at 1400 but 12.9% at 2560; the stage gets 2161-2176px. Body text is 14px, but 50 of the 62 font-size declarations in style.css are 10-12px (26x12px, 14x11px, 10x10px). The Examples/Check/Reset buttons are 19px tall with 10px text. The 18 visible ? badges are 14x14px with a 10px glyph. The Steps/CFG/Mu/Seed/Batch/Runs/W/H captions are 11px, size pills 11px, hints 11px and tooltips 11px. The prompt box, the main input, is 296x125 (rows=5, about 40 characters per line). An 82-word prompt (FLUX's guide asks for 30-80 words) has scrollHeight 270 against clientHeight 123, so 45% of it is visible. The layout is the same at 1400x900 and 2560x1305; only the stage got wider.
sources.why_it_matters: At 100% scaling on a QHD monitor (about 109 PPI on 27") 10-11px labels are hard to read, and the 14px controls are small targets. The prompt, which the user rewrites every session, sits in a 296px box beside 2000px of image area, so a guide-length prompt has to be scrolled to be read or edited. This is the 'never liked the UI' feeling with a measurable cause.

findings.title: Most visible text is 10-12 px at QHD 100%, and the prompt's own Examples/Check/Reset buttons are 10 px on 19 px targets
surfaces: Panel typography: labels, hints, tiny buttons, badges, presets
Panel width, label/hint/button type sizes
Whole page at 2560x1305: panel labels, hints, tips, prompt toolbar, check panel
findings.recommendation:
In one block, `@media (min-width: 2200px)` (QHD at 100% only; the 2000px viewer tier is left alone):
- `main { grid-template-columns: clamp(360px, 17vw, 440px) minmax(0, 1fr) }`
- `.sub i, .hint, .tip, .menu li, .analysis-note.sub, .compare-note { font-size: 12.5px }`
- `.field > span, .section > summary { font-size: 13px }`
- `.ghost.tiny { font-size: 12px; padding: 2px 9px }` (24 px tall)
- `.presets button { font-size: 12.5px; padding: 5px 9px }`
- `.help { width: 17px; height: 17px; font-size: 11px }`
- `.prompt-analysis { font-size: 13px }`, `.analysis-section h3 { font-size: 12px }`, `.analysis-source, .analysis-stale, .critic-kind { font-size: 11px }`

Leave body at 14px: inputs and buttons inherit it, and they are not the problem. Optionally scale the .tag-validation ::before/::after text to 12px. Never ship the type change without the width change.
findings.documented_rule: No rule sets the type scale. Related rules: style.css:98-101 keeps `.field em` as a colour (#a2a2b0), not an opacity. style.css:70-73 makes the panel position:static only below 900 px of height, so on taller screens it is sticky and a taller panel is less likely to fit. The 8-column viewer tier keys off min-width 2000px (design-notes 'The running batch on wide screens').
findings.rule_tension: The type bump on its own breaks the 330 px panel. Injected at 2560, '4 MP' wrapped to a second tier row, Orientation became a two-line box, the 'True CFG' label wrapped away from its ?, the Reference images note wrapped, and the panel grew from 1089 to 1200 px, leaving 29 px before the 1305 px viewport bottom. With the panel at clamp(360px,17vw,440px) (435 px at 2560) in the same media query, the same type gave a 1087 px panel: height-neutral, no wraps, and the Seed box went to 211 px, wide enough for a full 16-digit seed. So the type change must ship together with the M16 panel-width change. Gate it at min-width 2200px, not 2000px. At 125% Windows scaling (2048 CSS px) the OS already renders 11 px as 13.75 device px, and that panel is already 1089 px tall in a 1040 px viewport. The .field em colour rule is untouched.
findings.smokes_affected: None if the change stays behind min-width 2200px. Every smoke runs at 1400x900. The one font assertion (smoke-animagine.json step 13: chip font-size === '12px') and the layout assertions (smoke-paging.json step 15, smoke-animagine.json steps 59-60/94-96, smoke-analysis.json 226-229) all run below the breakpoint.
findings.how_checked: Fresh FLUX.1 Krea [dev] fake on 7901, 2560x1305 DPR 1 and 2048x1040 DPR 1.25. Walked the visible text nodes, skipping closed dialogs, .tip, option and textarea. Measured rects and computed fonts of the prompt toolbar, ? badges, presets, Seed and LoRA. Then injected the proposed CSS live and re-measured, first with the panel at 330 px and then with it widened to clamp(360px,17vw,440px).
findings.verifier_notes: The numbers reproduce within state differences: 84% vs my 79.5% is down to the other reviewer having the check panel open. The finding is real. The problem is the recommendation: as the three source findings write it (body 15px plus the label bumps, at min-width 2000px, with the panel width left to another cluster), it causes wraps and +111 px of sticky-panel height at 330 px. It would also enlarge text that 125% scaling has already enlarged. walkthrough-10's LoRA-select point duplicates M31, and its panel-width point belongs to M16. This cluster's fix depends on M16 and should land with it.
findings.merge_note: panel-6 counts the panel's font sizes alone (38 at 11px, 20 at 10px). walkthrough-10 also notes the Seed box shows 9 of 16 digits, and pairs the type with the panel-width fix in M16.

sources.surface: Whole page at 2560x1305: panel labels, hints, tips, prompt toolbar, check panel
sources.observation: A text-node walk over the visible page, excluding dialogs, tips and input values, measured 751 characters: 302 at 11px, 36 at 10px, 291 at 12px, and only 53 at 14px. That is 45% at 10-11px and 84% at 12px or less. Examples, Check and Reset, the prompt's own tools, are 10px in 19px-tall buttons; so are the Apply/Use rewrite/Use reordered buttons and the 'GUIDE' source badges. Field labels (Steps, CFG, Seed, Batch, Runs) and every hint, tip and size line are 11px. Body is 14px. On a 27-inch QHD screen at 100% scaling, 11px is about 2.9 mm cap-to-descender.
sources.why_it_matters: The user 'never liked the UI', and QHD at 100% is exactly where small text costs reading effort. The panel's explanatory copy (hints, notes, tips) is where this app puts its guidance.

sources.surface: Panel typography: labels, hints, tiny buttons, badges, presets
sources.observation: Computed font sizes of the visible text nodes in the panel: 38 at 11px, 20 at 10px, 9 at 12px, 1 at 13px, and only 3 at the 14px body size. Field labels (Steps, CFG, Mu, Seed, Batch, Runs, W, H) are 11px; the Examples/Check/Reset buttons are 10px text on 19 px-tall targets; the ? badges are 14x14 px with a 10px glyph; preset buttons are 11px on 32x27 px; hints (size line, run hint, cell note) and tooltips are 11px. The section captions (PROMPT, SIZE) are 12px uppercase while the sampling labels are 11px sentence case, so there are two label systems and neither stands out.
sources.why_it_matters: At 100% scaling on a 27-inch QHD screen (about 109 ppi), 10-11px text is roughly 2.5 mm tall, and 14-19 px targets are slow to hit. These hints are where the app explains itself: the 'needs True CFG > 1' note, the run hint, the size warnings. findings.title: Sheet cells size to the stage width only, so a multi-row matrix never fits the QHD screen and 384 px thumbnails are upscaled up to 2.8x
surfaces: Contact sheet cells
Contact sheet grid (#sheet-grid)
Sheet view reached from the gallery header (Runs picker, ⊞ tool, Sheet)
findings.recommendation: In renderSheet (sheet.js:372-383), set two custom properties on .sheet-grid: --sheet-rows = rowValues.length and --sheet-ar = width/height of the commonest aspect, as a number. Build columns as `auto repeat(${n}, minmax(96px, var(--cell-max)))`. In CSS: `.sheet-grid{--cell-max:calc((100vh - 230px) / var(--sheet-rows) * var(--sheet-ar) - 6px); justify-content:center}`. A fixed max in minmax grows like 1fr up to the cap, and vh tracks a resize without JS; tune 230px to topbar + gallery head + controls + header row. With M4's scroll to the gallery head, a 4x3 at QHD becomes about 355 px cells with the whole matrix on one screen, a 3x2 about 530 px, and a 4x3 at 125% about 265 px. For sharpness, give sheet images `srcset=`${rec.thumb_url} 384w, ${rec.url} ${rec.width}w`` and `sizes` = the computed cap in px (min(stage width / n, (innerHeight-230) / rows * ar)), keeping loading=lazy. Keep the export on thumbnails. Optional: a Fit/Fill width toggle in sheet-controls, stored under a local-diffusion.* key inside try/catch. walkthrough-12's extra: after a panel-submitted /api/grid finishes, add an 'Open sheet' link in #cell-note that calls showJob(jobId) (not fresh). Grids still do not auto-open.
findings.documented_rule: Design notes 'The contact sheet': the whole run comes in one page, and a third axis becomes a pin. Design notes 'Panel persistence' (end) and style.css:753-756: the commonest aspect ratio, object-fit: contain. style.css:736-738: many columns scroll sideways rather than squeezing, and the page never scrolls horizontally. sheet.js:433-439: the export draws thumbnails from sheetLayout.
findings.rule_tension: Compatible. A height cap through minmax(96px, cap) keeps the 96 px floor, so wide matrices still scroll sideways inside .sheet-scroll, and aspect and contain are untouched. Export reads sheetLayout and its own sizes, not DOM sizes. Lazy loading stays, so a srcset only fetches a PNG for cells actually on screen and wider than 384 device px.
findings.smokes_affected: No smoke asserts sheet cell sizes. Re-run smoke.json 62-102 (sheet, export, axis order), smoke-paging.json 26-33 (10x6 sheet), smoke-comparison.json, smoke-refine.json 79-82 and smoke-analysis.json 134-135, since renderSheet's column template changes.

sources.surface: Panel: last-run banner under Generate

findings.title: Run status is a 113x5 px bar with 11-12 px text in the left column, far from the image; the tab title never shows progress
surfaces: Panel progress block, topbar, document title
Progress block under Generate; last-run banner
findings.recommendation: (1) S: in streamJob, mirror progress in the tab title: `${Math.round(f*100)}% · run 2/4 — Local Diffusion`, '⏸ Paused — Local Diffusion' while paused, and '✓ Finished 4 images — Local Diffusion' at done until the next focus or input. Restore the title in setBusy(false) and onerror. Nothing in web/ writes document.title today. (2) S: put Pause and Cancel on their own row under the bars, so the bars grow from 113px to about 230px, with progress text at 13px and the ETA at 12px. (3) S: replace the guessed threshold with a measured sticky offset. In app.js, a ResizeObserver on .panel plus a resize listener sets `--panel-top = min(68px, innerHeight - panel.offsetHeight - 12px)`, and `.panel { top: var(--panel-top, 68px) }`. A panel taller than the window then scrolls until its bottom shows and sticks there, keeping Generate, the progress, the ETA and Grid search reachable at 125%. (4) Instead of a new sticky strip across the stage (M effort; at QHD the sticky panel already keeps the progress on screen while scrolling), mirror one compact line in the existing sticky topbar, aria-hidden: 'run 2/4 · 5/10 · ~8s left' plus a 2px progress line along its bottom edge. It is visible at any scroll position and scaling, and fills the topbar's ~1900px of unused width. Making Generate visually quieter while busy is taste, so skip it. The stale-banner part of panel-16 duplicates M19.
findings.documented_rule: web/style.css:70-73 'Sticky only where the whole panel fits' (`@media (max-height: 900px) { .panel { position: static } }`, so Generate, Cancel, the error line and Run grid stay reachable). docs/design-notes.md 'The browser's queue' (Generate stays live while busy) and 'waiting_on and the ETA' (#cell-note is outside #progress). CLAUDE.md: role=progressbar/status, and aria-disabled on Pause and Cancel.
findings.rule_tension: The 900px threshold is stale. The panel is 1071px idle and 1147px running, so at 1040px it stays sticky and its bottom is never reachable, which defeats the rule's purpose. The compatible fix measures the panel instead of guessing a viewport height. Generate stays live, and the topbar mirror is aria-hidden so role=status stays on #progress-text.
findings.smokes_affected: None. No smoke reads document.title or the progress geometry, and none clicks Pause or Cancel by coordinates. The smokes run at 1400x900, where the existing (max-height: 900px) query already makes the panel static, so a --panel-top change does not move them. Run smoke.json, which checks #cell-note's 'Finished' text at :157, to be sure.

sources.surface: Refine dialog: Strength box, its ? tip, its refusals
sources.observation: Clearing Strength shows the placeholder '0.4 or 0.3,0.4,0.5', while the preview says 'strength 0.1' (blank means the server's 0.1). The tip is 499 characters of 11 px text in a 300x161 box. On hover it covers Strength, Versions, Seed, the seed hint, the fold summary and the preview line, and it explains schedule mechanics ('a flow-matching checkpoint's shift puts the same strength at a noisier point than SDXL's') rather than what to type. Its sweep examples, '0.3,0.4,0.5 or 0.2-0.5x0.1', are fixed text in _REFINE_HINTS for every checkpoint, and on FLUX all fall in the 0.2-0.6 range verified.md says 'repaint the man'. Out-of-range values come back in pydantic wording ('strength: Input should be less than or equal to 1', "strength: 'abc' is not a number"). Strength 1 previews as 'about 28 of 28 steps run' with no note that this keeps nothing of the source. A sweep, the tool the notes say 'exists to put the candidates on one sheet', is reachable only by knowing the comma syntax, and the box always opens filled, so the placeholder is never seen.
sources.why_it_matters: Strength is the one number that decides whether the pass keeps the picture, and its meaning changes per checkpoint by a factor of 4 (0.1 on FLUX, 0.4 on SDXL). Copy that suggests SDXL values on FLUX leads to repainted results, and the sweep that would settle the question is hidden.

sources.surface: Refine dialog: Strength box and its ? tip
sources.observation: Strength opens prefilled ('0.1' on FLUX.1), so its placeholder '0.4 or 0.3,0.4,0.5' is never seen. If a user clears the box to read it, it suggests 0.4, which the design notes say repaints a face on FLUX.1. The sweep syntax appears only in a 78-word hover tip that leads with schedule theory. There is no visible control for 'try a few'. Task count for 'try three strengths and pick one': ⤢ (1), click Strength, select all, type '0.05, 0.1, 0.2' (2 plus typing), Refine (3), click a sheet cell (4), F, Escape, then Sheet (5) and clear the job: search (6). Once found it is efficient; the preview line does say '3 images · strength 0.05, 0.1, 0.2 / Opens as a sheet when it is done.'
sources.why_it_matters: The design notes call the strength axis the way 'to put the candidates on one sheet', and it is the safe answer to refine-flow-1. A user who cannot see it falls back to running passes one at a time and comparing from memory.

findings.title: The LoRA select renders as an unstyled white native control, and there is no dark color-scheme for checkboxes and scrollbars
surfaces: LoRA row
Native form controls page-wide: #lora select, the Favorites/All models/Resume/Original checkboxes, the page and sheet scrollbars
findings.recommendation:
1) In :root add `color-scheme: dark; accent-color: var(--accent);`. Live, this turned the sheet's white horizontal scrollbar, the page scrollbar and the Favorites/All models/Original checkboxes dark. It does not fix the select: #lora went to rgb(59,59,59), still 19 px and radius 0.
2) Change style.css:994 to `#lora, .refine-dialog select { width: 100%; padding: 9px 6px; font: inherit; background: var(--panel-2); border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: 8px; color: var(--text); }`, and add `#lora:focus { outline: none; border-color: var(--accent); }`. Live, #lora became 226x41 and both the LoRA and Weight labels sat at y 733; the panel height did not change, because the row height was already set by the 41 px Weight input.
3) Leave the gallery-head, compare and sheet selects as they are. They are already dark, and a shared rule plus a .compact class is optional cleanup, not a fix.
findings.documented_rule: None for the select's look. Related: style.css:519 `.row.disabled select` dims the row when adapters are unsupported. CLAUDE.md says the comparison selects are read directly and are autocomplete=off.
findings.rule_tension: `.row.disabled select` (0,2,1) still sets opacity under a `#lora` rule, which sets no opacity, so it keeps working. A global `select {}` (visual-2) or a `.panel select` rule (panel-7) would also restyle `.compare-seeds select`: under 901 px the prompt check lives inside .panel, and a later equal-specificity rule makes those selects width:100% with 9px padding. Scope the rule to `#lora` (or `.sub select`) plus the existing `.refine-dialog select`. visual-2's `.compact` modifier would also need sheet.js to add the class to the sheet pickers it creates. Ids, values and autocomplete are untouched either way.
findings.smokes_affected: None. smoke-conditioning.json drives the adapter select by value, and no smoke reads #lora's size, colour or colorScheme.
findings.how_checked: Computed styles and rects of #lora, its label and the Weight label at 2560x1305. colorScheme and accentColor on <html>. Screenshots of the white checkboxes, the LoRA row and the sheet's horizontal scrollbar (an 80-cell, 40-column run: scrollWidth 4115 vs 2176). Then set color-scheme:dark live to see what it fixes on its own, and injected a scoped select rule to check the alignment.
findings.verifier_notes: Real as stated. It is the brightest object in the panel on every visit. Adjusted only for the selector: both source recommendations would restyle selects they did not mean to (compare selects under 901 px, the sheet pickers), so scope the rule to #lora and the dialog. color-scheme:dark and the select rule are both needed; neither is enough alone.
findings.merge_note: panel-7 measures the 19 px select beside 41 px inputs (labels misaligned by 17 px), and proposes generalising the refine-dialog select rule.

sources.surface: Native form controls page-wide: #lora select, the Favorites/All models/Resume/Original checkboxes, the page and sheet scrollbars
sources.observation: :root has no `color-scheme`; getComputedStyle(html).colorScheme = 'normal'. The panel's LoRA <select> is the only unstyled select. It measures 226x19px with background rgb(255,255,255), black text, a 1px #767676 border and 0 radius, while every input beside it is 41px tall on #1a1a21 with an 8px radius. Its 'LoRA' label sits 22px lower than the 'Weight' label in the same row (y=755 vs 733), because the row is align-items:flex-end. Selects are styled four separate ways: .gallery-head .runs (radius 6, padding 5px 6px, 12px, 30px tall), .compare-seeds select (padding 2px 6px), .sheet-pick select (padding 4px 6px) and .refine-dialog select (radius 8, padding 9px 6px, about 41px). #lora gets none of them.
sources.why_it_matters: The white select is the brightest object in the settings column after Generate, and it looks broken next to its 41px neighbours. The light scrollbars and checkboxes break the dark theme on every screen. This is much of why the UI reads as unfinished.

sources.surface: LoRA row
sources.observation: Computed style of #lora: background rgb(255,255,255), color black, border-radius 0, height 19 px, font 13.33px. It is the only white element on the dark page. Weight next to it is 41 px tall, so in the flex-end row the 'LoRA' label sits 17 px lower than the 'Weight' label (a02, b01). style.css styles `.refine-dialog select` (994-997) and `.gallery-head .runs` (709-712), but nothing in the panel.
sources.why_it_matters: It's the most eye-catching thing in the panel on every visit, and it makes the panel look unfinished. That matches the user's general dislike of the UI. The misaligned labels also make the row harder to scan.

findings.title: Refined images look like any other card, and 'refine of 14' / 'Refine image 9' name database ids the page never shows
surfaces: Gallery cards; lightbox settings line; Refine dialog title
Refine dialog title, source line, 'Prompt and sampling' note; lightbox settings line
findings.recommendation: (1) In card() (web/gallery.js:91-93), add the class 'refined' and set data-strength when rec.refine != null. Draw a top-left chip with .card.refined::before { content: '⤢ ' attr(data-strength); position:absolute; top:6px; left:6px; z-index:1; padding:2px 7px; border-radius:10px; background:rgba(0,0,0,.62); color:#fff; font-size:12px; pointer-events:none }. This is the same recipe as .card.fav::after, so it reads on light and dark images and does not collide with the star. Do the same for .sheet-cell when the sheet is not already a strength axis. (2) Show the id wherever the page names an image. Prefix the lightbox settings line (lightbox.js:99) with '#<id> · ' and append it to the counter ('1/3 · #5'). Write the provenance as 'refine of #4 @ 0.1', and make it a small link that opens the source with openLightbox(source, [source, rec]) after GET /api/images/4, so ← returns to the pass. Add '#<id>' to the thumb aria-label (panel.js:294). In refine.js:108/112/142/150 and sizes.js:216, replace 'image N' with '#N': 'Refine #4', 'itself a refine of #4', 'as #5 was made', 'Remove #12'. (3) In the lightbox, add a 'Its passes' link that sets the search to refine:<id> and closes the lightbox. (4) Add 'id': ('id', int) to search.FILTERS and the search tip.
findings.documented_rule: CLAUDE.md Reproduction: 'Reference images are gallery ids, never paths'. A refine source is likewise a gallery id ('GenerateRequest.refine - a gallery id, like a reference'). search.py says search terms are key:value predicates. No rule says a pass should look like a direct render or that ids should stay hidden.
findings.rule_tension: None. Showing '#id' keeps ids as the only way a page names an image. An 'id:' filter is one more key:value predicate in search.FILTERS (('id', int)), so it stays inside the grammar. The badge has to be a pseudo-element (or carry aria-hidden) and sit top-left, so the .tools row (revealed on hover/focus) and the .card.fav::after star (top-right) are untouched.
findings.smokes_affected: smoke-refine.json:22 (refineTitle === 'Refine image ' + id); smoke-refine.json:55 (lbMeta includes 'refine of ' + id + ' @ 0.1'); smoke-refine.json:60 (refineSourceLine includes 'itself a refine of image ' + id); smoke-refine.json:138 ('Image 424242, the source this was refined from' if that note is also changed to '#424242'). smoke-conditioning.json:50 (lbMeta includes 'ref ') and smoke-flux.json:45 (lbMeta includes 'CFG 3.5, true CFG 1.5') still pass if the '#id · ' prefix goes at the front and 'ref ' stays. No smoke checks lbCount or the card className.
findings.how_checked: Fake FLUX.1 Krea [dev] on port 7909, viewport 2560x1305. I made two direct renders (ids 3 and 4, both 1264x848), pressed ⤢ on card 4 and ran a 0.1 pass, which became id 5 at 1904x1280. Then I measured the three cards' class, innerText, alt and aria-label, the lightbox settings line (text, font and colour) and the counter, and ran a refine:4 search. I also used Reuse on pass 5 and read the dialog's title and fold note. Finally I grepped web/ for any place that renders rec.id, and checked backend/search.py FILTERS.
findings.verifier_notes: Reproduced exactly as described. One extra fact strengthens copy-a11y-4: Reuse on a pass shows two different unexplained ids in one dialog ('Refine image 4' in the title, 'as image 5 was made' in the fold), with three images in the gallery. On the fake, refine info is stamped on the pixels, which hides the problem; real passes at 0.1 are near-identical to their source, so the card badge matters more in real use. For (2), open the source in the lightbox with a two-item list rather than replacing lbList, so the user can get back to the pass.
findings.merge_note: copy-a11y-4 lists every place the id appears (dialog title, fold note, source line, lightbox) and proposes showing '#id' in the lightbox counter and card labels.

sources.surface: Gallery cards; lightbox settings line; Refine dialog title
sources.observation: A refined card and a direct render have identical DOM and styling (className 'card' for both, same six tools, same alt text). In d02 the 2528×1696 pass and its 1264×848 source sit side by side as the first two cards and cannot be told apart. The lightbox marks a pass only by 'refine of 3 @ 0.1' inside a 12px muted settings line. Image ids appear nowhere on a card or in the lightbox (card innerText is just the six glyphs), the search grammar has no id: key (backend/search.py FILTERS), and refine:<id> needs the source's id, which only the Refine dialog title ('Refine image 3') shows. So 'refine of 3' leads nowhere, and from a source there is no way to list its passes without that number.
sources.why_it_matters: Passes and sources are near-identical thumbnails by design: a pass keeps the picture. Without a mark, starring and deleting ('keep the better one') is guesswork, and the refine: search the tooltip advertises is unusable in practice.

sources.surface: Refine dialog title, source line, 'Prompt and sampling' note; lightbox settings line
sources.observation: The dialog's title reads 'Refine image 9' while the gallery header says '(7)' (d03-2048-refine.png). In the 2560 run it was 'Refine image 7' with 3 images in the gallery. The fold says 'as image 9 was made'. A refined source reads 'itself a refine of image 5', the lightbox settings line says 'refine of 9 @ 0.1', and reference chips say 'Remove image 12'. No card, lightbox or sheet ever shows an image's own id, so these numbers cannot be traced back to a picture. The search tip's `refine:12` filter depends on the same invisible id.
sources.why_it_matters: The first words of the new feature's dialog look like a count or an index and match neither. A refined image's provenance ('refine of 9') is unusable without the id.

findings.title: Every fresh page load opens with an empty 380 px 'Generated images appear here' box above a full gallery
surfaces: Results viewer, empty state (first run and every reload)
findings.recommendation: Pure CSS, no JS state: `.viewer:has(> .placeholder) { min-height: 0; padding: 10px 14px; justify-content: flex-start; }`. Chromium and Firefox 121+ support :has; there is no build step. Make the placeholder one line, e.g. 'Nothing generated this session - Ctrl+Enter runs the prompt; click a gallery image to open it.' For the zero-image case, add a `.viewer.empty-install` class from the first gallery page (set when total === 0 && !other_models). Under it keep the tall box and add a button that calls els.examplesBtn.click(). If JS is preferred, toggle the class in clearResults() and appendResult(), both of which already run before any preview is appended, but never derive it from viewerRecords.length alone.
findings.documented_rule: The viewer is session-only by design (gallery.js:247-248; panel.js:256-258). streamJob clears it only when the first image or preview frame of a job arrives, so the previous results stay up through the queue wait and the load (generation.js:380-382). No note covers the 380px min-height, which dates from the first commit.
findings.rule_tension: Collapsing the empty state keeps the session-only rule; nothing is filled from the gallery. One catch in the recommendation as written: a preview frame calls clearResults() while viewerRecords is still empty (generation.js:416-423). An `idle` class computed from `!viewerRecords.length` would therefore stay on while the live preview shows, and the preview would render in the collapsed, left-aligned box. Key the state on the placeholder's presence instead. clearResults() removes it on the first preview or image.
findings.smokes_affected: None found. The smokes reach the viewer only through viewerRecords and '#viewer img' (smoke-refine 15/51-53/81/105, smoke-preview 8/10, smoke-flux 35-50, smoke-conditioning 23/47-48/69-73, smoke-anima 20-21). smoke-paging.json step 15 (`els.more.top > innerHeight + 400` at 1400x900) still passes with a collapsed viewer: estimated top about 1600 vs 1300 needed.
findings.how_checked: Loaded the page fresh with 0 images for this checkpoint, then reloaded after making 15 and then 95 images. Measured #viewer at 2560x1305 and 2048x1040@1.25. Read clearResults/appendResult (panel.js:250-276) and how streamJob inserts the live preview (generation.js:380-426). Grepped the smokes for viewer, placeholder and coordinate dependencies.
findings.verifier_notes: The other reviewer's 2161 px width (vs my 2176) is just their page scrollbar. Medium holds: 335 px of a 1305 px screen, about two gallery rows, wasted on every reload, more at 125%. Adjusted because the JS toggle as written mis-handles the live-preview phase; the :has() rule avoids that.

sources.surface: Results viewer, empty state (first run and every reload)
sources.observation: The viewer holds only this session's images (viewerRecords; clearResults empties it). After a reload with 157 images in the gallery, the top of the stage is a 2161x380 bordered box with one 14px muted line, 'Generated images appear here.' That is 29% of the 1305px viewport. At 2048x1040@1.25 it is 1649x380, 37% of the height. On a truly empty install (0 images) the page is that box plus a gallery bar with a disabled 'No runs yet' select. The 755px below the bar is bare background, with no pointer to the prompt, Examples or Ctrl+Enter.
sources.why_it_matters: The first thing on screen after every reload is a placeholder, and the user's work starts lower down. On first run the page offers no next step, though the checkpoint's authors' examples are one click away under a 19px 'Examples' button.

findings.title: Input and button borders measure 1.15-1.24:1, so empty fields and secondary buttons almost disappear
surfaces: Colour tokens: --line, --panel, --panel-2, used on every input, select and ghost button
findings.recommendation: Add `--line-strong: #666680` (3.33:1 on --panel, 3.11:1 on --panel-2, 3.54:1 on --bg). Use it for `textarea, input[type=number|search|text], select, .ghost, .help` borders. Keep --line for .panel, .viewer, .card, .section and other dividers. Keep `.ghost:disabled, .ghost[aria-disabled="true"] { opacity: .45 }`, optionally with `border-style: dashed` as a second, non-colour cue. Drop the #1d1d26 fill change. Leave the placeholder as is (#757575 is 3.76:1; placeholders are hint text).
findings.documented_rule: CLAUDE.md 'Frontend and CLI': Generate, Run grid, Ask the critic and Refine are aria-disabled, never disabled, so they keep focus. style.css:597-599 explains the same for .primary. style.css:98-101 keeps .field em at #a2a2b0.
findings.rule_tension: Border colour does not touch the aria-disabled behaviour or .field em. The proposed disabled opacity 0.7 does conflict with the point of disabled styling. With the stronger border it made the disabled 'Run comparison' look almost the same as the enabled 'Ask the critic', and the disabled Orientation look like an enabled ghost (shots/v53, v52). Keep disabled at 0.45. With the new border that is still 1.63:1 border and 2.08:1 text against 3.3:1 and 5.5:1 when enabled, and WCAG exempts disabled controls. Also, #62627a is only 2.92:1 on --panel-2, and raising the fill to #1d1d26 moves fill-vs-panel only from 1.07 to 1.11, which you cannot see.
findings.smokes_affected: None. No smoke asserts opacity, border colour or colorScheme.
findings.how_checked: WCAG contrast computed in Python from the :root tokens. Live injection at 2560x1305 of stronger borders for input/textarea/select/.ghost/.help plus the proposed disabled opacity 0.7, comparing panel and Prompt check screenshots before and after.
findings.verifier_notes: Every measured number reproduces. The stronger border is a clear, cheap improvement (WCAG 1.4.11 on every control, every session), so medium stands. Two parts of the recommendation are wrong: the 0.7 disabled opacity, which removes the enabled/disabled distinction, and the #1d1d26 fill, which does nothing visible. The colour value is also corrected so it reaches 3:1 on both fills.

sources.surface: Colour tokens: --line, --panel, --panel-2, used on every input, select and ghost button
sources.observation: --line #26262f is the border of every input, textarea, ghost button, ? badge and chip. It measures 1.24:1 on --panel #131318 and 1.15:1 on --panel-2. Input fill --panel-2 against --panel is 1.07:1. WCAG 1.4.11 asks 3:1 for the edge that identifies a control. The empty Mu box, the 'off' True CFG box and the 'random' Seed box read as unlabelled dark patches; Examples/Check/Reset, Sheet, Ask the critic and the size tiers' outlines are barely there. Disabled ghost buttons (opacity .45) drop to 2.08:1, so 'Run comparison' and 'Orientation' are near-invisible. Their reason sits in a title tooltip, which does not show everywhere (style.css:132-134 says so). The placeholder, #757575 on #1a1a21, is 3.76:1. Muted text itself is fine at 5.52:1 on --panel.
sources.why_it_matters: With low-contrast edges the controls are hard to find, especially on a large bright-surround monitor, and greyed versus empty states blur together. It also adds to the 'flat, murky' feel of the UI.

findings.title: Each finished job resets the gallery, scrolling to the top and dropping loaded pages
surfaces: Gallery grid below the viewer (resetGallery on done)
findings.recommendation: Replace `resetGallery()` on done (web/generation.js:480) with `prependNew(made)`, outside sheet mode. Fetch /api/gallery under the same search, favorites and all_models params with `limit = Math.min(made + PAGE, sheetPage)`, so a large grid needs no fallback that could leave a gap. Unshift the records whose id is greater than galleryRecords[0].id, insert `card(rec)` with els.gallery.prepend(fragment), and update total, the count, otherModels, syncRerender() and syncDeleteUnstarred(). Chain after galleryPending and drop the result if galleryEpoch changed. Fall back to resetGallery() when the gallery is empty or the fetched page contains no id the page already holds. Leave overflow-anchor at its default: scroll anchoring keeps the same rows on screen, though an auto-fill grid reflows each row by N slots.
findings.documented_rule: docs/design-notes.md 'Paging by id' (line 1472): the browser's anchor is the last record it holds (before=); the moreWatcher/watchMore contract. No design note requires the gallery to reset on job end; the only resetGallery mention is under Delete unstarred.
findings.rule_tension: Compatible. Prepending leaves the last record, and so the keyset anchor, untouched. Sheet mode keeps its reset or showJob path, because the sheet lays itself out from the whole run.
findings.smokes_affected: These read the gallery's head right after a job, and prepend keeps newest-first, so they should pass but must be re-run: smoke.json:166 (galleryRecords[0].run_id), smoke-refine.json:20 (galleryRecords[0].id), smoke-conditioning.json:45 and :92 (galleryRecords[0], slice(0,3)). smoke-paging.json calls resetGallery explicitly and must still pass.
findings.how_checked: 2560x1305 with 281 gallery images. I wheel-scrolled until every page loaded (scrollY 3613, 281 cards), started a job with Generate and measured after done. I then replaced resetGallery in the page only (eval, not the repo) with a prepend prototype: fetch page 1 under the same filters, unshift ids newer than galleryRecords[0], and prepend their cards. I scrolled deep again, ran another job and measured.
findings.verifier_notes: Code: web/generation.js:478-480, web/gallery.js:7-21 (resetGallery empties galleryRecords and the grid), 23-77 (loadGallery and the epoch). When the user is at the top, the common case, prepend and reset look the same, so the change only matters when it helps.

sources.surface: Gallery grid below the viewer (resetGallery on done)
sources.observation: I scrolled the gallery to scrollY 2709 with 224 cards loaded (5 pages) and started a 10-step job. When the job finished, scrollY was 0, the gallery held 48 cards (page 1 only) and the document had shrunk from 4014 to 1904 px. This happens on every job that produces images: generation.js:480 calls resetGallery(), which empties galleryRecords and the grid (gallery.js:7-21).
sources.why_it_matters: Browsing older images while a render runs is the natural thing to do during the wait, and every job end throws that position away. With Runs or a queue this happens once per job, and any page the user paged in has to be scrolled and loaded again.

findings.title: The viewer collapses at the first preview frame and regrows, so the gallery jumps about 540 px twice per Generate
surfaces: Results viewer (#viewer) and live preview
findings.recommendation: Do it in this order. (a) Draw the preview in the box the result will take, not at a fixed min(34vh,320px) (style.css:674). Set previewEl.style.aspectRatio = `${w}/${h}` from the job's size, and give it the same max-height as its tier: 68vh for one expected image, the multi height for 2-4, the many grid cell otherwise. object-fit: contain, keep the dashed 0.85-opacity look. (b) Choose the tier from the expected count, not the running count. Expected count = payload num_images x total_runs, and total_runs is in the first status frame. Toggle .multi/.many there, so an 8-run sweep starts at its final 258 px tiles and does not reflow 887 -> 444 -> 258. (c) Then clearing at the first preview frame no longer moves the gallery, because the preview fills the same height. If you also want the old result kept up for comparison, move clearResults() into show() only. Put the preview in its own slot (absolutely positioned at the viewer's right edge, or in place of the oldest tile), not appended to the flow. Appending wraps a 9th cell in the 8-column many grid, and at 125% it wraps after four 354 px multi tiles (4x354+320+48 = 1784 > 1619 content px). (d) A fallback that needs no layout change: at the first preview frame set els.viewer.style.minHeight to the current offsetHeight, and clear it in show() on the first image.
findings.documented_rule: generation.js:380-381 says results replace the viewer only once the first image of the job lands. That rule is broken by generation.js:418, which calls clearResults() at the first preview frame; nothing in the commit that added the preview (8616111) or in design-notes explains that clear. Also relevant: the panel.js:264 comment ('two size tiers, so a long sweep does not push the gallery a screen further down'), design-notes 'The running batch on wide screens' (8 columns at >=2000 px, preview shares the columns) and 'The live preview' (the preview is never a record).
findings.rule_tension: None real. The fix brings the preview branch into line with the documented intent. It keeps the preview a non-record element that is dropped when the image lands, and it leaves the many tier's 8 columns alone.
findings.smokes_affected: smoke-preview.json steps 5-8 (expects #viewer img.preview while busy and none after, with viewerRecords.length 1). The semantics are kept, but rerun it. No smoke asserts viewer heights or tier classes.
findings.how_checked: Fresh fake on 7905 (black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-Krea-dev, --step 0.3). I made one 1024x1024 image, then started a second job while a 40 ms recorder logged #viewer's height, .gallery-head's page y and every viewer img's size. I also ran an 8-run sweep. Then I repeated the single-image case at 2048x1040, DPR 1.25.
findings.verifier_notes: All shot paths are under scratchpad/ux/. The reviewer's numbers reproduce exactly at 2560x1305. The many tile is 258 px, not 256. This happens on every Generate with a preview-capable checkpoint (FLUX.1, Krea 2), a few steps into the render; klein has no preview. The fix fits together with M41: best-fit tiles keep the viewer at about 917 px for 1-4 images, so the tier change between jobs stops moving the gallery too.

sources.surface: Results viewer (#viewer) and live preview
sources.observation: After a 1024x1024 result the viewer is 2176x917 and the gallery heading sits at y=1046. At the next job's first preview frame the old result is removed and the viewer shrinks to 380 px tall. The gallery heading jumps to y=509, then returns to 1046 when the image lands: two 537 px shifts per image. The preview is a fixed 320x320 (style.css:674, min(34vh,320px)) and the final image is 887x887, so the preview has about 13% of the final's area and sits in a different box. Within one sweep the tiles reflow twice more: 887 px for image 1 (with the 320 px preview beside it), 444 px from image 2, 256 px from image 5. The code comment at generation.js:380-381 says results are replaced only once the first image lands, but the preview branch at :418 clears them at the first preview frame.
sources.why_it_matters: The page moves under the pointer twice per Generate and several times early in a sweep. A user reading or clicking in the gallery during a render loses the target. The last result disappears seconds into the next render, so the user cannot compare it with the new preview.

findings.title: The model-loading wait is a static 'loading weights…' with no elapsed time, and the topbar drops the model name
surfaces: Loading/unloaded states: panel progress, viewer placeholder, topbar
findings.recommendation: (a) While the last status frame has waiting_on === 'load', run a 1 s client ticker from submit. Write it to progress text as 'loading weights · 0:42' and to #cell-note as 'The first load of a session takes a few minutes.' Use the viewer placeholder only when the viewer is empty. (b) Give .fill an indeterminate sliding gradient while waiting_on is 'load'. The existing global reduced-motion rule (style.css:1005) already stills it. (c) Topbar: `${short} · loading…` and `${short} · not loaded`, where short = s.model_id.split('/').pop(). (d) Call refreshStatus() as soon as the POST returns, so the topbar does not say 'not loaded' beside the panel's 'loading weights…'. (e) Add syncUnload() as above, and hide Unload while Load is shown (state 'unloaded'). Today both buttons sit side by side, and Unload on an unloaded model is a 200 no-op. (f) On a cancelled done frame whose last status had waiting_on 'load', say 'Cancelled — the weights keep loading, so the next Generate starts sooner.' (g) When the state turns ready, clear an Unload 409 that is still shown.
findings.documented_rule: design-notes 'waiting_on and the ETA': waiting_on is a field beside status, not a fourth state, and Cancel during a load stays instant; elapsed is server-clock. 'Loading happens in one place': POST /api/model/unload answers 409 while a load is live. CLAUDE.md Frontend: the critic and Expand hold Unload (syncPromptExpansion, status.js:83), and setBusy also writes it (generation.js:48). generation.js:380-381: the previous result stays up through the queue wait and the load.
findings.rule_tension: Compatible with care. (1) els.unload.disabled has two writers today: setBusy and syncPromptExpansion, which overwrite each other. A third, status-driven writer would fight them on each 3 s poll. Fold all three into one syncUnload(): `busy || expandingPrompt || critiquing || modelState === 'loading'`. (2) Per generation.js:380, the viewer usually still shows the previous result during a load, so the viewer placeholder is the wrong home for the timer. Put it in the panel's progress text and cell note. (3) Don't compute elapsed from Date.now() minus a server timestamp. Use a client ticker started at submit; the server's elapsed only starts once the job runs.
findings.smokes_affected: smoke-analysis.json lines 56, 60 and 265 assert els.unload.disabled while the critic holds the card and !disabled afterwards. They still pass on a ready fake (the fake starts loaded) if the writers are merged into one function. No smoke asserts 'loading weights…', 'not loaded', #status-text or the placeholder.
findings.how_checked: Same fake through a scratch wrapper that makes the fake's load take 15 s. Nothing in the repo was changed. Three flows, each sampled every 100 ms (topbar text, dot class, progress text, fill width, cell note, viewer text, Unload disabled, #error): Generate from unloaded; Generate then Cancel at 3.5 s, then click Unload; and the topbar's Load button followed by an Unload click.
findings.verifier_notes: Shot paths are relative to scratchpad/ux/verify-results-2/shots/. Two corrections to the description. 'Unload was enabled throughout' is wrong: setBusy disables it during a load the page is watching. It is live only after a cancel and during a Load-button load (which also shows no panel progress at all). The pulsing topbar dot means the wait is not completely static. The core problem stands: a minutes-long first load shows no elapsed time and never names the model.

sources.surface: Loading/unloaded states: panel progress, viewer placeholder, topbar
sources.observation: The model is not loaded at startup, so the first Generate of every session waits for the load. I patched the fake's load to take 15 s. Throughout the wait the panel showed 'loading weights…' beside an empty 75 px bar, the ETA line stayed blank (no elapsed counter), and the 2176x380 viewer kept saying 'Generated images appear here.' The topbar replaces the checkpoint name with 'loading weights…' and, when unloaded, with 'not loaded', so the page never says which model it is loading (status.js:214-218). For about 2.5 s after Generate the topbar still said 'not loaded' while the panel said 'loading weights…' (3 s poll). After I cancelled during the load, the panel said 'Cancelled before anything finished.' while the topbar kept 'loading weights…' for about 10 s more, and Unload was enabled throughout, although the server refuses unload while a load is live.
sources.why_it_matters: A real first load takes minutes (CLAUDE.md), and an unchanging 0% bar over that time looks the same as a hang. The page does not say which checkpoint is coming or that a cancel did not stop the load. The Unload button invites a click the server will refuse.

findings.title: The just-finished image has no actions where it is shown (star, reuse, refine are gallery-card only)
surfaces: Results viewer images
findings.recommendation: In appendResult, wrap each viewer image in `<figure class="result" data-id>`. Inside go the thumb() img and a `.tools` row built from the card's helpers: reuseButton(rec), the ⤢ handler card() uses (openRefine(rec)), the ☆ star → setFavorite and ⌦ → deleteImage. Skip ❐ and ⊞, which are gallery-browsing actions. Show the row always in the single and multi tiers, on hover/focus in the many tier, with the card's existing CSS scoped to `.result .tools`. Optionally, for a single result, add a 300 px caption column (seed, WxH, steps/CFG, duration from the done summary) in the empty side space. That is secondary; the buttons are the fix.
findings.documented_rule: CLAUDE.md Frontend, Refine: openRefine is reached from a card's ⤢, the lightbox's Refine (which closes the lightbox) and Reuse on a refined record; a ⤢ on a checkpoint with no pass says so and opens nothing. The app.js:230-231 comment says the just-generated image exists only in the viewer, so Reuse is reachable from the lightbox. setFavorite updates `.card[data-id]` (gallery.js:208); forgetImages removes every [data-id] (gallery.js:246).
findings.rule_tension: Compatible. A viewer ⤢ would be a third entry point. It must use the same handler as the card's, so on klein it shows the reason and opens nothing, and CLAUDE.md's list of entry points needs the new one. The wrapper must not use the `.card` class: smoke.json counts `.card` elements, and line 121 expects 0 after a scope change. Use `.result`, extend setFavorite to `.card[data-id], .result[data-id]`, and keep the inner img from thumb() so it stays focusable and still opens the lightbox.
findings.smokes_affected: smoke.json lines 37, 121 and 181 count `.card` (so don't reuse that class). smoke-refine.json:20 and smoke-conditioning.json:28/33 select `.card .tools button` (unaffected if the class is `.result`). smoke-conditioning.json lines 28 and 52-53 (klein: card ⤢ and lightbox Refine refuse with the reason) would need a third step for the viewer ⤢. smoke-flux.json:43, smoke-conditioning.json:48 and smoke-refine.json:53 click `#viewer img` (still the result image).
findings.how_checked: After real Generates on the same fake I checked the viewer's DOM (children and buttons), the newest gallery card's buttons and position, and the lightbox's visible buttons. I measured a single 1:1 and a single 2:3 result at 2560x1305, and the first card's position at 2048x1040 DPR 1.25.
findings.verifier_notes: Shot paths are relative to scratchpad/ux/verify-results-2/shots/. The description overstates the cost. Clicking the result opens the lightbox, where all four actions are visible, so refining what was just made takes 2 clicks (image, then ⤢ Refine), or a hover plus a click on the newest card, which is on screen at 100% scaling. The real cost is that extra click and a fullscreen context switch after every Generate, on the flow the user called clunky. It is medium only because it recurs on every result.

sources.surface: Results viewer images
sources.observation: A single 1024x1024 result is drawn at 887x887 in a 2161x917 viewer, leaving about 1274 px of the width empty. A 2:3 result (595x887) leaves about 72% empty. The viewer comes from thumb() (panel.js:285-301) and has no tool row. Star, Reuse, Refine (⤢), reference and Delete exist only on a gallery card's hover row (gallery.js:103-136) or inside the lightbox. To star or refine what was just made, the user has to open the lightbox or find the same image among the gallery cards below.
sources.why_it_matters: Judge, star, refine or reuse is the main loop after every Generate. The Refine dialog, the feature the user called clunky, starts from a card or the lightbox and never from the result the user is looking at. Each action costs an extra open and close, while the screen space beside the result goes unused.

findings.title: Square cover-cropped thumbnails hide up to 43% of a landscape or portrait image
surfaces: Gallery grid cards
findings.recommendation: Set `.card img { object-fit: contain; }` (web/style.css:782). Let the card's own `background: var(--panel-2)` be the letterbox, the same as .sheet-cell (or #000 if preferred). Square images are unchanged. Landscape and portrait images show the whole frame, including edges and text placement, at the cost of a 16:9 thumbnail drawing 171x98 inside its 171px cell. Thumbnails stay the 384px webp source, and cards stay position: relative.
findings.documented_rule: No rule covers the cards' cover crop (it dates from the initial commit). The opposite decision is recorded for the sheet: the style.css:752-756 comment ('cover centre-cropped every cell to its middle 68% on a portrait run') and design-notes 'Panel persistence' (sheet `object-fit: contain`).
findings.smokes_affected: None. smoke.json:40 clicks '.card img', which is unaffected.
findings.how_checked: FLUX fake on 7907 with 1344x768, 768x1344, 896x1152, 1024x1024 and 2016x1152 (refine) records. I logged each size's thumbnail naturalWidth/Height against its box and computed object-fit, then fetched the thumbnail of record 6 to confirm the seed/steps stamp sits top-left. I took elshots of the cabin cards under the shipped `cover` and under an injected in-browser `object-fit: contain` (page style only, repo untouched).
findings.verifier_notes: Reproduces as stated: 1 - 768/1344 = 43% hidden on 16:9 and 7:4-class images, 22% on 896x1152. Letterboxing is the same trade the sheet already made deliberately, so the change follows the codebase's own precedent.

sources.surface: Gallery grid cards
sources.observation: `.card { aspect-ratio: 1 }` plus `.card img { object-fit: cover }` centre-crops every non-square image. The 1344x768 cards show 57% of the width: their seed/steps stamp, top-left in every fake image, is missing from all four cabin cards in g01. 896x1152 cards lose 22% of the height, and 768x1344 loses 43%. The thumbnails are 384px on the long side (measured natural 384x219 for 1344x768), so they hold the whole frame; the crop is only CSS. The contact sheet already switched to `contain` for exactly this reason (style.css comment at .sheet-cell: 'cover centre-cropped every cell to its middle 68% on a portrait run').
sources.why_it_matters: Composition is what one scans a gallery for. Edges, subjects at the thirds and text placement disappear, and landscape and portrait images can't be told from square ones. The user then has to open the lightbox just to see the image.

findings.title: Lightbox side column: 280 px of 12-13 px text over about 930 px of empty space, missing the negative prompt, date and run
surfaces: Lightbox .lb-side (prompt, settings line, actions)
findings.recommendation: At `@media (min-width: 2000px)`: `.lb-side { flex-basis: 360px; width: 360px } .lb-prompt { font-size: 15px }`. In renderLightbox (lightbox.js:99-112), replace the comma-joined line with a 13px `<dl class="lb-facts">` inside #lb-meta, with rows Model / Size / Steps · CFG · True CFG · Mu / Negative (when non-null) / LoRA / Reference / Refined from @ strength / Variables / Seed / Created (toLocaleString of created_at) / Run. Make the Run row a button that does what the card's ⊞ does: closeLightbox(); els.search.value = `run:${rec.run_id}` (or `job:`); setSheet(true). Set `.lightbox { background: #000 }` (or 0.97) so the panel and cards stop showing through behind the 12-13px text. Keep #lb-meta scrolling, the controls pinned and #lb-close autofocus.
findings.documented_rule: design-notes 'The lightbox zooms': the 280px .lb-side column sits beside the stage because fits are height-bound; the meta scrolls (flex 1 1 auto; min-height 0); the controls are pinned to the bottom so they stay put from image to image; #lb-close keeps autofocus; below 900px the column becomes a wrapping row (style.css:949).
findings.rule_tension: Widening to 360px only at ≥2000px keeps the note's reasoning: square and portrait images stay height-bound at 1269px, and only a 16:9 image shrinks (165% -> about 159%, 1263 -> 1218px tall). The facts list stays inside the scrolling .lb-meta, so the pinned controls and autofocus are untouched.
findings.smokes_affected: Three expects read els.lbMeta.textContent: smoke-conditioning.json:50 ('ref '), smoke-flux.json:45 ('CFG 3.5, true CFG 1.5'), smoke-refine.json:55 ('refine of <id> @ 0.1'). Either keep those substrings in the dl's text or update the three expects.
findings.how_checked: FLUX fake on 7907. I opened the lightbox via openLightbox on records 65 (1024x1024 with negative prompt 'blurry, watermark, text, oversaturated, cartoon' and true_cfg 1.5), 6 (1344x768) and 10 (768x1344). I measured .lb-side, the font sizes, the settings bottom against the zoom group top, the overlay colour and the fit size of each record, and searched the side column's text for the negative prompt and a date. I also grepped web/*.js for anywhere negative_prompt is displayed.
findings.verifier_notes: Every measurement reproduces. The missing negative prompt is the strongest part: it belongs to the reproduction set, and the lightbox shows 'true CFG 1.5' without the text it applied to. The recommendation is sound and fits the design note.

sources.surface: Lightbox .lb-side (prompt, settings line, actions)
sources.observation: The column is 280px of 2560. The prompt is 13px and the settings are one 12px comma-joined line ('FLUX.1-Krea-dev, 1024×1024, 28 steps, CFG 3.5, true CFG 1.5, no mu, LoRA demo-style.safetensors @ 0.8, seed 4242, 0.2s'). Between the settings (bottom about y=140) and the Fit row (y=1066) about 930px is empty. A record with negative_prompt 'blurry, watermark, text, oversaturated, cartoon' shows 'true CFG 1.5' but never the negative text (sideText includes 'blurry' = false). created_at, variables (a comparison's version label) and the run are not shown either. The column offers 4 actions (Favourite, Reuse, Refine, Delete), while the card has 6: no 'Show run as sheet', no reference. The overlay is rgba(0,0,0,0.92), so the gallery header ('All models (+8) Sheet ⌦ Delete unstarred') and cards show through behind the column.
sources.why_it_matters: The lightbox is where an image is judged and where one decides to reuse it. The reproduction set is incomplete there (the negative prompt), the seed is buried mid-sentence, and the run an image came from can't be reached. For square and portrait images the stage is bound by height, so the column's width costs the image nothing.

findings.title: No direct path from a finished grid to its sheet; the Sheet button builds a 13,000 px matrix of the whole gallery
surfaces: Finish line (#cell-note), gallery head Sheet button, card ⊞ tool
findings.recommendation: (1) In streamJob's done branch (generation.js:451-460), write the 'Finished …' text first, then append a ghost small button. For a grid done with images and no jobsToShow entry it calls showRun(data.run_id); for a job-only record it calls showJob(jobId). data.run_id is already in Job.snapshot. A grid is not auto-opened, because that would yank the gallery of a user who is browsing while a night ends. (2) The last-run banner from page load stays visible during and after a new job. Its Show run still points at the previous run. Either hide els.lastRun in startJob, or on done fill it from the finished snapshot through a shared helper with announceLastRun and remember(ANNOUNCED_KEY, jobId). (3) In els.sheetBtn.onclick (app.js:217), only when els.search.value.trim() is empty and galleryRecords hold more than one run_id: set the search to run:${galleryRecords[0].run_id} and set a sheetNotice: 'Showing the newest run - clear the search for the whole gallery'. (4) In reconcileAxes (sheet.js:240-249), pin each axis to the value with the most records under the other pins instead of values[key][0]. That first value is null ('none') for every variable axis in a mixed gallery. On a full run the counts tie and the first value still wins, so smoke sheets do not change.
findings.documented_rule: Design notes 'The contact sheet' and 'The morning after: runs and finished jobs'. The sheet's filters are the gallery's. The Runs picker plus the ⊞ button are the way into one run. The last-run banner is shown at load, once per job per browser. generation.js:474-480: a comparison opens its job (showJob fresh) because run ids are shared, and a refine sweep opens its sheet too, but a plain grid only resets the gallery.
findings.rule_tension: A button only adds a path; it does not change what the gallery's filters mean. Opening the newest run fits the rule if it writes run:<id> into the search box, as showRun already does, and says so in sheetNotice. A free-text search therefore stays a free-text sheet. Only an EMPTY search box should redirect. A search like 'fox cfg:2' across several runs is a legitimate sheet and must not be redirected. A comparison keeps showJob. The banner fix still announces each job once if done marks the job announced.
findings.smokes_affected: smoke.json step at line 157 expects els.cellNote.textContent to include 'Finished 6 images' and 'Only 2 distinct'. It still passes if the button is appended after the text node; do not replace the text. smoke-paging.json lines 29 and 32 click els.sheetBtn with search 'run:'+__run, which the empty-search rule leaves alone. smoke.json lines 61-102 call setSheet(true) after setting a run: search, which is not the button handler. No smoke reads the last-run banner.
findings.how_checked: Fresh FLUX.1 Krea [dev] fake on 7913. I seeded 6 runs and 124 images: two direct batches of 4, and grids of 24, 44 and 24 plus one I ran from the panel. In the panel I filled a variable grid, pressed Run grid and waited for done. Then I measured #cell-note and the card tools and pressed Sheet with the search box empty. Next I opened the run from the Runs picker. Last I reloaded and read the last-run banner. Screenshots are m53-01-done.png, m53-02-sheet-unfiltered.png and m53-03-sheet-run.png in verify-grid-2.
findings.verifier_notes: Reproduces worse than reported: 0 of 124 cells filled, not 10 of 238. The cause is reconcileAxes pinning every variable axis to null ('none', sorted first), so no record matches all the pins at once. New detail: the stale last-run banner. Its Show run sits right under the just-finished grid and opens the previous run, which actively misleads. The original recommendation (2) would also have redirected free-text searches; I narrowed it to an empty box.

sources.surface: Finish line (#cell-note), gallery head Sheet button, card ⊞ tool
sources.observation: A finished grid leaves only 'Finished 24 images in 12s.' with no action. A comparison and a refine sweep auto-open their sheet (jobsToShow), but a grid does not. Pressing Sheet with the gallery unfiltered (6 runs, 238 images) gave Columns=Seed (128 values) × Rows=Steps (11): 1397 cells, 10 non-empty, scrollWidth 13,027 px. Five pin selects defaulted to 'none' (subject, style, size, ground) and CFG 0, and the note read '10 of 238 loaded · pinned to subject none, style none, size none, ground none, cfg 0'. The working routes are a native 'Runs…' select or ⊞ ('Show this run as a sheet'), one of six 12 px glyphs on a 171 px card that appear only on hover. The last-run banner's Show run appears only on page load.
sources.why_it_matters: The sheet is the payoff of a grid. A user who presses the visible Sheet button after a run gets a mostly empty wall plus a set of 'none' pins, and may decide the sheet is broken. Finding the right control depends on knowing about Runs or the ⊞ glyph.

findings.title: Sheet headers are 11 px grey, scroll away while reading lower rows, and clip long values
surfaces: Sheet column/row headers and controls
findings.recommendation: (1) `.sheet-grid .head, .sheet-grid .rowhead { font-size: 13px; color: var(--text) }`. Contrast is not the problem: #8b8b9a on #0b0b0e is about 5.9:1. Size is, at 11px over 658-990 px cells. (2) Sticky headers. Set `.sheet-scroll { overflow: auto; max-height: calc(100vh - 58px - 16px) }`; 58px is the sticky .topbar. Add `.sheet-grid .head { position: sticky; top: 0; z-index: 1; background: var(--bg) }`, `.sheet-grid .rowhead { position: sticky; left: 0; z-index: 1; background: var(--bg) }` and the corner cell sticky on both edges at z-index 2. Give .sheet `scroll-margin-top: 66px` and call els.sheet.scrollIntoView() when showSheetScope opens a sheet, so the controls and headers start on screen together. Today the sheet opens at y=568, under an empty 380 px viewer. (3) On screen, render headers from the unclipped string: a raw text helper beside valueText, with promptShort labels unclipped. Clamp with `display:-webkit-box; -webkit-line-clamp:3; -webkit-box-orient:vertical; overflow:hidden` and set title= to the full value. Keep clip() for the canvas and the pin options. (4) `.sheet-grid .rowhead.text { max-width: clamp(170px, 12vw, 320px) }`, about 307px at 2560.
findings.documented_rule: Design notes 'Prompt labels on the sheet' (only the words that vary, position-addressed pins) and 'The sheet exports client-side' (the canvas shares valueText/clip). style.css:748-752 comment: the prose row heading 'is capped rather than eating the sheet' (max-width 170px). .sheet-scroll is overflow-x:auto so a wide sheet never scrolls the page sideways.
findings.rule_tension: The cap stays a cap, just wider and relative to the viewport. promptLabels and position-addressed pins are untouched; only the on-screen 44-character clip goes. LABEL_CHARS stays for the canvas export and the pin <select> options. Sticky headers need a scroll container. .sheet-scroll already is one (overflow-x:auto), so a sticky top inside it never sticks against the page. Making it the vertical scroller keeps the 'page never scrolls horizontally' rule.
findings.smokes_affected: smoke.json lines 83, 88, 97 and 102 (window.__heads) and smoke-analysis.json lines 135 and 316 compare header/rowhead textContent exactly ('size small,size big', 'Seed 20,Seed 21', 'variant original,variant rewrite'). Keep the DOM text '<label> <value>' with no extra text nodes; add only title and CSS. smoke.json lines 66-68 build the canvas and are unaffected while LABEL_CHARS stays for export.
findings.how_checked: Same fake on 7913. I opened run 50a3fb29292c, which has long subject/style variable values, CFG 2/3.5/5 and 2 seeds, with showRun. I measured the header and rowhead boxes, font and colour, then set Columns=subject and Rows=style. I scrolled the second row to the viewport centre and re-measured. I also opened the fox variables run and the 11x4 steps run. Screenshots: m54-01-long-default.png, m54-02-long-subject-cols.png, m54-05-scrolled-row2.png, m54-06-steps-sheet.png.
findings.verifier_notes: The 'grey' part of the original claim does not hold up as a contrast failure (about 5.9:1 passes AA); size and position are the costs. The original sticky recipe used top:0 against a page with a 58px sticky .topbar and gave no way to bring the scroller on screen. I added the scroll-into-view and the topbar offset. A softer alternative to the nested scroller is to cap the cell edge in renderSheet so rows ≤ 3 fit (innerHeight - 58 - controls) / rows, keeping the lightbox for detail. Separate observation for the visual cluster: the empty 380 px 'Generated images appear here.' viewer sits above every sheet opened from the Runs picker.

sources.surface: Sheet column/row headers and controls
sources.observation: Headers and row heads are 11 px #8b8b9a above 527-696 px cells. Scrolled to rows 2-3 of the 4x3 sheet, the first column header is at y=-362 and the controls at -402, so the user sees 'CFG 3.5'/'CFG 5' rows with no column labels (37-sheet-scrolled). With long variable values, headers are cut at 44 characters ('subject weathered old fisherman with a grey beard a…') although each column is 658 px wide, and row heads are capped at max-width 170 px, wrapping to 2 lines and cut ('style oil painting with thick impasto brushstroke…'). The distinguishing words ('knitted wool cap') are the part removed.
sources.why_it_matters: In a matrix the labels carry the meaning. Losing them on scroll, or truncating the words that differ, forces the user back up the page or into the lightbox to learn which setting a cell is.

findings.title: Every keystroke turns all chips to dashed '…', and the half-typed tag flashes red
surfaces: Tag validation tray while typing in the prompt
findings.recommendation: Keep a Map from canonical tag text to its last result, cleared when the checkpoint changes. In scheduleTagValidation (tags.js:503), render cached results at once and mark only new or changed items as unchecked. Requests can stay as they are. For the item under the caret, while the prompt has focus and its text changed since the last keystroke: if the result is unknown, render it neutral (.typing: solid --line border, no mark) until a comma is typed, the caret leaves the item, or 1.5 s pass. A valid result shows as valid at once. Drop the min-height part of the recommendation: the unchecked state never changed the tray height (mark width differs by 0-3px). The reflow the finding measured comes from a new chip being added and wrapping, which min-height cannot prevent.
findings.documented_rule: tags.js:483-505 and design-notes 'Animagine XL 4.0': every prompt change from outside the editor goes through scheduleTagValidation and closes an open editor. An unavailable lookup is unchecked, never invalid. The epoch guards against stale responses.
findings.rule_tension: A result cache is compatible with all of these. It must be keyed per checkpoint, because the vocabulary cutoff and the special tags differ: clear it in syncTagVocabulary or on a status model change, or Animagine's verdicts would show under Kohaku's 2024-07-10 cutoff. The epoch guard and the editor-closing reset stay. A neutral caret-item state must not hide a completed tag. Accepting a suggestion leaves the caret inside the item, and smoke-animagine 10 expects that chip to be .valid.
findings.smokes_affected: smoke-animagine 12-14: 'made up tag' is appended while the prompt still has focus with the caret inside it, then expected to be .unknown. With the caret-item rule it would be .typing, so the step needs a blur or a trailing comma. smoke-animagine 10, smoke-illustrious 13 and smoke-kohaku 12 expect every chip .valid with the caret in the accepted item; they hold if valid results show at once. smoke-animagine 54 expects 4 chips right after input, which still holds.
findings.how_checked: 13-tag all-valid prompt on the Animagine fake. Typed ', sm', 'ile' one character at a time with real insertText, sampling chip classes, tray height and the next sibling's top after every key and after 200 and 600 ms pauses. Measured each chip's width in the ✓ state against the … state.
findings.verifier_notes: The flicker and the red half-typed word reproduce exactly. The layout-shift part does not reproduce as a cost of the unchecked state, so I dropped it. On the fake the round trip is instant. On real Danbooru an uncached lookup keeps the whole tray grey for the network time. Medium fits: it happens on every typing session on four tag checkpoints and is a main source of the 'clunky' feel, though it never changes the output.

sources.surface: Tag validation tray while typing in the prompt
sources.observation: On an 18-tag prompt with all chips valid, typing ', sm' immediately re-rendered all 19 chips as 'unchecked' (dashed border, '…' instead of ✓). They went back to green about 450 ms later. Typing '1girl, fire' showed '? fire' as a red unknown chip, as did '? lo' and '? sm', before the word was finished. The re-render also reflows the tray: it grew from 69px to 80px and the viewer below jumped from y=163 to y=174.
sources.why_it_matters: The tray sits in the user's peripheral vision while they type, and it flickers grey-green across its whole width on every pause. The one chip that is red is the word they are still writing, so red stops meaning 'fix this'. Layout shifts in the viewer below add to the noise.

findings.title: The viewer forgets every earlier result, so iterating on a prompt means hunting in the gallery
surfaces: Results viewer
findings.recommendation: (1) S, highest value. In thumb()'s open for the viewer (panel.js:268, or in openLightbox at lightbox.js:7), when the list is viewerRecords with length 1 and !sheetMode, look up the same id in galleryRecords. If it is there, open the lightbox on galleryRecords at the gallery's copy of that record, so the counter and ArrowRight walk back through earlier results. Otherwise fall back to [rec]. (2) M. At @media (min-width: 2000px), when the viewer is in the single-image tier (not .multi or .many), show a sibling <aside id="recent"> beside #viewer (wrap both in a grid with columns minmax(0,1fr) clamp(280px,16vw,420px)). It holds this page session's previous up to 6 results from a separate sessionRecords list (not viewerRecords, not galleryRecords) at about 190px tall each.
