A click opens the lightbox on [current, ...sessionRecords]. This uses the ~1260px that sits empty beside a square result, and it keeps earlier results on screen when the Prompt check panel or the 2048x1040 viewport pushes the gallery row below the fold. (3) Optional, low priority: once any image has landed, give .viewer at >=2000px min-height: calc(68vh + 30px) so a many-to-single tier change does not move the gallery. The first-image jump (380 to 917) stays because the empty state is deliberately short.
findings.documented_rule: There is no CLAUDE.md rule that the viewer shows only the latest job. The relevant constraints are panel.js:250-276 (clearResults/appendResult: the strip is replaced once the job's first image lands and is capped at VIEWER_MAX 48) and design-notes 'The running batch on wide screens' (the 8-column 'many' tier at >=2000px). Many smokes assert viewerRecords.length === N and click document.querySelector('#viewer img').
findings.rule_tension: A history kept inside #viewer or in viewerRecords would break the smoke asserts (viewerRecords.length === 1 in the anima, kohaku, netayume, newbie, wai, conditioning, flux and refine smokes) and the '#viewer img' clicks. The history therefore has to be a separate list and a sibling element outside #viewer, like #viewer-note is. It should show only in the single-image tier so the 8-column 'many' tier keeps its full width. The lightbox fix leaves viewerRecords alone for multi-image jobs, so 'the lightbox walks every record of the run through viewerRecords' still holds.
findings.smokes_affected: None should break. Re-run smoke-conditioning.json:48-50 and smoke-flux.json:43-45: they click '#viewer img' after a single-image job and read els.lbMeta. With fix (1) they open the gallery's copy of the same record, so the metadata matches, but the list changes. smoke-refine.json:53/58 opens a 2-image viewer, which fix (1) does not touch. Any new #recent element must stay outside #viewer so the '#viewer img' selectors in smoke-conditioning, smoke-flux, smoke-refine and smoke-preview keep hitting the newest result.
findings.how_checked: Fresh FLUX.1 Krea [dev] fake on 7919. Typed six prompt edits and ran each with a real Ctrl+Enter, measuring #viewer, #viewer img, .gallery-head and .card after each one. Opened the viewer image and then a gallery card, and arrowed through the lightbox. Repeated at 2048x1040 DPR 1.25, and again with the Prompt check panel open (els.analyze.click()).
findings.verifier_notes: The core claim is real but overstated for the primary viewport. At 2560x1305 with Check closed, the gallery's first row already works as a 12-wide, newest-first history directly under the viewer, and a card's lightbox walks it (1 click plus arrows). The real costs are: (a) clicking the big result, the most natural click, gives a dead-end 1-image lightbox; (b) about 1260px of the viewer is empty beside a square result at QHD; (c) the history row is fully off-screen whenever the Prompt check panel is open (it is part of the iteration loop) and at 2048x1040. The original proposal of a history column inside .viewer and min-height 68vh needed the corrections above to stay compatible with the smokes and the 8-column tier. Medium stands: this is recurring friction in the core loop and a clear waste of the QHD screen.

sources.surface: Results viewer
sources.observation: Task 2: five prompt edits, each a 1-image Ctrl+Enter. After each job the viewer held only the newest image (viewerRecords=1 every time). The viewer was a 2176x917 box with one 887x887 image in the middle and about 1290 px of empty width beside it. Opening that image gave a 1-image lightbox: no counter, both arrows disabled (refined result, t3-05). To compare the five, I had to scroll to the 172 px gallery cards (first row at y=1105, half below the fold), open a card and arrow through it (1 click + 4 keys), or search + Sheet (mislabelled; see walkthrough-6). When a new image landed, the viewer jumped from 380 to 917 px and the gallery head moved from y=509 to y=1046.
sources.why_it_matters: Iterating on a prompt is the core loop, and the large screen shows one picture at a time. The user cannot see whether edit 4 was better than edit 2 without leaving the viewer.

findings.title: The card's ❐ gives no feedback where it was clicked: adding is silent, re-adding is a silent no-op, and the limit refusal is below the fold at 125%
surfaces: Gallery card ❐ tool → panel #reference-list / #error
findings.recommendation: As proposed. Add syncReferenceMarks(), called from renderReferences, which sets class 'ref' and data-ref-n on .card[data-id] and .sheet-cell[data-id]. Style .card.ref with an `outline: 2px solid var(--accent)`, because .card.fav already uses border and box-shadow, plus a ::before number badge (.card has no ::before today; .sheet-cell.fav uses ::after). Make ❐ a toggle with aria-pressed and the label 'Reference image N - click to remove'. Keep its textContent '❐', which smoke-conditioning.json:33 finds it by. At four references, set aria-disabled on the ❐ of non-reference cards. Show a ~2 s role=status bubble positioned over the card's tool row: 'Added as image N', 'Removed', or 'Four is the most here; remove one first'.
findings.documented_rule: gallery.js:117 deliberately re-runs setReferences on a re-add, which is a no-op. The limit message goes to the panel's #error slot (showError). CLAUDE.md uses aria-disabled rather than disabled for buttons that must keep focus and say why (Refine, Ask the critic). setReferences is the one writer.
findings.rule_tension: None of the rules is in the way. Use aria-disabled at the cap so the button stays focusable and can explain the cap, as the Refine and critic buttons do. A toggle that removes a reference must still go through setReferences(). Moving all notices out of #error is cluster M25's fix and is not repeated here; the in-card confirmation proposed here works whichever way M25 is resolved.
findings.smokes_affected: smoke-conditioning.json:33 clicks the ❐ found by textContent === '❐'; keep the glyph. No smoke clicks ❐ twice, so the toggle breaks nothing. Add a step for .card.ref and data-ref-n.
findings.how_checked: Real hover and click on cards' ❐ at 2560x1305 DPR 1 and at 2048x1040 DPR 1.25. Logged card classes and aria-pressed, referenceIds, the #error text and rect, and the viewport height. Re-clicked ❐ on a card that was already a reference. Opened Check and measured the first gallery row's ❐.
findings.verifier_notes: Every claim reproduced. This does not duplicate G3.2: that cluster numbers the chips, and this one shows the same number on the source card and confirms the click where it happened. The below-the-fold #error at 125% overlaps M25 and should be fixed there.

sources.surface: Gallery card ❐ tool → panel #reference-list / #error
sources.observation: ❐ is a 25x24 px glyph shown only on card hover. After a click, focus stays on ❐ and the card is unchanged (k03-card-after-add1.png): no pressed state, no 'in use' marker, no toast. The only change is a 52 px chip in the panel. At 2560x1305 the chip list's left edge (x 35) is 404 px from card 1's ❐ (x 439) and 1,679 px from card 8's (x 1714). Clicking ❐ on an image that is already a reference runs setReferences(referenceIds), which changes nothing visible. The 5th add writes 'Four reference images is the limit; each one lengthens the sequence.' to panel #error at y 1053. At 100% that is 1,134 px left of the clicked card (x 1169). At 2048x1040 @1.25 the same message lands at y 1053, beyond the 1040 px viewport, so the click shows nothing at all (k51-125-fifth.png). With the prompt check open at QHD, the first gallery row's ❐ sits at y 1300 of 1305.
sources.why_it_matters: Every reference is added from a gallery the user is scanning, often far from the panel. With no confirmation at the point of action, users click again, unsure whether it took. They can't tell which cards are already references, and at 125% they hit the limit with no response. This is the friction four earlier reviewers listed as untested.

findings.title: On klein the Reference images help says 'This checkpoint's pipeline takes none', and the count note warns of a cost the app measured as absent
surfaces: Reference images ? tip and #reference-note
findings.recommendation: In syncConditioning (sizes.js:186), set els.referenceTip.textContent from the capability. Supported: 'Up to four gallery images the picture is conditioned on, in this order. With two or more, say in the prompt what to take from each by its number - "the jacket from image 1". Each is resized to about 1 MP on the way in.' (The last two sentences paraphrase KLEIN_GUIDE's prompt and size prose.) Unsupported: keep today's sentence. Change the note in renderReferences (sizes.js:202-205): n = 0 gives '(add one with ❐ on a gallery image)', n = 1 gives '(1 of 4)', n ≥ 2 gives `(${n} of 4 - name them image 1…${n} in the prompt)`. Drop 'each lengthening the sequence', which the card measurements contradict. Change gallery.js:119 to 'Four reference images is the most this panel sends; remove one first.'
findings.documented_rule: index.html:226-228 and sizes.js:183-185: the conditioning controls are greyed rather than hidden, and 'the reason is in the badge beside it'. design-notes 'Reference images, by gallery id': 'The 2-3x cost the review predicted did not appear' (10.2 s with no reference; 9.2/8.2 s with one; 11.3 s with two). design-notes:2992 and prompt_rules.py:1606: one reference needs no 'image 1'.
findings.rule_tension: The rule wants the badge to carry the reason for a greyed field, so the unsupported wording stays and only the supported state gets new text. The proposed note '(n of 4 - image 1-n in the prompt)' would push 'image 1' on a single reference, which the app deliberately does not ask for (BFL's own one-reference example names none). Ask for numbers only at two or more.
findings.smokes_affected: smoke-conditioning.json:37 expects referenceNote to include 'lengthening the sequence'; update it to the new wording (e.g. includes('1 of 4')). smoke-flux.json:27 expects 'takes none' on an unsupported checkpoint, which stays.
findings.how_checked: On the klein fake (referenceSupported true) I logged #reference-tip's text and hovered the ? badge with a real mouse move to screenshot the tip. Logged the note after adds. Grepped web/ for writes to referenceTip and read the measured cost in design-notes 'Reference images, by gallery id'.
findings.verifier_notes: The core claim is right: the tip tells the one supported checkpoint that it takes none. I adjusted the recommendation so the note does not demand 'image 1' for a single reference, which would contradict the app's deliberate exemption, and so the copy does not hard-code 'klein'.

sources.surface: Reference images ? tip and #reference-note
sources.observation: With referenceSupported === true on the klein fake, #reference-tip reads: 'Reference images condition the picture on one you have already made. This checkpoint's pipeline takes none - FLUX.2 [klein] is the one here that does.' The text is static markup (index.html:232-234), and status.js and syncConditioning never rewrite it; els.referenceTip is defined but never assigned. The tip also says nothing about the 4-image cap, the 'image 1' naming the guide asks for, or the ~1 MP resize. Once references are attached, the note reads '(2, each lengthening the sequence)', which is transformer jargon. design-notes 'Reference images, by gallery id' records 'The 2-3x cost the review predicted did not appear', measured at 10.2 s with none and 8.2-11.3 s with one or two.
sources.why_it_matters: The one checkpoint that takes references tells the user it doesn't, in the help they open to learn how references work. The note spends the field's only line of guidance on a cost the user can't act on and that wasn't measured, instead of the one thing that changes the output: naming each image by its number.

findings.title: Ctrl+Enter inside the grid fold runs Generate, rendering the literal {placeholders} as one image instead of the grid
surfaces: Global keydown handler; Prompt variables / axis boxes
Keyboard submit: Generate, Run grid
findings.recommendation: In app.js:259-262: `if (els.refineDialog.open) void runRefine(); else if (els.gridSection.open && e.target.closest?.('#grid-section')) els.gridRun.click(); else generate();`. gridRun's handler runs startJob('/api/grid', gridPayload()) with the same critic and expansion guards. Make the shortcut visible: title='Generate (Ctrl+Enter)' on #btn-generate (index.html:262) and title='Run grid (Ctrl+Enter from a grid box)' on #btn-grid (index.html:410). Update README.md:228. Optionally, in generate() (generation.js:217): if els.gridSection.open, els.gridPrompt.value.trim() is non-empty and the prompt matches /\{[A-Za-z_]\w*\}/, call showError('Run grid fills the {placeholders}; Generate would render the braces.') and return. Keep this client-only and scoped to the open grid. Do not add the GenerateRequest refusal.
findings.documented_rule: CLAUDE.md Frontend: 'Ctrl+Enter in the dialog runs the pass, not Generate'. README.md:228: 'Ctrl/Cmd + Enter generates from anywhere in the page.' The comment at app.js:256-258 says the same.
findings.rule_tension: Generating from anywhere is documented, so the fix changes a documented shortcut: README.md:228 needs a sentence. The Refine dialog already makes Ctrl+Enter context-dependent, so the fix follows that precedent. The proposed server-side refusal in GenerateRequest is not compatible. Plain Generate deliberately takes the prompt as typed, and a {word} can be literal text or NovelAI-style {tag} emphasis pasted into a tag prompt. The grid already refuses a placeholder with no values (grid.prompt_assignments), and that refusal also covers the CLI grid.
findings.smokes_affected: smoke-refine.json 100-103 (Ctrl+Enter inside the dialog) must still pass; that branch is unchanged. No smoke presses Ctrl+Enter in the grid fold or reads the Generate/Run grid titles. README.md:228 needs its wording updated.
findings.how_checked: Fake on 7912. Prompt 'a {size} fox sitting on {ground}, golden hour', grid fold open, variables 'size = big | small' and 'ground = grass | dirt', CFG axis 2,4; the preview read 8 images. Focused #grid-cfg, pressed a real Ctrl+Enter over CDP, and recorded every fetch POST. Repeated from #grid-steps ('20-32x4'). Read the titles of Generate and Run grid, searched the DOM for 'Ctrl+Enter', and read app.js:255-263 and README.md:228.
findings.verifier_notes: grid-2 and panel-4 report the same bug, so the merge is correct. Reproduced exactly. Severity lowered from grid-2's high to medium. The wrong output shows at once: one image, step progress rather than run x/y, and literal braces in the alt and prompt. It costs one image and a junk entry in Runs, unless the user walks away straight after pressing. It still risks a lost overnight run when the user walks away right after pressing, so it should be fixed with the other S items. Also observed: with the fold closed, Ctrl+Enter on a braced prompt still renders the braces. That is plain Generate working as documented, not this bug.
findings.merge_note: panel-4 reproduces the bug with a grid Steps axis. It adds that the shortcut is shown nowhere: Generate has an empty title.

sources.surface: Global keydown handler; Prompt variables / axis boxes
sources.observation: The prompt was 'a {size} fox sitting on {ground}, golden hour' with variables size/ground and CFG 2,4. With focus in the CFG axis box, Ctrl+Enter gave 'Finished 1 image in 1s.' Gallery count went 24 to 25, and the new image's alt is the raw template with braces. The Runs picker gained a run '1 img · a {size} fox sitting on {ground}, golden ho…'. The grid would have refused an unfilled placeholder, but /api/generate accepted it.
sources.why_it_matters: Ctrl+Enter is the page's 'submit' shortcut, and the Refine dialog already redirects it to its own action. A user who has just filled in grid axes and presses it gets one wrong image (literal braces, panel settings rather than the axes) and a junk entry in Runs, not the sweep they set up.

sources.surface: Keyboard submit: Generate, Run grid
sources.observation: With the grid fold open, I focused grid Steps, typed '20-32x4' and pressed Ctrl+Enter. The only POST was /api/generate, and the cell note read 'Finished 1 image in 0s.' The grid didn't run. The handler always calls generate() unless the Refine dialog is open (app.js:259-262). Generate has an empty title attribute, and nothing in the panel mentions Ctrl+Enter. Refine's button says 'Run the pass (Ctrl+Enter)' (refine.js:239). The shortcut is in the README only.
sources.why_it_matters: The Refine dialog already set the precedent that Ctrl+Enter means 'run what these boxes are for'. A user editing grid axes gets a stray single image plus a queue slot, and may think the grid started. A first-time user never learns the shortcut, which matters here because Generate is 36 Tabs from the prompt (panel-10).

findings.title: Use rewrite, Use reordered and Apply replace the prompt and drop the original from Compare and the critic's answer
surfaces: Order > Use reordered, finding Apply, Critic > Use rewrite, Compare
Prompt check: Critic > Rewrite > Use rewrite, then Compare on the same seeds
findings.recommendation: In the critic's Use rewrite and Use reordered handlers, before usePromptText(text): if els.compareOwn.value.trim() is empty, set els.compareOwn.value = analysisResult.source, set compareChoice.yours = true, and put a one-line note under Compare: 'Your version holds the prompt before Use rewrite - Run comparison tests both on the same seeds.' After the automatic re-check, Compare then offers Original (the rewrite) and Your version (the prior prompt) instead of a dead Run comparison. Add 'Compare first? Use replaces the prompt; Ctrl+Z brings it back.' to both titles. Extending the same step to Check's Use reordered and the finding Apply is reasonable, but it changes four Animagine smoke expectations (below). The duplicate is low priority: on the order finding, whose suggestion equals body.reordered, replace its Apply with the text 'Same as Use reordered above' so the panel offers one button for one action.
findings.documented_rule: CLAUDE.md Frontend: 'Use and Apply write through replaceBoxText (so Ctrl+Z restores) and check again'. The comparison 'never writes els.prompt or els.gridPrompt, drops a version identical to another'; 'its Your version box (yours) is the one way to test order on prose'. design-notes 'The prompt analyser' (The page): 'The critic's answer is always about the checked text ... a check of other text drops the answer', and Your version is 'kept across checks ..., cleared with the rest of the panel, never persisted'. Its history line about Ctrl+Z reads: 'the re-check that follows would have made the replacement the comparison's original, leaving the typed prompt nowhere on the page'.
findings.rule_tension: Writing the replaced text into Your version only when that box is empty touches only the comparison's own box. It keeps replaceBoxText and its undo, keeps the critic answer dropped (no stale answer survives), and adds no new variant label. The comparison then reads Original (new text) against Your version (the old text), which is what the user wants to see on the same seeds. A separate 'previous' label (analysis-5) is not needed: 'yours' is already the user's own text with defined lifetime rules, and a fifth row adds a code path and a sheet row label.
findings.smokes_affected: Scoped to the critic's Use buttons, nothing fails. smoke-analysis.json step 85 (Use rewrite) is followed by a reload at step 94 that clears Your version, so steps 85-92 only gain a new expectation that compareOwn holds window.__beforeRewrite. Extended to Check's Use reordered/Apply, smoke-animagine.json step 98 (Use reordered) leaves Your version = 'masterpiece, green hair, 1girl', which is kept across checks. Steps 107, 111 and 137 (expect 'Original,Rewrite') and step 129 ('Original,Reordered,Rewrite') would then gain 'Your version' unless the smoke clears the box. smoke-analysis.json step 40 (quote Apply) has no compare-list expectation before the reload. Hiding the order finding's Apply leaves smoke-animagine step 99 (finding text and Guide label) intact.
findings.how_checked: FLUX fake: Check, really clicked Ask the critic and then the critic's 'Use rewrite' (430,606, 66x19), then read compare options, #compare-run state and title, #critic-result, critiqueResult, els.compareOwn and document.body.innerText. Animagine fake, 18 out-of-order tags: compared each finding's suggestion with body.reordered, really clicked the order finding's Apply, then undid with execCommand('undo').
findings.verifier_notes: One claim did not reproduce: analysis-5's 223 px page scroll after Use or Apply. scrollY stayed 0 in both of my runs; that reviewer had probably scrolled first. Severity drops from walkthrough-2's high to medium: nothing is lost for good (Ctrl+Z restores the text, as documented and as I checked with execCommand('undo')). The cost is a dead end plus a critic rerun (about 15 s on the GPU). The undo is still undiscoverable, and the flow the user was most likely to try ends in a disabled Run comparison.
findings.merge_note: analysis-5 adds that on Animagine the order finding's Apply duplicates Use reordered byte for byte, so the panel has two buttons for the same action.

sources.surface: Prompt check: Critic > Rewrite > Use rewrite, then Compare on the same seeds
sources.observation: Task 6 done in the order the user wrote it (check, ask the critic, use its rewrite, run a comparison). Before Use, Compare offered Original, Reordered and Rewrite ('12 images · 3 variants × 4 seeds'). After one click on Use rewrite, the prompt became the rewrite and was checked again. The critic's answer was gone (critic-result children=0), Compare offered only 'Original' (now the rewrite), and Run comparison was disabled with the title 'Needs a second version of the prompt to compare against'. The text that had been replaced appeared nowhere on the page. Ctrl+Z in the prompt did bring it back, but the check then went stale, so the comparison needed Check again plus Ask the critic again (about 15 s on the GPU).
sources.why_it_matters: Trying the rewrite and then comparing it with what you had is the obvious order. The page punishes it with a dead end and a second critic run, and the only way back is an undo nobody is told about.

sources.surface: Order > Use reordered, finding Apply, Critic > Use rewrite, Compare
sources.observation: On Animagine, the order finding's Apply suggestion is byte-identical to body.reordered (run log: guide.order -> true). So 'Use reordered' in Order (79x19 px at y=405) and 'Apply' under the first finding are two buttons doing the same thing. Pressing either replaces the prompt and re-checks. Compare then offers only 'Original', which is now the reordered text, and Run comparison is disabled. The critic's answer (its rewrite and its set-aside notes) disappears: critiqueResult becomes null and #critic-result has 0 children. The page also scrolled 223 px, which put the panel head off-screen. After that, the typed prompt exists only in the undo history (Ctrl+Z). Compare sits 300-700 px below the Use buttons.
sources.why_it_matters: The natural order is to see a better version and press Use. That removes the very comparison the section exists for: the old prompt against the new one on the same seeds. It also throws away a critique that takes about 15 s of GPU time. Nothing on screen warns about either.

findings.title: Queued jobs have no identity: the page never names the running or queued job that Cancel acts on
surfaces: Panel progress block and queue note (#progress, #queue-note)
findings.recommendation: Backend (one line): add `"prompt": self.request.prompt[:120]` to Job.snapshot (backend/jobs.py:123). Job.request is the first cell's settings; the finding's `self.cells[0].request.prompt` is not the field. Optionally also add `"images": len(self.cells) * self.request.num_images` and the request's width/height. That way /api/jobs and every status frame can name the job, including after a reload: resumeActiveJob silently reattached to a job a previous page had queued, with nothing naming it. Frontend: (1) Under Generate, above the bars, show 'Now: <first 60 chars> · 1024×1024 · 2 images' at 13px, filled from the stream's status frame. Set Cancel's title to 'Stop "<snippet>" after the current step'. (2) Render #queue-note as one row per queued id: the snippet from /api/jobs, fetched once after each queued POST and in watchNext/resumeActiveJob, plus an × button (aria-label 'Cancel queued job: <snippet>', aria-disabled while its POST runs) that POSTs /api/jobs/{id}/cancel and drops the id from queuedIds. Keep 'Cancel queued' when 2 or more are waiting. Severity is medium, not high: Cancel keeps the images already finished, its title says what it stops, and with one queued job 'Cancel queued' is exactly right. The real costs are not knowing what is running or waiting and having no way to drop one of several queued jobs.
findings.documented_rule: docs/design-notes.md 'The browser's queue' (line 1048): Cancel acts on the watched job and 'Cancel queued' on the rest; resumeActiveJob attaches to the running job, else the oldest queued. CLAUDE.md Frontend: buttons are held with aria-disabled only during the POST.
findings.rule_tension: No conflict. Both buttons keep their documented targets. The fix only adds names, plus a per-row cancel that calls the same /api/jobs/{id}/cancel that cancelQueued already uses.
findings.smokes_affected: None. grep of tools/smoke*.json finds no #queue-note, queue text, 'Cancel queued' or Cancel step. No test asserts the exact snapshot key set; re-run tests/test_api*.py for the jobs routes after adding the field.
findings.how_checked: Fake FLUX.1 Krea [dev] server on 7904 (--step 0.3), 2560x1305 DPR 1. Queued three jobs (A fox, B whale, C parrot; 10 steps, Runs 2) through the Generate button. While B ran I logged the panel state, /api/jobs and document.body.innerText, and took a panel elshot. In a second run I really clicked Cancel at (304,993) while the box showed C, then read /api/jobs?include_finished=true to see which job ended.
findings.verifier_notes: Code: web/generation.js:67-71 (syncQueueNote, count only), 124-165 (startJob pushes bare ids), 192-199 (cancelQueued, all or nothing), backend/jobs.py:123-160 (snapshot has no prompt). The live preview in the viewer does show the running job's picture on FLUX/Krea 2, so it is identifiable by sight, but not on klein, and never for the queued jobs. The Steps box in my first panel shot reads 28 while the job ran at 10: that is my eval setup (value set without an input event), not an app bug.

sources.surface: Panel progress block and queue note (#progress, #queue-note)
sources.observation: I queued three jobs with different prompts (A fox, B whale, C parrot; 2 runs each). While job B ran, the prompt box still held 'job C: a green parrot in a jungle'. The only status was 'run 1/2' plus '9/10' and the line '1 more job queued behind this one.' Nothing on the page names the running job or the queued one. /api/jobs snapshots carry no prompt either (jobs.py snapshot fields). 'Cancel queued' cancels every waiting job with no per-job choice. The single Cancel (53x26 px, 12 px text) stops the watched job, which by then is B, not the C the box shows.
sources.why_it_matters: Queueing is a deliberate feature: Generate turns into 'Generate (queue)'. After a few submissions the user cannot tell what is rendering or what is waiting. A user who wants to drop the job they just queued (C) and presses Cancel stops the job in progress (B) and loses its remaining cells. The panel looks like it describes the running job, but it does not.

findings.title: At QHD the lightbox never shows a 1 MP image at 1:1; the 1:1 button, the 1 key and double-click do nothing
surfaces: Lightbox zoom (Fit / 1:1 / zoom label, stage double-click)
findings.recommendation:
(1) zoomLightbox (lightbox.js:64): `const floor = Math.min(1, oneToOneScale(rec)); const next = Math.min(ceiling, Math.max(floor, lbView.scale * factor));` and keep `if (next <= 1) lbView.x = lbView.y = 0;`.
(2) Label in layoutLightbox (lightbox.js:55): `Math.abs(scale - one) < 1e-3 ? '1:1' : scale === 1 ? `fit · ${p}%` : `${p}%``. Testing '1:1' first is not enough: a wheel stop between 1:1 and fit would otherwise read 'fit · 112%'.
(3) ondblclick (lightbox.js:213): `if (lbView.scale !== 1) { zoomFit(); return; }`, so a second double-click goes back to fit from a below-fit 1:1.
Keep the `.zoomed` class at > 1 and the stage-click close at <= 1; nothing is pannable below fit. No persisted 'Fit ≤1:1' toggle is needed.
findings.documented_rule: design-notes 'The lightbox zooms': 'a scale relative to fit (never below 1)' and '1:1 is below fit, which the zoom never goes to'. Comments at lightbox.js:13 and lightbox.js:61-63. The same section requires the DPR-exact 1:1 so a sharpening sweep is judged without resampling.
findings.rule_tension: The floor at fit defeats the stated purpose of 1:1 on QHD, where every preset up to about 2 MP fits above 100%. The fix changes the documented floor only. Fit as the open state, the stage-click close only at <= 1, the explicit width/height layout and the DPR divide all stay. The design-notes sentence and the lightbox.js comments need updating.
findings.smokes_affected: None break. smoke.json:40-56 runs 1152x896 cells at 1400x900, where 1:1 is above fit, so its '1:1' and 'fit' expectations still hold. Add a smoke.json step with an image below fit at 1400x900 (e.g. 768x768): key 1 gives '1:1', double-click gives 'fit'.
findings.how_checked: FLUX fake on 7906. Opened the lightbox on 1024², 1360x768 and 896x1152 images at 2560x1305, DPR 1, and on a 1024² image at 2048x1040, DPR 1.25. I used the real 1 key, a real click on the 1:1 button and a real double-click on the image centre (1131,653), and read #lb-zoom and lbView.scale after each.
findings.verifier_notes: Lowered from high to medium. The zoom label honestly reports the magnification, and no output is wrong. The cost is three controls that silently do nothing on every default-size image at the target screen, and judging sharpness through a 1.1-1.65x upscale. A pass at 1.5-2x is larger than the stage, so 1:1 already works on passes; on their 1 MP sources it does not.

sources.surface: Lightbox zoom (Fit / 1:1 / zoom label, stage double-click)
sources.observation: The stage is 2211x1269 at 2560x1305. A 1024x1024 image fits at "fit · 124%", 1344x768 at "fit · 165%" and 896x1152 at "fit · 110%". I zoomed to 411% and pressed 1: the zoom became 'fit · 124%' at scale 1, not 1:1. Clicking the 1:1 button on the 896x1152 image left 'fit · 110%', scale 1. At 2048x1040 DPR 1.25 the stage is 1699x1004, and a 1024² image is 'fit · 123%' with the 1 key again doing nothing. The stage title still promises 'double-click for 1:1'. zoomLightbox clamps at Math.max(1, ...), so 1:1 is out of reach whenever an image is smaller than the stage, which at QHD means every default-size image.
sources.why_it_matters: The DPR-exact 1:1 exists so a sharpening, steps or refine sweep is judged without resampling (design notes). On the target screen every default-size image is judged through a 1.1x-1.65x upscale. The control that promises otherwise silently does nothing.

findings.title: Pause gives no acknowledgement until the cell ends: the next progress event overwrites 'pausing after this cell…' and the button keeps saying Pause
surfaces: Pause/Resume button and progress text
Progress row: Pause button and progress text
findings.recommendation: (1) On click, set the label to 'Pausing…' with aria-pressed=true. togglePause decides by `textContent === 'Pause'` (web/generation.js:205-215), so treat 'Pausing…' as the withdraw branch: POST value=false and set the label back to 'Pause'. Also derive 'Pausing…' from `pause_requested`, which is already in every status snapshot, so a reattached page shows it. (2) While a pause is requested, the progress handler (generation.js:403-411) writes 'run 2/6 · pausing after this run' instead of overwriting it. (3) On the paused ack, keep .pt at 'run 1/3' so the bar keeps its width, and write 'Paused after run 1/3 · GPU handed back' into #cell-note (or let .pt wrap). Today the nowrap .pt (style.css:626, 152px of text) squeezes the bar to 5px. (4) Exclude #btn-pause from the danger hover: `.ghost.small:not(#btn-pause):hover…` at style.css:613. (5) When the watched job is running and total_runs === 1, make Pause aria-disabled with the title 'A single image has no pause point — Cancel stops it'. A Batch of N is one cell too. In plain jobs, say 'image' or 'run' rather than 'cell'.
findings.documented_rule: docs/design-notes.md 'Pause' (line 1033): the label flips to Resume on the worker's `paused` acknowledgement, never on the click, and the pause lands between cells. CLAUDE.md Jobs: pause is cooperative and polled at the cell boundary. CLAUDE.md Frontend: Pause and Cancel use aria-disabled, never disabled.
findings.rule_tension: Compatible. An interim 'Pausing…' does not claim the job is paused, so Resume still waits for the ack. Making Pause aria-disabled on a running one-cell job keeps it focusable. Leave a queued one-cell job alone: the server does hold it before its only cell, since _generate checks pause_requested at cell index 0.
findings.smokes_affected: None. No tools/smoke*.json step mentions pause, Pause, Resume or #btn-pause. smoke.json:157 checks that #cell-note reads 'Finished 6 images': keep the done summary overwriting #cell-note.
findings.how_checked: Fake FLUX server (--step 0.3), 2560x1305. For a 3-run, 10-step job I really clicked Pause at (244,993) and sampled the progress text, the Pause label, the cell note and the bar width every 20 ms for 6 s. I hovered Pause and read its computed colour, then measured the paused state. For a single-image 28-step job I clicked Pause at step 7 and sampled until it finished, then read /api/jobs.
findings.verifier_notes: Code: web/generation.js:205-215, 403-411, 434-440; web/style.css:613, 626; backend/jobs.py:487-492 (pause checked at the top of each cell, index 0 included). On the fake the ack came in under a second. On the card, one FLUX cell takes tens of seconds, which is how long the click currently looks ignored.
findings.merge_note: copy-a11y-9 adds that on a one-cell Generate, Pause never takes effect, and proposes making it aria-disabled there with a reason.

sources.surface: Pause/Resume button and progress text
sources.observation: 60 ms after Pause, togglePause had written 'pausing after this cell…', but the next progress event had already overwritten it with 'run 1/3' (generation.js:407-409). The button kept reading 'Pause' for the 4.5 s until the worker acknowledged. On the card, one FLUX cell takes tens of seconds, so the click looks ignored for that long. Once paused, the text 'paused — GPU handed back' is white-space:nowrap with min-width 4.5em (style.css:626) and squeezes the job bar from 113 px to 5 px, and the ETA line empties. Pause and Resume also turn danger-red on hover (style.css:613, the rule meant for Cancel). Pause is offered on a single-image job, where it has nothing to hold.
sources.why_it_matters: With no feedback, the likely next action is a second click or a Cancel, which ends the run instead of holding it. In the paused state the bar no longer shows how far the run got, and the red hover suggests Pause is destructive.

sources.surface: Progress row: Pause button and progress text
sources.observation: In a single-image 28-step job, Pause was pressed at step 6/28. After 150 ms the progress text already read '7/28' and the button still said 'Pause'. The job then ran to 'Finished 1 image in 9s.' and never paused (d.out poll). The click's acknowledgement is written into #progress-text ('pausing after this cell…'), which the next progress event overwrites within one step. The title says 'Hold after the current cell and hand the GPU back': a one-image job has no next cell, so the hold never happens.
sources.why_it_matters: Pause is the visible way to hand the GPU back. When it silently does nothing on the most common job, it looks broken, and the user has to Cancel and lose the image instead.

findings.title: Gallery and card notices appear in the panel's #error slot, about 2,400 px from the control that caused them
surfaces: #error slot under Generate; gallery cards and gallery head
Gallery header actions (Delete unstarred, search terms) and card tools (❐, ⊞)
findings.recommendation:
(1) Add `

` right after .gallery-head (index.html:423-466). (2) Generalise to `showError(message, note = false, slot = els.error)`, keeping the unhide-before-write and the lightbox mirror. findings.documented_rule: showError (state.js:316-329): it unhides before writing because #error is role=alert, and mirrors into #lb-error while the lightbox is open. design-notes 'Delete unstarred': whether the search is strict is the server's decision, a 422 at the click.

The panel is sticky at this height, so the message stays on screen; the problem is distance, not visibility: it lands a full column away from the gallery the user is working in. sources.surface: Gallery header actions (Delete unstarred, search terms) and card tools (❐, ⊞)
sources.observation: With 'lighthouse' in the search box, Delete unstarred (at x=2418,y=517) is refused, but the message ('Delete unstarred takes key:value terms or an empty search…') appears in red at x=35,y=1003, the bottom-left of the settings panel. sources.surface: #error slot under Generate; gallery cards and gallery head
sources.observation: Pressing ❐ on the last card (card at x=1095, y=568) wrote its refusal into the panel's #error at x=35, y=1003, about 1060 px left and 435 px below (c06). Gallery cards reach x≈2400 at QHD. The refusal text is developer phrasing with literal backticks: 'its pipeline has no `image` parameter'.

findings.title: Closing the lightbox, or cancelling a Refine opened from it, drops focus at the first card instead of where the user was
surfaces: Lightbox Refine -> Refine dialog -> Cancel/Escape
Lightbox close / lightbox → Refine dialog → Cancel
findings.recommendation:
(1) In closeLightbox (lightbox.js:156), before clearing, capture `const last = lbList[lbIndex]`. Set a module flag `lbHandoff = true` in the programmatic callers (openRefine, the lbReuse handler, forgetImages) before they call it. When !lbHandoff, after the native focus restore, run `requestAnimationFrame(() => document.querySelector(`#gallery .card[data-id="${last.id}"] img, #viewer img[data-id="${last.id}"]`)?.focus())`. The browser scrolls it into view and the focus ring marks it. Reset lbHandoff afterwards.
(2) In openRefine (refine.js:98), before closeLightbox(), save `refineReturn = els.lightbox.open ? { id: lbList[lbIndex].id, gallery: lbList === galleryRecords, list: lbList } : null`.
(3) runRefine sets refineReturn = null before els.refineDialog.close().
(4) refineClosed: when refineReturn is set, resolve the record by id in galleryRecords if gallery is true, because a job landing while the dialog was open may have reset the array; otherwise use the saved list. Then call openLightbox(rec, list) and clear refineReturn. Restoring lbView is optional.
Alternative: stack the dialog over the open lightbox. That restores everything natively but contradicts the documented rule. It would also need `if (els.refineDialog.open) return;` before the lightbox key block (app.js:266-270), where the arrows sit above the input guard and Escape closes the lightbox.
findings.documented_rule: CLAUDE.md Frontend: 'the lightbox's Refine (which closes the lightbox)', and refineSource is null once the dialog closes. app.js:235-238: openRefine closes the lightbox for its dialog; with no pass, the lightbox stays open with the mirrored note. lightbox.js:165-167: a fresh open starts at fit. refine.js:397-404: refineClosed runs for Refine, Cancel, the cross and Escape alike.
findings.rule_tension: Reopening on cancel keeps the lightbox closed while the dialog is up, so the documented rule holds. Returning focus to the last-viewed card must happen only on a user dismissal (Escape, ✕, a click on the backdrop or stage). closeLightbox also runs from Reuse (lbReuse, which then scrolls to the top at gallery.js:401), from openRefine and from forgetImages; focusing a card there would scroll the page back down and undo Reuse's scroll.
findings.smokes_affected: smoke-refine.json:58-71: the dialog is opened from the lightbox and dismissed with Escape at :69. With the fix the lightbox reopens. :71 still passes; add `els.lightbox.open` to it, and :74's openRefine closes the lightbox again. smoke.json:57-59 closes the lightbox with a backdrop click, so focus would move to the last-viewed card; the later steps use eval, not coordinates, so they still pass. smoke-conditioning.json:54-55 is unaffected (no pass, so the lightbox stays open).
findings.how_checked: FLUX fake on 7906, 60 images, 2560x1305, real clicks and keys throughout. Opened card 1 (id 62), pressed ArrowRight 40 times to 41/60 (id 22), pressed Escape, and read activeElement, scrollY and the last card's rect. Then opened card 6, walked to 9/60 (id 54), zoomed 2x, clicked the lightbox's ⤢ Refine at [2247,1205,280,37] and pressed Escape on the dialog.
findings.verifier_notes: Both halves reproduce, but the 'off-screen' part depends on scale. At QHD about 48 cards (4 rows of 12) fit on screen, so the last card I viewed (41st) was still visible. It goes off-screen after a longer walk, or when the walk starts further down. The cancel path matters more for this review, because it makes trying the Refine dialog cost the whole lightbox session. Adjusted because the source recommendations would focus a card on every close path, including Reuse, which would undo Reuse's scroll to the panel. They also reopened from a possibly stale list instead of resolving the record by id.
findings.merge_note: refine-dialog-5 details the Refine path: openRefine closes the lightbox, so Cancel can't return to it. It proposes saving and restoring lbList and lbIndex.

sources.surface: Lightbox close / lightbox → Refine dialog → Cancel
sources.observation: I opened the first card, walked 100 images with ArrowRight to 101/143, and pressed Escape. Focus returned to the first card at scrollY 0. The card of the image last viewed was at y=2015, off-screen and not marked. From image 6/96 in the lightbox I pressed Refine: openRefine closes the lightbox. Escape on the Refine dialog then leaves both dialogs closed, with focus on IMG 152 (the card first opened) at scrollY 0. The walked-to position is gone.
sources.why_it_matters: Triage is walk, close, act. Losing the place after each close means scrolling and hunting for the same image again. For Refine, looking at the dialog and cancelling costs the whole lightbox session, which makes trying the dialog feel risky.

sources.surface: Lightbox Refine -> Refine dialog -> Cancel/Escape
sources.observation: Clicking the lightbox's '⤢ Refine' (a 280x37 button at 2262,1205) closes the lightbox before the dialog opens (lightbox=false, dialog=true). Escape or Cancel then leaves focus on a gallery card image, and the lightbox is not reopened. Its strip position and zoom are gone (closeLightbox resets lbList, lbIndex and lbView.key).
sources.why_it_matters: The lightbox is where people inspect images and decide to refine one. Backing out of the dialog, which is common after seeing the size or strength options, costs a reopen and a walk back to the same image in the strip, every time.

findings.title: Reuse scrolls the page to the top even when the sticky panel is in view, throwing away the gallery position
surfaces: Card ↻ Reuse / lightbox Reuse settings
Viewer vs. scroll position; reuseIntoPanel scrollTo
findings.recommendation: (1) In reuseIntoPanel (web/gallery.js:400-401), replace the unconditional window.scrollTo(0) with `const r = els.prompt.getBoundingClientRect(); if (r.top < 0 || r.bottom > innerHeight) els.prompt.scrollIntoView({ block: 'nearest', behavior: reduce ? 'auto' : 'smooth' });`. At QHD and at 125% the sticky prompt sits at y=111-236, so Reuse no longer jumps. (2) Today's scroll to 0 is also what accidentally brings #viewer into view for the next Generate, so removing it alone makes the off-screen-result problem more frequent. Pair it with a 'New image ↑' button next to #progress-text in the sticky panel. Show the button when a job's first image or first preview frame lands while `els.viewer.getBoundingClientRect().bottom < 0`. Its click runs `els.viewer.scrollIntoView({ block: 'start' })`, honouring reduced motion. Hide it once the viewer is in view. Never auto-scroll. (3) The job end's `resetGallery()` (web/generation.js:480) empties #gallery and reloads page 1. At QHD that collapsed scrollY 700 -> 0 and cut 127 cards to 96, so the position kept by (1) only lasts until the next job ends. To keep it across a job: when the search box is empty, Favorites is unticked and All models is off, prepend the done event's `data.images` with `card()` and `galleryRecords.unshift(...)`, and let scroll anchoring hold the view. Fall back to resetGallery() whenever a filter is active.
findings.documented_rule: No rule covers the scroll. design-notes 'Per-control defaults and Reuse' never mentions it, and it dates from the initial commit. Related constraints: style.css:65-73 (the panel is sticky only above 900px wide and 900px tall, static otherwise), prefers-reduced-motion at gallery.js:400, and design-notes 'Paging by id' (the browser's anchor is the last record it holds).
findings.rule_tension: The conditional scroll keeps reduced-motion handling, and it still scrolls in the static-panel layouts (under 901px wide or 900px tall, which includes the smokes' 1400x900), where the prompt really is off-screen. Prepending at job end leaves the paging anchor (the last record) untouched, so 'Paging by id' still holds.
findings.smokes_affected: No smoke asserts the Reuse scroll. These call reuse() at 1400x900, where the panel is static and the page sits near scroll 0, and should be re-run: smoke-conditioning.json:79,110, smoke-flux.json:41,52, smoke-refine.json:121-135. If (3) is done, re-run smoke.json (card counts after jobs and Delete unstarred, e.g. :181) and smoke-paging.json, which both depend on the gallery reloading after a job.
findings.how_checked: FLUX.1 Krea [dev] fakes on 7907 (instant) and 8907 (--step 0.3), sharing one gallery of about 130 mixed-size images. At 2560x1305 DPR 1 and at 2048x1040 DPR 1.25 I placed a card mid-viewport, hovered it, clicked its ↻ with a real mouse click, and logged scrollY, the panel and prompt rects and the prompt value. Then, scrolled into the gallery, I pressed Ctrl+Enter (batch 1, and batch 4 at QHD) and logged the #viewer rect and scrollY while the job ran and after it ended.
findings.verifier_notes: The Reuse scroll is real and useless where the panel is sticky. The other reviewers' recommendation missed two things. First, the scroll to 0 is what currently puts the viewer on screen before the next Generate. Second, the job end resets the gallery anyway, so fixing Reuse alone preserves little in the reuse -> generate loop. walkthrough-14's off-screen result reproduces exactly at 125% (scrollY 815, viewer top -739). At QHD it shows only while a job runs, because the reset at job end collapses the page to the top. Side observation: at 2048x1040 the sticky panel is 1071px tall in a 1040px viewport. The 'sticky only where the whole panel fits' threshold (max-height 900px) does not catch that, though Generate and the finish line stayed visible.
findings.merge_note: walkthrough-14 adds a related issue: a result generated while scrolled into the gallery lands above the viewport (scroll anchoring), and the only sign is the finish line.

sources.surface: Card ↻ Reuse / lightbox Reuse settings
sources.observation: Deep in the gallery (scrollY 1110), pressing a card's ↻ filled the panel and smooth-scrolled the window to 0. At 2560x1305 the panel is sticky (top 68, height 1071, fully visible at any scroll: panelTop measured 76), so the scroll shows nothing new. It only throws away the gallery position. The scroll is not mentioned in the 'Per-control defaults and Reuse' design note.
sources.why_it_matters: Reuse is how one iterates from a past image: reuse, tweak, generate, look back at neighbours. Each reuse costs a scroll back down and a hunt for the spot.

sources.surface: Viewer vs. scroll position; reuseIntoPanel scrollTo
sources.observation: At 2048x1040 @125%, scrolled into the gallery (scrollY 458), Ctrl+Enter generated an image whose viewer then grew above the viewport. Scroll anchoring moved the page to scrollY 815 and the viewer's top to -739, entirely off-screen. The only signs were 'Finished 1 image in 4s.' and a new top-left card. Reuse from a card always called window.scrollTo(0): 532 -> 0 at QHD and 815 -> 0 at 125%, even though the panel is sticky and its prompt was already in view. Every Reuse from deep in the gallery or a sheet loses the user's place.
sources.why_it_matters: Moving between panel, viewer and gallery is the task-level friction the user describes as clunky. Each Reuse means scrolling back to find where they were, and a result that lands off-screen looks like nothing happened.

findings.title: No one-click way to keep the seed of the image just made; the seed is shown only in the lightbox
surfaces: Panel Seed box; viewer
Seed / dice; finished line under Generate
findings.recommendation: Do not put the button next to the dice. The Seed row is full at 296 px (Seed 107, Batch 62, Runs 62, dice 41, 3 gaps); a 41 px button would leave Seed about 58 px, 3-4 digits. Put it in the finish line instead (generation.js:453-461): `Finished 1 image in 4s · seed 5720723289104536` plus an inline `Use seed` button, or 'seeds X–Y' for a batch with the button writing data.images[0].seed. Use seed sets only els.seed, then syncRuns(); schedulePreview(); persistPanel(). Show the same line as a caption under the viewer when it holds one image. Let the box show all 16 digits: `#seed { font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; -moz-appearance: textfield; } #seed::-webkit-inner-spin-button { display: none; }`, or get the width from M16's wider panel. When a grid wrote the base back, have the run hint say 'Seed fixed at …; 🎲 for a random one'.
findings.documented_rule: generation.js:151-161: a blank Seed draws a fresh seed on every Generate, and only a grid writes its base back, for Resume (design-notes 'Panel persistence' lists the seed written back after Run grid; 'Resume keys on settings'). design-notes 'Seeds fit in a double'. CLAUDE.md: Unload also stops the critic's server and drops the tokenizers (main._stop_critic).
findings.rule_tension: An explicit 'Use seed' keeps both deliberate behaviours: a blank box stays random, and the grid write-back stays. walkthrough-15's 'disable Unload while unloaded' conflicts with the critic and tokenizer release Unload still performs when the image model is unloaded, so drop that part.
findings.smokes_affected: smoke.json:157 expects cellNote includes('Finished 6 images') and includes('Only 2 distinct'); append the seed text after these and they still hold. No smoke references #btn-dice.
findings.how_checked: On the FLUX fake, typed a prompt and pressed Generate with a real click and the Seed box blank, then read the box, #cell-note, viewerRecords, the viewer's text and its img title. Measured the Seed row and took an element shot of a 16-digit seed. Ran a grid with a blank Seed, then a plain Generate, and compared seeds. Called /api/model/unload and read the topbar after a reload.
findings.verifier_notes: The core claim holds: the only one-click route is a card's hover ↻, which also overwrites the prompt, size, steps and CFG (see M2), and the lightbox route takes two clicks. The placement in the recommendation is corrected. walkthrough-15's extras are minor: autofocusing an empty prompt is fine, but disabling Unload is not, because of the critic and tokenizer release.
findings.merge_note: walkthrough-15 adds that the viewer shows no metadata, the Seed box shows 9 of 16 digits, and the fixed-vs-random state isn't visible. It proposes a viewer caption with a 'Use this seed' button.

sources.surface: Seed / dice; finished line under Generate
sources.observation: After Generate with a blank Seed, the box stays 'random' and the line under the button says 'Finished 1 image in 0s.' without the seed. The only control beside Seed is the dice, which clears it ('Clear seed (randomize)'). To lock a composition and change the prompt, the user has to open the lightbox and use Reuse settings. That also overwrites the prompt, steps, CFG, mu and size, and per panel-2 the prompt can't be undone.
sources.why_it_matters: 'Same seed, tweak the prompt' is the usual loop once something good turns up. Here it costs a lightbox round-trip and risks the prompt being edited. Keeping a blank seed random on each click is deliberate (generation.js:151-161), so the fix is a quick way to opt in, not a change of default.

sources.surface: Panel Seed box; viewer
sources.observation: A result's seed is shown only in the lightbox (12 px muted settings line); the viewer shows no metadata. To iterate on a fixed seed (Task 2) the route was open lightbox -> Reuse settings (2 clicks), which also rewrites the prompt and size. Once fixed, the 107 px Seed box showed 9 of 16 digits. Run grid with a blank Seed writes its base seed back (6024067162964337, deliberate for Resume), so every later plain Generate silently reuses that seed until 🎲 is pressed. Cold start also showed Load and an enabled Unload side by side while 'not loaded', and the prompt was not focused (activeElement BODY), which costs one more click.
sources.why_it_matters: Whether the next image will vary or repeat is a core expectation. Here it changes as a side effect of grids and Reuse, and the only signal is a truncated number.

findings.title: A single-axis sheet is laid out as one horizontal ribbon of 96 px cells, several screens wide
surfaces: Contact sheet (#sheet-grid) for a run with one varying axis
Contact sheet for runs where only one axis varies (seeds-only, a lone CFG sweep)
findings.recommendation: In renderSheet (sheet.js:341-418), handle rowAxis null with colValues.length * 102 > els.sheet.clientWidth - 40. In that case, lay out `gridTemplateColumns = 'repeat(auto-fill, minmax(200px, 1fr))'` with no header row or rowhead. Each cell carries its own label, e.g. an absolutely positioned `Seed 903` at the cell's bottom edge. Cells stay in colValues order, so `shown` and the lightbox keep reading order. In buildSheetCanvas, wrap the same way (columns = Math.ceil(Math.sqrt(n)), a label under each cell). This also fixes the export of a long 1-D sheet: the 96 px floor at sheet.js:462 currently overrides EXPORT_MAX_EDGE. Keep the strip when the axis fits at its current size.
findings.documented_rule: chooseAxes (sheet.js:210-215): a seeds-only run keeps Seed as its one dimension. style.css:736-738: many columns scroll sideways, and the page never scrolls horizontally. sheet.js:204-205: a variant axis alone stays a strip. Design notes 'The contact sheet': the variant axis takes the rows when another axis varies.
findings.rule_tension: Compatible. The wrap changes only how a 1-D sheet is drawn: Seed remains its one dimension, nothing is squeezed below 96 px, and the page still never scrolls sideways. It must apply only when rowAxis is null, so any 2-D or variant-row sheet keeps the matrix.
findings.smokes_affected: Probably none. The wrap applies only to 1-D sheets wider than the stage. smoke.json 62-67 (6-cell sheet) and its head/rowhead checks at 83, 97 and 102 are 2-D or narrow, but re-run them along with smoke-paging.json 26-33.
findings.how_checked: Fake on 7912. Made a 28-image Generate (Batch 4 x Runs 7, only the seed varies) and a 120-seed grid at 512 px. Opened both with showRun at QHD and at 125%. Measured .sheet-scroll scrollWidth against clientWidth, cell size and visible cells. Toggled Sheet off to compare with the gallery view of the same run, and ran buildSheetCanvas() on the 120-seed sheet.
findings.verifier_notes: grid-7 and visual-13 report the same thing, so the merge is right; this is not a duplicate of M18, though it shares the code. Medium rather than low: every multi-image Generate (Batch or Runs) is a seeds-only run in the Runs picker, and picking it always opens this 96 px ribbon. A workaround exists (untick Sheet), but nothing on the page points to it.
findings.merge_note: visual-13 shows the same for a 28-image seed-only batch, with about 1000 px empty below it.

sources.surface: Contact sheet for runs where only one axis varies (seeds-only, a lone CFG sweep)
sources.observation: Run 719e… (120 seeds, nothing else varying): Columns=Seed, Rows=—, 120 columns at minmax(96px,1fr). Measured scrollWidth 12,246 px against a client width of 2,176; 21 cells visible, horizontal scrollbar, ~800 px of empty page below. The export would be 120 cells wide (EXPORT_MAX_EDGE caps each cell at 96 px).
sources.why_it_matters: 'Seeds' is the most common sweep (pick the best composition). At QHD it gets the worst layout: tiny thumbnails behind a sideways scroll, while the vertical space goes unused.

sources.surface: Contact sheet (#sheet-grid) for a run with one varying axis
sources.observation: Opening Sheet on the 28-image batch (only the seed varies) lays out one row of `minmax(96px, 1fr)` columns. 28 x (96+6) = 2856px is wider than the 2161px stage, so the cells shrink to the 96px minimum and the row scrolls sideways under a light native scrollbar. The 1000px below it is empty.
sources.why_it_matters: At QHD the sheet, the tool for comparing a run, shows each image at 96px and hides a quarter of them off to the side. The user has to scroll horizontally on a screen with plenty of vertical room.

findings.title: Batches of 2-4 are shown at 34vh, using about 42% of the viewer width at QHD
surfaces: Results viewer, multi tier (.viewer.multi img { max-height: 34vh })
findings.recommendation: Correction: the proposed `repeat(var(--n), 1fr)` with max-height 68vh puts every image on one row. That shrinks landscape batches. Four 16:9 images today wrap to 2x2 at 786x444; on one row they would be about 523x295, half the area. Pick the column count in JS instead. In appendResult, and on a ResizeObserver on #viewer, let W = viewer content width, H = 68vh, a = rec.width/rec.height, n = the expected count from M40 (else viewerRecords.length, capped at 4). For c in 1..n: rows = ceil(n/c), tile = min((W-(c-1)*12)/c, ((H-(rows-1)*12)/rows)*a). Keep the c with the largest tile. Set --cols and --tile-h (tile/a) on els.viewer. CSS: `.viewer.multi { display:grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(var(--cols), auto); justify-content:center } .viewer.multi img { max-height: var(--tile-h); max-width:100% }`. Results at 2560: 2 squares 887 (now 444), 3 squares 702 (444), 4 squares 523 (444), three 2:3 at 595x887 (298x444), four 16:9 at 2x2 776x437 (786x444, the same). Where a grid's size axis mixes aspects, fall back to today's flex wrap. Leave the >4 eight-column rule unchanged.
findings.documented_rule: design-notes 'The running batch on wide screens' governs only the more-than-four tier. It says the 1 and 2-4 tiers 'keep their existing layout', which is a scope statement, not a reason. Also the panel.js:264-265 comment: tiers exist so a long sweep does not push the gallery a screen further down per image.
findings.rule_tension: Compatible. A best-fit layout keeps every 1-4 image result in one viewer about 917 px tall (the single tier's height), so the gallery never moves further down per image. Update the design-notes sentence to describe the new 2-4 rule.
findings.smokes_affected: None assert tile sizes or the .multi class. smoke.json, smoke-flux.json:43, smoke-conditioning.json:48 and smoke-refine.json:53 click `#viewer img`, which is still the first result.
findings.how_checked: Same fake, real jobs measured with getBoundingClientRect: batch 2 at 1:1, batch 3 at 2:3, batch 4 at 1:1 and batch 4 at 16:9, at 2560x1305. Batch 2 repeated at 2048x1040 DPR 1.25. I then worked out the proposed CSS-grid layout against the same widths.
findings.verifier_notes: Shot paths are relative to scratchpad/ux/verify-results-2/. The claim is real: a batch of 2 squares gets a quarter of the area the screen allows. Only the recommended CSS needed correcting for landscape. The same best-fit gains at 1400x900 too, so it need not be gated at 2000 px.

sources.surface: Results viewer, multi tier (.viewer.multi img { max-height: 34vh })
sources.observation: Batch 2 at 1024x1024 rendered as two 444x444 tiles in a 2161 px wide viewer (900 px used). Batch 3 at 848x1264 rendered as three 298x444 tiles (906 px used). At the single-image height of 68vh (887 px) both still fit in one row: 2x887+12 = 1786 px and 3x595+24 = 1809 px, against 2133 px available. A batch of 4 squares could be 528 px rather than 444. The 34vh rule (style.css:669) depends only on count, not on width.
sources.why_it_matters: On a 2560 screen, a batch of 2 or 3 (the common way to compare seeds) is shown at a quarter of the area the screen has room for. The user then has to open the lightbox to judge detail, while more than half of the viewer is empty.

findings.title: Starring on the sheet needs a lightbox round trip, the star mark is a 12 px glyph, and the Favorites sheet drops shared settings
surfaces: Sheet cells (.sheet-cell), Favorites tick in sheet mode
findings.recommendation:
(1) style.css:768-771: give .sheet-cell.fav the card's treatment. Share `.card.fav, .sheet-cell.fav {border-color:#fbbf24; box-shadow:0 0 0 1px #fbbf24}` and the 28 px badge ::after rule (style.css:816-833). (2) Star without the lightbox: one keydown listener on #sheet-grid that, when F is pressed on a focused cell image and the lightbox is closed, calls setFavorite(rec, !rec.favorite) for that cell's record (cell.dataset.id). Optionally add a hover-only ☆ with tabindex=-1, created on pointerenter. (3) Constants: in renderSheet, collect the axes of sheetAxesList whose values[key].length === 1 and print them in a new `

` above the grid, e.g. 'Fixed: steps 4 · CFG 2 · seed 5872080855328996'. Use a separate element, not #sheet-note. Optionally add the same line to the export caption.
findings.documented_rule: Design notes 'Panel persistence' (end): sheet cells carry .fav, which setFavorite toggles by class and never by re-rendering. style.css:765-767: the sheet star exists 'so where the keepers cluster is visible on the sheet'. CLAUDE.md: the sheet's filters are the gallery's (Favorites).
findings.rule_tension: The CSS change and a keyboard F on the focused cell both keep setFavorite's toggle-by-class rule. A ☆ button rendered in every cell would add up to 1024 tab stops, the problem the card tools' comment at style.css:793-795 already describes, so use a delegated key handler and, if wanted, a hover-only button with tabindex=-1. Appending 'Fixed:' to #sheet-note would break smokes that match the note exactly, so give it its own element.
findings.smokes_affected: For item (3), if the line went into #sheet-note: smoke.json 97 ('3 of 3 loaded') and 102 ('4 of 4 loaded') and smoke-analysis.json 319 ('8 of 8 loaded') compare the note exactly; a separate #sheet-fixed avoids them. Items (1) and (2) touch no smoke step. smoke.json 85-89 stars cells by setFavorite and should be re-run.
findings.how_checked: Fake on 7912, 3x2 variable run (seed 5872080855328996, steps 4, CFG 2). Starred two sheet cells by clicking the image, pressing a real F key and a real Escape. Read getComputedStyle(cell,'::after') and the border of .sheet-cell.fav, and compared a .card.fav probe element. Counted buttons in a sheet cell. Checked that the lightbox walks the sheet (ArrowRight). Ticked Favorites and read the axes, layout, note and sheetRecords' shared settings.
findings.verifier_notes: Reproduced: the 12 px star, no tools on cells, and the shared settings missing under Favorites. Corrected one claim: starring is not three actions per cell. The lightbox walks the sheet in reading order, so triaging k cells is one click, then arrow plus F per keeper, then Escape. The cost is losing the side-by-side view while choosing, not the keystrokes. The star size alone defeats the sheet star's documented purpose. Its Favorites-sheet upscaling (2.71x) belongs to M18.

sources.surface: Sheet cells (.sheet-cell), Favorites tick in sheet mode
sources.observation: Sheet cells have no tools: starring means click → lightbox (opens at '1/6') → F → Escape. The starred cell then shows `.sheet-cell.fav::after` at 12 px, no badge or ring, barely visible in a 696 px cell (15b, 15c). A gallery card gets a 28 px dark badge with an 18 px star plus an amber ring. Ticking Favorites on the fox run's sheet re-derived the axes from the 2 starred images: two 1070 px cells headed 'size big' / 'size none', note '2 of 2 loaded'. That both keepers were ground grass, CFG 2, seed 5872080855328996 is shown nowhere.
sources.why_it_matters: Marking keepers on the sheet is how a night's results get narrowed down. Three steps per cell and an almost invisible mark make that slow. The filtered view then hides the very settings the user starred them to remember.

findings.title: A strength sweep's sheet has no source cell to compare against, and its cells run off the screen
surfaces: Contact sheet opened by a strength sweep; viewer strip above it
findings.recommendation: (a) In renderSheet (sheet.js ~372), when every sheetRecord has the same non-null refine, fetch GET /api/images/{refine} once, cache it by id, and add one leading column: gridTemplateColumns = `auto minmax(96px,1fr) repeat(n, minmax(96px,1fr))`. Put a .sheet-cell.source in it with head 'Source #4', spanning all rows (grid-row: span rowValues.length). Open it with openLightbox(source, [source, ...sheetRecords]), and put the source at the head of the list that sheet cells open too, so ←/→ flips source against each pass at the same fit size. Draw it as the export's first column. (b) After a fresh sweep sheet (generation.js:479 / showJob fresh), call els.sheet.scrollIntoView({block:'start'}) and add .sheet { scroll-margin-top: 64px } so the sticky topbar does not cover the heads. (c) Do not put max-height on .sheet-cell: on an aspect-ratio box that letterboxes the image instead of shrinking it. Cap the column width in JS instead: maxW = Math.floor((innerHeight - 160) * aspect), and use repeat(n, minmax(96px, ${maxW}px)) with justify-content:center. That only matters for 1-2 column sweeps of square or portrait images. (d) Optional polish: .sheet-grid .head at 13px var(--text).
findings.documented_rule: design-notes 'The contact sheet': the layout contract and the export are client-side (sheet.js renderSheet/buildSheetCanvas). design-notes 'The refine pass': 'The strength axis exists to put the candidates on one sheet.' CLAUDE.md Frontend: a strength sweep opens as its sheet via startJob(path, body, { sheet, panel:false }). setSheet(true) hides the gallery (els.gallery.hidden = on).
findings.rule_tension: Compatible if the source is not a sheet record. Render it as an extra leading grid column of class .sheet-cell.source, captioned 'Source #4 · 1264×848', drawn from a separate fetched record, and never fed to axesFor/chooseAxes, sheetLayout.cellOf, keep_rates or 'stats --by strength'. Strength null therefore still means a direct render. buildSheetCanvas draws it as a labelled first column, which keeps the export client-side.
findings.smokes_affected: smoke-refine.json:79-82 (expects sheetMode and a 'strength' row/col axis in sheetLayout; still holds if the source is not an axis and not in cellOf). No smoke counts sheet cells on a refine sheet. smoke-analysis.json:134 and smoke-comparison*.json count '#sheet-grid .sheet-cell:not(.empty)' on comparison sheets, which have no common refine and get no source column; still, exclude '.source' from such counts. smoke-paging.json:29-33 toggles the sheet with the topbar at scrollTo(0,0) and is unaffected by (b), which applies only to fresh sheets.
findings.how_checked: On port 7909 I ran 0.05,0.1,0.2 sweeps from the Refine dialog twice: on a 3:2 source (1264x848 to 1904x1280) and on a 1:1 source (1024x1024 to 1536x1536). Both ran at 2560x1305 DPR 1, and the square case also ran at 2048x1040 DPR 1.25. I measured the sheet cells' rects, the head font, the viewer strip, scrollY and document height, whether the source's id appeared in any visible img, and the list the lightbox walks when opened from a sheet cell.
findings.verifier_notes: The core claim holds: in sheet mode the source is nowhere on screen (gallery hidden, strip shows only the passes, lightbox list is passes only), so a strength is chosen without the original beside it. That defeats the stated purpose of the strength axis. Two corrections. First, the cells run off screen only for square or portrait sources: a 3:2 sweep fits at QHD. 'The page does not scroll' means it is not scrolled to the sheet automatically; the document does scroll. Second, the proposed max-height on cells would letterbox rather than shrink them, so (c) replaces it. Unrelated, seen here: the Re-render button reads 'Re-render 3 at 1024×1024' on a sheet of 1536x1536 passes, because it uses the panel's size by design. Worth a separate look at what it does to passes.

sources.surface: Contact sheet opened by a strength sweep; viewer strip above it
sources.observation: A three-strength sweep opens as a sheet automatically, which works well. But the sheet is three 712×712 cells labelled 'Strength 0.05 / 0.1 / 0.2' in 11px #8b8b9a, the first at y=632-726 depending on the strip. The bottom edge (y 1344-1438) lands below the 1305px viewport, and the page does not scroll. The strip above shows the same three images again at about 444px each (b02). The source the user is judging the strengths against appears nowhere on the sheet.
sources.why_it_matters: Picking a strength means asking 'which one still looks like the original but sharper'. Without the original in the row, the user compares three passes with each other. The duplicate strip spends roughly 470px of a 1305px screen.

findings.title: Clicking a finding selects its words in the prompt box but leaves them scrolled out of view
surfaces: Findings list > .analysis-item.selectable, and the #prompt textarea
findings.recommendation: The reviewer's fix does not work. In this Chromium build, selecting before focusing left scrollTop at 105 with the selection out of view, as did blur-then-focus-twice and a collapsed-then-range selection. What works, verified: after el.setSelectionRange(...) in selectIn (analysis.js:289-290), scroll the box to the selection with a hidden mirror. Create a div with the textarea's computed width, box-sizing, padding, border widths, font, line-height, letter/word spacing, white-space:pre-wrap and overflow-wrap; give it the text up to the selection start plus a zero-width marker span; then set el.scrollTop = Math.max(0, marker.offsetTop - el.clientHeight / 3) and remove the div. That is about 15 lines in one helper. It serves finding clicks, the 'stops reading at' cut link and the critic issues' quotes, which all call selectIn. Optionally add a 600 ms outline flash on the box (`outline: 2px solid var(--accent-2)`, #4ad6c8) as visible confirmation.
findings.documented_rule: CLAUDE.md Frontend: 'a finding's words selected only while still where the check found them'; 'Server offsets count code points; the page converts them (units()) before selecting'. A greyed negative box selects nothing (selectIn returns false when el.disabled).
findings.rule_tension: The fix runs only after the existing still-in-place guard and the units() conversion succeed, and changes nothing else: it only sets the textarea's scrollTop. The disabled-box early return stays first.
findings.smokes_affected: None fail: they check selectionStart/End, which do not change. smoke-analysis.json steps 24-27 (finding click selects 'no people'; the cut link selects from 'a 35mm lens') and 34-35 (a stale finding still selecting) should each gain an expectation that the selection's line lies inside the box's scroll window.
findings.how_checked: FLUX fake. Typed the 76-word prompt with Input.insertText, so the caret and scroll end where real typing leaves them, then Check, then a real click on the 'no people' warning and on the 'stops reading at' link. Read the textarea's selection and its scrollTop, clientHeight and scrollHeight, with elshots of #prompt. Ran the reviewer's proposed ordering in-page (blur, then setSelectionRange, then focus) plus two other focus tricks and a mirror-div scroll, and measured each.
findings.verifier_notes: It reproduces on the common path: after typing a long prompt the box sits scrolled to the bottom, so any finding about the first half of the prompt selects words out of view. The cut link fails the other way round once the box has been scrolled up. Only the recommended mechanism was wrong, which is why this is adjusted. A taller prompt box at QHD (a likely finding elsewhere) would make this rarer but not fix it.

sources.surface: Findings list > .analysis-item.selectable, and the #prompt textarea
sources.observation: The Prompt box is 296x125 px (5 rows) and needs scrollHeight 249 for a 76-word prompt. Clicking the '"no people" asks for an absence' warning set the selection correctly (code points 34-43, 'no people'). But the textarea stayed scrolled to its bottom (scrollTop 126, clientHeight 123), so the highlighted words on line 2 were out of view. The screenshot shows only the last 6 lines. The only hints that a row can be clicked are the title 'Select these words' and a 4%-white hover.
sources.why_it_matters: 'Click a finding to find its words' is how you act on a warning that has no Apply, like the negation one. The click looks like it does nothing, so the user reads through the whole prompt by hand or decides the feature is broken.

findings.title: The critic's answer is a 500 px stack of full-width boxes; the diff is collapsed, and the rewrite's findings repeat the prompt's
surfaces: #critic-result: parts, issues, Rewrite, rewrite_findings, Reordered
findings.recommendation:
1) Add `.analysis-text, .critic-diff { max-width: 120ch; }` in style.css near line 365. At 12 px that is about 140 characters a line instead of 403 at QHD (305 at 2048), and it also fixes #compare-own (M61), which uses the same class. 2) Wrap the Rewrite and Reordered `.critic-variant` blocks in `
`, and from `@media (min-width:1800px)` give it `display:grid; grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fit,minmax(min(100%,60ch),1fr)); gap:16px; align-items:start`. Keep the `.critic-variant` class on each block. 3) In rewriteChanges (analysis.js:803), add a muted line after `` (a sibling inside the details, outside the summary, so it shows while collapsed; or right after the details), built from the first one to three changed runs of promptChanges, up to about 80 characters: `+ "Rewritten: "` / `- "no people"`, with '...' after that. Leave the summary's text and the closed default as they are. 4) In renderCritic (analysis.js:684-697), keep every rewrite finding. Mark each with a small tag: 'also in your prompt' when analysisResult.body.findings has the same `rule`, else 'new'. After the list, add 'No longer flagged: '. Do not collapse by rule: on Animagine the rewrite's guide.order finding ('"Rewritten: masterpiece" before "1girl"') is a different instance from the prompt's ('"masterpiece" before "green hair"'). 5) Put a caption 'How the critic read it' (a

, not a dt) above the .critic-parts list.
findings.documented_rule: CLAUDE.md, Frontend and CLI: 'Rewrites show character counts and an expandable exact diff against the checked source (promptChanges)... no rewrite says so, with the server's set-aside explanations.' design-notes.md, 'The prompt analyser' > 'The page.': 'A retained rewrite shows Changed from original, with character counts and an expandable exact diff', and the page 'shows every version to be read before it is used'. The rewrite's findings select inside its textarea (selectIn(area), analysis.js:690-693), and the answer takes focus (#critic-result).
findings.rule_tension: Keep the diff expandable and closed by default. Opened, it prints the whole 427-character rewrite in a 53 px box directly above the identical 55 px textarea, so opening it by default would show the text twice and would break smoke-rewrite's click-to-open step. Put a short gist of the change outside <summary> instead. The rewrite textarea stays visible and focusable for selectIn. 'The same check, run on the rewrite:' and the set-aside notes stay. Nothing calls the rewrite trusted. Keep all of the rewrite's findings listed and tag them instead of collapsing them, because the same rule can be a different instance (seen on Animagine).
findings.smokes_affected: smoke-rewrite.json:6 (summary must still start 'Changed from original:'), :7-8 (clicks the summary to open it, so the diff must stay closed by default), :11-12 (exact summary textContent, so the gist must sit outside <summary>); smoke-analysis.json:61 (first .critic-parts dt must be 'Subject', so the caption must not be a dt), :63 ('.critic-checked .analysis-item' must still exist); smoke-animagine.json:150 (b.closest('.critic-variant').querySelector('textarea'), so keep the class on each block inside the new wrapper).
findings.how_checked: Fresh FLUX.1 Krea [dev] fake on 7916 and Animagine fake on 8916. Ran the 416-character harbour prompt (the smoke-analysis prompt): Check, then Ask the critic, at 2560x1305 DPR 1 and 2048x1040 DPR 1.25. Measured #critic-result and each child with getBoundingClientRect. Measured characters per line in each textarea with canvas measureText in the textarea's own font. Compared critiqueResult.body.rewrite_findings[].rule with analysisResult.body.findings[].rule. Opened the details and measured the diff against the textarea. Checked whether Run comparison falls below innerHeight.
findings.verifier_notes: The finder's '~330 characters a line' measures as about 403 at QHD. The '449-510 px' stack measures 461 px on FLUX and 358 px on Animagine (no issue kept, reordered set aside). The fake critic's rewrite only prepends 'Rewritten: ', so in the fake every prompt finding carries over. With the real critic (docs/verified.md 2026-09-29 rows) rewrites drew a mix of carried-over findings and new lint findings (brackets, CLIP cut, 26 added words), so marking which is which matters more there. sources.surface: #critic-result: parts, issues, Rewrite, rewrite_findings, Reordered
sources.observation:
The answer stacks 449-510 px of full-width content:
- an unlabelled Subject/Setting/Text-to-render list
- the issue
- 'Rewrite' with a 2135 px read-only textarea (~330 characters a line)

findings.title: Autocomplete pre-selects the first item and ranks guide tags first, so 'lo'+Tab inserts 'low quality'
surfaces: Prompt autocomplete (#tag-suggestions)
findings.recommendation: Fix the ranking first (backend/main.py:353-364). Order the list as: an exact match; then remote and local together by match quality (whole-word prefix before substring), with local guide tags placed by prefix-match length instead of always first. Never put a tag from the guide's recommended negative prompt (low quality, worst quality, low score, bad score, average score) at index 0 of a positive-prompt suggestion unless it is an exact match.
