Then change pre-selection in renderTagSuggestions (tags.js:91) and renderEditorSuggestions (tags.js:218) the same way: pre-select item 0 only when the query is 3 or more characters and item 0 starts with it. Otherwise leave the index at -1, so Tab moves on and Enter inserts a newline (app.js:142 already requires tagSuggestionIndex >= 0). ArrowDown still selects. Optionally relabel the 'model' kind to 'guide' to match the chip tooltip 'Checkpoint guide tag'.
findings.documented_rule: design-notes 'Animagine XL 4.0' (docs/design-notes.md:1805): finite special tags are 'merged into autocomplete ahead of remote results and remain available offline'. In the chip editor (design-notes:1829), 'Click, Enter or Tab accepts a suggestion', and suggestions start with the first keystroke so that Enter on an untouched edit keeps the tag.
findings.rule_tension: Putting guide tags first is deliberate, but the stated reason is offline availability, not ranking. Merging them after or among the remote results by match quality keeps them available offline: when the remote lookup fails, local is the whole list. The finding's constraint that the chip editor 'already behaves this way by design' is wrong. The editor also pre-selects item 0 once typing starts (tags.js:218), and I reproduced 'lo'+Tab in the insert editor writing 'low quality'. Only an untouched edit is protected. Removing pre-selection everywhere would change the documented Enter/Tab accept in the chip editor and the Enter step in four smokes. That is a bigger change than the harm needs.
findings.smokes_affected: smoke-animagine 61 asserts `.tag-kind` textContent === 'model' and only changes if the label is renamed. With the 3-character threshold, the 'green h' + Enter steps keep working: smoke-animagine 5-10, smoke-illustrious 10-13, smoke-kohaku 9-12, smoke-wai 11-13, and the chip-editor step smoke-animagine 41 ('green e' → li.active green eyes). If pre-selection were removed outright as the finding proposes, all of those would need an ArrowDown step.
findings.how_checked: Real keystrokes (Input.insertText per character, then key Tab/Enter) in the prompt on the Animagine fake. curl on /api/tags/suggest. Also the chip insert editor (openTagInsert, then typing 'lo' and Tab).
findings.verifier_notes: Real and costly. Fast Tab or Enter puts quality-lowering tags into the positive prompt, and the chip turns green. The original recommendation is half right. Its main lever, removing pre-selection, is not needed once the ranking is fixed, and it rests on a wrong premise about the chip editor. Popular A1111 tag autocompletes pre-select the top match and accept on Tab, so users expect that. The bug is which tag ends up on top.

sources.surface: Prompt autocomplete (#tag-suggestions)
sources.observation: On the server's own suggestion route, typing '1girl, solo, lo' lists 'MODEL low quality | MODEL low score' with item 0 already active. Tab, pressed to leave the box, wrote '1girl, solo, low quality' and focus stayed in the prompt. 'gre' lists 'great score' (model) ahead of green hair/green eyes (900k posts), and Enter wrote 'great score'. With a richer index, ', green'+Tab became 'green hat'. Model-card tags are always merged ahead of the Danbooru results (backend/main.py:363), and renderTagSuggestions selects item 0 every time (tags.js:91). Enter and Tab therefore always replace the word being typed whenever the list is open. The category label for those tags reads 'MODEL'.
sources.why_it_matters: A fast typist who presses Tab to move on gets a quality-lowering tag ('low quality', 'low score', 'worst quality') in the positive prompt, or a different tag than the one typed. The chip turns green either way, so nothing flags it. The design notes already avoided this exact trap in the chip editor: 'suggestions start with the first keystroke … so Enter on an untouched edit keeps the tag rather than taking the top match'.

findings.title: The Tags helper popover covers 71% of the prompt it inserts into, and appends a rating after the quality tags
surfaces: Tags helper popover (#tags-menu) and its Rating/Person-count buttons
findings.recommendation: (1) Stop covering the prompt. Anchor the popover under the textarea, over the Negative prompt and Size fields, which are irrelevant while tagging. Move #tags-menu into .prompt-editor after the textarea with `top: calc(100% + 6px); left: 0; width: 100%` (the panel is 330px and the menu 320px). Extend app.js:153's outside-click test to `closest('#tag-helper, #tags-menu')`. The autocomplete list can share that anchor, since it only opens while the prompt is focused and typing. Do not float it right over the stage: that covers chips 1-4 of the tray at x 366-676, the very confirmation of what the click did. (2) Name the insertion point in the menu: replace the static note (tags.js:690) with one computed from tagCursorIndex() on open and after each insert, e.g. 'Inserts after "absurdres" (the end of the prompt) - the guide puts Rating before Details.' Exclusive groups still replace in place. (3) If automatic slotting is wanted, the server should supply each helper group's slot in tag_helper, and the design-notes contract should be changed explicitly. (4) Raise .tag-menu from 11px to 12px to match the 12px chips; the tag-group heading is 10px.
findings.documented_rule: design-notes 'Animagine XL 4.0' (docs/design-notes.md:1777): 'Each tag is an explicit editor action at the current caret; active tags toggle off, exclusive person/rating choices replace one another'. tags.js:556-558: nothing silently reorders free-form tags. CLAUDE.md:641: the page has no reorder rule of its own.
findings.rule_tension: Part (2) of the recommendation contradicts the documented 'at the current caret' contract. Its slot logic ('Rating after the last character/copyright chip, else after person count') is also Animagine-only. Kohaku's order puts Rating last, and smoke-kohaku 15-17 expects 'safe' appended to '1girl, green hair'. Illustrious puts Rating third. WAI maps Rating to Subject and scene. Client-side placement would be the page's own copy of analysis.order. A compatible fix keeps caret insertion but makes the caret visible and named, and leaves placement to Check's Use reordered.
findings.smokes_affected: Positioning and the note text change no asserted behaviour: smoke-animagine 80-85, smoke-illustrious 14-25, smoke-kohaku 13-18 and smoke-wai 15-26 click options through eval and check prompt values. Moving #tags-menu out of #tag-helper requires the app.js:153 outside-click selector to change, or every option click closes the menu. Automatic slotting (finding part 2) would break smoke-kohaku 17 ('1girl, green hair, safe') and need per-guide data.
findings.how_checked: 17-tag Animagine prompt with no rating and the caret at the end (as after typing). Real click on Tags at (207,104) and on 'safe' at (150,251). Measured the rects of #tags-menu, #prompt and .panel at 2560x1305 DPR 1 and at 2048x1040 DPR 1.25, read computed font sizes, then pressed Check. Checked the four guides' tag_helper.order.
findings.verifier_notes: Both observations reproduce exactly. Severity stays medium because the helper's own note ('insert at the prompt caret') points at a caret it hides. Clicking the visible strip of the prompt to move the caret closes the menu (app.js:153), so placing a tag costs click prompt → reopen Tags → click tag → Check → Apply. The fix that slots by category was rejected as Animagine-specific and as a documented-contract change, and replaced with visibility plus a named insertion point.

sources.surface: Tags helper popover (#tags-menu) and its Rating/Person-count buttons
sources.observation: The popover opens at x=122-442, y=119-579. The prompt box is x=35-331, y=119-244, so 209 of its 296px width are covered over its full height, including the caret the note says tags 'insert at'. On a 17-tag prompt without a rating, clicking 'safe' wrote '…, masterpiece, high score, great score, absurdres, safe'. The caret was at the end, so the rating landed after the quality tags. The first line of the same popover reads 'Recommended order: Person count → Character → Series → Rating → Details → Quality'. Check then reported 'green hair (Details) comes before safe (Rating)'. The text inside the popover is 10-11px.
sources.why_it_matters: The helper's own instructions depend on a caret the user cannot see, and its usual result goes against the order it displays. One click on a rating produces a prompt the checker then flags, and the fix (Use reordered or a drag) is in another panel.

findings.title: Checkboxes show no keyboard focus at all (outline:none, with a border colour that doesn't render)
surfaces: Gallery head (Favorites, All models), grid Resume, comparison version ticks
findings.recommendation: Add `input[type=checkbox]:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent-2); outline-offset: 2px; }` to web/style.css. Its specificity (0,2,1) already beats style.css:114 `textarea:focus, input:focus { outline: none }` (0,1,1), so narrowing the global rule to `input:not([type=checkbox]):not([type=radio]):focus` is tidier but optional. --accent-2 is 10.4:1 on --panel and 11.0:1 on --bg. The text-input part of the original recommendation (a box-shadow ring) is optional polish, not a WCAG fix: the focused border #7c5cff against the unfocused #26262f is already 3.45:1, which passes 1.4.11.
findings.rule_tension: No documented rule covers checkbox focus. CLAUDE.md's focus rules (aria-disabled so focus stays put, focus moves after Check and the critic) depend on focus being visible, so this fix supports them.
findings.smokes_affected: None. No smoke step reads outline, box-shadow or computed focus styles. grep for outline, focus-visible and getComputedStyle found only smoke-animagine.json:13, which checks tag-chip font and colour.
findings.how_checked: Fresh FLUX.1 Krea [dev] fake on 7920, 2560x1305 DPR 1. Focused #search, then pressed real Tab keys through the gallery head and logged each step: Tab 2 = #fav-only (:focus-visible true; computed outline 'rgb(0,0,0) none 3px', border '0px none', appearance auto, box-shadow none), Tab 3 = #all-models (:focus-visible true), Tab 4 = #btn-sheet. Took an elshot of .gallery-head in each state and pixel-diffed them with PIL against the blurred state. Favorites focused and All models focused are both identical to no focus (diff bbox None). Sheet focused differs at x 2127-2176, so focus does render elsewhere on the page. Opened the grid <details>, tabbed from #grid-budget to #grid-resume (:focus-visible true, outline none), and its focused and unfocused label shots are also identical. The comparison ticks (analysis.js:937) match the same input:focus rule.
findings.verifier_notes: Reproduced exactly as claimed. A Space pressed while focus is invisible toggles Favorites or All models, and app.js:216 then runs resetGallery()+loadRuns(), so the gallery silently re-scopes. Ghost buttons and selects keep the UA focus ring because the global rule names only textarea and input.

sources.surface: Gallery head (Favorites, All models), grid Resume, comparison version ticks
sources.observation: When Tab lands on the Favorites or All models checkbox, its computed style is outline:none, and the border colour that the same rule sets does not show on a native checkbox. The focused and unfocused gallery heads are pixel-identical: crop b-checkbox-compare.png has Favorites focused on top and All models focused below. The tab log (a.out T44/T45) records `outline:none 3px rgb(0,0,0)` with :focus-visible true. The cause is the global rule `textarea:focus, input:focus { outline: none; border-color: var(--accent) }`, which also catches every checkbox: grid Resume and the comparison's Original/Reordered/Rewrite ticks.
sources.why_it_matters: A keyboard user cannot see where focus is. A Space pressed on what looks like nothing toggles Favorites or All models, and the gallery silently re-filters (resetGallery). This fails WCAG 2.4.7 Focus Visible (AA).

findings.title: The grid fold's key readouts are its smallest text: a 77 px Run grid button and an 11 px muted preview
surfaces: Grid fold: summary, preview, Run grid
findings.recommendation: (1) Root cause of the 77px button: in Edge 154 a <details> lays its children out inside ::details-content, which is a block box (CSS.supports('selector(::details-content)') is true). So .section's display:flex/column/gap:10px applies only to the summary and that wrapper. #btn-grid is then a shrink-to-fit inline-block, and the rows inside the fold sit with 0 gap. Fix: `#btn-grid { width: 100%; }`, or `display:block`. Do not add a flex gap to .section::details-content: that adds about 70px to a fold that already overflows the viewport. (2) In previewGrid (generation.js:331-344), render the first line as `<span class="totals">` with display:block, font-size 13px, color var(--text) and weight 600, and the axes and prompts below it in the current 11px muted style. Keep the .warn class on #grid-preview with a `#grid-preview.warn .totals { color:#fbbf24 }` rule, and keep all the text in its textContent. (3) Client-side only, trim factors equal to 1 other than seeds, since line 2 already lists every axis: `p.summary.replace(/(^| x )1 (steps|CFG|mu|LoRA|strength)(?= x |$)/g, '').replace(/^ x /, '').replaceAll(' x ', ' × ')`. Fall back to p.summary when this comes out empty. The × matches the comparison preview, which already says '2 variants × 4 seeds'. (4) The real cost on the target screen: make the readouts visible. Opening the fold makes the sticky panel 1403-1504px tall in a 1305px viewport (1040 at 125%). The preview and Run grid stay below the fold until the gallery's very end, and the gallery keeps paging in more images as you scroll. Keyboard focus on Run grid does not reveal it either. Minimal fix in app.js: `const fitPanel = () => { panel.style.top = Math.min(68, innerHeight - panel.offsetHeight - 18) + 'px'; }; new ResizeObserver(fitPanel).observe(panel); addEventListener('resize', fitPanel);`. A panel that fits keeps top:68. A taller one scrolls until its bottom meets the viewport, then sticks there, so Generate, the preview and Run grid stay on screen while the gallery scrolls, and the prompt comes back when you scroll up. The alternative that follows the comment literally is a `.panel.unstuck{position:static}` class toggled the same way. If another cluster owns the sticky-panel overflow, fold point (4) into it, and this cluster is low on its own.
findings.documented_rule: index.html:302 and style.css:480-481: the grid stays folded by default ('a grid is an overnight tool, not the workflow'). style.css:70-73: 'Sticky only where the whole panel fits ... Run grid - was simply not reachable until the very end of the gallery released it', which is implemented only as @media (max-height: 900px). grid.py:425-447 describe() feeds both the preview and the CLI log, and its ASCII 'x' plus the factors equal to 1 are pinned by tests/test_grid.py:359 and tests/test_api_grid.py:278. design-notes 'Grid preview and the per-step estimate': the preview's count, axes and error text are the server's own. CLAUDE.md Frontend: primary buttons use aria-disabled, and smoke-analysis checks els.gridRun's aria-disabled.
findings.rule_tension: No conflict. The fold stays closed by default. The 'x 1 mu' trimming and the switch to x-multiply signs (×) happen client-side only, so grid.describe and its tests and the CLI's ASCII log stay as they are. The preview still shows the server's own numbers. The sticky fix carries out the stated purpose of style.css:70-73 ('everything reachable') by measuring the panel, where the 900px media query only guesses; that query still makes the panel static at the smokes' 1400x900. Renaming the summary's em is taste. 'Sweeps and comparisons' would also be read as the prompt check's Compare, which lives in analysis.js and not in this fold, so I dropped that part.
findings.smokes_affected:
None should break, but these steps read the elements the fix touches: tools/smoke.json:154 expects #grid-preview to keep class 'warn' and to have '2 would be identical' in its textContent (keep the class on the

and the text in its subtree). tools/smoke-conditioning.json:66 expects els.gridPreview.textContent to include '3 images' and 'LoRA 0, 0.5, 1'; the trim must not touch line 2 or a LoRA factor greater than 1. tools/smoke-analysis.json:56 and :265 check els.gridRun's aria-disabled, which a width change does not affect. No smoke reads 'overnight', the ' x ' separators or .panel's position. All smokes run at 1400x900, where @media (max-height: 900px) keeps the panel static, so the JS top only takes effect above that height.
findings.how_checked: Fresh fake on 7914 (krea/Krea-2-Turbo, so the Mu axis is live), driven with shot.mjs at 2560x1305 DPR 1 and 2048x1040 DPR 1.25. I rendered two direct images so the preview carries a time estimate, opened the fold, then measured with getBoundingClientRect/getComputedStyle three states: empty axes, a 3-value CFG check, and the 648-image spec (steps 4-38x2, CFG 0-4x0.5, 4 seeds). Then I planted 120 more images, scrolled the gallery and focused Run grid to see whether the readouts can be seen at all. Last, I prototyped the fix by injecting a <style> and a ResizeObserver at run time (nothing in the repo changed) and measured again. The server is stopped.
findings.verifier_notes: The finding's numbers reproduce: 77x43 vs 296x43, 11px muted preview, 4 lines for 648 images, and 'x 1 mu' padding. Its time of '11 min' was real-card timing; the fake says 2 min. Changes to the recommendation: (a) the 77px width is not a design choice but a side effect of ::details-content making the fold's content block flow, and the same cause zeroes the intended 10px gap between rows. (b) The proposed `filter(f => !/^1 /.test(f))` also drops '1 seed'/'1 listed seed' and leaves an empty string for a 1-image grid, so it needs a fallback and should spare seeds. (c) Rename dropped: 'comparisons' collides with the prompt check's Compare, and the 'overnight' framing is documented intent. (d) The bigger cost at QHD is that the preview and Run grid cannot be seen: opening the fold breaks the style.css:70-73 assumption that the sticky panel fits in a viewport taller than 900px. That is why severity goes from low to medium. If another cluster in this review covers the sticky panel overflowing the viewport, treat point (4) as part of it and keep this one low. Contrast is fine (about 5.5:1). Server on 7914 stopped; scratch files in scratchpad/ux/verify-grid-3.

sources.surface: Grid fold: summary, preview, Run grid
sources.observation: Run grid is 77x43 px against Generate's 296x43. The preview, the one place that says what a night will do, is 11 px #8b8b9a. At 296 px it wraps a 648-image spec into 4 lines ('648 images · 18 steps x 9 CFG x 1 mu x 4 seeds · about 11 min · ~6.1 MB' then three lines of steps values). The summary pads with single-value factors ('x 1 mu', 'x 1 steps'). The fold's own summary is 12 px uppercase #8b8b9a at the panel's bottom, labelled 'overnight sweeps', although a 3-value CFG check takes seconds.
sources.why_it_matters: The count, time and disk totals are what decide whether to start a run. Rendering them as the faintest text in the panel, beside a button a quarter the width of Generate, makes the grid look secondary and the totals easy to misread.

findings.title: A new user's first Generate on the gated default checkpoint fails with a raw 6-line GatedRepoError: no link, no steps, and the retry button is 2,368 px away
surfaces: Panel #error slot, empty viewer and topbar after a failed first load (FLUX.1 Krea [dev] gated 403)
findings.recommendation: (1) Server: in main.ensure_loaded's except (main.py:100-106), map the exception by class name over its MRO, as prompt_encoding._reason already does for tokenizers (prompt_encoding.py:1144-1160): GatedRepoError, RepositoryNotFoundError, LocalEntryNotFoundError, OfflineModeIsEnabled. For a gate, set detail to ' is gated on Hugging Face. Accept its terms on the model page (FLUX.1 Krea [dev] is click-through), run `uv run hf auth login` once with a read token, then press Retry load.' Take the gate kind from launch.CHECKPOINTS[*].gate where the repo matches. Add `detail_url = https://huggingface.co/` and `detail_kind = 'gated'` to ModelStatus. Keep short_error(exc) in the log line. The Check panel already says 'the tokenizer's repo is gated - accept its terms on huggingface.co and log in', so this also makes the two failures read alike. (2) Page: while s.state === 'error', fill the viewer placeholder (index.html:416-418) with a card: the heading 'Couldn't load ', the detail, an Open the model page link, and a primary 'Retry load' button that calls els.load.onclick. While in error, set the topbar button's text and title to 'Retry load'. (3) Call refreshStatus() in streamJob's 'done' branch (generation.js:445-449). The Load handler already calls it (app.js:196), so the original finding's 'and after the Load POST' is not needed. (4) In announceLastRun (panel.js:168-194), skip the banner when the job ended at the load (status 'error', image_count 0, error equal to the current status detail). Otherwise a reload shows the same gated text twice.
findings.documented_rule: CLAUDE.md Model and loader: 'Loading happens only in main.ensure_loaded() under its asyncio lock'. design-notes 'Loading happens in one place'. index.html:17-19 comment: the Load button exists to start or retry a load (after a gated-repo 403) without queueing an image. main.py:101 comment: 'A gated-repo 403 is user-actionable, not a crash'.
findings.rule_tension: No conflict. Only the detail text changes inside ensure_loaded's existing except; the load stays in one place. The card's Retry calls the existing Load handler (app.js:189), so retry still goes through POST /api/model/load and never queues an image. #error stays role=alert and keeps the unhide-first order. short_error's full text stays in the log line.
findings.smokes_affected: None. No smoke reaches state 'error': every fake starts loaded, and fake_server.py has no load-failure switch. grep finds no step on btn-load, 'load failed', 'Load the weights now' or the viewer placeholder text. A smoke for the card would need a --fail-load flag added to tools/fake_server.py.
findings.how_checked: Own scratch wrapper around tools/fake_server.py (vserver.py, patched in memory, repo untouched) on port 7971, started unloaded, with load() raising a GatedRepoError built the way huggingface_hub 1.29 builds it: the Request ID first line, which short_error drops. Fresh profile, typed a prompt, pressed Generate, sampled the page every 500 ms. Ran at 2560x1305@1 and at 2048x1040@1.25. Then cleared the flag and pressed Load. Read main.py:82-108, jobs.py:35-54, status.js:118-231, app.js:189-197, prompt_encoding.py:1141-1160 and the huggingface_hub source.
findings.verifier_notes: Reproduced, with three corrections. (a) The real text does not start with '403 Client Error.'. huggingface_hub puts the Request ID on that first line, and short_error drops any line containing 'Request ID', so the user sees 'GatedRepoError: Cannot access gated repo for url …/resolve/main/model_index.json. Access to model … is restricted. You must have access to it and be authenticated to access it. Please log in.' (278 chars). (b) The words do name the cause (gated, needs access, log in), and the start-up menu labels FLUX.1 Krea [dev] 'click-through gate' (launch.py:407). The page lacks the steps and a link, but the remedy is not only in the README. When the user is logged in but has not accepted the terms, HF's server message (not reproducible offline) should include 'Visit https://huggingface.co/<id> to ask for access' as plain text. (c) New: after a reload, the last-run banner repeats the same error, 178 px tall, so the gated text appears twice. Severity lowered to medium: it happens once per install and per gated checkpoint, the text names the cause, and Load recovers. It is still the likeliest first failure on the default checkpoint.

sources.surface: Panel #error slot, empty viewer and topbar after a failed first load (FLUX.1 Krea [dev] gated 403)
sources.observation: Generate on a fresh page with the gated 403 injected. Load took 4 s, then #error appeared at (35,1003), 296x108 px: 12 px red, 296 characters, 6 lines. It reads 'GatedRepoError: 403 Client Error. Cannot access gated repo for url https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-Krea-dev/resolve/main/model_index.json. Access to model ... is restricted. You must have access to it and be authenticated to access it. Please log in.' The URL points at model_index.json, not the model page that has the Agree button. It is plain text, not a link. The message never mentions `uv run hf auth login` (README.md:45-47), never says this gate is click-through, and never says to press Load afterwards. The 2,176x380 viewer still says 'Generated images appear here.' The topbar shows 13 px grey 'load failed' with a small red dot, and a ghost 'Load' button at x=2403 titled 'Load the weights now' (not 'Retry'); that is 2,368 px from the message. The topbar lags the panel by up to 3 s in both directions. For 3 s after the failure it still said 'loading weights…' (f1-03-failed.png). During a retry it said 'load failed' while the panel said 'loading weights…'. At 2048x1040@1.25 the message spans y 1003-1111, so only its first two lines are above the 1040 fold ('GatedRepoError: 403 Client Error. Cannot access gated repo for url https://huggingface.co/black-forest-'), and the 'you must have access… log in' half is hidden. Recovery does work once access exists: removing the flag, pressing Load, and the state was ready 4.6 s later; Generate then made an image. Pressing Generate again also retries the load, but nothing says that.
sources.why_it_matters: FLUX.1 Krea [dev] is the default checkpoint and is gated, so this is the likeliest first thing a new user sees. The remedy (accept the terms on the model page, log in with a read token, retry) exists only in the README. The page offers an HTTP status, a JSON file URL and a button labelled for something else. At 125% scaling the actionable half is not even on screen.

findings.title: The load-failure text is re-posted every 3 s, overwriting any other message, and follows the user into the lightbox
surfaces: Shared #error slot and lightbox #lb-error while the status is 'error'
findings.recommendation: In refreshStatus, keep `let shownLoadDetail = null`. Call showError(s.detail, false, { mirror: false }) only when s.state === 'error' and s.detail !== shownLoadDetail, and reset shownLoadDetail when the state leaves 'error'. Extend showError(message, note = false, { mirror = true } = {}) so only user-action messages reach #lb-error. Better still, give the load failure the persistent viewer card proposed in G1.1, so #error stays free for the action the user just took. Leave the topbar 'load failed' as the ambient signal.
findings.documented_rule: No CLAUDE.md rule. In the code, state.js:318-329: showError unhides before writing because the slot is role=alert, and mirrors into #lb-error while the lightbox is open because the lightbox covers the panel's slot.
findings.rule_tension: Compatible. Post the load detail only when it changes, and pass a no-mirror option from status.js. User-caused messages still mirror into the lightbox: smoke-conditioning.json:54 depends on the lightbox Refine's 'no refine pass' reason reaching #lb-error.
findings.smokes_affected: smoke-conditioning.json:54 (expects #lb-error to show the lightbox Refine's 'no refine pass' reason; the mirror must stay the default for user-action messages). No smoke covers the status-driven re-post.
findings.how_checked: Same gated-failure session on 7971 at QHD and at 2048@1.25. With the status in 'error', pressed Check, then Generate with an empty prompt, then ticked All models and opened another checkpoint's (Krea-2-Turbo) planted image in the lightbox, sampling #error and #lb-error every 500 ms. Read status.js:219 and state.js:318-329.
findings.verifier_notes: Reproduced as stated. With 53 showError call sites sharing one slot, any message lasts at most until the next 3 s poll while a load has failed. Not measured: whether a screen reader re-announces identical text on each re-post. Rewriting a role=alert node's text usually does, but that was not tested. The fix overlaps G1.1 (the persistent card) and is independent of it.

sources.surface: Shared #error slot and lightbox #lb-error while the status is 'error'
sources.observation: status.js:219 calls showError(s.detail) on every 3 s poll while state === 'error'. Measured: a successful Check cleared the slot, and the 403 was back 3.3 s later. Generate with an empty prompt showed 'Enter a prompt first.' (18 px tall), and the 108 px 403 replaced it within 3.3 s. Ticking All models and opening another checkpoint's image in the lightbox put the whole 6-line 403 in red into the lightbox's own error slot, under that image's facts, every poll (f1-06-lightbox.png; lb.hidden false). Nothing dismisses it until a load is retried.
sources.why_it_matters: While a load has failed, every other message the page has (validation, a failed delete, a check's notes) survives at most 3 s. The user browsing old images, unrelated to the load, gets an alarm in the lightbox. The slot is role=alert, so a screen reader re-announces 296 characters on each re-post.

findings.title: The per-image confirm can't tell apart the images a slip would confuse: all 9 cells of a steps×CFG grid read the same, and so do a source and its pass
surfaces: Card ⌦ and lightbox Delete confirm()
findings.recommendation:
Factor the settings line out of renderLightbox (lightbox.js:99-113) into settingsLine(rec), and use it in both the lightbox and confirmDelete (gallery.js:224): `Delete image ${rec.id}${rec.favorite ? ' (starred)' : ''}?

${settingsLine(rec)}
"${snippet}"

The PNG is deleted from disk, not moved to the Recycle Bin.` The line then carries size, steps, CFG, mu, LoRA, references, 'refine of N @ s', seed and any variables (k=v). Teapot cells then read '20 steps, CFG 2.5' against '36 steps, CFG 4.5', and source and pass read 1024×1024 against 1536×1536 with 'refine of 63 @ 0.1'.
findings.documented_rule: web/gallery.js:222-223 comment: 'on a card the button sits a few pixels from the star. Say which image, so a slip is caught here.' CLAUDE.md says nothing about the confirm's content.
findings.rule_tension: None. The fix keeps the native confirm and the favourite flag, and only adds identifying fields. It serves the comment's purpose better.
findings.smokes_affected: None. No smoke stubs window.confirm or reads the per-image confirm (grep -c confirm is 0 in every tools/smoke*.json). smoke-refine.json:55 reads the lightbox's settings text ('refine of ' + source + ' @ 0.1'), which a shared settingsLine must keep word for word.
findings.how_checked: Same seeded gallery. I stubbed window.confirm to record its message and refuse, clicked the card ⌦ of teapot cells 64, 67, 70 and 72 (they differ in steps and CFG), source 63, pass 78 and fox cells 73 and 74, and logged each text. I also read the buttons' title and aria-label.
findings.verifier_notes: Real as described. I lowered high to medium: the comment's own purpose (catching a star-for-delete slip) is served by any confirm at all. The missing identity matters when the wrong image is under the pointer or in view, which is G2.3's reflow and G2.5's boundary step, so this compounds those rather than standing alone as a core-flow blocker. Cheap, and high value alongside G2.3 and G2.5.

sources.surface: Card ⌦ and lightbox Delete confirm()
sources.observation:
Deleting cells 68, 71 and 74 of the 3×3 teapot grid produced three identical confirms: 'Delete this image (seed 300)?

"a teapot on a windowsill, morning light"

The file is removed from disk.' The cells differ only in steps and CFG, which the text leaves out. Source 67 (1024×1024) and its pass 82 (1536×1536, strength 0.1) both confirm as 'Delete this image (seed 400)? "portrait of an old fisherman…"'. Neighbours in a batch differ by one digit (seed 9100 vs 9101). In the lightbox a delete takes two keystrokes, Del and then Enter on the native OK. The buttons themselves say only 'Delete' (card title) and 'Delete (Del)' (lightbox title).
sources.why_it_matters: gallery.js:222-223 says the confirm exists so that 'a slip is caught here'. In a sweep, where every image looks alike, it carries nothing that identifies the image, so it can't catch the slip, and the PNG is deleted from disk with no trash or undo.

findings.title: A card delete reflows the page under the pointer: another card's ⌦ lands under the cursor, focus drops to <body>, and the viewer is left as a bare 380 px box
surfaces: Gallery grid and viewer after a card ⌦
findings.recommendation:
In forgetImages (gallery.js:244), for a single-id card delete: replace the `.card[data-id]` contents with `
Deleted · seed N
`, remove its data-id, and add `.card.gone { pointer-events: none; opacity: .35 }`, so the grid keeps the slot and nothing slides under the cursor. For a viewer tile, freeze its width and height from getBoundingClientRect before emptying it, so the viewer doesn't collapse from 917 to 380 px and the gallery doesn't jump 537 px. When viewerRecords becomes empty, re-append `

Generated images appear here.

`. If the removed element held focus, focus the next card's img (else the previous) once the DELETE resolves. Leave cellNote alone: 'Finished 1 image' is still a true statement about the run.
findings.documented_rule: design-notes 'Delete unstarred' > 'The page forgets by id': forgetImages drops the ids from every list and element in one pass. CLAUDE.md: '`forgetImages` is the one place the page drops deleted ids.' Viewer min-height 380px (style.css .viewer). clearResults removes the placeholder.
findings.rule_tension: Compatible. Tombstones are made inside forgetImages, so it stays the one place deleted ids are dropped. The records still leave galleryRecords, viewerRecords and lbList, and `total` and paging by id are unaffected because a tombstone is DOM-only with no data-id. Delete unstarred already calls resetGallery(), which empties #gallery and so clears tombstones.
findings.smokes_affected: No smoke clicks a card ⌦ or deletes a viewer tile. smoke.json:177-181 runs forgetImages through Delunstarred and then expects `document.querySelectorAll('.card').length === window.__k`. That still holds because resetGallery empties #gallery after the sweep. If tombstones are added for bulk deletes too, keep them out of `.card` (use a .tomb class) or apply them only on the single-id path.
findings.how_checked: On 7972 at --step 0.3 with steps set to 4, I generated one image with a real Generate click and measured the layout. I hovered and real-clicked the ⌦ of the new image's card at (528,1257) with confirm stubbed true, then measured again and read document.elementFromPoint at the pointer. I repeated this with a 4-image batch, real-clicking the second card's ⌦ at (709,814). For the keyboard path I focused a card's ⌦, activated it and read document.activeElement.
findings.verifier_notes: Reproduced with the same coordinates the reviewer reported. Where a ⌦ lands after the single-image collapse depends on the shift: 537 px is about 3 card pitches of 181 px. In the batch case it is systematic, since the next card always slides into the slot. The confirm is the only stop, and G2.2 shows it can't tell neighbours apart, so this and G2.2 together are the slip path. M45 (moving ⌦ away from ☆) is complementary.

sources.surface: Gallery grid and viewer after a card ⌦
sources.observation: Real click on the ⌦ (514,1245, 29×24) of the card for the image shown alone in the viewer. The viewer shrank from 917 to 380 px and the gallery rose 537 px. The pointer at (529,1257) then sat on the 37th card, with its tool row revealed and its ⌦ highlighted (a03). Deleting tile 2 of a 4-image batch from its card slid the next card into the slot, again with its ⌦ highlighted under the pointer (a05). document.activeElement was BODY after each delete, including the keyboard path (focus the ⌦, activate). The viewer after the single delete held no img and no text: the 'Generated images appear here.' placeholder had been removed by clearResults, the box stayed 380 px tall, and 'Finished 1 image in 0s.' stayed under Generate (a03, b05). On the card, ☆ and ⌦ are 4 px apart (centres 31 px) and one Tab stop apart (f01).
sources.why_it_matters: In quick triage (click ⌦, Enter, click ⌦) the second click lands on a different image from the one aimed at, and the confirm (finding 2) is the only stop. Keyboard users lose their place in a grid of 80+ cards, and the empty viewer gives no sign of what happened.

findings.title: Deleting the last loaded image in the lightbox steps back to an image already seen, although more are on the server
surfaces: Lightbox walking the gallery strip
findings.recommendation: In forgetImages (gallery.js:267): `if (!lbList.length && !canPage()) closeLightbox(); else if (lbIndex >= lbList.length && canPage()) { loadGallery().catch(() => {}).then(() => { if (!els.lightbox.open) return; lbIndex = Math.min(lbIndex, lbList.length - 1); if (lbIndex >= 0) renderLightbox(); else closeLightbox(); }); } else { lbIndex = Math.min(lbIndex, lbList.length - 1); renderLightbox(); }` Without the catch and clamp, renderLightbox's `if (!rec) closeLightbox()` would close the viewer on a failed page. While the page loads, set els.lbImg.src to '' or show 'Loading next…' so the deleted image is not left on screen with a live Delete button.
findings.documented_rule: web/gallery.js:265-268 comment: 'The strip has closed up under the viewer: the next image already sits at this index, unless this was the last one.' lightbox.js stepLightbox guard (lightbox.js:142-149). design-notes 'Paging by id'.
findings.rule_tension: None. Paging in from forgetImages uses the same serialised loadGallery. loadGallery's own .finally already calls renderLightbox() while the lightbox is open (gallery.js:73), so after the page lands lbIndex (still == old length) points at the next unseen image.
findings.smokes_affected: None. No smoke deletes from the lightbox. smoke-paging.json covers scroll paging, which is unchanged.
findings.how_checked: At 76 images the QHD page auto-loaded everything (galleryMore false), so I added 120 more through the API (192 in all). A fresh page then held 96 loaded, with galleryMore true. I opened the lightbox on the last loaded card (96/96) with confirm stubbed true, pressed Delete twice and then ArrowRight, logging id, index, length and count each time. I also deleted in mid-strip (card 20) for comparison.
findings.verifier_notes: Reproduced. The reviewer's '48/48' was their gallery's figure; on the QHD target the first boundary is 96 and later ones every 48, which leaves the finding intact. Medium because it recurs at every page boundary of a delete-heavy triage pass. When it hits, it shows an already-judged image whose confirm names only a seed (G2.2).

sources.surface: Lightbox walking the gallery strip
sources.observation: 48 of 87 loaded (galleryMore true). Lightbox at 48/48 on id 42, then Delete: it showed id 43 at '47/47', the image before, which had already been judged. Only ArrowRight paged in more and reached id 41 at '48/86'. In the middle of the strip a delete moves forward instead (20/82 → 20/81 showed the next image, then 20/80, 20/79), so the direction flips at each 48-image page boundary.
sources.why_it_matters: A forward triage pass (Del, Enter, Del, Enter) reaches a page boundary every 48 images. There the next Delete targets an image the user had already decided to keep, and the confirm only names its seed.

findings.title: A klein user cannot bring in their own photo or sketch, yet klein's Examples menu offers the edit prompt 'Turn this cat into a dog' and the check calls it fine
surfaces: Reference images field, Examples menu, prompt check (klein)
findings.recommendation: Split this into a quick fix now and a planned feature. (A) Quick fix, S. 1) In prompt_rules._references, when the count is 0 and the profile supports references, add a heuristic info finding (no cite) for an edit imperative aimed at an existing picture, e.g. /^\s*(turn|change|make|replace|remove|put|give)\b.*\b(this|these|the (photo|image|picture)|image \d)\b/i. Message: 'This reads as an edit of an existing picture, but no reference image is attached - it will render from the prompt alone. Add one with the ❐ button on a gallery image.' 2) In showExamples (app.js:20-55), when referenceSupported and referenceIds is empty, append a muted ' - needs a reference image' span to an example the same regex matches. The example text stays verbatim, so the guide data is untouched. 3) Add document-level dragover/drop handlers that call preventDefault when event.dataTransfer.types includes 'Files', so a stray file drop can no longer leave the page. (B) Planned feature, L. Add POST /api/images/import. python-multipart is already a dependency (pyproject.toml:18), so UploadFile works. Accept PNG/JPEG/WebP under a size cap and store the file as a row with source='import' (a _migrate entry, the row going through _insert_row) plus a local-diffusion chunk carrying that marker, so reindex keeps it. Exclude source='import' rows from rerender, completed_cells, the duplicate count and keep_rates, and let _model_scope admit them on every checkpoint. On the page, add a '+ Add image…' button after the chips (<input type=file accept='image/*'>) and accept a drop or paste on #reference-field. The response's id goes through setReferences([...referenceIds, id]). The same route would also give Refine an entry point for outside images, since its source is a gallery id too.
findings.documented_rule: CLAUDE.md, Reproduction: 'Reference images are gallery ids, never paths' (storage.reference_paths is the only resolver). design-notes 'Reference images, by gallery id': a dropped reference 'renders a plain text-to-image that looks like a success'. design-notes:2992: a single klein reference with no 'image 1' is deliberately not checked, because BFL's own 'Turn this cat into a dog' names none. The reference tip scopes the feature to 'one you have already made'. No document decides against importing images; that is simply unbuilt.
findings.rule_tension: An import has to create a gallery row and hand back an id, never a path. Such a row has none of the reproduction set (prompt, steps, CFG, seed, checkpoint, hash), so it must be kept out of Re-render, resume (storage.completed_cells), the duplicate count, keep_rates/stats and run_id. The gallery is scoped by settings.model_id (main._model_scope), so an import needs a scope that every checkpoint admits. The new column needs a _migrate entry and must go through _insert_row/_COLUMNS. reindex rebuilds rows from the local-diffusion PNG chunk, so the import must write a chunk marked as an import or it is lost on a rebuild. A zero-reference rule finding has no author sentence behind it, so it must be labelled heuristic with no cite. The authors'-examples test (tests/test_prompt_rules.py:220) forbids only severity 'warn', so an 'info' finding is allowed.
findings.smokes_affected: None asserts the examples or a zero-reference klein check. Rerun smoke-conditioning.json:93-110: its reference-check steps run with references attached ('Put the jacket from image 1…', 'a fox in the snow'), and the new regex must not fire on them. If (B) lands, add a step: import, see a chip, see the id in collect().reference.
findings.how_checked: klein fake on 7973 (fresh), 2560x1305 DPR 1. Opened Examples with a real click and picked 'Turn this cat into a dog' with no references, then pressed Check. Logged document/body/field ondrop and onpaste. Grepped web/*.js for drop/paste/dragover listeners and backend/main.py for POST routes and UploadFile. Read prompt_rules._references, the design note at docs/design-notes.md:2992 and pyproject.toml. I did not reproduce the claim that a file drop navigates the page away, because the driver cannot drop a real file.
findings.verifier_notes: The problem is real, but 'high' overstates it. References were designed and labelled as conditioning on images already in the gallery, and the edit-example mismatch costs one render, not lost work. The original recommendation's reason for avoiding multipart is moot, because the dependency is already installed. It also understated how far an imported row reaches: re-render, resume, stats, scope and reindex all read rows as reproduction sets. The quick fix (A) addresses the misleading half today and leaves the documented single-reference exemption alone.

sources.surface: Reference images field, Examples menu, prompt check (klein)
sources.observation: References can come only from this app's own gallery. There is no upload or import route (backend/main.py has no UploadFile or multipart handler and no POST route that takes a file), and web/ has no drop or paste handler (grep for dragover/ondrop/paste: none; document.ondrop === null). The only way to add a reference is the card's ❐ tool. On the klein fake, Examples lists 'Turn this cat into a dog' (backend/guides.py:198). Picking it with no reference gave prompt 'Turn this cat into a dog', refs [], and the note '(add one with the ❐ button on a gallery image)'. Check then said '6 words, prose · no warnings · 1 note'; the only note was the word count. prompt_rules._references returns early when count < 2 (prompt_rules.py:1606-1607), so a zero-reference edit prompt raises nothing. The edit example therefore runs as a plain text-to-image, which design-notes 'Reference images, by gallery id' calls 'a plain text-to-image that looks like a success'. Code-read, not run: with no drop handler, Chromium's default for a file dropped on the page is to navigate to it, which leaves the app.
sources.why_it_matters: klein is the catalogue's only reference-conditioning checkpoint, and editing an outside photo is its headline use. A user who wants to edit a real photo or a sketch has no way in, and nothing on the page says so. The Examples menu and the check both suggest editing works, so the user spends a render and gets an unrelated image.

findings.title: Chips carry no number, though the prompt, the guide and the check all name references as 'image 1, image 2, image 3'; order can't be changed
surfaces: Reference images chips (#reference-list)
findings.recommendation: In renderReferences (sizes.js:199-222): 1) Number each chip with a ${i+1} badge at bottom-left (12px/600, rgba(0,0,0,.7), padding 1px 5px). Set img.alt = `Reference image ${i+1} (gallery #${id})` and chip.title to the same text. Change the × aria-label to `Remove reference image ${i+1}`. 2) Make chips draggable=true with dragstart/dragover/drop handlers that splice a copy of referenceIds and call setReferences(). Add Alt+ArrowLeft/Right and Delete on the focused ×, mirroring tags.js:402-425. 3) After a ×, focus the next chip's ×, else the previous one's, else the field's ? badge. 4) Grow chips to 66px (4x66 + 3x6 gap = 282 px, which fits the measured 296 px list). The original 80px is 338 px and would wrap at the current 330 px panel. Linking the 'image 3' in a finding to its chip is optional polish.
findings.documented_rule: sizes.js:196-198 and CLAUDE.md: chips are rendered from referenceIds, and setReferences() is the one writer (it persists, reschedules the preview and marks the check stale). The tag chips are the precedent for reordering: design-notes 'Those chips are a round-trip editor' (HTML drag/drop plus Alt+Left/Right, × or Delete). The 4-reference cap is gallery.js:118.
findings.rule_tension: Reordering must build a new array and go through setReferences(), never move DOM nodes, so persistence, the preview and the 'references changed since' stale badge all follow. The tag chips already do exactly this through writePromptTags, so copying their handlers (tags.js:402-425) keeps one interaction model. Ids stay ids.
findings.smokes_affected: smoke-conditioning.json:36 counts '#reference-list .chip' (still fine). Lines :40 (document.querySelector('#reference-list .chip button')) and :100 ([...'#reference-list .chip button'].pop()) select the × as the chip's only button. Keep the badge a non-button <b>, or give the × a class and update both selectors. The stale-badge steps at :95-110 should be rerun after the reorder lands.
findings.how_checked: klein fake on 7973, 2560x1305. Added references with real clicks on cards' ❐ and measured the chips. Dragged chip 1 onto chip 3 with real mouse events and pressed Alt+ArrowRight on the focused ×, then logged referenceIds each time. Removed a chip with a real × click and logged document.activeElement. Ran Check with 3 references on a prompt that names only images 1 and 2.
findings.verifier_notes: Every measurement in the original reproduces. I lowered severity from high to medium for two reasons. Only klein sessions with two or more references are affected, so 'every-session' is too broad. And the chips do sit in a left-to-right row in reference order, so a careful user can work out the numbers. The real costs are that the order cannot be changed without removing and re-adding images, that nothing ties 'image 3' to a chip, and that focus is lost after removing one. I corrected the chip-size arithmetic: 80px chips do not fit the current panel.

sources.surface: Reference images chips (#reference-list)
sources.observation: Each chip is a 52x52 px cover-cropped 384 px thumbnail with an 18x18 × in its corner. It shows no number, no id and no tooltip: chip.title is '', img.title is '', img alt is '' (empty). Only the ×'s title says 'Remove image 8'. Four chips take 52 px each of the 296 px field, so 0.08% of the 2560x1305 screen apiece. Images from one prompt look alike at that size (k05-field-4.png: two of four chips are indistinguishable). klein's guide asks to 'say how each is used - the jacket from image 1', and the check reported '3 reference images are attached, but the prompt never says what to take from image 3.', yet nothing marks which chip is image 3. Reorder: dragging chip 1 onto chip 3 left referenceIds unchanged [8,10,3]; chips are not draggable and have no key binding. The only way to reorder is to × everything and re-add in order from the gallery. After × removes a chip, focus falls to <body>.
sources.why_it_matters: On klein the order of the chips is the meaning of 'image 1' and 'image 2' in the prompt. If the user can't see which chip is which number, or fix the order, the jacket is taken from the wrong image. That is wrong output that still looks like a success, and it costs a render each time. The rule finding points at a number the page never shows.

findings.title: The contact sheet has no references axis, so a with/without-reference comparison collapses to one cell that reads '1 of 3 loaded'
surfaces: Contact sheet (#sheet) over a klein search
findings.recommendation: 1) Add { key: 'ref', label: 'References', of: (r) => r.reference?.length ? r.reference.map((id) => '#' + id).join(' + ') : null } after 'lora' in SHEET_AXES (sheet.js:27). Optionally add { key: 'adapter', label: 'Adapter', of: (r) => r.lora ? r.lora.replace(/\.safetensors$/, '') : null }. 2) In renderSheet, count records that pass the pins but find their cell taken (`cellOf.has(at)`). When the count is above zero, replace 'loaded' wording with `${shown.length} of ${sheetRecords.length} shown - ${hidden} share a cell with another image and differ in something the sheet does not lay out (size, checkpoint, references…)`. This second part is the more valuable fix, because it covers every collapse, not only references.
findings.documented_rule: CLAUDE.md: the sheet's layout contract lives in the client and the export draws sheetLayout. In sheet.js, the first record wins a cell (:353-354). Size is deliberately not a sheet axis (:373-375). The LoRA and Strength axes return null where they do not apply, 'so a mixed search does not invent an axis' (:24-29). The listlike rule and VARIANT_AXIS placement apply too.
findings.rule_tension: A references axis is compatible if it follows the existing null convention. Return null for no references rather than the string 'none'; valueText already prints null as 'none'. An all-null axis has one value and is ignored, so non-klein sheets are unchanged. I checked the listlike rule: with three records and three reference values, the axis is the only varying one, so it survives as the column axis. Size stays off the axes by design, so for size, checkpoint and quantization the collision note is the compatible fix.
findings.smokes_affected: smoke.json:97 and :102 and smoke-analysis.json:319 assert the exact note 'N of N loaded'. These are unchanged when there are no collisions, but rerun them. smoke-conditioning.json:75 checks only the axis key 'lora'.
findings.how_checked: Generated 'a husky in a red scarf sitting in snow' at seed 77 three times on klein (no reference, [8], [8,10]), searched 'husky' and opened the Sheet, then logged sheetRecords, sheetLayout, filled cells and the note. To test whether the collapse goes beyond references, I also generated 'a teapot on a wooden table' at seed 9 at 1024x1024 and at 768x1344 and opened its sheet.
findings.verifier_notes: Reproduced. I changed 'none' to null to match the existing axis convention, and checked that the axis survives the listlike rule. The collision note matters beyond klein: any search mixing sizes (deliberately not an axis) loses images under a 'loaded' count that implies they are still arriving. 'Common' is overstated for the references case, but the general collapse keeps this at medium.

sources.surface: Contact sheet (#sheet) over a klein search
sources.observation: Same prompt ('a husky in a red scarf sitting in snow') and seed 77, rendered with no reference, with [12], and with [12,11]. A search 'husky' with Sheet gave sheetRecords 3 but cells 1. Columns '—', Rows '—', note '1 of 3 loaded'. Two of the three images are not shown, and 'loaded' suggests they are still arriving. SHEET_AXES has no entry for `reference` (nor for the adapter name: the LoRA axis reads `lora_scale` only), and renderSheet keeps 'first record wins a cell'. The grid has no reference axis either, so these comparisons can only be made as separate runs, which is exactly the case this sheet then collapses.
sources.why_it_matters: 'Did the reference help, and which one?' is the core klein evaluation, and the sheet is the app's comparison tool. Here it hides two of three images and gives a misleading count, so the user concludes the runs were identical or lost.

findings.title: A result says which references made it only as 'ref 8+4' in a 12 px run-on line; the gallery never shows ids
surfaces: Lightbox settings line; viewer after a referenced Generate
findings.recommendation: As proposed. When rec.reference?.length, add a .lb-refs block in #lb-meta under the settings line: a 'References' caption, then one 64 px cover thumb per id (/api/images/${id}/thumb) labelled 'image 1', 'image 2' to match G3.2's chip numbers. Each thumb is a button that opens that record via GET /api/images/{id}, with a 'deleted' placeholder from img.onerror. Add a ghost 'Use these references' button that calls setReferences(rec.reference) only, and only when referenceSupported (aria-disabled with the reason otherwise). Keep the 'ref 8+4' text in the line until smoke-conditioning.json:50 is changed to assert the block (e.g. document.querySelectorAll('.lb-refs img').length === 1).
findings.documented_rule: lightbox.js:96-113 builds one run-on settings line; references appear only when present ('ref 8+4'). References are gallery ids, resolved through /api/images/{id} and /thumb, never paths.
findings.rule_tension: None beyond the id rule, which the thumbs respect. The smoke (smoke-conditioning.json:50) asserts lbMeta includes 'ref ', so either keep that fragment or update the smoke when the block replaces it.
findings.smokes_affected: smoke-conditioning.json:50 expects els.lbMeta.textContent.includes('ref '). Note that 'References' does not contain 'ref ', so dropping the fragment fails it.
findings.how_checked: Generated with references [8,4] by a real Generate click, looked at the viewer, opened the result's lightbox with a real click, and measured lbSettings and .lb-side. Logged card alt, aria-label and title, and chip titles.
findings.verifier_notes: Reproduced as stated. This is not a duplicate of G3.2: that cluster fixes the chips in the panel, and this one is the lineage view of a finished image.

sources.surface: Lightbox settings line; viewer after a referenced Generate
sources.observation: After rendering with references [8,4], the viewer showed the 887x887 result with no mention of references (only 'Finished 1 image in 0s.'). The lightbox side line reads 'FLUX.2-klein-4B, 1024×1024, 4 steps, CFG 1, no mu, ref 8+4, seed 8929931418676791, 0.0s' at 12 px in a 280 px column. Gallery cards show no ids (alt and aria-label are the prompt), chips show no ids, so '8' and '4' can't be matched to any picture on the page. Nothing in the lightbox opens a reference or puts just the references back in the panel. Reuse settings restores them, but it also overwrites prompt, seed, steps and size.
sources.why_it_matters: Judging a klein edit means looking at the inputs beside the output. With bare ids the user has to remember which gallery images they picked or reconstruct it by trial. Iterating on the same references with a new prompt forces a Reuse that clobbers the panel.

findings.title: A tag added at the end of the Refine prompt lands past SDXL's 77-token cut and does nothing, and the dialog never says so
surfaces: Refine dialog > Prompt and sampling > Prompt textarea (SDXL tag checkpoints: Animagine, Kohaku, Illustrious, WAI)
findings.recommendation:
In refine.js, add refineCheckTimer and refineCheckEpoch. Run checkRefinePrompt() 0 ms after openRefine and 400 ms after input on refinePrompt or refineNegative. It POSTs refineRequest().body to /api/prompt/analyze and drops stale replies by epoch. Render into a new

placed just above #refine-preview (outside the fold), so the line is visible with the fold closed. For each encoder with a non-null cut on field 'prompt' or 'negative_prompt', write e.g. 'CLIP-L/CLIP-G read 22 of 42 tags (75 of 132 tokens); the rest - from "outstretched arm" - is never read.' Add a ghost tiny 'Show' button. It opens the fold and selects from the cut to the end of els.refinePrompt, converting the server's code-point offsets with units(). Also list rule findings that carry a whole-field suggestion, each with an Apply that calls replaceBoxText(els.refinePrompt, f.suggestion). Its input event already runs refineChanged(). This covers G4.3. Show 'checking…' while a first-use tokenizer load is pending (up to LOAD_WAIT 30 s) and never block Refine. Wrong output on SDXL is silent, which justifies the effort. Severity is medium rather than high: edits in the dialog are a secondary path (the fold is closed by default), and the panel itself only reports the cut when Check is pressed.
findings.documented_rule: CLAUDE.md, Prompt analyser: Check works cold, using CPU tokenizers on a _detached thread, and never calls ensure_loaded or takes the gate. CLAUDE.md, Frontend: 'The prompt check describes one text: the prompt and negative prompt as collect() sent them', and 'collect() sends refine: null'. design-notes 'The refine pass': 'A dialog, not a mode of the panel' (the dialog starts from the record; the fold is closed because 'a pass usually wants them as they were').
findings.rule_tension: No conflict if the dialog makes its own call. The panel's Check stays bound to collect(). PromptAnalysisRequest subclasses GenerateRequest, so the pass body (refine id, strength, 1248x1824) is accepted: I got a 200 with the cut and the findings, so no new route is needed. The call stays off the gate and never writes els.prompt. Two corrections to the original recommendation: (1) do not guard with refineEpoch. previewRefine increments it on every call, so the two requests would cancel each other's replies; use a separate refineCheckEpoch, also bumped in refineClosed(). (2) Do not auto-open the fold. That contradicts the folded-by-default design and smoke-refine step 20. Put the line outside the fold instead.
findings.smokes_affected: None break. smoke-refine.json runs on a FLUX fake with 'a fox in the snow' (no cut), so the new line stays hidden. Step 20 (expects !els.refineMore.open) would break only if the fold were auto-opened, which is why the line goes outside it. Add a step to smoke-animagine.json (port 7866): a long tag prompt opened in Refine shows #refine-encoders, and Apply on the order finding rewrites els.refinePrompt but not els.prompt.
findings.how_checked: Fresh Animagine fake (cagliostrolab/animagine-xl-4.0) on 7974 at 2560x1305 DPR 1. I made a 41-tag source at 832x1216 (seed 5) and opened Refine on it. I opened the fold with a real click on its summary, put the caret at the end and typed ', sm' and then 'irk' (Input.insertText). Then I measured the dialog, POSTed refineRequest().body to /api/prompt/analyze from the page, and counted the same text with the real cached CLIPTokenizer (both towers, HF offline).
findings.verifier_notes: The real tokenizer numbers (132 tokens with smirk, cut inside tag 23) match the original finding (129 without smirk). The fake server's word tokenizer gives 123/75, which is enough for smokes. One more point strengthens the case: Animagine's documented quality suffix sits at the end, so on any prompt over the cut the suffix itself is unread, in the panel as well. The guide's prompt tip says '77 tokens', but the dialog has no tip at all. G4.3 is the same missing dialog-side check viewed from the order rule, so its fix is folded in here.

sources.surface: Refine dialog > Prompt and sampling > Prompt textarea (SDXL tag checkpoints: Animagine, Kohaku, Illustrious, WAI)
sources.observation: The source prompt has 41 Animagine tags and ends with the card's quality suffix (masterpiece, high score, great score, absurdres). The real Animagine CLIP tokenizer (cached, CPU) counts it at 129 tokens, and the cut falls inside tag 23 ('outstretched arm'): only 22 of 41 tags are ever read. In the dialog I appended ', smirk' by real typing, which is the natural way to tweak a pass. The preview line stayed '1 image · strength 0.4 · about 11 of 28 steps run' and Refine stayed live. After the typing the 3-row box is scrolled to the tail (scrollTop 116 of 207 px). Its visible text, 'outstretched arm, outdoors, night, … absurdres, smirk', is roughly the part CLIP never reads (qhd-a07-edited.png). Pasting the same text into the panel and pressing Check gave: CLIP-L and CLIP-G read 75 of 124 tokens (fake tokenizer) and stop at code point 329, after 22 tags, with the warning 'the rest never reaches them'. Check also flagged '"masterpiece" (Quality) comes before "smirk"'. The dialog offers neither. On FLUX (T5, 512 tokens) an appended tag is read, so this problem is new on SDXL.
sources.why_it_matters: Adding or changing detail tags is what people do in a hires-style pass. On every SDXL checkpoint, an addition at the end of a long tag prompt has no effect. The user waits for the pass (15-46 s per image measured on WAI, verified.md:367-369), sees no change, and nothing in the dialog explains why.

findings.title: The Refine prompt is a plain 3-row box showing 15 of 41 tags, with no chips, autocomplete or validation, so a typo goes straight into the pass
surfaces: Refine dialog > Prompt and sampling (refine-prompt, refine-negative)
findings.recommendation:
(a) Autosize #refine-prompt on open, on fold toggle and on input: el.style.height = Math.min(el.scrollHeight + 2, Math.round(innerHeight * 0.4)) + 'px'. Measured: the dialog goes from 833 to 959 px and sits at y=41 within max-height calc(100vh - 32px) = 1008 at 2048x1040, and the box shows 207/207 px. At QHD, also consider widening the dialog: it is 460 px of 2560 (18%). For example, @media (min-width: 1800px) { .refine-dialog { width: 600px } }. (b) Below the box, add

. Debounce it at 400 ms, POST /api/tags/validate with els.refinePrompt.value.split(',').map(s => s.trim()).filter(Boolean), and show only invalid items ('Not found in Danbooru: smlie'). Only when tagVocabularyEnabled; silent on failure. (c) Caption the header line, e.g. a small 'Source prompt:' label or title attribute on #refine-prompt-line, so two differing prompts are not shown unlabelled. (d) Optional autocomplete: tags.js already has input-agnostic scheduleEditorSuggestions(input, menu) and renderEditorSuggestions(input, menu, suggestions) (tags.js:193-232) for the chip editor, but each item's click calls commitTagEdit. Add an onPick parameter and a

    inside the dialog's Prompt label to reuse them.
findings.documented_rule: CLAUDE.md, Frontend: 'Tag autocomplete and comma-item validation use the fixed Danbooru tag API through backend/tags.py … lookup failure stays advisory and never blocks', and chip mutations go through writePromptTags (which writes els.prompt only). style.css:989 '.rf-prompt: The source's prompt as a reminder of which picture this is, not to read'. design-notes 'A dialog, not a mode of the panel'.
findings.rule_tension: Compatible. A dialog-side problem line must not reuse writePromptTags or touch els.prompt. It uses /api/tags/validate on els.refinePrompt's comma items and stays silent on lookup failure, as the panel does. Gate it on tagVocabularyEnabled (and skip hybrid single-sentence prompts as scheduleTagValidation does) so FLUX and other prose checkpoints show nothing. The header line is deliberate, so caption it rather than remove it.
findings.smokes_affected: None break. smoke-refine.json is on a FLUX fake, so tagVocabularyEnabled is false and the new line stays hidden. Its only prompt assertion is step 18 (els.refinePrompt.value === 'a fox in the snow'), which autosize does not touch. smoke-animagine/illustrious/kohaku/wai assert els.tagSuggestions for the panel only, which is unaffected unless (d) reuses #tag-suggestions itself (it should not). Add a step to smoke-animagine.json for the dialog's unknown-tag line.
findings.how_checked: Same Animagine fake. A client-side fetch stub stood in for /api/tags/suggest and /api/tags/validate with a Danbooru-like vocabulary; 'smlie' is unknown. Measured at 2560x1305 DPR 1 and 2048x1040 DPR 1.25. Fold opened by a real click. Typed ', sm' at the end via Input.insertText and logged #tag-suggestions and the stub's call log. Replaced 'blush' with 'smlie' by selection plus insertText and looked for any mark in the dialog. Typed the same typo in the panel for comparison. Applied the proposed autosize by hand to check that the dialog still fits.
findings.verifier_notes: Minor correction: I count 14 whole tags visible, not 15. With an empty negative, the negative box was 60/60 for me; the original 60/81 had a negative filled in. Everything else matches at both viewports. The header-versus-box duplication is real but low on its own, because the header is documented as a reminder of the picture, so the fix is to label it.

sources.surface: Refine dialog > Prompt and sampling (refine-prompt, refine-negative)
sources.observation:
At 2560x1305 the textarea is 81 px of 207 px of content (39%). A mirror measurement shows 15 of 41 tags fully visible. The panel's 5-row box shows 42%, has a 41-chip tray under it, and has autocomplete. The negative is 60 of 81 px (74%). The numbers are the same at 2048x1040 @1.25 (81/207). Real typing in the dialog:
- Typing ', sm' opened no suggestions, and the page made no /api/tags/suggest call (the stub's call log was unchanged).
- Replacing 'smile' with 'open mouth' and 'blush' with the typo 'smlie' produced no mark. The preview stayed '1 image · strength 0.4 · about 11 of 28 steps run' and Refine stayed live.
- The same 'smlie' in the panel turns its chip red '? smlie' within about 0.5 s.
With the fold open, the dialog shows the prompt twice. The header line (.rf-prompt, 3-line clamp, 338 px wide) keeps the source's text ('… smile, blush …') while the box below says 'open mouth, smlie'. Neither is labelled as the source's or the pass's. The sweep then ran with 'smlie' in all three cells.
sources.why_it_matters: Every SDXL checkpoint here is a Danbooru-tag model whose guide says unknown tags are wasted. The panel spends a whole subsystem on catching them. The dialog is where the user named the clunkiness, and the same edit there gets none of that help. A misspelled tag costs a full pass, and on a 4-version sweep that is minutes.

findings.title: On SDXL a pass sends no preview frames, so the stage shows an unrelated earlier image and the panel's prompt chips for the whole pass
surfaces: Viewer and chip tray during a Refine job on an SDXL checkpoint
findings.recommendation: Pass a placeholder through startJob's options instead of a global: startJob(path, body, {sheet, panel:false, placeholder:{src: refineSource.url, w, h, label:`Refining image ${refineSource.id} → ${w}×${h} · strength ${strength}`}}), forwarded to streamJob(jobId, opts). This keys it to that job, so a pass queued behind another job cannot paint over it. In streamJob, at the first 'progress' event when !cleared && !previewEl && opts.placeholder: clearResults(), cleared = true, and insert as previewEl, so dropPreview() and show() remove it and a FLUX frame replaces it. CSS: .pending img { aspect-ratio: var(--w)/var(--h); max-height: min(70vh, 900px); opacity: .45; filter: blur(1px) }. Update the figcaption with label + ' · step 4/11 · 2s left' in the progress branch. Root fix, for direct SDXL renders too, in the backend: a 4x3 SDXL latent map in latent_preview, fitted on the card like the others. Hardening seen while testing: the Ctrl+Enter keydown handler (app.js:255-260) does not call preventDefault().
findings.documented_rule: generation.js:380-381: 'Results replace the viewer only once the first image of this job lands, so the previous one stays up through the queue wait and the model load'. The preview path already clears at the first frame (generation.js:414-427). CLAUDE.md, Jobs: 'A preview needs a matrix for the VAE' (design-notes 'The live preview': none fitted for SDXL's 4-channel VAE). refine.js:354-357: a pass queues like Generate's, with its progress in the panel and its images in the strip.
findings.rule_tension: Compatible if the placeholder appears at the first 'progress' event, which only arrives once the job runs, after any queue wait or load, exactly as a first preview frame does today. The chip tray describing the panel's prompt is by design: validation of the panel's box lives above the results on a two-column page. It is not job state, so it is not a defect to fix.
findings.smokes_affected: None break. smoke-refine.json (FLUX fake, preview frames on) clicks '#viewer img' at step 45 only after the pass ends, when the placeholder is gone. smoke-preview.json steps 5 and 7 check img.preview on a direct render, which gets no placeholder. The fake server sends preview frames even when claiming an SDXL checkpoint, so no smoke can see this bug. A new step needs the frames dropped in-page, or a fake flag such as --no-preview.
findings.how_checked: The Animagine fake sends preview frames, which real SDXL does not (verified.md:176, :343), so I dropped 'preview' SSE events in the page (64 and 21 dropped). At 2560x1305: made the source, then an unrelated direct render (1boy, 1024², id 9), opened Refine on the source, clicked Refine with a real click, and sampled the viewer, progress, chips and title every 250 ms. At 2048x1040 @1.25: scrolled to the gallery, opened the dialog with a real click on the card's ⤢, set Versions 2 and ran with Ctrl+Enter from the Strength box.
findings.verifier_notes: The core claim is reproduced: on SDXL a pass gives no picture and nothing on the stage names the source. I adjusted the description: the chip tray showing the panel's tags is documented placement, not a defect. Direct SDXL renders have the same blank wait, but there the panel prompt beside the bar matches the job; for a pass nothing does, and the dialog the user acted in is gone. Harness artifact, not reported as a finding: my driver's Ctrl+Enter sends char '\r'. That Enter keypress lands on the ⤢ button the closed dialog hands focus back to, and reopens the dialog (window.__opens 2). With '\n', which is what Windows sends for Ctrl+Enter, or with no char, it does not reopen. Other reviewers' Ctrl+Enter shots may show this artifact. Calling e.preventDefault() in app.js's Ctrl+Enter branch would rule it out on every platform.

sources.surface: Viewer and chip tray during a Refine job on an SDXL checkpoint
sources.observation:
Real SDXL delivers no preview frames (verified.md:176 and :343), so I dropped the fake's 'preview' events in the page (37 and 48 frames dropped).
At 2560x1305 (lightbox Refine on image 3, 1.5x, 0.4): from 262 ms to 2,501 ms the viewer kept image 9, the unrelated direct render made just before, while progress counted 1/11 … 10/11. Progress is a 54x18 px, 12 px label at (157,950) in the left column. The 2161x917 viewer and the 2161x48 chip tray never referred to the pass: the tray showed the panel's 9 chips, not the pass's 41 tags. The tab title stayed 'Local Diffusion'.
At 2048x1040 @1.25 (Versions 2, run by Ctrl+Enter): image 11 stayed for 5.25 s, then both results appeared together, because a cell's images land only when the cell ends. The page had also scrolled the stage top off-screen.
On FLUX the first preview frame replaces the viewer (generation.js:414-427), so the wait has a picture. On SDXL it has none. On the card, a WAI 1.5x pass is 15.2 s and 8.6 MP is 46.2 s per image, so Versions 4 at 2x is about 1.5 min of an unchanged stage.
sources.why_it_matters: With no picture of the work, the only signs that anything is happening are a 12 px counter about 1,000 px from the image area and a dimmed Generate. The user can't tell which image is being refined or whether the click did anything. Meanwhile the stage shows an image and a tag list that are not the job, which invites wrong conclusions.

findings.title: Reset wipes the whole panel and grid spec in one click with no confirmation or undo, and looks just like Check
surfaces: Prompt caption toolbar: Reset
findings.recommendation: Factor persistPanel's state builder into `panelState()`. In resetPanel, before forget(), take `const undo = {panel: panelState(), refine: remembered(REFINE_KEY), owned: {...owned}}`. After resetting, call showError('Panel reset.', true) with an inline Undo button live for about 20 s. Undo writes PANEL_FIELDS, gridOpen, referenceIds and the sampling values back (calling own() for the owned keys), re-remembers both keys, and runs syncSize(); syncCfg(); syncConditioning(); syncRuns(); schedulePreview(); scheduleTagValidation(0). Resume stays unticked. Add the danger affordance the other destructive buttons get: `.field > span .reset:hover { color: var(--danger); border-color: var(--danger); }`.
findings.documented_rule: design-notes 'Panel persistence': Reset is the one thing that empties the store and sits away from Generate because it costs the prompt. CLAUDE.md Frontend: resetPanel is the one thing that forgets the panel and the Refine dialog's remembered strength. Resume is never stored.
findings.rule_tension: An in-memory Undo is compatible: Reset still removes both stores at once and nothing survives a reload (smoke.json:139-144 checks this). Undo is an explicit user action within the session, never restores Resume, and Reset stays at the caption's far end. panel-3's `remembered(PANEL_KEY)` snapshot is wrong in two cases. It is stale for up to 300 ms, because persistPanel is debounced (panel.js:25-42) and Reset clears the pending write. And it is empty in a private or blocked-storage window, where the page is meant to work without memory. Snapshot the live DOM instead.
findings.smokes_affected: smoke.json:139-144: the store must be null right after Reset and still empty after a reload; an in-memory snapshot keeps both true. smoke-refine.json:6, 112, 145 and smoke-refine-unavailable.json:5 call resetPanel(); showError(''), which clears the note, so they are unaffected.
findings.how_checked: On the FLUX fake, typed a prompt and set Steps 32, Seed 4471, 16:9 at 1.5 MP, grid Steps '20-32x4' with the fold open, and a local-diffusion.refine.v1 entry. Hovered and then clicked Reset with real mouse events and read the computed hover colours, every field, #error and both stores. Pressed Ctrl+Z (real key codes) and reloaded. Read panel.js resetPanel and persistPanel and the smoke.json Reset steps.
findings.verifier_notes: Reproduces exactly as described. The only change is the snapshot source, from storage to the live DOM, for the debounce and blocked-storage reasons above. Medium is right: the loss is large (the prompt plus a grid spec that must be retyped exactly for Resume to match), but a misclick is occasional, since Reset sits 66 px from Check, at the far end of the caption.

sources.surface: Prompt caption toolbar: Reset
sources.observation: Before the click: prompt filled, Steps 32 (owned), Seed 4471, grid Steps '20-32x4', size 16:9 at 1.5 MP. One click on Reset (40x19 px, 10px text, centre at x=311) gave an empty prompt, Steps 28, a blank Seed, an empty grid and 1024x1024. Ctrl+Z restored nothing (i01). It also forgets the Refine dialog's remembered strengths. Reset uses the same `.ghost.tiny` style as Check (43x19, centre x=203, 108 px away) and Examples. Nothing about it marks it as destructive, and unlike `.ghost.small` its hover doesn't turn red.
sources.why_it_matters: Design notes ('Panel persistence') put Reset away from Generate so that a slip doesn't cost the prompt. It now sits in the toolbar the user reaches for to Check a prompt. It also erases the grid spec, which the same notes describe as painful to retype exactly, since a slightly different axis breaks Resume.

findings.title: A reshaped size crops away part of the source with only a text note, and W/H have no aspect lock
surfaces: Refine dialog: W/H boxes and size line
findings.recommendation: (1) Make the size line quantitative, keeping the phrase: 'the source cropped to this shape: keeps the middle 56% of its width' (s = max(W/sw, H/sh); kept = W/(sw*s) of the width or H/(sh*s) of the height). This is independent of M6. (2) Add an aspect lock between W and H (a toggle, on by default). On a trusted input in W, set H = round16(W * sh / sw), and the reverse for H; turn it off for deliberate reframing. (3) Once M6's large source exists, draw the kept region over it: an absolutely positioned frame sized by the same cover math and redrawn in syncRefine, with the rest dimmed by box-shadow: 0 0 0 9999px rgba(0,0,0,.55) inside an overflow:hidden wrapper.
findings.documented_rule: Design notes 'The source is covered and cropped, never stretched': 'a size of another shape is a reframing, and the size line says "cropped to this shape"'. Reframing is deliberate.
findings.rule_tension: Reframing must stay possible, so the lock has to be a toggle. The overlay must mirror refine.fitted exactly (cover, then centre-crop, never stretch). No rule forbids either. Guard the lock with e.isTrusted, or run it on 'change', so script-driven paired assignments are left alone.
findings.smokes_affected: smoke-refine.json steps 32-33 set W=1024 and H=1024 by script and dispatch input on W only, then expect 'cropped to this shape'. They survive if the lock ignores untrusted events (or listens on 'change') and the new text keeps that phrase. Step 28's exact '2.3 MP — 1.5× the source' is the uncropped branch, so it is unaffected.
