Steps 56-57 set both sides by script.
findings.how_checked: FLUX fake on 7910. Set 1536x1536 on the 1664x928 source and read the size line and thumbnail. Then put the cursor in W on the 896x1152 source (1344x1728 at 1.5x), typed '2000' with real key input, and read W, H and the size line. Computed the kept fraction with refine.fitted's cover-and-centre-crop rule.
findings.verifier_notes: Reproduced. The finding's 2000x2304 came from a remembered 2x scale; from a fresh start it gives 2000x1728, with the same behaviour. Medium stands: typing one side is the natural way to ask for 'make it 2000 wide', it silently reframes, and the only signal is a muted phrase with no quantity, which turns amber only when the VRAM note fires as well. The finding already noted the smoke constraint; e.isTrusted is the simplest guard.

sources.surface: Refine dialog: W/H boxes and size line
sources.observation: Typing 1536x1536 for the 1664x928 harbour gives '2.4 MP — the source cropped to this shape'. By refine.fitted's cover-and-centre-crop, that keeps 56% of the width and throws away 44% of the picture, with nothing drawn. The thumbnail beside it is itself a square cover crop, so it looks the same whether or not anything is cropped. Editing one box does not move the other: typing W=2000 on the 7:9 fox gave 2000x2304 (4.6 MP), a crop the user probably did not intend, flagged by the same muted phrase.
sources.why_it_matters: An unintended crop reaches the user only as a finished image without the harbour's edges, after a pass that may take minutes. With a single W edit being the easiest way to ask for a custom scale, accidental reframing is likely.

findings.title: Resume needs the run's base seed but no control supplies it, and the error starts with pydantic's 'Value error,'
surfaces: Resume tick, preview/error line, Runs picker, sheet controls
findings.recommendation: As proposed, with three refinements. (1) With exactly one run on the sheet (search run:<id>), add 'Resume this run' to #sheet-controls. It fetches /api/runs, sets els.seed to that run's seed and dispatches input, ticks els.gridResume, opens the fold, runs previewGrid and scrolls Run grid into view. If the preview then reports p.skipped === 0, say in the preview that the panel's grid does not match this run (prompt/axes changed), so the user does not render a different grid. (2) In the last-run banner for cancelled or budget-stopped jobs, add 'Resume' using the snapshot's own `seed` (Job.snapshot publishes the base). (3) In state.js readableDetail, use `e.msg.replace(/^Value error, /, '')`.
findings.documented_rule: CLAUDE.md Reproduction: Resume keys on settings and requires an explicit seed unless the seed axis is a list. Design notes 'Resume keys on settings': the UI writes the base into a blank Seed box after Run grid, and the recovery instruction says the oldest image. panel.js:13-15: Resume is never remembered.
findings.rule_tension: The button only fills the seed and ticks Resume for this session; nothing is persisted, so 'Resume is never remembered' holds. The server still refuses a missing seed. The panel's axes are not stored per run, so the button relies on the preview's 'N already done', which is the documented confirmation. Stripping pydantic's prefix is display-only.
findings.smokes_affected: smoke.json line 129 expects els.gridResume.checked === false after a reload; the button must not persist Resume, and it doesn't. smoke.json line 65 counts #sheet-controls labels ≥ 2, so a button does not affect it. No smoke matches 'Value error' or 'resume needs'.
findings.how_checked: On 7913 I filled the fox variable grid (same template, CFG 2,5, Seeds 3) with a blank Seed box, ticked Resume with .click(), and read the preview. I pressed Run grid and read #error. I compared /api/runs with the Runs picker labels and opened the run's sheet to look for any Resume control. I then tried the newest image's seed, then the true base seed. Last I tried Reuse on the oldest image, the 'oldest image carries it' path, and read the lightbox settings line. Screenshot: m56-01-resume-blank.png.
findings.verifier_notes: Confirmed with stronger evidence. The obvious 'take its seed' action (Reuse) breaks the grid spec, and a near-miss seed gives a partly overlapping grid. The persisted Seed box usually still holds the base. It is lost after the dice, a Reuse, Reset, another grid, or a grid run from the CLI or another browser, which is why the frequency is 'occasional'.

sources.surface: Resume tick, preview/error line, Runs picker, sheet controls
sources.observation: With a blank Seed box, ticking Resume turned the preview into the warning 'Value error, resume needs the seed the grid was started from - the Seed box shows it after Run grid, and the oldest image of the run carries it'. Run grid showed the same in #error. /api/runs already returns that base seed (run c6f465991da2 → seed 5872080855328996), and loadRuns uses only the date, count, stars and prompt. Neither the Runs picker, the run's sheet nor the last-run banner offers 'Resume'. Filling the seed by hand gave '0 images … · 24 already done' and Run grid 'every cell is already rendered', so the mechanism works once the seed is found.
sources.why_it_matters: Resume is the recovery path for a night that died at cell 300 of 480 ('a Resume finishes the rest'). Making the user find the oldest image of the run and copy a 16-digit seed is error-prone, and a wrong seed renders a different grid, not a resume.

findings.title: Keyboard chip editing drops focus to <body> after one Alt+Arrow or Delete, and 70 chips are 140 tab stops
surfaces: Tag chips (keyboard and screen reader)
code_pointers: web/tags.js:150-160 (closeTagEditor refocuses: the pattern to reuse)
findings.recommendation: Add a top-level `tagFocusIndex`. movePromptTag sets it to `to` and deletePromptTag to min(index, length-1), both before writePromptTags. At the end of renderTagValidation, if it is set and focus is on BODY or was inside the tray, focus `.tag-check[data-index=N]`. Clear it on a tray focusout whose relatedTarget is outside the tray. Use a roving tabindex: the focused or first chip gets tabIndex 0, the rest -1. Left/Right/Home/End move between chips (Alt+Left/Right still move the tag). .tag-remove gets tabIndex -1, since Delete does the same and the × stays clickable. Change the aria-label to '<tag>, <known/unknown/unchecked>. Enter edits, Alt+Left/Right moves, Delete removes.' Drop 'drag to reorder' and say how to insert. Remove role=status from the interactive tray (index.html:65). Add a visually hidden aria-live=polite summary ('11 known, 1 unknown'), and remove tag-validation from the textarea's aria-describedby (index.html:60).
findings.documented_rule: design-notes 'Animagine XL 4.0' (docs/design-notes.md:1823): 'Alt+Left/Right is the keyboard equivalent' of drag, and every chip takes Delete/Backspace. closeTagEditor refocuses the chip (tags.js:150-160). CLAUDE.md Frontend: all mutations go through writePromptTags, and placeTagValidation keeps focus and selection across the 901px move.
findings.rule_tension: No conflict. Refocusing after the rebuild reuses closeTagEditor's own pattern. Mutations still go through writePromptTags. A roving tabindex works with placeTagValidation, since moveBefore and the manual restore keep whatever element has focus. One implementation detail: writePromptTags → scheduleTagValidation(0) renders the tray twice (pending, then result), so the pending focus index must survive both renders and be cleared only on focusout to outside the tray.
findings.smokes_affected: No existing step breaks: smoke-animagine 36 (Escape → focus on chip [1]) and 37 (Enter on the focused chip) still hold with a roving tabindex. No smoke asserts role=status, the aria-label text, aria-describedby or the × tabIndex. New smoke-animagine steps are recommended: Alt+Left twice moves the tag two places with focus on the moved chip, and Delete leaves focus on the next chip.
findings.how_checked: 12-tag prompt on the Animagine fake. Focused chip [data-index=2], pressed real Alt+ArrowLeft (CDP keycombo), read activeElement after 50 ms, pressed Alt+ArrowLeft again, focused chip 3 and pressed Delete. Then checked the reference pattern (Enter, then Escape refocuses the chip), counted tab stops and read the role, aria-label and aria-describedby.
findings.verifier_notes: Reproduced exactly as stated. The documented keyboard equivalent of drag works for one step only, then focus falls to <body>. Medium is right: it breaks a documented interaction, though only for keyboard users (occasional), and nothing is lost. The recommendation is sound and feasible in plain JS.

sources.surface: Tag chips (keyboard and screen reader)
sources.observation: I focused chip 3 and pressed Alt+Left. The tag moved, but 50 ms later document.activeElement was BODY, and a second Alt+Left did nothing. Delete on a focused chip also left focus on BODY. With 70 tags the tray holds 140 tab stops (each chip plus its × button) between the settings panel and the viewer. Each chip's aria-label is '1girl. Enter edits it; drag to reorder; Delete removes it.', which names a mouse-only action and leaves out Alt+Left/Right and Shift+F10 for insert. The tray is role=status and is rebuilt twice per edit (pending, then result), and the prompt textarea's aria-describedby points at it. A screen reader therefore hears the whole 70-tag list as the prompt's description and as live updates.
sources.why_it_matters: Keyboard reordering is documented as the equivalent of drag (CLAUDE.md, design notes), but it works for one step only. The user then has to Tab back through up to 140 stops to find the chip again. Closing the chip editor already refocuses the chip (closeTagEditor), so the project expects focus to survive a rebuild.

findings.title: A sheet of prompt iterations has truncated, duplicate column labels in alphabetical order
surfaces: Contact sheet, prompt axis
findings.recommendation: In promptLabels (web/sheet.js:98), after the existing paths, if the labels are not all distinct or any is over LABEL_CHARS, fall back to a word-level LCS diff of each prompt against the oldest one (prompts[0] once ordered by age): '+35mm photo,', '+deeply', '−dawn +dusk'. The oldest prompt keeps its own clipped text. This is about 20 lines of vanilla JS, O(n·m) on prompts of 10-80 words. In sheetValues (web/sheet.js:132-150), make written = axis.key.startsWith('var:') || axis.key === 'prompt' so prompt columns read in the order they were made. In renderSheet (web/sheet.js:391-402), set the head cell's title to the full prompt. Do not clip the DOM label at 44 characters where the .text head already wraps: a 540px column showed a 44-char label on half its width. Keep clipText for the canvas export.
findings.documented_rule: design-notes 'Prompt labels on the sheet': labels keep only the words that vary; equal word counts pick out positions exactly; otherwise the shared head and tail come off; pins address values by position because a label need not round-trip. sheet.js:122-129: non-variable axes sort ascending, variables by oldest image. CLAUDE.md 'Frontend and CLI': a variable axis lists its values by first appearance, not alphabetically.
findings.rule_tension: Compatible. A word-diff fallback is a refinement of 'keep what varies' and only runs when the documented head/tail strip leaves duplicate or over-long labels. The equal-word-count positional path (two-variable grids such as 'size small, size big') stays. Pins already address values by position, so labels that do not round-trip are fine. Ordering the prompt axis by oldest image extends the first-appearance rule that variables already follow. The export uses valueText too (sheet.js:485/491/520), so it gets the same labels.
findings.smokes_affected: None assert prompt-axis labels or their order. Re-run smoke-comparison.json:20-25 (showRun on a shared run, setAxis('cols','prompt'), then a colValues/cellOf consistency check that does not depend on order) and smoke.json's sheet section (lines 78-90 assert var: and Seed heads only).
findings.how_checked: Same 7919 fake. Typed 'fisherman' into the search box and clicked Sheet over the 6 random-seed iterations, then logged the head texts, head titles, axes and cell order. Then made 22 iterations matching 'harbour at', and separately 4 fixed-seed (seed 42) iterations matching 'tram' with words added in the middle and at the end. Measured the head font, width and title.
findings.verifier_notes: Reproduced exactly as described, and the recommendation is sound. A related cost the finding does not mention: over random-seed iterations, the prompt and seed axes both have one value per image, so the listlike rule (chooseAxes, sheet.js:212-215) drops neither and the sheet is a mostly-empty diagonal. When one prompt repeats, seed is dropped and then pinned by reconcileAxes (sheet.js:236-246), and the sheet shows 1 of 24 images. That is a separate layout issue (an S fix is a sheet note pointing to Compare on the same seeds when a pinned axis is a one-per-image seed; an M fix is a list layout). It is not needed to fix the labels, which also fail in the correct fixed-seed flow.

sources.surface: Contact sheet, prompt axis
sources.observation: Task 2: searching 'fisherman' and pressing Sheet over the 6 iterations made a Prompt axis whose column headers were 'Prompt 35mm photo, portrait of an old fisherman, d…', 'Prompt portrait of an old fisherman, deeply weathe…' twice and 'Prompt portrait of an old fisherman, weathered fac…' three times. Five of six columns could not be told apart. The iterations had different word counts and the last one added a word at the front, so promptLabels' shared head/tail strip removed nothing and every label was the full prompt clipped to 44 characters. The columns were also sorted with localeCompare ('35mm…' first), not in the order the prompts were written.
sources.why_it_matters: The sheet is the app's comparison tool, and for the most common comparison (successive edits) it cannot say which column is which. The user has to open each cell to read the prompt.

findings.title: The topbar stays green with the model name for the whole time the server is dead
surfaces: Topbar status dot and text during a server outage
findings.recommendation: In refreshStatus's catch (status.js:230), when the error is a network rejection (the TypeError from fetch, or err.offline from G1.5's api() wrapper): set els.dot.className = 'dot error', set els.statusText to 'server not answering — retrying', hide Load, and set aria-disabled with title 'The server is not answering' on Generate, Run grid, Refine and Unload. Keep the 3 s poll and the statusPending guard as they are. Add `started_at: float` to ModelStatus, set once at import in main.py. On the first good poll after a failure, or when started_at differs from the value first seen, write a note: 'The server restarted at HH:MM — the model is not loaded, and any job that was running ended with it.' Then clear any connection-kind message (G1.5). The existing model-change branch (status.js:125-135) already re-scopes the gallery after a restart under another checkpoint.
findings.documented_rule: CLAUDE.md Prompt analyser and the critique route: /api/status must stay cheap (file checks, never a tokenizer load). Frontend: submit and critic controls are aria-disabled, never disabled. status.js:119: the statusPending guard keeps a stalled poll from queueing more.
findings.rule_tension: Compatible. A boot timestamp is one constant in ModelStatus. 'Not answering' must count only fetch rejections, never a slow poll: /api/status can stall behind a CUDA read during a load (status.js:112-114), and the statusPending guard already absorbs that. Hold buttons with aria-disabled plus a title.
findings.smokes_affected: None. No smoke stops a server or reads #status-text or the dot class. Adding a ModelStatus field changes no smoke step.
findings.how_checked: Ran 7971 with --step 0.3 under a scratch supervisor and started a Runs-4 job. At T+12.3 s a scratch PUT /__die called os._exit(1), a hard crash with sockets reset. The supervisor restarted the server unloaded after 30 s (and after 1 s in a second run). Sampled the topbar every 500 ms throughout. Read status.js:118-231.
findings.verifier_notes: Reproduced: about 35 s of a green 'ready' topbar over a dead server, then a silent switch to 'not loaded'. Severity lowered from high to medium. While a job is watched, the panel shows 'reconnecting… (n)' within half a second, so the topbar is not the only signal there. The misleading case is the idle page. That includes the common restart to change checkpoints (the start-up menu is the only way to switch), where the old page shows the old checkpoint green until something fails. Implement together with G1.5 as one 'server unreachable' state.

sources.surface: Topbar status dot and text during a server outage
sources.observation: With a Runs 4 job going (--step 0.3), the server was hard-killed 12.6 s in. Samples every 0.5 s show 'dot ready' and 'FLUX.1-Krea-dev' (green) from the kill at T+13 until the restarted server first answered at T+52: 39 s of a 'ready' topbar over no server. refreshStatus's `catch { /* server not up yet */ }` (status.js:230) swallows every failed poll. When the server came back, the topbar silently became 'not loaded' plus a Load button, with nothing saying the server had restarted or that the running job had died with it (f3-12-t58-back.png). Unload stayed clickable throughout.
sources.why_it_matters: The topbar is the page's only health indicator, and it says the opposite of the truth exactly when the user needs it. Every action then fails with 'Failed to fetch' (gap-failure-and-recovery-5) under a green 'ready', and the stream message claims the run carries on (gap-failure-and-recovery-4). A user leaving an overnight grid running cannot tell a crash from a slow cell.

findings.title: A grid's skipped cells are invisible while it runs, named only by count at the end, and the retry (Resume) is never offered; Run grid again re-renders everything
surfaces: Panel cell line, #error and the grid fold after a grid with failed cells
findings.recommendation: (1) Progress events carry no `failures` (jobs.py:446-460); only status events do. So keep `let skipped = 0` in streamJob, update it from each status/done snapshot's data.failures, and have showCell append ' · N skipped' in var(--danger) when it is above 0. (2) Server: on a skipped cell, append {label, seed, error} to a new Job.failed_cells (jobs.py:532-541) and include it in snapshot(), so the done text can read '1 of 12 cells was skipped: 3 steps, seed …656635 (RuntimeError: …)'. (3) In streamJob's done branch, for an /api/grid job with data.failures > 0, put a ghost button in #cell-note: 'Retry the N skipped cell(s)'. It re-submits the job's own submitted payload, kept in a Map by job id in startJob, with resume: true and seed set to the base seed the POST returned. It must not re-read the panel, which may have been edited since. (4) In preview_grid (main.py:1162), when resume is off and the seed is explicit or a seed list is set, count the completed cells with the same lookup Resume uses and add a warn line to the preview: '11 of these are already in the gallery — tick Resume to skip them'.
findings.documented_rule: design-notes 'A cell's failure is the cell's': skip and continue, and a finished job with failures is 'done' with an error line. design-notes 'Resume keys on settings': an explicit seed is required unless the seed axis is a list, and the UI writes the base seed back after Run grid. CLAUDE.md Jobs: no new status, every end through _finish.
findings.rule_tension: Compatible. The skipping rule and the 'done' status stay. The retry re-submits with resume:true and the job's explicit base seed, which satisfies Resume's seed rule. A preview count of already-rendered cells is a read-only use of storage.completed_cells and changes no behaviour.
findings.smokes_affected: smoke.json:154 (expects gridPreview to have class warn and include '2 would be identical'; an added 'already in the gallery' clause must not replace that text). smoke.json:157 (expects cellNote textContent to include 'Finished 6 images' and 'Only 2 distinct'; a retry button added to #cell-note keeps that only if it is appended, not replacing the text). pytest tests/test_api_jobs.py:176 asserts '1 cell(s) failed' in done['error'], so a rewording must update it.
findings.how_checked: Grid of 12 cells (steps 2,3,4 x 4 seeds, blank seed) on 7971, with a scratch flag making the 5th generate() call raise. Sampled the cell line every 250 ms and measured the done state and the Resume and Run grid rects at QHD and 2048@1.25. Read the preview before and after ticking Resume. Then pressed Run grid again without Resume (failure flag cleared) and counted gallery rows. Read generation.js:95-109 and 445-474, jobs.py:404-420 and 532-541, main.py:1162-1193, grid.py:505 and design-notes 'Resume keys on settings'.
findings.verifier_notes: Reproduced exactly as described. Verdict adjusted for the recommendation only. The original reads data.failures in showCell, but progress events do not carry it. Its retry re-read the panel (els.gridResume plus els.gridRun.click()), which re-runs whatever the panel now holds; it should re-submit the job's own payload. Severity medium stands: real cell failures (an OOM) are occasional, but the obvious retry re-renders the whole grid.

sources.surface: Panel cell line, #error and the grid fold after a grid with failed cells
sources.observation: In a 12-cell grid (steps 2,3,4 x 4 seeds) where cell 5 raised, the cell line jumped from 'cell 4/12 · 2 steps…' to 'cell 6/12 · 4 steps…' with no mark. The status events carry failures: 1 and error, but showCell ignores them. At the end: 'Finished 11 images in 11s.' and, in red, '1 cell(s) failed and were skipped; last: RuntimeError: cell 5 blew up'. Which cell failed (its label or seed) is not reported; 'cell 5' is the fake's own exception text, and a real OOM names none. The retry is the Resume tick plus Run grid. At QHD Resume sits at y=1343 and Run grid at y=1395, both below the 1305 fold. At 2048@1.25 they are at y=1480/1548 against a 1040 viewport, and the steps file's click missed Run grid there. Nothing points at them. Pressing Run grid again without Resume (the seed box now holds the written-back seed) re-renders every cell: a second run added 3 duplicates (cards 73 to 76) before its own failures. The preview had said only '12 images · 3 steps x 1 CFG x 1 mu x 4 seeds', with no 'already rendered'. Ticking Resume works: the preview reads '1 image · … · 11 already done', and the run made exactly the missing cell.
sources.why_it_matters: Grids are the overnight tool. One skipped cell leaves a hole in the sheet that the user must find by eye. The obvious retry (Run grid) wastes the night re-rendering what exists, while the correct one is a below-the-fold checkbox the message never mentions.

findings.title: A grid stopped by three failures in a row shows only the last exception, and the next day's banner reads '6/12 cells' for 3 images
surfaces: Panel after the job's 'error' end; the last-run banner after a reload
findings.recommendation: In _run's except (jobs.py:397-402), when job.failures > 0 (the failure rule raised), set job.stopped_by = 'failures'. Prefix the error with wording that covers both rules: f'Stopped at cell {job.run} of {job.total_runs} after {job.failures} cells failed; {len(job.images)} images kept. Last: {short_error(exc)}'. Keep the last exception in the text, which tests/test_api_grid.py:820 expects. In streamJob's 'error' branch, when stopped_by === 'failures', offer G1.7's retry button labelled 'Resume the remaining N cells' (N = total_runs - image cells). In announceLastRun (panel.js:181), for status 'error' or 'cancelled' with total_runs > 1, write 'stopped at cell ${run} of ${total_runs}' instead of '(run/total cells)'. When run is 0 (the load failed, as in G1.1), write 'never started' instead.
findings.documented_rule: CLAUDE.md Jobs: three failures in a row, or more than a third of the grid, ends the job. Every terminal transition goes through _finish, and a budget stop returns through the cancel path rather than a fourth status (design-notes 'Time budget', 'A cell's failure is the cell's'). design-notes 'The morning after': a banner for a job finished within 24 h.
findings.rule_tension: Compatible. The status stays 'error' and the end still goes through _finish. Setting the existing stopped_by field to 'failures' adds no status. The banner change is copy only.
findings.smokes_affected: None in tools/smoke-*.json: no step reads #last-run or a failure-ended job. pytest: tests/test_api_grid.py:820 ('blew up' in job error) holds if the last error is kept; tests/test_api_grid.py:144 (stopped_by 'budget') is unaffected.
findings.how_checked: Second grid (new prompt, blank seed, 12 cells) with calls 4-6 made to raise, so the three-in-a-row rule ended the job. Captured the panel at the end and the /api/jobs?include_finished=true snapshot, then reloaded for the last-run banner and measured it at QHD and 2048@1.25. Read jobs.py:396-420, generation.js:445-474, panel.js:168-194 and design-notes 'Time budget' (stopped_by).
findings.verifier_notes: Reproduced exactly. Adjusted only in the recommendation. The job can also end on the 'more than a third' rule, so the copy must not say 'in a row' unconditionally. An 'error' job can also be one whose load failed (run 0, image_count 0), which the banner change must not word as 'stopped at cell 0'.

sources.surface: Panel after the job's 'error' end; the last-run banner after a reload
sources.observation: Second grid: cells 4-6 failed, so the job ended by the three-in-a-row rule. The panel went straight from 'cell 3/12 · 4 steps … ~9s left' to an empty cell line and red 'RuntimeError: cell 18 blew up' (f2-03-grid2-stopped.png). There is no 'Finished' line, because status 'error' skips it. Nothing says the job stopped, at cell 6 of 12, or why. It also doesn't say that 3 images were kept (they are in the viewer), that 6 cells never ran, or that Resume would run them. After a reload, the banner read 'Last run failed at 4 Oct, 04:18 pm: 3 images (6/12 cells). RuntimeError: cell 18 blew up'. '(6/12 cells)' is the cell it reached, which reads as 6 done. At 2048@1.25 the 106 px banner spans y 1003-1109, so its Show run and dismiss buttons sit below the 1040 fold.
sources.why_it_matters: An overnight grid that stopped a third of the way through looks like one bad cell, so the user doesn't know to resume it. The word 'failed' with an image count suggests nothing usable was kept, while in fact half the grid can still be rendered with one tick.

findings.title: A deleted image comes back as a broken viewer tile after a reload during its run, and deleting it again shows 'unknown image'
surfaces: Viewer and lightbox after resumeActiveJob reattaches
findings.recommendation: Server: in jobs.Job keep `produced` (what image_count reports, unchanged) and a `deleted` id set. Add jobs.forget_images(ids), called from main.delete and delete_unstarred after storage commits, which adds the ids to every live and finished job's set. snapshot(images=True) then sends `[r for r in images if r['id'] not in deleted]` and adds `deleted_count`. Client: in deleteImage's catch, when the message is 'unknown image', call forgetImages([rec.id]) and showError('Already deleted.', true) instead of the red error. As a cheap belt-and-braces, give viewer tiles an `onerror` that swaps in a 'Deleted' tombstone (the same one as G2.3). The 'Finished N images' note can then read `${made} images, ${deleted} since deleted`.
findings.documented_rule: design-notes 'A job outlives the page; per-stream queues' and generation.js resumeActiveJob: the stream's status snapshot replays every record the job made, so a reload finds a running sweep and what it made. tests/test_api_grid.py:102, :248 and :817 hold `image_count` to the number of images the job produced.
findings.rule_tension: The original recommendation (drop deleted records from Job.images) would also lower `image_count`. That field means 'how much a night produced' (jobs.py:147-151 comment), and three API tests assert it equals the cells rendered. Keep the replay and the produced count; filter only the records that are replayed, and add a separate deleted count.
findings.smokes_affected: None directly. smoke.json:157 expects cellNote to include 'Finished 6 images' and 'Only 2 distinct'. That stays true because no image of that run is deleted and the note keeps counting produced images. tests/test_api_grid.py:102/248/817 (image_count) stay valid with `produced`.
findings.how_checked: On 7972 at --step 0.3 I generated 5 runs at 10 steps from seed 720. When image 209 landed I opened it in the lightbox from the viewer and pressed Delete (confirm stubbed true), so the viewer went to []. I reloaded while the job ran, let resumeActiveJob reattach, and logged the viewer tiles (naturalWidth), viewerRecords and cellNote until done. I then clicked the broken tile, pressed Delete, and read #error and #lb-error. Finally I read /api/jobs?include_finished=true.
findings.verifier_notes: Reproduced. My counter read '1/5' where the reviewer saw '1/2' over 3 records, because of a different run length; the behaviour is the same. Adjusted because the original server fix would silently change image_count's documented and tested meaning. The client 404 path alone also fixes deletes from another tab. Medium stands: the documented workflow triages while a sweep runs and reattaches after reloads, and here a delete appears to undo itself, then the retry reads as a failure.

sources.surface: Viewer and lightbox after resumeActiveJob reattaches
sources.observation: Ran 5 cells at --step 0.3. Image 94 landed and was deleted from the lightbox (confirm accepted; viewer went to [95, 96]). After a reload, resumeActiveJob reattached: the viewer held [94 (naturalWidth 0), 95, 96, 97] and viewerRecords was [94, 95, 96, 97]. After the run ended, 94 was still a broken tile showing its alt text 'deleted during the run' (e07), and the cell note said 'Finished 5 images in 16s.' though 4 remained. Repeated with image 99: clicking the ghost opened the lightbox on a broken image, with the counter at '1/2' over 3 records. Delete asked 'Delete this image (seed 720)?' and then showed a red 'unknown image' in both #lb-error and #error, and the tile stayed (g01, g02). The server's jobs keep deleted records, so the last-run banner also counted '4 images (4/4 cells)' after all four had been deleted.
sources.why_it_matters: The user sees a delete undo itself, and the second attempt reads as a failure, which leaves them unsure whether the file is gone.

findings.title: A deleted image stays a reference chip: Reuse restores a broken chip with no note, a just-deleted image keeps its cached picture, and Generate fails with 'no gallery image with id 4'
surfaces: Reference chips after deletion; Reuse; card Delete confirm
findings.recommendation: As proposed, with two guards. 1) In forgetImages (gallery.js:244), after the splices: if any id in `gone` is in referenceIds, call setReferences(referenceIds.filter(id => !gone.has(id))) and showError(`Image ${ids} was a reference image; it is no longer in the references.`, true). Delete unstarred also benefits. 2) In confirmDelete (gallery.js:224), append `\n\nIt is reference image ${referenceIds.indexOf(rec.id)+1} in the panel.` when it applies. 3) In reuseIntoPanel, after the synchronous fill, ask GET /api/images/{id} for each restored id. Drop only those whose error matches /unknown image/ (the test reusePass already uses), and add a note in the reusePass style. 4) Set the chip's img.onerror to add class 'gone' (red border, 'deleted' label), so a stale localStorage id shows too.
findings.documented_rule: CLAUDE.md: 'forgetImages is the one place the page drops deleted ids'. setReferences is the one writer. Reuse notes are 'a note, not a failure' (gallery.js:385-397). The refine path's precedent is reusePass's 'no longer in the gallery' note (gallery.js:404-410). The server refuses an unknown id at submit (storage.reference_paths, main._refuse_unusable_inputs).
findings.rule_tension: Extend forgetImages rather than adding a second deletion path. Keep fillPanel synchronous, because smoke-conditioning.json:110-111 expects referenceIds.length === 1 immediately after reuse(). Prune dead ids in an async follow-up that only removes ids the server answers 'unknown image' for, so a live reference is never dropped by a transient error.
findings.smokes_affected: smoke-conditioning.json:110-111 (reuse then a synchronous referenceIds.length === 1 and the stale badge) must stay synchronous. smoke-refine.json's 'source has gone' steps are unaffected. No smoke asserts the confirm() text.
findings.how_checked: Case A: generated record 11 with references [8,4] by a real Generate click, then deleted card 4 through its ⌦ (confirm stubbed and logged). On a freshly loaded page I opened record 11's lightbox and clicked Reuse settings, logged the ids, the chip naturalWidth and #error, then clicked Generate. Case B: added card 5 as a reference with a real ❐ click, deleted card 5 with its ⌦, and logged the confirm text, referenceIds and the chip image.
findings.verifier_notes: Every claim reproduced, and the recommendation fits the 'one place' rule. I only added the guard that keeps the synchronous Reuse contract the smoke relies on.

sources.surface: Reference chips after deletion; Reuse; card Delete confirm
sources.observation: Case A. Record 11 was made with references [8,4]; image 4 was then deleted. Reuse (the lightbox's Reuse settings) set referenceIds [8,4] and rendered chip 2 as a broken image (naturalWidth 0, browser broken-image icon). There was no note and #error stayed empty. Pressing Generate produced 'no gallery image with id 4' in #error at y 1053, naming an id the chip doesn't show. Case B. ❐ on card 19 made it a reference; the card's ⌦ was then confirmed. The confirm text was 'Delete this image (seed 77)? … The file is removed from disk.', with no mention that it is a reference. The card disappeared, but referenceIds stayed [19] and the chip still showed the cached 384 px thumbnail, so it looks valid until a submit is refused. forgetImages drops ids from galleryRecords, viewerRecords and lbList but not referenceIds. By contrast, Reuse of a refined record whose source is gone gets a full sentence ('Image 14, the source this was refined from, is no longer in the gallery…', gallery.js:404-410).
sources.why_it_matters: A reference that looks present but isn't leads to a refused submit or, in a grid, a refused night, with an error the user can't map to a chip. Case B misleads because the picture is still there. The refine path already solved this, so references are the inconsistent one.

findings.title: Reusing a klein record on another checkpoint silently drops its references; the ⚠ note talks only about steps, CFG and mu
surfaces: Reuse (card ↻/⚠, lightbox Reuse settings) across checkpoints with All models
findings.recommendation: As proposed: in reuseIntoPanel, build notes from what fillPanel could not carry. If rec.reference?.length && !referenceSupported, add `Its ${n} reference image${s} (gallery ${ids}) are not used: ${short(loadedModel)} takes none, so this renders from the prompt alone.`. If rec.lora && els.lora.value !== rec.lora, add `Its adapter ${rec.lora} @ ${rec.lora_scale} is not applied here - ${reason}.`, with the reason taken from the /api/loras entry's detail when it is a misfit, else 'the file is no longer in the adapter directory'. That second note matters most on the same checkpoint, where today there is no note at all. Extend the ⚠ title in syncReuseButton to add 'references and adapter will not carry over' when the record has them.
findings.documented_rule: fillPanel (gallery.js:356-362) drops references and unlisted adapters on purpose, because the request would be refused at submit. The Reuse checkpoint note is 'a note, not a failure' (gallery.js:385-397). design-notes 'Reference images, by gallery id': a dropped reference renders 'a plain text-to-image that looks like a success'.
findings.rule_tension: None. Keep the drop and only say it, in the same note slot and style as the existing checkpoint note.
findings.smokes_affected: smoke-flux.json:42 asserts the Reuse note includes 'These settings were made on Krea-2-Turbo' and 'server is running FLUX.1-Krea-dev'; appending keeps both. smoke-conditioning.json:79-81 (Reuse with the adapter listed) is unaffected.
findings.how_checked: Started a Krea-2-Turbo fake on 8973 sharing the klein gallery. Ticked All models with a real click and clicked the ⚠ Reuse on klein record 14 (references [8,10]), then logged the panel and #error. As an extra check, I moved demo-style.safetensors out of my scratch loras/ dir, reloaded the klein fake's page and Reused klein record 16 (demo-style @ 0.5) on the same checkpoint. I restored the file afterwards.
findings.verifier_notes: Reproduced as stated. The same-checkpoint adapter case, verified here, is the stronger half: on the same checkpoint the user has no warning at all, while across checkpoints the existing note at least lists what carries over. Both are covered by the same S-sized fix, so medium stands.

sources.surface: Reuse (card ↻/⚠, lightbox Reuse settings) across checkpoints with All models
sources.observation: A Krea-2-Turbo fake on 8963 shared the klein gallery. With All models ticked, Reuse was clicked on klein record 21 (references [12,11]). Result: prompt and seed 77 restored, referenceIds [], note '(this checkpoint takes none)', and #error read 'These settings were made on FLUX.2-klein-4B; the server is running Krea-2-Turbo, whose steps, CFG and mu differ. Prompt, size and seed carry over; check the steps, CFG and mu boxes before generating.' Nothing says the two references were dropped. The card's ⚠ title is only 'Warning: generated with FLUX.2-klein-4B; the current model is Krea-2-Turbo'. fillPanel drops an adapter the list does not offer just as quietly (`listed ? rec.lora : ''`).
sources.why_it_matters: The server refuses a reference at submit precisely because 'a dropped reference renders a plain text-to-image that looks like a success' (design notes). Reuse does the same drop in the client without saying so. The user believes they are re-making the image and gets one with none of its conditioning.

findings.title: Gallery cards carry no prompt, seed, size or run, and there are no run breaks, so finding a past image means opening images one by one
surfaces: Gallery card
Gallery grid as a whole (cards, run boundaries)
findings.recommendation:
(1) In thumb() (panel.js:285) set `img.title = `${rec.width}×${rec.height} · seed ${rec.seed}${rec.refine != null ? ` · refine of ${rec.refine} @ ${rec.strength}` : ''}\n${rec.prompt}``. It costs nothing and keeps alt and aria-label.
(2) The refined badge from M5.
(3) In loadGallery's append loop (gallery.js:54-58), insert `<div class="gallery-break" style="grid-column:1/-1">` when the local day changes between consecutive records. A run_id break is optional, since the sheet already serves runs. Have forgetImages drop a divider left with no cards.
(4) Lightbox count (lightbox.js:114): when lbList === galleryRecords, show `${i}/${total}`, or append '+' while galleryMore.
Do not add a two-line caption under every card at QHD. It cuts 12 columns to about 9 and pushes rows below the fold. If a caption is wanted, make it a hover/focus overlay.
findings.documented_rule: design-notes 'Paging by id' and CLAUDE.md: the gallery pages by id and forgetImages is the one place deleted ids are dropped. thumb() (panel.js:285) is shared by the strip, the cards and the sheet. Neither rule says anything about captions.
findings.rule_tension: Compatible. A title, a badge and dividers carry no data-id, so paging and forgetImages are untouched. An emptied divider should be removed in forgetImages. The 'Load more' observer is unaffected by dividers.
findings.smokes_affected: None found. No smoke counts #gallery children or reads lb-count. smoke-paging.json counts '.card' only, which dividers would not change.
findings.how_checked: FLUX fake on 7906 with 60 images (12/row at 2560). I read the card DOM (img title, alt, aria-label, card innerText, className) and the refined card next to its source. I checked loadGallery's append loop for any grouping, and read the lightbox count against the loaded and total lengths.
findings.verifier_notes: Lowered to low. Every fake image is the same gradient, which overstates the problem. Real thumbnails show the actual picture, and same-prompt seed/steps sweeps have the contact sheet. What survives is no hover information (no title at all), no break between runs or days, and a misleading lightbox denominator. The tool-glyph part of walkthrough-11 duplicates M15, and the refined-card point duplicates M5's badge.
findings.merge_note: walkthrough-11 adds that a refined 2048 card is identical to its 1024 source, and proposes 220 px cards with a two-line caption. It also flags the unlabelled tool glyphs (M15).

sources.surface: Gallery grid as a whole (cards, run boundaries)
sources.observation: With 145 images the grid is 12 identical squares per row: no prompt, seed, size, date or run shown, and no break between runs. A 72-image grid sits flush against 4-image batches. thumb() sets alt and aria-label to the prompt but no title, so hovering a card shows nothing about the image. To learn one image's seed or prompt you open the lightbox. The lightbox counter then says '6/96' of the loaded records, not the 144 that match.
sources.why_it_matters: The user asked whether finding a past image is fast. It is only fast if you already know a search term. Visual scanning gets no help, and every 'which one was that?' costs a lightbox open and close.

sources.surface: Gallery card
sources.observation: Cards are 172x172 px (12 per row across 2176 px) with no caption. In Task 4 the two lighthouse prompts and their seeds could only be told apart by opening each. In Task 3 the 2048 refined card was identical to its 1024 source. On hover, a strip of six glyph-only buttons appears (↻ ⤢ ❐ ⊞ ★ ⌦, measured 23-29 x 24 px), only visible on hover. It includes ❐ 'Use as a reference image' on FLUX, which takes none (the click only explains that), and ⌦ Delete next to ★.
sources.why_it_matters: Finding an earlier image (Task 4) and acting on the right one depend on these cards. With glyphs, hover-only and adjacency, the user guesses, and the misses are the expensive ones (Reuse overwrite, Delete).

findings.title: In the wide host the prompt check stretches to 2161 px: finding text ends about 1200 px from its source badge, and the cite is hidden in a title
surfaces: .analysis-list > .analysis-item (Findings, and the rewrite's findings)
Prompt check panel (#prompt-analysis) in the wide host above the results
findings.recommendation: Adopt M3's side column. With it the findings column is about 735 px, and the measured text-to-badge gap falls from 825-1414 px to 35 px or less, with Your version about 735 px wide. For the full-width fallback (901-1799 px, or if M3 is not adopted): `.analysis-list, .compare-own, .critic-result .analysis-text { max-width: 120ch; }`, so a finding's badge sits at most about 800 px from where its text starts. Optional, at any width: when a guide or author cite is under about 80 characters, render it after the message as `<q class="analysis-cite">` (`color: var(--muted); font-style: italic`) and keep the title for long encoder cites (133 characters here). Do not apply visual-6's two-column body inside the side column.
findings.documented_rule: CLAUDE.md Prompt analyser: 'Every finding says what it rests on: source, cite and url'; a heuristic has no cite. style.css:398-400: 'a mark, the message, and what it rests on at the right'. Focus goes to the panel heading after Check (scroll-margin-top 72px).
findings.rule_tension: Capping line length and moving short cites inline keeps the badge, its link and its title, so every finding still shows its source, cite and URL. Heuristic findings keep their title text. visual-6's two-column .analysis-body at 2000 px or more conflicts with M3's side column: it would split a 735 px column into two of about 350 px. Apply it only where the panel is full-width.
findings.smokes_affected: None fail. smoke-analysis.json step 16 expects the warn finding's label.title.length > 0 and an href starting https://docs.bfl.ai/, so keep the title and link on the badge if the cite also goes inline. No smoke asserts the findings' geometry.
findings.how_checked: FLUX fake, the 76-word harbour prompt at 2560x1305, Check. For each finding, measured the text's right edge with a Range over .analysis-message, the .analysis-source rect and its title (the cite), plus #compare-own's rect and font. Repeated with the corrected side-column CSS from M3 injected.
findings.verifier_notes: Real, and it matches both source findings to the pixel. But the same width problem is what M3 fixes: once the check sits in a 520-760 px side column at 1800 px or more, finding text and badge are 13-35 px apart, and Your version is no longer 300 characters wide. On the target screen, what is left is the cite being hover-only, which is polish, so severity drops to low. It would stay medium if M3 is not adopted. Not marked a duplicate because the cite-in-title issue and the fallback below 1800 px stand on their own.
findings.merge_note: analysis-4 measures 825-1414 px gaps between each claim and its badge, and proposes a 120ch cap with the cite inline. visual-6 adds that 'Your version' becomes a 300-character-wide line, and proposes two columns above 2000 px.

sources.surface: Prompt check panel (#prompt-analysis) in the wide host above the results
sources.observation: On a two-column page the check sits in #tag-validation-wide and takes the full stage width (2161px at 2560). Findings use `grid-template-columns: 16px minmax(0,1fr) auto`. Each message starts at x=410, short ones end near x=1240, and the source badge (GUIDE/ENCODER) sits at x=2459-2476. A finding longer than about 1200px of 12px text runs to x=2451 on one line. The 'Your version' textarea is 2150px wide at 12px, roughly 300 characters per line. Encoders and Order fill only the left 600px of their row. The panel is 540px tall and pushes the viewer from y=76 to y=634 and the gallery heading from 1219 to 1776.
sources.why_it_matters: The eye has to cross 1200px to tie a finding to its source, and a 300-character line is unreadable for a prompt the user is editing. Meanwhile half a screen of height goes to whitespace, and the results are pushed below the fold while the user checks the prompt they are about to run.

sources.surface: .analysis-list > .analysis-item (Findings, and the rewrite's findings)
sources.observation: Each finding's message cell is 2058 px wide. The text ends at x=1047-1636, while its GUIDE/ENCODER badge sits at x=2444-2461: 825-1414 px of blank row between a claim and what it rests on. The cite itself (the authors' words) appears only in a native title on the 46x17 px, 10 px badge, even though it is short: 'text in quotation marks' (23 characters), 'no negative prompt without True CFG' (35). Apply sits on a separate line under the message: 41x19 px, 10 px muted text.
sources.why_it_matters: The panel's main promise is that each finding shows its source. At QHD the eye has to cross most of the screen to connect a finding to its source, and the cite needs a hover-and-wait. Tooltips also fail with keyboard focus and are read by no one.

findings.title: Nearly every size preset is 'recommended' green, so green carries no meaning and the selected preset barely stands out
surfaces: Size presets (#presets, #tiers)
Size: aspect strip, MP tiers
findings.recommendation: Make the selection read first: `.presets button.active, .presets button.active.recommended { background: var(--accent); border-color: var(--accent); color: #fff; }`. Mark recommendation with a mark, not a fill: `.presets button.recommended { color: var(--text); border-color: #287548; background: var(--panel-2); } .presets button.recommended::after { content: ''; display: inline-block; width: 5px; height: 5px; margin-left: 5px; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--ok); vertical-align: 2px; }`. In syncSize, call `b.setAttribute('aria-pressed', String(b.classList.contains('active')))` on both strips. Optionally, `els.presets.classList.toggle('all-guided', every aspect guided)` drops the dots where they say nothing (FLUX's aspect row, everything on Turbo), leaving the tier row and the size line to carry the range.
findings.documented_rule: design-notes 'The prompting guide' and sizes.js:126-134: the buttons and the size line share one 'within range' definition (presetIsInGuide, a tenth either way), and each strip previews the preset a click would choose. describePreset writes the title and aria wording. .pair draws a portrait/landscape pair as one segmented box.
findings.rule_tension: The fix is a restyle only. presetIsInGuide, the .recommended and .active classes and describePreset's wording stay. Adding aria-pressed and an optional all-guided container class changes no logic.
findings.smokes_affected: None if the classes stay: smoke-flux.json:9-19, smoke.json:17, smoke-animagine.json:65-66 and 80, smoke-illustrious.json:28 and smoke-z-anime.json:17 read .recommended and .active.
findings.how_checked: On the FLUX (7902), Animagine (8902) and Krea 2 Turbo (8902, restarted) fakes, counted .recommended and .active across the aspect and tier strips at 1 MP and again after choose() moved to 2 MP or 4 MP. Read the computed colours and aria attributes, computed WCAG contrast ratios between the active and recommended states, and took an element shot of #presets.
findings.verifier_notes: 'Green carries no meaning' holds for Turbo and for FLUX's aspect row only. The tier row is informative on FLUX, and the aspect row is informative on checkpoints with an aspect list (Animagine). The weak active state and the missing aria-pressed are real; the screen-reader gap is the most concrete cost. Downgraded to low (polish) from panel-9's medium, in line with visual-10.
findings.merge_note: visual-10 measures 13 of 13 aspects green on FLUX, outshining the prompt, and proposes an all-guided class that draws them plain.

sources.surface: Size: aspect strip, MP tiers
sources.observation: On Krea 2 Turbo all 17 buttons (13 aspects + 4 tiers) are 'recommended' green (f01 crop). On FLUX 15 of 17 are. The active preset differs from its recommended neighbours by background contrast of only 1.37:1 (rgb 23,65,40 vs 17,39,26) and text contrast of 1.61:1 (#d8ffe5 vs #4ade80). Border contrast is 3.23:1. In the 2x crop, 1:1 and 1 MP read as only slightly brighter. The active button has no aria-pressed, and its aria-label says only '1:1, within the size range this checkpoint is recommended for', so a screen reader can't tell which preset is chosen. The strip plus Orientation takes 3 rows, about 95 px.
sources.why_it_matters: The current size is the most important state in this block, and it is the least visible. When every button is green, the 'recommended' cue no longer separates good choices from risky ones. The real signal ('above the 1.6 MP this checkpoint is recommended for') is in an 11px line below the strip.

sources.surface: Size presets (#presets, #tiers)
sources.observation: On the FLUX.1 Krea fake, 13 of 13 aspect pills and 2 of 4 MP tiers carry `.recommended`: #4ade80 text on #11271a with a #287548 border. They form the largest saturated block in the panel, two rows of bright green pills at 11px. The active pick (1:1, 1 MP) differs only by a slightly brighter fill.
sources.why_it_matters: When everything is recommended the highlight carries no information, but it still pulls the eye away from the prompt and Generate. The selected size is hard to pick out of 13 green pills.

findings.title: The card tool row overflows the card: Delete is clipped, and the reference tool stays live on a checkpoint without references
surfaces: Gallery card hover tools (↻ ⤢ ❐ ⊞ ☆ ⌦)
findings.recommendation: (a) Make the row fit at any card width: `.card .tools button { flex: 1 1 0; min-width: 0; padding: 3px 0; }`. Six buttons then share the row at about 23px each in a 171px card, and about 21px at the grid's 160px minimum, with no overflow. (b) On a checkpoint without the capability, give ❐ (when !referenceSupported) and the card's ⤢ (when !refineSupported) `aria-disabled="true"` and a title naming the reason, plus `.card .tools [aria-disabled=true] { opacity: .35 }`. The click keeps explaining, as #lb-refine does. Cards can render before /api/status answers, so set this in card() and refresh it from the status handler, where syncReuseButtons() already runs: give the two tools classes and query `.card .tools .ref-tool, .card .tools .refine-tool`. (c) Separate the star from Delete by moving the star onto the badge (M85); Delete then follows ⊞. Drop the proposed caption strip: aria-label and title already name every tool, and it adds a moving part for little gain. Card size belongs to another cluster.
findings.documented_rule: CLAUDE.md Frontend and CLI: 'A ⤢ on a checkpoint without a pass says so and opens nothing'. style.css:796-798 comment: tools are revealed by keyboard focus and on coarse pointers. gallery.js tool(): every tool keeps an aria-label. confirmDelete names the image. lightbox.js:117-121 sets aria-disabled on #lb-refine with its reason as the title.
findings.rule_tension: Making ❐ and ⤢ aria-disabled (never disabled) keeps the tab stop and the explaining click. That is the pattern the lightbox's Refine already follows, so it fits the ⤢ rule. Equal-width flex buttons change no behaviour.
findings.smokes_affected: smoke-conditioning.json:28 clicks the card's ⤢ on klein and expects the 'no refine pass' error; it still passes because the click still explains. Add an aria-disabled expect there if (b) lands. smoke-conditioning.json:32 clicks ❐ on klein (referenceSupported true), so it is unaffected. smoke-refine.json:20 clicks ⤢ on FLUX, also unaffected. All of them find tools by glyph in '.card .tools button', so moving the star out of .tools breaks none of them.
findings.how_checked: FLUX fake on 7907. I measured every card's .tools children with getBoundingClientRect against the card's clientWidth at QHD and at 2048@1.25. I hovered card 6 (1344x768) and the starred card 3 with a real mouse and took elshots. I checked the ❐ button's aria state with referenceSupported false, clicked it, and read the #error slot's text and rect.
findings.verifier_notes: Every fact in the finding reproduces. Lowered from medium to low: the clipped Delete still works (about 23px of its 29px remain visible and clickable), the dead ❐ explains itself on the first press, and a slip onto Delete is caught by confirmDelete. The card's ⤢ has the same unmarked-dead problem on checkpoints with no pass, so fix both together for consistency with the lightbox.

sources.surface: Gallery card hover tools (↻ ⤢ ❐ ⊞ ☆ ⌦)
sources.observation: At QHD 100% a card is 170.9px wide. The six tools are 23/23/25/26/24/29px wide and 24px tall, with 4px gaps and 6px padding, so the row needs about 176px and the Delete glyph is cut off at the card's right edge (overflow: hidden). At 2048@1.25 the row ends at 177px in a 174px card. The glyphs are 12px and only native title tooltips name them (no visible label; the tooltip appears after a delay). Delete sits 4px from the star. ❐ 'Use as a reference image' is offered on FLUX.1 Krea, which takes no references; pressing it only writes an error into the panel's slot at (35,1003). ↻ means Reuse here, but the header uses ↻ for Re-render (gallery-14).
sources.why_it_matters: These buttons are the gallery's main actions: Refine, Reuse, star, delete. Six unlabeled 12px glyphs, one clipped and one dead, have to be learned by hovering each one. A slip from the star lands on Delete. That is guarded by a confirm, but it still costs a dialog.

findings.title: After Refine, all feedback moves to the panel 1,000 px away, and a submit-time refusal loses the dialog
surfaces: Refine dialog submit handoff: progress, queue note, error line, viewer
findings.recommendation: (1) In runRefine (refine.js:371-373), close the dialog only once the POST has answered. Split startJob (generation.js:124-171) into a submit step that returns the job_id and the existing watch/queue step, or pass an onAccepted callback. On a refusal, call refineFailed(err.message) and leave the dialog and its edits open. (2) At submit, record a label per queued job id ('refine of image 10'), so syncQueueNote (generation.js:65-69) says '1 refine of image 10 queued behind this one' instead of '1 more job'. (3) When a refine result lands in the viewer, set #viewer-note to 'Refined from image 10 at 0.5 · 1344×1728', with a button that opens the source in the lightbox; the lightbox meta already says 'refine of 10 @ 0.5'. Drop the proposed 'short-lived line near the viewer top': when nothing is queued, the pass's live preview already appears at the centre of the stage.
findings.documented_rule: refine.js:354-357: 'Refine: the dialog closes and the job queues like Generate's - behind a running one if there is one, its progress in the panel, its images in the strip'. CLAUDE.md Frontend: startJob(path, body, { sheet, panel: false }) 'never writes the panel's Seed box'. Design notes: 'A source deleted while the dialog is open is the server's to refuse at submit, by name.'
findings.rule_tension: Awaiting the POST before closing keeps every rule: the job still queues like Generate's, panel:false still never writes Seed, a sweep is still added to jobsToShow, and the server still refuses the deleted source by name, only now inside the dialog (#refine-error). The refine.js comment and the smoke description of the deleted-source case change wording only.
findings.smokes_affected: smoke-refine.json step 127 expects the deleted-source case to close the dialog and put 'no gallery image with id …' in els.error. It would need to expect els.refineDialog.open and the text in els.refineError. Steps 42 and 93 (dialog closed after a successful run) are unaffected because acceptance comes first. Step 72 (a sweep opening as its sheet) is unaffected.
findings.how_checked: A second FLUX fake on 8910 with --step 0.3. Started a batch-4 Generate, opened ⤢ while it ran, clicked Refine, and read the dialog, progress, queue note and error rects. Waited for both jobs and read the viewer, #last-run and lightbox meta. Repeated with nothing running and a strength-0.5 pass (14 steps) to see what the stage shows. Then deleted the source through the API while the dialog was open with a prompt edit, and pressed Refine.
findings.verifier_notes: Partly reproduced. 'All feedback moves to the panel' is overstated: when the pass runs at once, the stage at the centre shows its live preview. The real gaps are three. In the queued case (rarer, and announced beforehand by 'Refine (queue)'), the confirmation is an 11px generic line in the panel. The finished image carries no 'refined from' in the viewer. A submit-time refusal loses the dialog, but that is rare, because every edit already runs the same validation through /api/grid/preview, so in practice only a source deleted elsewhere reaches it. Hence low, down from medium. Process warning for the orchestrator: my first run of this flow was hijacked mid-wait. shot.mjs picks a DevTools port at random from 9333-9832, another agent's driver landed on the same port, and it navigated my headless tab to its own fake server, showing a prompt-check page at a different viewport. I discarded that run and re-ran with every eval guarded by a location.port check; the evidence above comes from the guarded run. Before I noticed, two of my steps may have run in that agent's page: setting refineMore.open and refinePrompt on a closed dialog, and a refineRun click that returns early with no source. Both are harmless, but other verifiers' long-wait runs could be contaminated the same way.

sources.surface: Refine dialog submit handoff: progress, queue note, error line, viewer
sources.observation: Pressing Refine at (1371,871) closes the dialog at once. Progress then shows as a 296x26 bar at (35,972), bottom-left in the panel. With a job running, the button reads 'Refine (queue)' and, after the click, the only trace is '1 more job queued behind this one.' at 11 px in the panel, which does not say it is a refine of image 4. The panel's main button reads 'Generate (queue)'. The finished pass appears in the viewer (887x887) with no link to its source. runRefine closes the dialog before startJob's POST resolves, so a refusal at submit (here 'no gallery image with id 5', the source deleted while the dialog was open) appears in the panel's error line at (35,1003) at 12 px, and the edited prompt in the fold is gone.
sources.why_it_matters: The user's attention is centre-screen. With no in-place acknowledgement it is unclear whether the click took, what was queued, and which image the result came from. A refusal costs the user's dialog edits.

findings.title: The prompt check uses 10-12 px type and 19 px buttons; primary actions look disabled, and Close is 2,300 px from Check
surfaces: .prompt-analysis typography and buttons
findings.recommendation: Move the type-size part into the page-wide QHD typography finding instead of a panel-only override. Introduce size tokens (for example --fs-xs/--fs-sm/--fs-base) used by .ghost.tiny, .hint, .analysis-source, h3s and .prompt-analysis, and raise them together at min-width 1800px (10->12, 11->12.5, 12->13.5, 14->15). Panel-specific, keep: (a) the two actions the panel builds towards get an enabled look: `#critic-ask:not([aria-disabled="true"]), #compare-run:not(:disabled):not([aria-disabled="true"]) { color: var(--text); border-color: var(--accent); background: rgba(124,92,255,0.12); }`; (b) `.analysis-head .analysis-close { min-width: 28px; min-height: 28px; padding: 4px 8px; }`. Drop the 'Close is 2,300 px from Check' point: Close sits in the panel's own head, where the user is looking, and with M3 at the side column's top right.
findings.documented_rule: CLAUDE.md Frontend: 'Ask the critic is aria-disabled, never disabled, so it keeps focus'. Run comparison's disabled vs aria-disabled semantics. The stale state: 'dimmed, every Use/Apply and Run comparison dead' (design-notes 'The prompt analyser': stale results stay visible, dimmed, with 'Check again' and the badge at full strength). style.css:173 '.ghost.tiny' and :612 '.ghost:disabled, .ghost[aria-disabled=true] { opacity: 0.45 }' are page-wide.
findings.rule_tension: Styling the enabled state of the two call-to-action buttons leaves both disabled semantics intact; selectors must exclude both [aria-disabled="true"] and :disabled. The stale dimming of dead buttons (0.55 x 0.45 = 0.25) is the documented stale state working as designed and should stay. The type-size part conflicts with nothing documented, but it is page-wide: raising only the panel would make it outgrow the sidebar's 10-11 px labels.
findings.smokes_affected: None at the panel level: no smoke asserts panel font sizes or button colours. smoke-animagine.json has one computed-style expect (.tag-check.valid fontSize === '12px'). The smokes run at 1400x900, so a token change gated at 1800px leaves it passing; if the tokens also change below 1800px, that step must be updated.
findings.how_checked: FLUX fake at 2560x1305: getComputedStyle font sizes, colours, borders and opacity in the panel, and rects of Check, Close, Apply, Ask the critic and Run comparison. Run comparison was measured enabled (a Your version typed) and disabled. Opacity was measured in the stale state. Font sizes of every visible text element in the settings aside were counted for comparison, with elshots of the panel.
findings.verifier_notes: The measurements reproduce exactly. Three corrections. The panel's 10-12 px type is the page's standard scale, not an outlier: the sidebar is mostly 10-11 px, so this belongs with a page-wide QHD typography fix, where it may well be medium. 'Primary actions look disabled' is overstated: enabled is muted grey at full opacity and disabled the same at 0.45. Both read as tertiary, and opacity is the only cue between the states. The stale 25% buttons are intended. What remains specific to the panel is CTA emphasis and Close's target size, which is polish.

sources.surface: .prompt-analysis typography and buttons
sources.observation: Inside the panel: body text 12px/17.4px; section heads 11px uppercase muted; source and stale badges 10px; every small button (Check, Apply, Use reordered, Use rewrite, Start from the prompt, Check again) is 10 px text in a 41-79 x 19 px box. Close (✕) is 20x15 px at x=2494, 2,300 px from Check at x=182. The panel's two main actions, Ask the critic (92x33) and Run comparison (110x33), are ghost buttons with muted grey text rgb(139,139,154) on no fill. A disabled Run comparison looks the same at 0.45 opacity. In the stale state, disabled buttons inside the 0.55-dimmed body end up at about 25% opacity. The page's own base size is 14 px.
sources.why_it_matters: At QHD and 100% scaling, 10 px text is hard to read. 19 px targets slow every Apply and Use. When enabled looks like disabled, people hesitate before Ask the critic and Run comparison, the two actions the panel builds towards.

findings.title: Valid chips all look the same, with no category, order group or duplicate mark, though the order rule depends on them
surfaces: Tag validation chips
findings.recommendation: Colour the valid chip's left edge by the fact the lookup returned, not by an order slot. Use result.category for Danbooru tags (character, copyright, artist, general, meta) and 'guide' for source 'model', on a 3px border-left in a Danbooru-like palette. Keep the ✓, the light text and the charcoal background. Unknown and unchecked chips get no category colour. Add a short legend as ::after text or a title, not as a child element. If chips should show order slots, the server must supply them: add `slot` to TagValidationResult from the guide's analysis.order (groups, categories, suffix, year), so the page never maps anything itself. Mark later copies by equal `canonical` with a .duplicate class (amber dotted outline, title 'repeated: adds nothing (heuristic)'), matching Check's heuristic.repeated.
findings.documented_rule: design-notes 'Animagine XL 4.0' (docs/design-notes.md:1840): a valid chip keeps light text on charcoal, with green only on the mark and outline. CLAUDE.md:501, 'order placed from the guide's own groups, never guessed'. CLAUDE.md:641, 'the page has no reorder rule of its own'. The category-to-slot mapping lives server-side in each guide's analysis.order.categories and groups.
findings.rule_tension: Mapping categories to order groups in the client, as the finding proposes, would be a second copy of analysis.order, and orders differ per checkpoint. Animagine: Person count → Character → Series → Rating → Details → Quality. Kohaku has Artist, Date and Meta slots and puts Rating last. Illustrious puts Rating third and has an Artist slot. WAI has only Subject and scene, then Quality, with Rating mapped to Subject and scene. The finding's palette (artist → Artist, general → Details) is already wrong for Animagine, where artist and meta map to Details. Showing the Danbooru category is not a placement. It is data /api/tags/validate already returns, so it is compatible.
findings.smokes_affected: smoke-animagine 11 asserts the valid chip's fontSize 12px, color rgb(242,244,247) and background rgb(23,25,28). A border-left colour keeps those. Steps that iterate `els.tagValidation.children` (animagine 10 and 14, illustrious 13, 21 and 24, kohaku 12 and 17, wai 17) break only if a legend is inserted as a child element.
findings.how_checked: 12-tag prompt on the Animagine fake: person count, character, series, rating, details, a duplicated 'green hair', guide quality tags. I read each chip's class and title, compared computed border, background, colour and border-left width across the valid chips, then pressed Check.
findings.verifier_notes: Real, but polish. Check (one click) names the out-of-order tag and the repeat, and Use reordered fixes the order in one more click, so the cost is a click and a context switch, not an error. That makes it low. The finding's client-side slot mapping would break a documented rule and be wrong on Kohaku, Illustrious and WAI. I corrected the recommendation to category colour, with server-supplied slots if wanted.

sources.surface: Tag validation chips
sources.observation: In the 18-tag prompt, '1girl' (person count), 'firefly (honkai: star rail)' (character), 'honkai: star rail' (series), 'safe' (rating), 'smile' (details) and 'masterpiece' (quality) all render as the same green-outlined charcoal pill with ✓. The category is only in a native title ('Danbooru character tag · 15.4k posts'). The guide's order is Person count → Character → Series → Rating → Details → Quality. With 'safe' appended after 'absurdres', the out-of-order tag was visible only by pressing Check and reading '"green hair" (Details) comes before "safe" (Rating)'. A repeated 'smile' showed two identical green chips. The Check has a heuristic for repeats (prompt_rules._repeated), but the chips do not mark them.
sources.why_it_matters: The chips exist so tags can be reordered by drag, but they show nothing about the property the reorder is for. Users have to cross-reference a separate panel to know where a chip belongs, or hover each chip and wait for a tooltip.

findings.title: Ctrl+Enter and the lightbox keys are never shown, and Generate is 36 Tab stops from the prompt
surfaces: Generate button, lightbox side column, Refine button
findings.recommendation:
1) Add `#btn-generate::after, #refine-run::after { content: 'Ctrl+Enter' / ''; margin-left: 8px; font-size: 11px; font-weight: 400; opacity: .7; }` (the `/ ''` alt syntax keeps it out of the accessible name; Chromium, Firefox 128+, Safari 17.4+), and set `aria-keyshortcuts="Control+Enter"` plus `title="Generate (Ctrl+Enter)"` on #btn-generate in index.html:262. The other route is to wrap the label in a span that setBusy writes instead of the button. 2) In the lightbox, add `

← → walk · F star · Del delete · 0 fit · 1 1:1 · +/− zoom · Esc close

` between #lb-meta and .lb-zoom-group (index.html:510-517), outside #lb-meta. That column has 945 px of measured empty height at QHD. Hide the line in the narrow layout (style.css:951-956), where .lb-meta is capped at 6em. Drop the '36 Tab stops' angle as a separate fix: Ctrl+Enter already solves it once it is visible.

sources.surface: Generate button, lightbox side column, Refine button

findings.title: On FLUX the box labelled 'CFG' is, by its own tip, not CFG; True CFG and Mu go unexplained in their labels
surfaces: Panel Steps/CFG/Mu/True CFG row, negative-prompt note, lightbox settings line
findings.recommendation: 1) Give Mu the placeholder 'auto' whenever the profile's mu is null and mu_supported is true (status.js applies defaults; set els.mu.placeholder, and the grid Mu box's, from defaults.mu == null). A blank box then reads as the pipeline's own shift, which is what the tip says. 2) Use the panel's casing in the lightbox: 'True CFG' and 'Mu' / 'no Mu' (lightbox.js:104-107). 3) Optionally, a profile `labels` hint for the FLUX.1 family, {guidance_scale: 'CFG (distilled)'}, applied by applyHints to the panel's and the grid's CFG labels, ids unchanged. 'True CFG (negative)' does not fit a 68 px box at 11 px unless the panel widens. 4) Keep the negative note's wording: it is correct and the smokes match it.
findings.documented_rule: design-notes 'True CFG is its own field': True CFG is greyed, not hidden, and the negative prompt follows whichever box decides. CLAUDE.md: 'krea-dev ... is the flux profile in every number and control hint'. Guide prose (hints.prompt) is the authors' and cannot be reworded.
findings.rule_tension: The key claim of the finding fails: a user who raises CFG on FLUX cannot make the negative bite unnoticed, because the negative box stays greyed and its caption names True CFG (verified at CFG 7). Relabelling the box 'Guidance' would contradict the authors' own 'CFG 3.5-5' in the Prompt tip, the `cfg:` search key, the grid's CFG axis and the lightbox. A qualifier keeps the word CFG. A labels hint must sit on the flux profile so krea-dev inherits it. Ids and request field names stay.
findings.smokes_affected: smoke-flux.json:45 expects els.lbMeta.textContent to include 'CFG 3.5, true CFG 1.5', so recasing to 'True CFG' needs that step updated. smoke-flux.json:29 ('needs True CFG > 1'), smoke.json:148 ('needs CFG > 0') and smoke-animagine.json:79 ('CFG > 1') constrain the negative note, so the proposed rewording to 'only with True CFG above 1' would break all three; keep it. No smoke reads the #cfg label text or the Mu placeholder.
findings.how_checked: Fresh profile on 7920 (FLUX.1 Krea [dev]), resetPanel(). Logged the panel labels ['Steps','CFG','Mu','True CFG'] and the CFG tip ('...not classifier-free guidance. The negative prompt is driven by True CFG, the box beside this one.'). The negative note reads '(needs True CFG > 1 — ~2× slower)'. Set CFG to 7: the negative stayed disabled and the note still names True CFG. The Mu input's placeholder is '' (empty). True CFG shows 'off'. Read lightbox.js:104-107: 'CFG 3.5', 'true CFG x', 'no mu'. Read the FLUX hints: the author-sourced prompt guide says 'Krea recommends 28-32 steps and CFG 3.5-5.' The Steps/CFG/Mu/True CFG row is 296 px wide, about 68 px per box.
findings.verifier_notes: Partly reproduced. The naming quirks are real: two boxes both say CFG, Mu is blank and unexplained, and the lightbox uses lowercase 'true CFG' and 'no mu'. The harm the finding describes does not happen: the UI already blocks it and the note names the right box. The authors call the guidance value 'CFG', so a rename to 'Guidance' fights the guide; the qualifier and the Mu placeholder are the compatible fixes. Low severity.

sources.surface: Panel Steps/CFG/Mu/True CFG row, negative-prompt note, lightbox settings line
sources.observation: On the default checkpoint (FLUX.1 Krea), the 3.5 box is labelled 'CFG', and its own tip says 'this is the distilled guidance value … not classifier-free guidance'. The next box, 'True CFG', is the real CFG. The negative prompt's caption says '(needs True CFG > 1 — ~2× slower)'. 'Mu' is labelled only 'Mu', and its tip says 'Flow-matching timestep shift … leave this blank'. The lightbox and its settings line say 'CFG 3.5, no mu' (lowercase 'mu', and 'true CFG' in lightbox.js), and the search tip uses 'tcfg:'. Four labels are jargon, and the one a FLUX user reads first is wrong for the checkpoint.
sources.why_it_matters: A user who turns up 'CFG' to make the negative prompt bite gets nothing: the negative follows True CFG. Without an explanatory label, the greyed negative box looks broken.

findings.title: 'Run' means three different things, and Batch/Runs have no help badge
surfaces: Panel Seed/Batch/Runs row, gallery 'Runs…' picker, Last run banner, progress text
findings.recommendation: Keep 'run' for a submission and rename the panel's count. 1) index.html:257: change the label to 'Repeat'; id 'runs', the persistence key, request field and --runs are unchanged. 2) sizes.js:236-244: change the hint to '6 images: 3 batches of 2, one after another, seed +2 each, from a random start.' and '2 images at once — all held in VRAM together.', dropping 'pass', which is the Refine dialog's word. 3) generation.js:407-409: show progress as 'batch 2/3' for a plain repeat and 'cell 5/24' for a grid (the job snapshot already distinguishes the two), matching the banner's '(3/4 cells)'. 4) Add a ? badge on Batch: 'Images rendered at once, all held in VRAM. 'Run' already means the submission in the picker, the run: search key, the Last run banner, Show run and app.js:215. findings.how_checked: On 7920: set Batch 2 and Runs 3, and the hint read '6 images over 3 passes, seed +2 each, from a random start.'. Batch 2 alone gives '2 images in one pass — all held in VRAM together.', and the defaults give ''. The panel has 17 help badges; Seed, Batch and Runs have none. sources.surface: Panel Seed/Batch/Runs row, gallery 'Runs…' picker, Last run banner, progress text
sources.observation: 'Runs' in the panel is the number of sequential batches. The gallery's 'Runs…' select lists grid runs (a run_id, the `run:` search key). The 'Last run finished at 4 Oct, 03:40 pm' banner and its 'Show run' button refer to the last job, and progress shows 'run 2/4'.
