findings.title: Placeholders, the Generate label and a stale prompt check fall below WCAG contrast
surfaces: All inputs' placeholders, Generate/Run grid buttons, the stale prompt check
findings.recommendation: 1) `::placeholder { color: var(--muted); opacity: 1; }` gives 5.16:1 on --panel-2 and is still clearly distinct from typed values (#e8e8ee). 2) Give .primary its own background, #6d4ff2 (white 5.18:1), and keep --accent for borders, active presets and the progress gradient. 14px/600 is not large text (that needs 18.66px bold), so 4.35:1 fails AA, narrowly. 3) Change style.css:333 to `.prompt-analysis.stale .analysis-body { opacity: .8; --muted: #a2a2b0; }`, if the body's muted text reads var(--muted), or else add an explicit colour rule for .analysis-note/.critic-line. Composited on --panel this gives muted 5.11:1, #b2b2c0 6.04:1, body text 9.94:1 and amber 7.41:1, against 2.52, 3.49, 5.26 and 4.09 today.
findings.documented_rule: CLAUDE.md Frontend: a stale check is 'dimmed, every Use/Apply and Run comparison dead'. style.css:323: 'Stale results stay readable - they are still the last answer - but dimmed'. style.css:597: aria-disabled .primary at opacity .5.
findings.rule_tension: The rule requires a visible dim, not a particular opacity. At .8 opacity with the muted token lifted inside the stale body, the panel is still visibly dimmed (body text drops from 15.2:1 to 9.9:1). The amber 'PROMPT CHANGED SINCE' badge and the dead Use/Apply buttons carry the stale signal. The aria-disabled Generate at .5 is an inactive control and is exempt under 1.4.3, so it can stay.
findings.smokes_affected: None. No smoke checks opacity, placeholder colour or the .primary background. smoke-animagine.json:13 checks only the tag chip's colour and font.
findings.how_checked: On 7920, read getComputedStyle(el,'::placeholder').color for #prompt, #seed, #true-cfg, #search and #grid-budget: rgb(117,117,117) on rgb(26,26,33). Generate is rgb(255,255,255) on rgb(124,92,255) at 14px/600. Ran Check on a prose prompt, then typed into the prompt to make it stale: .analysis-body opacity 0.55, host #tag-validation-wide with --panel rgb(19,19,24). Listed the text colours inside the body: 8b8b9a, e8e8ee, b2b2c0, fbbf24, 4ad6c8. No a2a2b0 there. Computed WCAG ratios in Python with alpha compositing.
findings.verifier_notes: All three shortfalls reproduce: placeholder 3.76, Generate 4.35, stale muted 2.52. One correction: the finding's '#a2a2b0 at 3.07' is for a colour not used in the analysis body. The summary-grey text there is #b2b2c0, at 3.49 when stale. Two of the three are near misses (3.76 and 4.35 against 4.5), and the stale panel is one Check again away from fresh, so low rather than medium. All three fixes are CSS-only. Both fake servers (7920, 8920) were stopped and the repo is unchanged (git status clean).

sources.surface: All inputs' placeholders, Generate/Run grid buttons, the stale prompt check
sources.observation: Computed: the placeholder colour is the UA default #757575 on #1a1a21, which is 3.76:1 (AA needs 4.5:1). The placeholders carry state: Seed 'random', True CFG 'off', Budget 'min', and the grid syntax examples. White on --accent #7c5cff, the Generate and Run grid label (14px/600), is 4.35:1. The stale check dims .analysis-body to opacity .55 (measured), which puts muted notes at 2.52:1 and #a2a2b0 text at 3.07:1, although the CSS comment says stale results 'stay readable - they are still the last answer'. For reference, muted #8b8b9a on the panel is 5.52:1 and passes.
sources.why_it_matters: Users read 'random' and 'off' to know what a blank box will do, and the stale check is meant to stay readable as the last answer. At these ratios, on a dark QHD panel at 11-14 px, the text washes out.

findings.title: The gallery search box is capped at 240 px with a truncated placeholder beside 1,000+ px of empty header
surfaces: Gallery head search box
Gallery header (search, ? grammar, Runs select)
findings.recommendation: (1) `@media (min-width: 2000px) { .gallery-head input[type=search] { max-width: 480px } }` (style.css:707). (2) Keep the Runs select showing the run on screen by syncing it from the search, not from the select's own change event. In resetGallery (web/gallery.js:7) and at the end of loadRuns (panel.js:205), run `const m = /^run:([0-9a-f]+)$/.exec(els.search.value.trim()); els.runList.value = m && [...els.runList.options].some(o => o.value === m[1]) ? m[1] : '';`, and drop `els.runList.value = ''` from app.js:220. Clearing only in els.search.oninput, as proposed, would leave a stale run selected after the card's ⊞, the Show run banner or setSheet, all of which write the box without firing input. (3) The proposed '⤢' prefix for refine-only runs is not feasible from the page alone: /api/runs returns no refine flag (storage.runs). It needs a backend field, or should be dropped. One caveat: re-picking the run already shown fires no change event, which is harmless because that run is already on screen.
findings.smokes_affected: None expected. smoke.json:38,110,114,160 only count or inspect #run-list options, never its value. smoke-comparison.json:20 calls showRun() directly. Re-run smoke.json after (2).

sources.surface: Gallery header (search, ? grammar, Runs select)

findings.title: Every small ghost button (Sheet, Pause, Export PNG, Show run) turns danger-red on hover, like Delete unstarred
surfaces: Button system: .ghost.small hover
Gallery head Sheet toggle, sheet Export PNG, last-run Show run
findings.recommendation: Delete style.css:613. Add `.ghost.danger:hover:not(:disabled):not([aria-disabled="true"]) { color: var(--danger); border-color: var(--danger); }`. Add class `danger` to #btn-cancel, #btn-cancel-queued and #btn-delete-unstarred. #lb-delete already has its own red hover at style.css:913. Remove the now-redundant style.css:644. Add `.ghost:disabled:hover, .ghost[aria-disabled="true"]:hover { color: var(--muted); border-color: var(--line); }` so a disabled Orientation does not brighten under the plain .ghost:hover rule.
findings.documented_rule: None for the hover colour. index.html:460-462 puts Delete unstarred last in the bar, 'away from the view toggle', which shows the authors want Delete kept distinct. style.css:644 already opts Show run out of the red hover.
findings.rule_tension: No rule conflict; the fix sharpens the distinction the authors wanted. Specificity trap: `.ghost.small:hover:not(:disabled):not([aria-disabled="true"])` is (0,5,0) and beats `.ghost.small.active` (0,3,0). That is why the active Sheet goes red, and grid-14's neutral replacement at the same specificity would still override the active accent. visual-9's version, which deletes the small-hover rule and adds an opt-in .danger rule, avoids this: `.ghost.small.active` (0,3,0) then beats `.ghost:hover` (0,2,0).

findings.how_checked: Real mouse hover via CDP at 2560x1305 over #btn-sheet (inactive and active), #btn-delete-unstarred and #btn-orientation, with computed colour and border read while :hover matched. Listed every .ghost.small in the DOM and in the scripts (sheet.js:318 makes Export PNG one). Worked out the CSS specificity of the proposed fixes.
findings.verifier_notes: Both source findings are accurate. Prefer visual-9's CSS shape, because grid-14's neutral hover rule would keep overriding the active Sheet accent. Low severity is right.
findings.merge_note: grid-14 adds that the hover overrides Sheet's active accent and that the last-run banner already opts out. Both propose an opt-in .danger class.

findings.title: Two caption systems (12 px uppercase vs 11 px sentence-case italic), six text greys and about 20 spacing values
surfaces: Page-wide tokens and labels
Panel captions vs field labels; check panel headings and badges
findings.recommendation:
Narrow it to the user-visible parts and drop the token refactor as a requirement (it is optional code hygiene, no user cost).
1) Hierarchy: keep the uppercase caption for groups, but give the sampling row one. Add `<span>` 'Sampling' as a `.field > span`-styled caption above Steps/CFG/Mu/True CFG (index.html:190). Today that row sits under SIZE and the '1.0 MP' hint with no caption of its own, so it reads as part of Size. Keep the controls' own labels in sentence case.
2) Make the check panel's 10px uppercase badges sentence case at 11px: `.analysis-source, .analysis-stale, .critic-kind { text-transform: none; letter-spacing: 0; font-size: 11px }`.
3) `#btn-grid { width: 100% }`. It is 77 px because children of a <details> are not flex items, while Generate stretches to 296.
4) `.primary { background: #6a4cf5 }` (white text 5.3:1, up from 4.35:1), leaving --accent as is.
findings.documented_rule: None for the caption system or tokens. style.css:98-101 (.field em colour) and the amber stale badge are deliberate colour choices to keep.
findings.rule_tension: None blocking. Sentence-casing badges or captions with CSS only changes rendering: no smoke or script reads innerText, so textContent assertions are unaffected. Darkening --accent globally would also lower every accent border and focus ring, so change only the .primary fill.
findings.smokes_affected: None found. No smoke uses innerText, #btn-grid's size, .primary's colour, or the panel's caption count. smoke-animagine.json 59-60/94-96 compare Generate's top before and after a re-render, which a new caption above the sampling row does not affect within a run.
findings.how_checked: Parsed web/style.css for hard-coded hex values after :root, gap declarations, radii and font sizes. Measured the heights of every visible button and select with the grid section and the check panel open. Measured #btn-grid against #btn-generate. Computed white-on-accent contrast. Read the panel screenshot for where the label hierarchy falls. Grepped the smokes and the scripts for innerText, which text-transform would change.
findings.verifier_notes: The facts mostly reproduce, with two corrections: the gap count is 14 lengths, not 20, and there are 11 control heights, not 7. On its own, most of this is code consistency with no user cost. The concrete user-facing pieces are the missing Sampling group caption (wrong grouping when scanning), the small Run grid button and Generate's slightly sub-AA contrast. Low severity. copy-a11y-13's 'one sentence-case label for everything' would remove group structure rather than fix it; adding the missing group caption is the better fix.
findings.merge_note: copy-a11y-13 adds that the Refine dialog and the check panel mix the two label styles too. visual-11 proposes tokens for greys, spacing and radii.

sources.surface: Page-wide tokens and labels
sources.observation: Captions of equal weight use two styles in one column. PROMPT / NEGATIVE PROMPT / SIZE / REFERENCE IMAGES / GRID SEARCH are 12px 600 uppercase with 0.04em tracking. Steps / CFG / Mu / True CFG / LoRA / Weight / Seed / Batch / Runs / W / H are 11px sentence case in <i>. Text greys: --muted #8b8b9a plus hard-coded #a2a2b0, #b2b2c0, #c8c8d4 and #cfd0dc. Outside :root there are 65 hard-coded hex uses with 32 distinct values; #fbbf24 amber is used for warn, favourite, stale and loading with no token. There are 20 distinct gap values (2-22px) and border radii of 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10, 50% and 999px. Buttons come in 7 heights: tiny 19, card tools 24, small 26, presets 27, ghost 37, dice 39, primary 43. Run grid is a 77px primary while Generate is 296px full width; white on --accent #7c5cff is 4.35:1, under AA for 14px text.
sources.why_it_matters: No single item is broken, but together they make the panel look assembled rather than designed. Hierarchy is unclear: is 'Steps' a sub-field of SIZE? Every new feature such as the check or Refine adds more one-off values.

sources.surface: Panel captions vs field labels; check panel headings and badges
sources.observation: PROMPT, NEGATIVE PROMPT, SIZE and REFERENCE IMAGES are 12px/600 uppercase with letter-spacing. The equally primary Steps, CFG, Mu, True CFG, LoRA, Weight, Seed, Batch and Runs are 11px/400 sentence case, and W/H are single letters. The Refine dialog mixes 'SIZE' with 'Strength'/'Versions'/'Seed'. The check panel adds uppercase ENCODERS/ORDER/FINDINGS/CRITIC, 10px uppercase 'GUIDE' badges, an uppercase 'PROMPT CHANGED SINCE' pill and an uppercase 'OTHER' critic kind. 'GRID SEARCH overnight sweeps' runs an uppercase label into a lowercase tagline.
sources.why_it_matters: Uppercase-vs-not signals hierarchy that does not exist here: Size is not more important than Steps. Uppercase 10-12px muted text is also the slowest to read, and the page leans on it for headings.

findings.title: Fixed explanations outweigh the check's findings, and the Order 'Not checked' note is self-referential jargon
surfaces: Order note, Compare hints, encoder rows vs findings
Prompt check: Order section
findings.recommendation: 1) analysis.js:457-460: replace the note with `Not checked: this app checks word order only in a tag checkpoint's comma-separated tags. ${promptCritiqueSupported ? 'Ask the critic, or test' : 'Test'} a reordered version under Compare on your own seeds.` That is 28 words instead of 36, with no 'Check' named in the third person, and accurate in both directions. 2) index.html:140: move 'Seeds is the total per version; Batch changes how many run together. Uses the main Seed field or a random start. The main Batch and Runs settings do not apply.' (30 words) into a `?...` after the Batch select (the pattern at index.html:32-34). Its first half already repeats the Batch select's own title (index.html:133). Keep the compare-note caveat (index.html:138) visible. 3) Leave the encoder role line and the order finding's chain alone: each saves only 12-16 words, the role line explains why the CLIP-L bar is drawn as a caution, and the finding text is matched by the critic's restatement filter and asserted in tests/test_api_analysis.py:995 and tests/test_critic.py:3578.
findings.documented_rule: CLAUDE.md, Prompt analyser: 'the page says a documented order it was not is "Not checked"' and 'never say the authors give none'. design-notes.md, 'The comparison is a grid, and its statistics are the caveat': 'Hence the line under the Seeds select: 4 seeds is a first look...' (placed there on purpose as the decision aid). The order finding's wording comes from backend/prompt_rules.py:1778, and the critic's restatement filter matches finding wording.
findings.rule_tension: Keep the 'Not checked:' prefix. The 4-vs-8 caveat stays visible beside Seeds, word for word, because it is the decision aid. Only the mechanics line moves into a tip. copy-a11y-17's proposed text ('the app checks order only in comma-separated tag prompts') is false: a comma tag prompt on FLUX returns style 'tags' with order_checked False, and prose on Animagine returns order_checked True. So the rewording has to name tag checkpoints. Do not trim the server's order-finding message: the critic's restatement filter and tests rely on its words.
findings.smokes_affected: smoke-analysis.json:36 (expects 'Not checked: Check can only place a tag checkpoint'), :142 (expects 'Ask the critic whether this prompt follows it'). :124 keeps passing, because textContent includes text inside a .tip span. smoke-animagine.json:99 and :104 ('the documented order is') pass only if the server message is left alone, as recommended.
findings.how_checked: Word counts with innerText on the FLUX fake (harbour prompt) and the Animagine fake ('masterpiece, green hair, 1girl, smile, outdoors, cherry blossoms, school uniform, looking at viewer'). Read the Order, Encoders, Findings and Compare text. Tested copy-a11y-17's proposed wording against the server: POST /api/prompt/analyze with a comma tag prompt on FLUX and a two-sentence prose prompt on Animagine.
findings.verifier_notes: This merges analysis-9 and copy-a11y-17. analysis-9's call to put the seed-count caveat into a tip goes against the deliberate placement in the design notes, so only the mechanics line moves. copy-a11y-17's wording would mislead (FLUX tag prompts are not order-checked). Pure copy polish, so severity stays low.
findings.merge_note: copy-a11y-17 proposes a reworded Order note ('the app checks order only in comma-separated tag prompts'). analysis-9 covers the 54 words of fixed Compare help.

sources.surface: Order note, Compare hints, encoder rows vs findings
sources.observation: On the Animagine check the panel holds 262 words, of which the findings are 58. Compare shows 54 words of fixed help on every check: the 4-vs-8 seeds statistics line, plus 'Seeds is the total per version; Batch changes how many run together. Uses the main Seed field or a random start. The main Batch and Runs settings do not apply.' Every FLUX prose check repeats Order's 37-word 'Not checked: Check can only place a tag checkpoint's comma tags in its order...'. The CLIP-L cut is said twice: in the encoder row ('one pooled vector, not the token sequence - T5-XXL carries the words · stops reading at ...') and as a finding ('CLIP-L reads the first 75 of the prompt's 85 tokens into one pooled vector and stops at ...'). The order finding repeats the chain drawn 150 px above it ('the documented order is Person count → Character → ...').
sources.why_it_matters: The user asked whether the copy is too long for where it sits. It is: what changes from one prompt to the next is buried in text that never changes, and people stop reading the panel.

sources.surface: Prompt check: Order section
sources.observation: For a FLUX prompt the Order section shows the chain 'subject first [GUIDE]' and then: 'Not checked: Check can only place a tag checkpoint's comma tags in its order. Ask the critic whether this prompt follows it, or write a reordered version under Compare to test it on your own seeds.' 'Check' names the feature in the third person, and 'place a tag checkpoint's comma tags' is internal vocabulary. On the default checkpoint this note appears on every check.
sources.why_it_matters: The useful message (the guide wants the subject first; the app cannot verify that in sentences; here is how to test it) is hidden behind phrasing only the author understands.

findings.title: LoRA Weight is disabled without an adapter but looks fully active
surfaces: LoRA Weight input
findings.recommendation: Add .panel input:disabled, .panel select:disabled { opacity: .45; cursor: not-allowed; }. In syncConditioning, set the reason on the Weight's wrapper, not the disabled input: els.loraScale.closest('.sub').title = els.lora.value ? '' : 'Pick an adapter first'. In the same row, give the panel's select the dark field style it lacks, reusing the .refine-dialog select rule: .panel select { width: 100%; padding: 9px 6px; font: inherit; background: var(--panel-2); border: 1px solid var(--line); border-radius: 8px; color: var(--text); }. #lora is the only unstyled native control in the panel: white, 20 px tall beside a 41 px Weight box, so the row's two halves misalign.
findings.documented_rule: CLAUDE.md and style.css:513-520: the conditioning rows are greyed for the checkpoint or installation (.row.disabled), never for a value, and the badge says why. app.js:206-208: selecting an adapter wakes the weight boxes.
findings.rule_tension: No conflict. ':disabled' dimming follows the element's own state and leaves .row.disabled (the checkpoint/installation reason) as it is. Other panel controls that would pick it up are #grid-seeds under a seed list (intended) and boxes already dimmed by .sub.disabled to the same 0.45 (no compounding, same element). A title on a disabled input may not show on hover, so put the reason on the wrapper.
findings.smokes_affected: None. smoke-conditioning.json:10, :60 and :81 check the disabled flags and values, not styles.
findings.how_checked: FLUX fake, LoRA 'none'. Compared getComputedStyle of #lora-scale with #steps, took elshots of the row, and checked the panel's CSS for select rules. Simulated the proposed CSS in the page only and took a shot of it.
findings.verifier_notes: The finding reproduced exactly. Adjusted only to add the white native LoRA select, the more visible defect in the same row (another reviewer may have reported it separately), and to move the hint from the disabled input to its wrapper.

sources.surface: LoRA Weight input
sources.observation: With LoRA 'none', #lora-scale is disabled but computes to opacity 1, color rgb(232,232,238) on rgb(26,26,33), the same as the enabled Steps box. Its '1' looks editable, and clicking does nothing. Dimming only exists for `.sub.disabled input` and `.row.disabled input`, which apply when the checkpoint or installation has no adapters, not when no adapter is chosen.
sources.why_it_matters: A control that looks live but ignores input reads as a bug, and there's no tip saying 'pick an adapter first'.

findings.title: The panel is one flat column with no group headings, and unsupported features still take full rows
surfaces: Panel structure: Reference images, LoRA, Seed/Batch/Runs, empty hint lines
findings.recommendation: Drop the 'Sampling' and 'Output' headings. That part is taste with no observed cost, and the headings would add about 64 px against this same finding's density argument. Keep the two cuts: #reference-field.disabled .chips { display: none } (the caption, badge and note stay) and #run-hint:empty { display: none }. Together they take the closed panel from 987 px to 930 px (-57 px, 6%). At the 125% target the pinned panel then ends at 998 px inside a 1040 px viewport instead of 1055 px. The gain is modest: before the change only the bottom padding was clipped and the Grid search summary (y 1010-1028) was already visible. The visible win is that the odd blank gap under 'REFERENCE IMAGES (this checkpoint takes none)' disappears.
findings.documented_rule: CLAUDE.md and index.html:226-228: reference images and LoRA are greyed rather than hidden where they do not apply, so the panel keeps its shape and the badge says why. #cell-note holds the job summary.
findings.rule_tension: Hiding only the empty chips row when the field is disabled keeps the caption, the ? badge and '(this checkpoint takes none)', which is the rule's purpose. The shape changes by 26 px only when reference support flips, which happens at most once, on load. #run-hint:empty collapsing moves Generate down 29 px the moment Batch or Runs goes above 1. That shift happens while the user types in those boxes, not near a click, so it is acceptable. Leave #cell-note alone, as the finding says.
findings.smokes_affected: None. smoke-flux.json:26-27 checks that #reference-field has the disabled class and the note text, not the chips row's size. smoke-conditioning.json:36-40 runs on klein, where references are supported and the rule does not apply. No smoke reads #run-hint.
findings.how_checked: FLUX fake at 2560x1305 and at 2048x1040 DPR 1.25 with the gallery made 4000 px tall in the page so the sticky panel would pin. Measured rects, then applied the space-saving CSS in the page only and measured again.
findings.verifier_notes: The measurements reproduced to the pixel. The grouping half is refuted as taste with no observed cost. The space half is real but small: with the grid fold open the panel is about 1405 px whatever happens here, and a 'Last run' banner adds about 100 px. The panel outgrowing the viewport is panel-1's issue and is not fixed here.

sources.surface: Panel structure: Reference images, LoRA, Seed/Batch/Runs, empty hint lines
sources.observation: Uppercase captions exist for Prompt, Negative, Size and Reference images, but Steps/CFG/Mu/True CFG, LoRA and Seed/Batch/Runs have no group heading. Everything is separated by the same 14 px gap. On FLUX and Turbo (references unsupported) the Reference images field still takes 44 px, 20 px of it an empty chips row, plus a gap, to say '(this checkpoint takes none)'. Two empty `.hint` lines (#run-hint and #cell-note, min-height 15 px each) leave about 45 px of blank space above Generate (a02).
sources.why_it_matters: A first-time user can't tell basic controls from advanced ones; Mu, True CFG and the references row look as important as Steps. The wasted rows are part of why the panel outgrows the viewport (panel-1).

findings.title: Fixed 160 px card minimum gives 12 small cards per row at QHD, with no size control
surfaces: Gallery grid density
findings.recommendation: In web/style.css:716-720, change the rule to `.grid { grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(var(--card-min, 160px), 1fr)); }` and add `@media (min-width: 2000px) { .grid { --card-min: 220px; } }`. Measured result: 9 cards of 231px per row at 2560x1305, and 7 of 227px (284 device px) at 2048@1.25. Both sizes are within the 299px short side of a 7:9 thumbnail. A 16:9 thumbnail is upscaled about 1.07x at QHD and 1.31x at 125%. The six card tools then fit: today they overflow at 171px (scrollWidth 176 vs clientWidth 169). Below 2000px nothing changes: at 1400 the cards are already 192px. A density control is optional. If added, make it a compact S/M (160/220) toggle in .gallery-head with `display:none` below 2000px; the head has about 1100px free at QHD. Offer L (about 280px) only together with THUMB_SIDE raised to 512 in backend/storage.py:41, accepting that thumbnails written before the change stay at 384 unless they are regenerated. Persist it under `local-diffusion.gallery.v1` in try/catch. It is a gallery preference, so resetPanel need not forget it. Update the THUMB_SIDE comment (storage.py:38) that says the cards are 160px.
findings.documented_rule: No rule fixes the 160px minimum. backend/storage.py:38-41 (THUMB_SIDE = 384) explains the thumbnail size as 'The gallery's cards are 160 px'. docs/design-notes.md 'The running batch on wide screens' is a precedent: the results viewer was already re-tuned at min-width 2000px for QHD, but the gallery was not. 'Panel persistence' / CLAUDE.md say app-owned browser keys use the local-diffusion.* prefix and every storage access is in try/catch. style.css:703-706 says the search box starts at 140px so the bar 'stays one row on a laptop'.
findings.rule_tension: Two parts of the original recommendation conflict with the code. (1) The upscaling claim is wrong. Cards are square with object-fit: cover (style.css:782), so the thumbnail's SHORT side must fill the card. A 7:9 thumbnail is 299x384 (measured) and a 16:9 one is 384x216. At L=300px a 16:9 thumbnail is upscaled 1.39x at DPR 1. At 125% scaling, L needs 375-402 device px, which is more than THUMB_SIDE allows for any shape. Raising THUMB_SIDE helps new images only: storage.thumbnail_for writes a thumbnail only when none exists, so old thumbnails stay at 384. (2) At 1400x900 the gallery head is already full: its children take 1001 of 1001px and the search box has shrunk to 188px. An S/M/L control there would wrap the bar to two rows, against the 'one row on a laptop' comment. Compatible fix: add the change only at min-width 2000px, matching the results viewer's precedent, and keep any control hidden below that width.
findings.smokes_affected: None if the change applies only at min-width 2000px: every smoke runs at 1400x900. smoke-paging.json:14,17,34,45 expect exactly 48 cards after the first page at 1400x900, which is unaffected. Do not apply a persisted density below 2000px, or those counts could change. smoke.json:37 (`.card` count >= 12) is unaffected.
findings.how_checked: Fresh FLUX.1 Krea [dev] fake on 7908 with 144 portrait 896x1152 images (one grid). Measured in headless Edge at 2560x1305@1, 2048x1040@1.25 and 1400x900@1: the gallery width, card size, cards per row, the thumbnail's natural size and the tool row's overflow. I then set gridTemplateColumns to minmax(220px) and minmax(300px) in eval to try the proposed sizes, and measured whether the .gallery-head bar has room for a new control at each viewport.
findings.verifier_notes: The numbers reproduce exactly (170.9px x 12, 174.3px x 9). The strongest evidence that the page was tuned at 1400 and stretched is that the cards are smaller at QHD (171px) than at the smoke viewport (192px). Low severity stands: the lightbox is where images are judged. Overlaps with gallery-3 (tool row overflow): 220px cards remove that overflow.

sources.surface: Gallery grid density
sources.observation: `.grid { grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fill, minmax(160px, 1fr)) }` gives 12 cards of 170.9px across the 2161px stage at QHD (6.7% of the width each). At 2048@1.25 it gives 9 of 174px. Thumbnails are 384px, so they could show at 230-300 CSS px without upscaling (300 x 1.25 = 375 device px). There is no density setting.
sources.why_it_matters: On a 27" QHD panel a 171px square is too small to judge anything without opening it, and it also makes the tool row overflow (gallery-3). Different jobs need different sizes: triaging a night's grid vs. scanning for one image.

findings.title: The scale buttons and the outcome summary are the least prominent things in the Refine dialog
surfaces: Refine dialog: scale buttons, W/H, preview line
findings.recommendation:
1) In syncRefine, set button.dataset.size = `${size[0]}×${size[1]}` next to the title. Add .refine-dialog .presets button { flex: 1; font-size: 13px; padding: 5px 10px } and .refine-dialog .presets button::after { content: attr(data-size); display: block; font-size: 10px; color: var(--muted) }. Tested: four 101x47 buttons, each showing its output size (e.g. '1.5×' over '1344×1728'). The dialog grows by 23px, and the disabled past-guard state keeps its 0.45 opacity.
2) Keep #refine-preview where it is, directly above Cancel and Refine. Do not move it into .rf-actions: at 13px the one-line summary is about 330px wide and the refusal messages are longer. Cancel (65px), Refine (120px) and the gaps leave about 220px of the 422px content width, so it would wrap to three or four lines. Instead, give it #refine-preview { font-size: 13px; color: var(--text) } with .warn still amber. That sets it apart from the 11px muted seed and size hints.
3) Optional at min-width 2000px: .refine-dialog { width: min(540px, calc(100vw - 32px)) } with .refine-dialog .sub i, .refine-dialog .hint { font-size: 12px }. Those sizes are px rules, so a dialog-level font-size alone does not reach them.
Drop the change that narrows W/H to 110px fields: these boxes are the precise control, and shrinking them has no stated user cost.
findings.documented_rule: None specific. The dialog reuses the panel's .presets button style (web/style.css:548-558, 11px). CLAUDE.md asks only that the dialog's scale buttons share refine.scaled's rounding with the CLI.
findings.rule_tension: None with a documented rule. Mind smoke-refine step 26, which checks the buttons' textContent is exactly '1×,1.25×,1.5×,2×'. A child element holding the size would break that step. A data-size attribute shown through CSS ::after does not, because pseudo-element content is not part of textContent. Tested: still '1×,1.25×,1.5×,2×'. Keep the title and the aria-label, which smoke step 55 reads on the past-guard button.
findings.smokes_affected: smoke-refine.json step 26 (scale buttons' textContent): unaffected with the ::after approach, broken by a child span. Step 55 (children[3].title includes 'past what a refine pass renders'): keep the title. Steps 24, 28, 53 and 68 read preview and size-hint text: unchanged by restyling.
findings.how_checked: Measured the scale buttons, W/H, the preview, the seed hint, the .sub i labels and h2 with getBoundingClientRect and getComputedStyle at 2560x1305. Collected every visible text font size in the dialog and on the page. Then injected CSS that shows each button's output size through ::after { content: attr(data-size) }, at 13px with flex: 1, and the preview at 13px var(--text). I confirmed the buttons' textContent is unchanged and took element screenshots of both versions.
findings.verifier_notes: Real but minor. The description overstates two points: 11px is not the page's smallest text (10px exists), and the chosen size is visible in W/H and the size line once picked; only the unpicked factors' sizes are hidden in titles. Changes: CSS ::after so smoke step 26 still holds, and the preview stays above the actions instead of being squeezed into them. The QHD font bump overlaps with any page-wide typography cluster.

sources.surface: Refine dialog: scale buttons, W/H, preview line
sources.observation: The scale buttons, the main way to pick a size, are 31x27 / 46x27 / 40x27 / 31x27 px at 11 px. Their resulting sizes exist only in a title attribute (e.g. '1344 × 1728'), which is not visible on hover-free devices. The W/H boxes below are 207x41 px at 14 px. The line that says what will happen ('1 image · strength 0.1 · about 3 of 28 steps run · about 1s') is 11 px var(--muted), styled like the seed hint, and sits between the fold and the buttons. Labels (.sub i) are 11 px. At QHD at 100%, 11 px is the smallest text on the page.
sources.why_it_matters: The visual weight is inverted: the precise boxes most users never touch dominate, while the factor choice and the commitment summary (image count, steps that run, time) are easy to miss before pressing Refine.

findings.title: All 20 '?' badges have the same accessible name, 'Help'
surfaces: Every .help badge (panel, grid, gallery search, Refine dialog)
findings.recommendation: Give each badge a name for what it explains, and expose its tip as its description. Do it statically in index.html, which avoids boot-time DOM walking: aria-label="Steps help" aria-describedby="steps-tip" and so on for all 20. Prefix the grid's duplicate captions so they stay distinct from the panel's: 'Steps axis help', 'CFG axis help', 'Mu axis help', 'LoRA weight axis help'. Use 'Refine size help' and 'Refine strength help' in the dialog. A boot loop in app.js works too, if preferred: for each .help, set aria-label to (caption label text) + ' help' and aria-describedby to its .tip id. Keep role=note, tabindex=0 and the badge's position outside the label.
findings.documented_rule: index.html:183-189 keeps the badge outside the <label> on purpose: a tap inside the label would be forwarded to the input and close the tooltip it opened. Tips are rewritten from /api/status on every poll (index.html:178-183). CLAUDE.md: classic scripts, and only app.js runs anything at load.
findings.rule_tension: None, provided the badge stays a sibling of the label and keeps tabindex=0, so sighted keyboard users can still open the CSS tip (style.css:155 .help:focus .tip). Static aria-labels in index.html need no script at all. If they are set at boot instead, that belongs in app.js, which the load-order rule allows. aria-describedby by id survives the status rewrites, which change the tip's text and keep the element.
findings.smokes_affected: None. No tools/smoke-*.json step reads '.help', aria-label 'Help' or role 'note'. tests/ and backend/ do not reference the badge markup.
findings.how_checked: Fresh FLUX fake on 7921 at 2560x1305 (steps m106.json). I inventoried every .help badge: aria-label, role, tabindex, caption, and whether some aria-describedby references its tip. I read Chrome's accessibility node for several badges and for the Steps input, using a CDP Accessibility.getPartialAXTree step I added to my driver copy. Then I focused the prompt and pressed real Tab keys (key code 9) 44 times, logging document.activeElement each time.
findings.verifier_notes: Reproduces as stated. The one correction is 7 'Help' stops between the prompt and Generate, not 8 (8 counting the Prompt badge before the textarea). The larger share of the 36 stops is the 18 size preset and tier buttons (T2-T18), which is outside this cluster. Do not take the badges out of the tab order: that would remove the only keyboard way for a sighted user to read a tip, since the inputs' aria-describedby is not visible.

sources.surface: Every .help badge (panel, grid, gallery search, Refine dialog)
sources.observation: There are 20 .help badges, 17 of them in the panel, each tabindex=0, role=note and aria-label="Help" (unique labels measured: ['Help']). A screen-reader user tabbing the panel hears 'Help, note' eight times before reaching Generate, with no clue which control each belongs to. Badges whose input already references the tip via aria-describedby (Steps, CFG, Mu, True CFG, LoRA, grid axes, search) duplicate that description as an extra stop.
sources.why_it_matters: These eight stops make up a large part of the 36 Tab presses from the prompt to Generate, and they announce nothing useful.

findings.title: Escape, Cancel or ✕ on the Refine dialog throws away a typed sweep, size and prompt edits
surfaces: Refine dialog close (Escape, Cancel, ✕)
Refine dialog: Cancel, ✕, Escape, reopen
findings.recommendation: Add `let refineDraft = null` ({id, values}). In refineClosed() (refine.js:399), save it only when the close was not a run (runRefine sets a flag before close()) and some value differs from what openRefine filled in: strength text, W/H, versions, seed, prompt, negative, steps, CFG, Mu, True CFG, and whether the fold was open. In openRefine(rec), when !pass && refineDraft?.id === rec.id, restore the values and show 'Your unsent settings for image N · Start over' in #refine-more-note (the fold opens if the prompt or sampling differ). Clear the draft on a run, on resetPanel, on a checkpoint change and when another source is opened. Land it with or after M6: with the source shown large in the dialog, the main reason to close it and look elsewhere goes away.
findings.documented_rule: CLAUDE.md Frontend: openRefine 'fills the dialog from the record'; 'refineSource is that record while the dialog is open and null once it closes'; 'The dialog remembers the scale, the versions and, per checkpoint, a single strength the user ran (local-diffusion.refine.v1); resetPanel forgets it'. refine.js:21-25: 'A sweep is not remembered, or the next open would start one unasked'.
findings.rule_tension: A draft kept in memory only, keyed by source id, restored only on reopening the same source without `pass` and announced with a visible 'Start over', never starts a sweep unasked on another image and never reaches local-diffusion.refine.v1. That preserves the purpose of both rules. The CLAUDE.md sentence 'fills the dialog from the record' needs a clause: 'unless an unsent draft for the same image is restored, which it says'.
findings.smokes_affected: None, if the draft is saved only when values differ and cleared on run and resetPanel. smoke-refine steps 56-64: the draft would be saved for __refined, which is never reopened, and step 64 opens __source. Steps 80-93: the edits end in a Ctrl+Enter run, which clears it. Steps 95-101: no edits before the Escape at 98, and resetPanel runs at 99. Steps 107-118 are Reuse, where `pass` is given, so no draft applies.
findings.how_checked: FLUX fake on 7910. Opened ⤢ on the 896x1152 fox. Typed '0.05,0.1,0.15' into Strength with real key input, pressed 1.25× (1120x1440), opened the fold and typed ', sharp detail' at the end of the prompt. Pressed Escape (a real key event), then reopened the same image with ⤢. Also clicked the backdrop to check whether it closes the dialog.
findings.verifier_notes: Reproduced exactly as both findings describe. I lowered the cluster to low: the work lost is a typed sweep, a size and occasionally a prompt edit; the backdrop does not close the dialog, so an accidental click outside cannot cause it; and the strongest motive to close-and-look (the 72 px source) is M6's to fix. refine-dialog-11 duplicates refine-flow-5 inside this cluster, and both propose the same in-memory draft.
findings.merge_note: refine-dialog-11 adds that Escape also closes the lightbox, so it is easy to press by accident. It proposes a per-source in-memory draft map.

sources.surface: Refine dialog: Cancel, ✕, Escape, reopen
sources.observation: I opened image 16's dialog, typed the sweep '0.05,0.1,0.15', pressed 1.25× (W 1280) and added ', sharp detail' to the prompt, then pressed Escape and reopened the same image with the same ⤢. Everything was back to the defaults: strength '0.1', W 1536, the original prompt, the fold closed. refineClosed() keeps nothing, and rememberRefine() runs only on Refine. The dialog is modal, so checking anything outside it (the source at size in the lightbox, a neighbouring image, the panel) means closing it.
sources.why_it_matters: Combined with the 72px source preview (refine-flow-4), the natural move of 'let me look at it first' costs the setup every time. A user who typed a sweep has to remember and retype it.

sources.surface: Refine dialog close (Escape, Cancel, ✕)
sources.observation: I edited the prompt in 'Prompt and sampling', pressed Escape, then reopened the same image with ⤢. The prompt was back to the record's ('a fox in the snow at dusk') and the fold was closed. Only scale, versions and a single strength are remembered, and only after Refine is pressed. A stray Escape (also the key that closes the lightbox and menus elsewhere on the page) loses a rewritten prompt.
sources.why_it_matters: Editing the prompt for a pass is the slowest thing done in the dialog, and Escape is used freely elsewhere on the page.

findings.title: On the default checkpoint the negative prompt is greyed out, and the True CFG box that enables it is far below
surfaces: Negative prompt and its activation note; True CFG / CFG
findings.recommendation: Turn #negative-field from a <label> into <div class="field" id="negative-field"> with <label for="negative">Negative prompt</label> in the caption. This is the same structure the Prompt field already uses for its caption buttons (index.html:26-31). While the box is off and negativeSupported is true, show a <button type="button" class="ghost tiny" id="neg-enable"> after #neg-note, labelled after the knob ('Set True CFG' or 'Set CFG'). On click it focuses and selects the deciding box (trueCfgSupported ? els.trueCfg : els.cfg) and writes nothing. syncCfg sets its hidden state and text. Optionally add #negative-field.disabled textarea { pointer-events: none } and a click handler on the field doing the same, so a press on the greyed box itself is no longer a dead click. That was tested: focus landed on #true-cfg from both the box and the caption. Keep the note's current wording as its prefix.
findings.documented_rule: design-notes 'True CFG is its own field': the True CFG box is greyed, not hidden, and the negative prompt follows whichever box decides. collect() sends no negative while the box is disabled. CLAUDE.md Frontend: syncCfg changing the negative's activation marks the prompt check stale. Profile values are the checkpoint's; the client invents none.
findings.rule_tension: The proposed button inside the note breaks the field's labelling. #negative-field is a <label>, and a <button> inside it becomes the label's control (measured: label.control '#neg-enable', negative.labels.length 0), so the textarea loses its name. Prefilling 1.5 hard-codes a value no profile publishes. Qwen-Image's true_cfg hint asks for about 4 and schnell's says blank is how it is meant to run, so 1.5 would be wrong on two of the three true-CFG profiles. A compatible fix keeps the greyed box and the note text, never writes a value, and lets syncCfg/syncAnalysisStale run as they do now when the user types into the knob.
findings.smokes_affected: None break if the note keeps its prefix: smoke-flux.json:29 (negNote includes 'needs True CFG > 1'), smoke.json:148 (includes 'needs CFG > 0') and smoke-animagine.json:79 (includes 'CFG > 1') use includes() on #neg-note, which is unchanged. Add a smoke-flux step: click #neg-enable and expect document.activeElement === els.trueCfg with the box still empty.
findings.how_checked: Fresh FLUX.1 Krea [dev] fake on 7903 and Krea 2 Turbo fake on 8903, 2560x1305 DPR 1. Measured rects, clicked the greyed box and the caption with real mouse events, typed 1.5 into True CFG. Then tried two fixes in the page only. (1) A button injected into #neg-note: it took the textarea's label. (2) pointer-events:none on the greyed textarea plus a click handler on the field: it moved focus to the deciding box.
findings.verifier_notes: Lowered from medium to low. The note already names the knob, the CFG tip says 'The negative prompt is driven by True CFG, the box beside this one', and FLUX's prompt guide says 'There is no negative prompt without True CFG'. Both boxes are inside the 1305 px viewport. The cost is learning it once plus a dead click, not friction every session. Do not adopt the original recommendation as written: its button would steal the textarea's label, and its prefill would be wrong on Qwen-Image and schnell.

sources.surface: Negative prompt and its activation note; True CFG / CFG
sources.observation: On FLUX.1 Krea [dev] (the default) the negative box is disabled on load. Its note, '(needs True CFG > 1 - ~2x slower)', wraps onto two lines at 330 px. Clicking the greyed box does nothing (focus stayed on body). The control that enables it is True CFG, the fourth input in the sampling row, at y=620 against the negative box at y=300. Its placeholder is 'off'. Typing 1.5 there enabled the negative box (negDis false), but nothing pointed me there or moved focus back. On Krea 2 Turbo the note is '(needs CFG > 0 - ~2x slower)' and the same dead-click applies.
sources.why_it_matters: The negative prompt is one of the first things a user tries, and on the default checkpoint it looks broken. The fix (True CFG, a separate knob only FLUX.1 has) is the least self-explanatory control in the panel. The True CFG hint suggests 'keep 3.5 and add a mild 1.5', but the user has to go and read it.

findings.title: On a checkpoint with no refine pass, the card's ⤢ looks live and its refusal lands in the panel
surfaces: Gallery card ⤢ and lightbox Refine on FLUX.2 [klein]
findings.recommendation: Give the card's capability-gated tools the lightbox's treatment: ⤢ against refineSupported, and also ❐ against referenceSupported, which has the same problem on the default FLUX.1 checkpoint. In card() (gallery.js:107-108), tag them (classes 'refine-tool' and 'ref-tool') and call a syncCardTools() that sets aria-disabled and the title ('This checkpoint has no refine pass' / 'This checkpoint takes no reference images'). Call it from card() and from status.js where refineSupported (~line 190) and referenceSupported (~line 180) flip, as syncReuseButtons does for Reuse. Add CSS: .card .tools button[aria-disabled='true'] { opacity:.45 } .card .tools button[aria-disabled='true']:hover { background: rgba(0,0,0,.55) }. Optionally add a transient .card-note (aria-hidden, absolutely positioned above .tools, removed after 4s) with the short reason, so the answer appears where the click was.
findings.documented_rule: CLAUDE.md Frontend: 'A ⤢ on a checkpoint without a pass says so and opens nothing'. 'Ask the critic is aria-disabled, never disabled, so it keeps focus' is the pattern lbRefine already follows (lightbox.js:120-125: 'aria-disabled, so the button keeps its place in the tab order and its click can still say why'). showError mirrors into the lightbox while it is open (state.js:324-328).
findings.rule_tension: None, if the card button gets aria-disabled='true' (never disabled), keeps its onclick so a press still explains, and keeps writing to the panel slot (role=alert) as well. A card-local note must have aria-hidden='true', or screen readers hear the message twice.
findings.smokes_affected: smoke-conditioning.json:28-29 (clicks the card ⤢ found by textContent '⤢' and expects els.error to include 'no refine pass'): still passes if the glyph, the click handler and the panel slot are kept. smoke-conditioning.json:54 (lightbox lbError) is unchanged. smoke-refine-unavailable.json:12-13 calls openRefine directly and is unaffected. smoke-refine.json:20 clicks ⤢ on a supported checkpoint and is unaffected.
findings.how_checked: Fake FLUX.2 [klein] on port 8909 (refineSupported false), at 2560x1305. I hovered the first card with the real mouse, read the ⤢ button's aria-disabled, opacity, colour and title, clicked it at (412,1259), then measured the panel's error slot and the dialog state. I opened the same image in the lightbox, read lbRefine's state and clicked it, and measured lbError against lbRefine. On FLUX (port 7909, referenceSupported false) I read the card's ❐ state and clicked it.
findings.verifier_notes: The inconsistency is real, but I lowered severity from medium to low. At QHD the note does land on screen, in the sticky panel about 380px left of and 240px above the click, and only klein-family users meet the ⤢ case. I broadened the fix to the ❐ button, which behaves the same way on the default checkpoint, so the card tools agree with the lightbox in both cases.

sources.surface: Gallery card ⤢ and lightbox Refine on FLUX.2 [klein]
sources.observation: On the klein fake (refineSupported false) the card's ⤢ has no aria-disabled, opacity 1 and the normal title ('Refine: scale this image up...'). The lightbox's Refine on the same image is aria-disabled, opacity 0.45, with the title 'This checkpoint has no refine pass'. Pressing ⤢ opens nothing and writes 'This checkpoint has no refine pass compatible with this app. The FLUX.1, SDXL, Z-Image and Qwen-Image checkpoints have one.' in 12px into the panel's error slot at (35,1022), as a muted note. The card was at (366,1105), so the answer appears about 330px left of the click, in grey.
sources.why_it_matters: The same capability shows two different states, and the card's answer is easy to miss. A user sees a click do nothing and repeats it.

findings.title: Export PNG covers only the pinned slice, omits the prompt, and every slice downloads under the same name
surfaces: Export PNG (buildSheetCanvas / exportSheet)
findings.recommendation: (1) Add a caption line with the prompt. For a variable run, give the top-left cell's prompt plus the variables as declared, e.g. 'size = big | small; ground = grass | dirt', from sheetValues' var: axes in written order. This avoids rebuilding a template, which is ambiguous. Otherwise give the shared prompt. Also list single-valued settings (steps 28, mu none). Grow `caption` from 52 to 52 + 20 per extra line. (2) Print the run's time, not the export's: use the oldest record's created_at instead of when(Date.now()). (3) Put the pins in the filename: `sheet-${run}-${pins.map(([a, v]) => `${a.key.replace('var:', '')}-${valueText(v)}`).join('_').replace(/[^\w.-]+/g, '-')}.png`. (4) Optional, M effort: an 'Export all pins' button that stacks one titled block per pin combination while the canvas stays within EXPORT_MAX_EDGE. Past that it downloads the slices one by one.
findings.documented_rule: Design notes 'The sheet exports client-side'. buildSheetCanvas draws the same axes, pins and labels as the screen, from thumbnails, with the longer edge under 8000 px. The caption names the search, the pins, the checkpoint, the run and the time. No server route.
findings.rule_tension: Exporting only the pinned slice is the documented contract (it mirrors the screen), so slice-only is not a defect. 'Export all pins' is an addition, and it has to stay client-side within EXPORT_MAX_EDGE. The caption and filename changes are client-only and compatible.
findings.smokes_affected: smoke.json lines 66-68 build the canvas and expect width>500 and height>300; a taller caption still passes. smoke.json line 65 counts #sheet-controls labels ≥ 2, so a new button does not affect it.
findings.how_checked: On 7913 with run 50fde9555e4e open (size x ground x CFG x 3 seeds, 24 images) I called buildSheetCanvas() and drew the result into an to screenshot it (m55-01-export.png). Then I stubbed HTMLAnchorElement.prototype.click to capture a.download and ran exportSheet() twice with different pins.
findings.verifier_notes: Severity lowered from medium to low. Export is occasional, the browser's ' (1)' suffix prevents overwriting, and slice-only matches the documented contract. The real defects are the missing prompt and the caption time, which is the export moment rather than the run's. The run id in the caption can still be searched in-app (run:<id>) while the gallery exists.

sources.surface: Export PNG (buildSheetCanvas / exportSheet)
sources.observation: The exported canvas of the variable run is 1326x872. Labels are 14 px white, more legible than on screen. It holds only the 6 cells of the pinned slice 'cfg 2, seed 5872…' out of 24. The caption reads 'run:c6f465991da2 · pinned to cfg 2, seed 5872080855328996' / 'FLUX.1-Krea-dev · 1024×1024 · run c6f465991da2 · 4 Oct, 03:42 pm', with no prompt or template. Covering a 2 CFG × 2 seed run takes 4 pin changes and 4 exports, each named sheet-c6f465991da2.png.
sources.why_it_matters: The design note calls the export 'the one artefact worth keeping from a night'. Without the prompt it cannot be understood later, and the four slices are hard to tell apart on disk.

findings.title: Help tooltips run to 90-130 words of 11 px jargon, and Strength's covers the fields it explains
surfaces: ? tooltips: Refine Strength, Search, Resume, Prompt variables, True CFG
findings.recommendation: 1) Rewrite the True branch of _REFINE_HINTS (model_defaults.py:891) to about 40 words with the action first: 'How much of the source is redrawn: low keeps the picture, 1 keeps nothing. Starts at {refine_strength:g} on this checkpoint; at one strength, 2x redraws more than 1.5x. Several values (0.3,0.4,0.5 or 0.2-0.5x0.1) run as one sweep.' Drop the 'Steps x Strength' sentence, which the preview line already states with real numbers. Move the flow-matching shift theory to README or design-notes 'The refine pass'. 2) In the dialog, open that tip upward (`.refine-dialog .help.up .tip { top: auto; bottom: calc(100% + 7px); }` with class up on the Strength badge). It then covers W/H, which are already set, instead of Versions/Seed, which come next. 3) Trim the Resume tip to its instruction ('Skips cells already rendered at this size and checkpoint. Needs the Seed the grid was started from; Run grid fills it in.') and move the 'night that died at cell 300' story to README. Keep the Search tip as a syntax card: its length is reference, not prose. 4) At min-width 2000px, set `.tip { width: 320px; font-size: 12.5px } .tip.wide { width: 380px }`. 5) A Versions badge is optional: #refine-versions is already described by #refine-seed-hint, which states the seeds.
findings.documented_rule: CLAUDE.md: guides are author-sourced. hints.prompt and hints.size are the guide's prose, and `test_every_cite_is_the_guides_own_words` holds every guide cite to be a verbatim substring of that prose. tests/test_refine.py:217 asserts 'starts at {strength}' in the refine hint. smoke-refine.json:27 requires 'starts at 0.1 on this checkpoint'.
findings.rule_tension: The ~35-word cap can apply only to app-owned copy: the static tips in index.html (Search, Resume, Prompt variables, Seed list, Budget) and model_defaults' _REFINE_HINTS / steps / guidance_scale / true_cfg / mu hints. The Prompt and Size tips come from guides.py prose. Shortening them would break analysis cites, so they keep their length and get only the font and width change. In the refine hint, keep 'starts at {refine_strength:g} on this checkpoint' and the False branch's 'no compatible image-to-image counterpart' (smoke-conditioning.json:18).
findings.smokes_affected: smoke-refine.json:27 (refineStrengthTip must keep 'starts at 0.1 on this checkpoint'); smoke-conditioning.json:18 ('no compatible image-to-image counterpart'); smoke-flux.json:24 (trueCfgTip 'unconditioned') and smoke.json:146 ('Not a separate knob') if the true_cfg hints are trimmed. Also tests/test_refine.py:217. The guide-based tips (promptTip/sizeTip checks in smoke.json:16 and every per-checkpoint smoke) must not be shortened.
findings.how_checked: Fresh profile on 7920 with the grid <details> opened. Focused each badge and measured its .tip (getBoundingClientRect, word count, font size): search-tip 129 words, 240x337; grid-resume-tip 124 words, 240x257, y 1048-1305 (fits exactly, not clipped); grid-prompt-tip 107 words, 240x289; true-cfg-tip 56; all 11px. Opened the Refine dialog with a card's ⤢: the dialog is only 460x561 at the 2560 viewport. The refine-strength-tip (91 words, 300x161, x 1103-1403, y 695-856) covers #refine-versions (1242-1304, 694-735), the left 91 px of #refine-seed, #refine-seed-hint (y 751-768) and the top of #refine-preview (y 841-857). The Versions sub has no badge. Read /api/status hints and model_defaults.py:884-899. The preview line already says '1 image · strength 0.1 · about 3 of 28 steps run'.
findings.verifier_notes: Every measurement reproduced. Severity is low rather than medium: a tip is read occasionally, not every session, and the overlap is transient because the tip closes on mouse-leave or blur. The original recommendation to cap every tip at 35 words would collide with the author-sourced guide tips and their cite tests, so it is limited to app copy. Side observation for another cluster: the Refine dialog is 460 px wide on a 2560 px screen.

sources.surface: ? tooltips: Refine Strength, Search, Resume, Prompt variables, True CFG
sources.observation: Measured with the badge focused: the Search tip has 129 words in a 240x337 px box; Resume has 124 words in 240x257 px, its bottom at y=1305, the viewport's edge; Prompt variables has 107 words in 240x289 px; Refine Strength, from the server hint, has 91 words in 300x161 px; True CFG has 56 words. All are 11 px. Strength's tip opens downward over the Versions select, the Seed box, the seed line and the preview (b13). Its content is schedule theory: 'a flow-matching checkpoint's shift puts the same strength at a noisier point than SDXL's, and FLUX.1's shift grows with the size'. The Resume tip reads like a design note ('A night that died at cell 300 of 480 costs the cell it died on'). Versions, the dialog's other new control, has no badge.
sources.why_it_matters: The Refine dialog is the area the user named. Its key number is explained in prose that needs diffusion internals and hides the controls being explained. Long tips at 11 px are skimmed or skipped, so the one actionable sentence is lost.

findings.title: Same glyph and word mean different things: ↻ is both Reuse and Re-render, and Favourite/Favorite/Favorites/starred are mixed
surfaces: Card tools, gallery header, lightbox actions
Lightbox button, card star, gallery tick, delete confirm, Delete unstarred, Runs list
findings.recommendation: (1) Fix the one real defect first: the card star's state labelling. In card() (gallery.js:100) build the star with a label and title from rec.favorite, and add aria-pressed. In setFavorite (gallery.js:209-213) update textContent, aria-label, title and aria-pressed together. Today a starred card renders with aria-label and title 'Favorite', becomes 'Unfavorite' only after an in-page toggle, and its title never changes. (2) Pick one term and use it everywhere. Recommended: 'star', because the glyph, 'Delete unstarred', 'keeping N starred' and the runs list's ★ already use it. That means: tick 'Starred' (index.html:446); lightbox '☆ Star' / '★ Starred' with title 'Star (F)' (index.html:523, lightbox.js:117); card label 'Star' / 'Unstar'; confirm '(starred, seed 33)' (gallery.js:226); sheet note 'Starred unticked: nothing in a new comparison is starred yet' (panel.js:247). Keep the F shortcut. If the user prefers 'favourite' (their own commit ad24fe5 says 'favourite star'), at least make the spelling consistent: one spelling of Favourite on the tick, the aria-label and the button. (3) Optional: drop ↻ from the Re-render label (generation.js:240), to read 'Re-render 3 at 1024×1024'. The text already disambiguates it, so this is polish. (4) Optional: add '⊞ Show run' to .lb-actions, closing the lightbox and running the card's ⊞ code (gallery.js:123-131). Add '❐ Reference' only where referenceSupported. The 280px lightbox column has about 900px of empty height above its four buttons at 1305px tall, so they fit without reflow.
findings.documented_rule: None forbids a rename. CLAUDE.md 'Frontend and CLI' uses 'Favorites' as the tick's name in several rules ('Favorites unticked first, and the sheet's note says so', 'unpersisted like Favorites', 'Under Favorites or a search narrower than the run'). 'Delete unstarred' is a documented feature name (design-notes '## Delete unstarred', CLAUDE.md search rules). syncReuseButton (gallery.js:160-178) swaps the card's ↻ for ⚠ on a checkpoint mismatch on purpose ('Warn before the click').
findings.rule_tension: Renaming the tick means rewording CLAUDE.md and design-notes prose, but no rule changes. Using 'star' keeps the documented 'Delete unstarred' name and the runs list's '3★' unchanged, so it is the lower-churn direction. 'Favourite' everywhere would leave 'Delete unstarred' as the odd one out. Keep the ⚠ mismatch glyph on the card's Reuse. The `favorites=` API parameter, `els.favOnly` and `#fav-only` keep their names.
findings.smokes_affected: smoke-analysis.json:315 (sheetNote endsWith ' · Favorites unticked: nothing in a new comparison is starred yet') and smoke-comparison.json:17 (sheetNote includes 'Favorites unticked') need the new note text. smoke.json:73 (includes('Re-render')) and smoke.json:176 ('unstarred images', 'keeping N starred') are unaffected. smoke-flux.json:40 (lbReuse '⚠ Reuse settings') is unaffected unless the lightbox Reuse label changes. No smoke reads the card star's aria-label or lb-fav's text.
findings.how_checked: Fresh FLUX.1 Krea [dev] fake on 7921 with 3 generated images. Driven at 2560x1305 with my own driver copy (verify-copy-a11y-2/drive.mjs, steps m77.json). I read every card tool's text, aria-label and title, toggled the star with a real button click, re-rendered the gallery and read the star again. I also captured the window.confirm text from deleteImage, ticked Favorites and searched 'fox' to show Re-render and Delete unstarred, opened the lightbox and read its .lb-actions, and took elshots of the gallery header and the lightbox column.
findings.verifier_notes: The cluster mixes one real bug (the star's state labelling: aria-label depends on render path, title static, no aria-pressed) with copy consistency and two taste-level items. The ↻ clash has little user cost, because Re-render always carries its text label and count. The claim 'Delete unstarred reads as a different concept' is weakly supported. The button is hidden while the Favorites tick is on (gallery.js:335), and its confirmation says 'keeping N starred' and requires typing the count, so a misread is unlikely to delete anything. That keeps severity at low. Lightbox parity (Show run) is a small real convenience, not a consistency fix.
findings.merge_note: copy-a11y-8 lists all five spellings, notes the card star's title doesn't follow state, and proposes 'star' everywhere.

sources.surface: Card tools, gallery header, lightbox actions
sources.observation: ↻ is 'Reuse settings' on every card (it fills the panel), and '↻ Re-render 19 at 1024×1024' in the header (it queues 19 GPU renders). The gallery tick says 'Favorites', the card's aria-label 'Favorite', the lightbox button '☆ Favourite' and the delete confirm 'favourite'. The card has six actions, while the lightbox has four with different glyphs and labels (Reuse is a text button with no ↻; there is no ⊞ or ❐).
sources.why_it_matters: An icon learned on the card as 'harmless, fills the panel' reappears on a button that starts a long GPU job. Mixed spelling and different action sets make the two surfaces feel like separate tools.

sources.surface: Lightbox button, card star, gallery tick, delete confirm, Delete unstarred, Runs list
sources.observation: The lightbox button reads '☆ Favourite' with the title 'Favourite (F)' (British). The card star's aria-label is 'Favorite', becoming 'Unfavorite' after a toggle (and the title stays 'Favorite' even when the card is starred). The gallery tick is 'Favorites'. The delete confirm says '(favourite, seed 31)'. The bulk action is '⌦ Delete unstarred … keeping N starred', the runs list marks '3★', and the sheet note reads 'Favorites unticked: nothing in a new comparison is starred yet'.
sources.why_it_matters: Mixed spelling and two different terms make 'Delete unstarred' read as a different concept from 'Favorites'. That is the one bulk delete on the page, so the user must be sure which images it keeps.

findings.title: Generate is 36 Tab presses from the prompt: 17 size buttons and 7 help badges in between
surfaces: Panel keyboard order
findings.recommendation: Give #presets and #tiers role="group" and aria-labels ('Aspect', 'Size in megapixels'). In syncSize, give the active button tabIndex 0 (the first button when the size matches no preset) and every other button -1, and set aria-pressed to match: today 'active' is only a class, so assistive tech cannot tell which preset is chosen. One keydown listener per strip moves focus on ArrowLeft/Right and Home/End across strip.querySelectorAll('button'). Enter or Space chooses, as now. Selecting on arrow is the radio pattern, but each choose() persists the panel and schedules a preview, so focus-only arrows are the safer pick. Measured result: Tab presses from the prompt to Generate go from 36 to 21. Separately, advertise the existing Ctrl+Enter (app.js:256) in Generate's title.
findings.documented_rule: CLAUDE.md and index.html:187-189: the ? badges sit outside the <label> on purpose, so a tap does not forward focus to the input. design-notes: syncSize walks the strip's buttons in ASPECTS order, and portrait/landscape pairs share a .pair box.
findings.rule_tension: None, if the badges stay focusable (they are the keyboard route to the tips) and the buttons keep their ASPECTS order inside the .pair boxes. Arrow-key handling must query strip.querySelectorAll('button'), not strip.children, because pairs are nested. The Refine dialog's #refine-scales already has role="group" with an aria-label, so the pattern has a precedent.
findings.smokes_affected: None. No smoke presses Tab or reads tabIndex on the strips. smoke-animagine.json:64-71 and smoke-flux.json:9-19 check the strip's structure and .click() its buttons; both are unchanged by a roving tabindex. Consider adding a step that focuses the active preset, presses ArrowRight and expects focus on the next button.
findings.how_checked: FLUX fake at 2560x1305. Recorded every real Tab press (CDP key with keyCode 9) through a focusin listener, starting at #prompt. Counted .help tab stops and preset buttons. Pressed ArrowRight on a preset button. Then gave both strips a roving tabindex in the page only (only the active button at tabIndex 0) and traced Tab again.
findings.verifier_notes: Every number reproduced exactly: 36, 17 size stops, 7 badges, 17 .help in all. Low is right. Ctrl+Enter already submits from anywhere, so this costs time only for someone tabbing to Steps, Seed or Batch. The missing aria-pressed is a small accessibility gap that the same change closes.

sources.surface: Panel keyboard order
sources.observation: Pressing real Tab from the prompt box on FLUX reached Generate on the 36th press. The stops were: size ?, 13 aspect buttons, 4 MP tiers, W, H, then a ? badge before each of Steps, CFG, Mu and True CFG, the Reference ?, the LoRA ?, the LoRA select, Seed, Batch, Runs and the dice. The panel has 17 `.help` tab stops in all, counting the grid fold. Each preset strip is a set of separate buttons, not a group with arrow-key movement.
sources.why_it_matters: Keyboard users, and anyone who tabs from the prompt to change Steps or Seed, wade through 17 size buttons every time. Ctrl+Enter avoids this only for submitting, and it isn't advertised (panel-4).

findings.title: Mu is a blank, unexplained box on FLUX, and the grid's Mu placeholder uses Turbo's 1.15 on every checkpoint
surfaces: Mu field and grid Mu axis
findings.recommendation: Set placeholder="auto" on #mu in index.html; blank means the pipeline's own shift, as the server's tip already says. In applyDefaults, set els.gridMu.placeholder = d.mu != null ? `none,${d.mu}` : '' so FLUX, Qwen-Image, NetaYume, NewBie and Z-Anime stop suggesting Turbo's 1.15. In the static #grid-mu-tip (index.html:351-354), change 'compares the pipeline's own against Turbo's' to 'compares the pipeline's own shift against a fixed 1.15'. Skip the optional warn class: the ? tip already says 'leave this blank'.
findings.documented_rule: design-notes 'mu is Turbo-only': FLUX derives its own shift and forcing Turbo's constant degrades it, so the profile leaves mu null. CLAUDE.md: mu_supported decides whether both Mu controls are disabled, so FLUX's Mu box must stay enabled. Per-checkpoint tooltips come from /api/status hints.
findings.rule_tension: None. A placeholder is not a value: els.mu.value stays '' and collect() still sends no mu. A grid placeholder taken from the profile (lastDefaults.mu) uses server data and invents nothing. The grid Mu tip is static syntax help, not a per-checkpoint hint, so removing 'Turbo's' from it keeps that rule.
findings.smokes_affected: None. The smokes check els.mu.value === '' (smoke-anima/kohaku/netayume/newbie/wai/z-anime :5) and the disabled flags (:6); a placeholder changes neither. No smoke reads either placeholder.
findings.how_checked: FLUX fake and Turbo fake. Read the placeholder, disabled state and value of #mu and #grid-mu, the server's mu hint, and the static #grid-mu-tip text. Checked backend profiles and the smokes for placeholder use.
findings.verifier_notes: Adjusted only in its description. Calling Mu 'unexplained' overstates it: its ? badge carries the server's 'leave this blank'. The real issues are the blank box beside True CFG's 'off' and the grid's Turbo-specific example and tip on every flow checkpoint, which suggest exactly the value the design notes say degrades FLUX. For null-mu profiles, use '' rather than a lone 'none', because 'none' alone is a one-cell axis that teaches nothing.

sources.surface: Mu field and grid Mu axis
sources.observation: On FLUX the Mu box is enabled and empty with no placeholder (True CFG next to it says 'off'). Its tip reads 'forcing a constant over it degrades the result: leave this blank'. The grid Mu field's placeholder is 'none,1.15', and its tip, static in index.html, says it 'compares the pipeline's own against Turbo's' on every checkpoint. status.js's tips map doesn't include it.
sources.why_it_matters: An empty box asks to be filled, and filling this one degrades FLUX output (design notes 'mu is Turbo-only'). A first-time user can't tell what Mu is or that blank means automatic. The grid example then suggests exactly the value that hurts this checkpoint.

findings.title: The starred-card badge looks like a button, but clicking it opens the lightbox
surfaces: Starred card badge (.card.fav::after)
findings.recommendation: Replace `.card.fav::after` (style.css:817-832) with a real `<button class="star fav-badge">` built in card(): top 6px, right 6px, 28px round, rgba(0,0,0,.62) background, amber 18px glyph. Show it always on .card.fav, and as ☆ on `.card:hover`, `.card:focus-within` and `@media (pointer: coarse)` for unstarred cards. Remove the star from .tools, so the per-card tab-stop count is unchanged and M45's row gets a slot back. Keep the aria-label toggle between Favorite and Unfavorite. Leave `.sheet-cell.fav::after` alone.
findings.documented_rule: style.css:827-830 comment: a starred card has to be found at a glance, with an amber ring and the star on a dark badge. style.css:796-798: tools are revealed by focus and on a coarse pointer. setFavorite (gallery.js:200-219) updates every element by id and class, never by re-rendering.
findings.rule_tension: A real button with the same look keeps the ring and the at-a-glance badge. Showing the unstarred ☆ only on hover, focus-within or coarse pointer follows the tools' reveal rule. Keeping class `star` on the new button means setFavorite's `.star` selector works unchanged.
findings.smokes_affected: None. No smoke selects .star, the badge or ::after; smoke.json:169 stars through setFavorite() directly. Re-run smoke.json for the Favorites and Delete unstarred steps.
findings.how_checked: FLUX fake on 7907, with card 3 starred through the API. I read the ::after computed style (content, size, offsets, pointer-events), clicked the badge's centre (1247,588) with a real mouse, and logged whether the lightbox opened and the record's favourite state. I hovered the card to measure where the real toggle sits.
findings.verifier_notes: Related to M45(c) (the star beside Delete) but not a duplicate: this is the misleading affordance of the badge. Doing both together removes the star from the overflowing row.

sources.surface: Starred card badge (.card.fav::after)
sources.observation: A starred card shows a 28px amber ★ in a dark circle at its top-right corner, the most button-like thing on the card. It is a pseudo-element with pointer-events: none. Clicking it on card id 60 opened the lightbox, and the image stayed starred. Unstarring needs the 24px ☆ in the hover row at the bottom, 4px from Delete.
sources.why_it_matters: Star and unstar are the triage gestures that Delete unstarred depends on. The obvious target does the wrong thing, and the real one sits next to the destructive button.

findings.title: Lightbox arrows are 40 px circles at the stage edges, and a near miss closes the lightbox
surfaces: Lightbox prev/next buttons and the stage backdrop
findings.recommendation: Keep the buttons outside .lb-stage. In layoutLightbox (web/lightbox.js), after placing the image, set `els.lbPrev.parentElement.style.setProperty('--lb-gutter', ...)` to `lbView.scale <= 1 ? clamp(48, gapBesideImage - 8, 160) : 48` px, where gapBesideImage is the image's left offset inside the stage. In web/style.css:927-946, make `.lb-nav { top: 20%; bottom: 20%; height: auto; transform: none; width: var(--lb-gutter, 48px); border: 0; border-radius: 12px; background: transparent; }`. Draw the existing 40px circle with `.lb-nav::before`, pinned to the strip's OUTER edge so it never moves between images of different aspect. Use `.lb-nav:hover:not(:disabled) { background: rgba(255,255,255,0.05) }` with the circle turning accent. The prev strip may also start at the dialog edge (`left: -18px`), so pushing the mouse to the screen edge hits it. The gutter never overlaps the fitted image, so no crop is covered and zoomed panning keeps its whole surface. The 20% top and bottom insets leave the corners as close targets: smoke.json's [30,30] still closes. Also add `.lb-stage:not(.zoomed) { cursor: default } .lb-stage:not(.zoomed) img { cursor: zoom-in }` at style.css:880: today the backdrop shows a zoom-in cursor where a click closes. A related, cheaper mitigation for the lost place: on close, scroll the walked-to card into view (`block: 'nearest'`). That card stays where it was: after walking to 42/96 and a near miss, it sat at y=1111 at QHD and below the fold (y=1305 of 1040) at 125%.
findings.documented_rule: docs/design-notes.md 'The lightbox zooms' (lines 979-1021) and index.html:484-487 / style.css:922-926: the arrows sit over the stage's edges but outside the stage in the tree, because the stage takes pointer capture. A click beside the image closes only at fit; zoomed in, the whole stage is a pan surface and only Escape or the cross close it. Arrows stay at the stage edges so a portrait crop is never covered.
findings.rule_tension: The proposed full-height 96px strip (top:0; bottom:0) conflicts twice. (a) tools/smoke.json:58 closes the lightbox with a click at [30,30]. At 1400x900 that point is inside a full-height prev strip, and lbIndex is 1 at that step, so the click would navigate and the `!open` expect at line 60 would fail. (b) Zoomed in, or for any image that fills the stage width (smoke.json's 1152x896 at 1400x900 touches both stage edges), transparent strips would take 96px bands of the pan surface: drags, wheel zoom and double-click there would go to the button. That breaks 'zoomed, the whole stage is a pan surface'. Compatible fix: size the hit area to the backdrop gap beside the fitted image, shrink it back to the circle when zoomed, and stop it short of the corners so a click on the backdrop still closes.
findings.smokes_affected: tools/smoke.json:58-60 (click [30,30], expect !lightbox.open): broken by the original full-height strip, unaffected by the gap-sized strip inset 20% from top and bottom. smoke.json:43-53 (click/dblclick [560,450], wheel [700,450]) stay clear of the strips. No smoke references .lb-nav's geometry; app.js:230-231 onclick handlers are unchanged.
findings.how_checked: On the same fake at 2560x1305@1 and 2048x1040@1.25, I opened a portrait image with a real click on its card and measured the rects of #lb-prev, #lb-next, #lb-img and #lb-stage. I then used real mouse clicks: the centre of each arrow; 10px and 42px right of the prev arrow; 20px above it; 10px left of the next arrow; and, zoomed in, 42px right of prev. I read the stage's computed cursor at fit. Lost place: I walked 40 images with ArrowRight, made a near-miss click, then measured where the walked-to card sits in the gallery.
findings.verifier_notes: The finding is accurate and worse than stated: even a 10px miss closes the lightbox, and the zoom-in cursor over the close zone misleads. The recommendation as written would break smoke.json's corner-close step and the documented zoomed pan surface, hence 'adjusted'. Low severity stands: the arrow keys work, and a miss costs re-finding the card, not work. The lost-place half overlaps gallery-9 (not in this batch).

sources.surface: Lightbox prev/next buttons and the stage backdrop
sources.observation: The prev arrow covers x=28-68 and next x=2179-2219 (40x40px, vertically centred). A portrait 896x1152 image spans x=630-1617, so about 560px of stage on each side is a close target at fit. A click at x=110, 42px right of the prev arrow, closed the lightbox.
sources.why_it_matters: Mouse users walking images aim at a small target far from the image. A slight miss throws them out of the lightbox and, with gallery-9, out of their place in the gallery.

findings.title: Turning off a sweep's sheet leaves the gallery filtered to that job
surfaces: Gallery after a strength sweep's sheet
findings.recommendation: Keep a module-level sheetReturn = null. In showSheetScope (panel.js:241), save the box's value before overwriting it (sheetReturn = { search: previous, wrote: search }), but only when sheetReturn is null or the sheet is off. That way back-to-back comparisons (smoke-comparison-batch) keep the original pre-sheet search. Route the card ⊞ handler (gallery.js:131-132) through showSheetScope too, so every page-opened sheet behaves the same; the run list already goes through showRun. In setSheet(false), if sheetReturn is set and els.search.value.trim() === sheetReturn.wrote, restore sheetReturn.search before resetGallery(). Always clear sheetReturn there and whenever the user types in the search box (app.js:228 oninput).
findings.documented_rule: sheet.js:551 setSheet: 'Off is a real escape hatch: whatever layout and pins were picked go with it' (layout and pins, not the search). panel.js:225-230: the gallery's filters are the sheet's, and Favorites is unticked for a fresh comparison and said so. design-notes 'The contact sheet'.
findings.rule_tension: Compatible. Restoring the search the page itself replaced does not touch layout and pins, and leaves a search the user typed alone. Trade-off: a user who turns Sheet off to see the run as cards loses that filter. The '(3)' count plus the visible job: text are the current cue. A light alternative or complement: show the gallery count as '(3 of 9)' whenever a search or Favorites narrows it.
