findings.smokes_affected: smoke-paging.json:27-33 types 'run:' into the box via eval and toggles els.sheetBtn, so it is not a page-written scope and is not restored: unaffected. smoke.json:69/89/105, smoke-analysis.json:137/320, smoke-conditioning.json:76 and smoke-refine.json:83 all call setSheet(false) and then set els.search.value themselves: unaffected. smoke-comparison-batch.json:9 and smoke-comparison.json:8-27 check the search only while the sheet is on: unaffected if sheetReturn is kept across consecutive showSheetScope calls.
findings.how_checked: On port 7909, after a 0.05,0.1,0.2 sweep opened its sheet (search 'job:88b58dc00b80', empty before), I clicked the real Sheet button (els.sheetBtn) and measured the search value, sheetMode, the gallery count and the record count. I took a screenshot, then read showSheetScope, setSheet, the card ⊞ handler and the run-list handler, and grepped the smokes for sheet-off steps.
findings.verifier_notes: Real as described, and minor: the job: text is visible in the search box, so the filter is discoverable, and it costs one extra clear. I marked it adjusted because the behaviour is not refine-specific: comparisons, the Runs list, 'Show run' and the card ⊞ all leave their scope behind. The fix has to keep the pre-sheet search across back-to-back page-opened sheets and route ⊞ through showSheetScope, as the corrected recommendation says. Both servers (7909, 8909) were stopped and are no longer listening.

sources.surface: Gallery after a strength sweep's sheet
sources.observation: A sweep opens its sheet through showSheetScope, which writes 'job:19990e689849' into the search box. Pressing Sheet to go back turns sheet mode off but keeps the search, so the gallery still shows only the 3 sweep images (total 3) until the user clears the box. That makes 6 clicks for 'try three strengths and pick one', where 4 would do.
sources.why_it_matters: It happens after every sweep, and a gallery showing 3 of its images looks as if the rest have gone.

findings.title: The Refine dialog re-centres on every height change, so its controls jump
surfaces: Refine dialog box position
findings.recommendation:
Anchor the dialog at a fixed top and let it grow downward. The margin must also come out of max-height:
.refine-dialog { margin-top: max(16px, 8vh); margin-bottom: auto; max-height: calc(100vh - max(16px, 8vh) - 16px); }
Measured with this CSS injected:
- QHD: the top stays at 104 in all four states. Strength stays at y 446 and the fold's summary at y 549 through fold toggle, sweep and refusal (baseline: summary 797 then 661, Strength 694/686/558/542).
- 2048x1040@1.25: fold open plus error is 907 tall at top 83, leaving a 50px bottom gap. It fits.
- 1400x900: it scrolls (scrollHeight 880, clientHeight 810), with a 16px bottom gap.
The proposed #refine-preview min-height (two lines reserved) is optional. With the top anchored, a second preview line only moves the controls below it (Refine moves down 20px) and no longer the box being typed in. Reserving two lines would add an empty line under every one-line preview, so skip it.
findings.documented_rule: web/style.css:964-966 comment: 'centred by the UA ... Scrolls on a short screen' (max-height: calc(100vh - 32px); overflow-y: auto). No CLAUDE.md or design-notes rule fixes the vertical position.
findings.rule_tension: The reviewer's CSS breaks the 'scrolls on a short screen' contract. Without injection, at 1400x900 (the smokes' size) with the fold open and the error shown, the dialog is 865px tall and the UA centres it at top 18. With only margin-top: max(16px, 8vh), the top is 72 and max-height stays 100vh-32px, so the dialog's bottom ends 36.5px below the viewport. The Refine button then sits at y 875-918, partly off a 900px screen, and the dialog does not scroll (scrollHeight 863 = clientHeight 863). The fix below takes the top margin out of max-height. Tested: at 1400x900 it scrolls inside a 16px bottom gap.
findings.smokes_affected: None. No smoke step reads the dialog's position or clicks by coordinates. All refine smokes click through eval.
findings.how_checked: Fresh FLUX.1 Krea [dev] fake on 7911. Opened the dialog from the card's ⤢ and measured getBoundingClientRect of the dialog, Refine, Strength and the fold's summary in four states: fold closed, fold open, a sweep typed into Strength with real key input, and a refused press. I ran this at 2560x1305@1, 2048x1040@1.25 and 1400x900@1. I then injected the reviewer's CSS and my corrected CSS through a <style> element (the repo was not edited) and measured again.
findings.verifier_notes: Every number the reviewer gave reproduced to the pixel. The strongest pointer cost is the fold's own summary jumping 136px: the user clicks 'Prompt and sampling' and a second click to close it misses. Low severity stands, since nothing is lost. The only correction is the max-height: as written, the fix breaks the short-screen scrolling the CSS comment promises.

sources.surface: Refine dialog box position
sources.observation: The UA centres the modal vertically, so any content change moves everything. Opening 'Prompt and sampling' moves the dialog's top from y=372 to 236 and the Refine button from y=892 to 1028 (136 px). Typing a sweep in Strength adds a second preview line and shifts the dialog, including the box being typed in, up 8 px (372 to 364). The refused-press error line shifts it another 16 px (236 to 220).
sources.why_it_matters: Controls moving under the pointer and caret is part of the 'clunky' feel. A user going for Refine after opening the fold finds it 136 px lower.

findings.title: Refine dialog controls drift from the panel's: no 🎲 on Seed, and Strength doesn't step with the arrow keys
surfaces: Refine dialog: Seed and Strength fields
findings.recommendation:
Add <button type="button" class="ghost square" id="refine-dice" title="Clear the seed (random)" aria-label="Clear the seed, so the pass draws a random one">🎲</button> after the Seed sub in the same .row (index.html:594). Wire it in app.js to els.refineSeed.value = ''; refineChanged(); and add it to els in state.js.
On #refine-strength keydown ArrowUp/ArrowDown, when SINGLE_STRENGTH matches the trimmed value: preventDefault, step by 0.05 (0.01 with Shift), round to 2 decimals, clamp to [0.01, 1], write the value and call refineChanged(). 0.05 is the FLUX.1 granularity in the design notes, and fine enough for SDXL's 0.35-0.5. Leave other keys and multi-value text alone.
findings.documented_rule: CLAUDE.md, Frontend and CLI: the dialog 'has its own size, strength, versions and seed' and never writes the panel's Seed box. index.html:589 'Text, not a number: several strengths are a sweep.' design-notes 'The refine pass': measured FLUX.1 granularity 0.05/0.1/0.15 (the face changed at 0.15), and WAI's author's 0.35-0.5 for SDXL.
findings.rule_tension: A 🎲 button that clears only #refine-seed and calls refineChanged keeps the seed the dialog's own. Arrow stepping applies only to a value matching SINGLE_STRENGTH, so a list or a range is never touched and the box stays type=text. The reviewer's step of refineDefaultStrength()/2 is 0.2 on SDXL: one press takes 0.4 to 0.6, past the 0.35-0.5 range the SDXL default is based on. On FLUX.1 it equals the 0.05 step that was measured. Use one fixed fine step instead.
findings.smokes_affected: None. Steps that read els.refineSeed.value (smoke-refine 18, 23, 66, 97, 109, 117) and the strength values are unaffected by a new button or a keydown handler. No smoke presses arrow keys in the dialog.
findings.how_checked: Logged the buttons in the dialog's Seed row: none, while the panel has #btn-dice at [290,831,41,39]. Logged #refine-strength's type: text. Focused Strength with the value '0.1' and pressed ArrowUp through the DevTools protocol: the value stayed '0.1'. Read the design notes' strength granularity table to check the proposed step size.
findings.verifier_notes: Both facts hold. The payoff is small: clearing the seed is already a select and a delete, and Versions 2/4 gives several seeds in one run, so the 'try a few seeds' case is partly covered. Keep it at low. The only change from the reviewer's version is the fixed 0.05 step, which keeps SDXL from jumping 0.2 per press.

sources.surface: Refine dialog: Seed and Strength fields
sources.observation: The panel's Seed row has a 🎲 button ('Clear seed (randomize)'). The dialog's Seed has none, so getting a fresh seed means selecting and deleting the number, after which the hint changes to 'a random seed'. Strength is a text box (for sweeps), so ArrowUp/Down do nothing, unlike every other numeric box in the panel and the fold (Steps, CFG, Mu, True CFG).
sources.why_it_matters: Trying a few seeds or nudging strength by one notch are the two most common adjustments in a refine loop, and both take more keystrokes than the panel's equivalents.

findings.title: Inserting between chips works only by right-click, hinted by 10 px text whose position moves
surfaces: Chip tray insertion affordance
findings.recommendation: Keep right-click. Three changes, all in tags.js and style.css. (1) In renderTagValidation, after the last chip and only when tagInsertAt !== results.length, append a real <button class="tag-add" type="button">+ tag</button> whose onclick calls openTagInsert(results.length). Style it as a dashed 12 px pill like .tag-check. This also gives keyboard users a visible insert. (2) On tray pointermove (throttled with requestAnimationFrame, and only when the target is the tray itself, not a chip), call tagInsertionIndexAtPoint(x, y). Show the boundary by adding the existing .drop-before/.drop-after classes to the neighbouring chip, the same 4 px accent bar drag uses, and clear it on pointerleave. A plain click on the tray itself (event.target === els.tagValidation) opens openTagInsert at that index. (3) Pin the hint so it stops travelling: '.tag-validation-wide .tag-validation { position: relative; padding-bottom: 26px }' with '::after { position: absolute; left: 12px; bottom: 7px; font-size: 11px }'. Reword it to 'double-click edits · drag or Alt+←/→ moves · right-click a gap, or + tag, inserts'. Also add the Menu-key insert to the chip aria-label (tags.js:392): 'Enter edits it; Alt+arrows move it; the Menu key inserts after it; Delete removes it.'
findings.documented_rule: CLAUDE.md, Frontend and CLI: 'Validation chips edit the prompt: drag (or Alt+Left/Right) reorders, × or Delete removes, and right-clicking a gap inserts there (a chip inserts after itself) with autocomplete. All mutations must go through writePromptTags.' design-notes.md, 'Those chips are a round-trip editor, not a second prompt' (context click in any flex gap; one editor at a time; any outside prompt change closes it).
findings.rule_tension: No conflict. A '+' pill or a click-in-gap path that calls openTagInsert() commits through commitTagEdit -> writePromptTags, the same as right-click, and right-click stays as the accelerator. The pill must not render while the editor is already open at results.length (renderTagValidation line 461), and the pill and the hover marker are lost on every re-render, which is the same lifecycle as the editor.
findings.smokes_affected: A '+ tag' child of #tag-validation breaks every step that asserts all children are valid chips: smoke-animagine.json:12, smoke-illustrious.json:15, 23 and 26, smoke-kohaku.json:14 and 19 ('[...els.tagValidation.children].every(chip => chip.classList.contains("valid"))'). Change them to querySelectorAll('.tag-check'). smoke-animagine.json:22-23 (contextmenu in the gap between chips 1 and 2 -> tagInsertAt === 2) must still pass. smoke-animagine.json:16 and 56 and smoke-wai.json:19 are unaffected.
findings.how_checked: Fresh Animagine fake on 7918 at 2560x1305, DPR 1, with real CDP mouse and key events. I added a right-button step to a scratch copy of the driver (verify-tags-2/shot2.mjs). With an 18-tag prompt I hovered a 9 px gap (x=995, between chips 4 and 5), then left-clicked it, right-clicked it, right-clicked empty space after the last chip, right-clicked the hint text, and pressed the ContextMenu key on a focused chip. I logged tagInsertAt each time and measured the ::after hint and the cursor. Repeated with 70 tags.
findings.verifier_notes: Two parts of the original claim are wrong, so the verdict is adjusted. 'No way to add a tag at the end from the tray': right-clicking the empty space after the last chip inserts at the end (index 18). What is missing is a visible control for it. 'No Copy on a chip's text': chips are user-select:none (style.css:267), so the native menu never had a selection to copy, and losing it costs nothing. One small oddity: with one chip row, the hint wraps under the chips, and right-clicking the hint text inserts at index 0, the start, although the hint sits visually after the last chip. Pinning the hint also fixes that. Severity stays low: the textarea right beside the tray is the main way to insert, and the chips are an extra.

sources.surface: Chip tray insertion affordance
sources.observation: Right-click in a gap opened the inline editor at the right index (tagInsertAt=5), and right-click on the tray label inserted at 0. Both work well. The only visible cue is the ::after line 'double-click to edit · drag to reorder · right-click between tags to insert', at 10px in #b2b2c0. It follows the last chip, so it sits at the start of row 2 with 18 tags and at x≈2048 on row 4 with 70 tags. Nothing appears on hover in a gap. There is no '+' control and no way to add a tag at the end from the tray. A right-click anywhere in the tray also replaces the browser's context menu (no Copy on a chip's text).
sources.why_it_matters: In a chip editor, adding a tag between two others is a core action. The usual cue for it (a '+' or a gap that lights up on hover) is missing, so most users will retype in the cramped textarea instead.

findings.title: An unknown tag shows a red '?' only; the reason, the cutoff and a fix are tooltip-only
surfaces: Unknown chips (.tag-check.unknown)
findings.recommendation: (1) Add one shared tooltip element (#tag-tip, reusing the .tip styling at style.css:144-155) outside the tray. Position it under the hovered or focused .tag-check.unknown and fill it with result.reason plus 'generation is still allowed'. Link it from the chip with aria-describedby. Keeping it out of the chip keeps chip.textContent unchanged and keeps it out of the tray's role="status" live region. Keep the native title for everything else. (2) Add a 'code' field to the validation results in backend/tags.py:_validation ('not_found' | 'deprecated' | 'empty' | 'no_date' | 'after_cutoff'). For after_cutoff, render a clock mark '⏲' in place of '?' with the same red outline. Today WAI never produces it, since its cutoff is None. (3) Show counts in the label: set els.tagValidation.dataset.label = 'Prompt tags · Danbooru · 2 unknown' in renderTagValidation and change .tag-validation::before to content: attr(data-label). (4) Drop the automatic 'did you mean'. /api/tags/suggest is an alias-aware prefix search (design-notes), so it returns nothing for typical typos ('gren hair') or OC names ('zzkx oc'). The existing double-click editor already autocompletes from the first keystroke, so the tip can just say 'double-click to fix'.
findings.documented_rule: design-notes.md, Animagine section: 'red means unknown, deprecated, empty or too new. An unavailable API makes ordinary tags grey and unchecked, not invalid, and never blocks generation'. 'A valid chip uses high-contrast light text ... unknown chips keep the corresponding red mark/outline'. CLAUDE.md: 'lookup failure stays advisory and never blocks'; WAI v17's cutoff stays None.
findings.rule_tension: Sharing one red for all four reasons is deliberate, and the reasons can be told apart without breaking that: keep the red outline and change only the mark and the visible reason. The advisory wording ('generation is still allowed') must stay. A suggestion must stay an offer, never an automatic rewrite. Matching on the free-text reason string to pick a glyph would be fragile. A small reason code from the backend is the compatible way to do it.
findings.smokes_affected: None if the tip lives outside the chip, since no smoke reads chip.title, the tray title or ::before. If the tip were put inside the chip instead, it would change chip.textContent, which smoke-animagine.json:16 ('textContent.includes("made up tag")') and smoke-wai.json:19 (filters chips by textContent containing 'quality' or 'masterpiece') read.
findings.how_checked: On the Animagine fake I rendered the backend's four 'unknown' reasons through the page's own renderTagValidation ('not found in Danbooru', 'created after this checkpoint's 2025-01-07 cutoff', 'deprecated Danbooru tag', 'Danbooru tag has no posts'; strings taken from backend/tags.py:180-192). I compared them in an element shot, read the chip titles and the ::before label from the DOM, and checked whether /api/tags/suggest (a prefix search) could produce a 'did you mean'.
findings.verifier_notes: The core claim reproduces: the reason is in a native title only, and four different reasons look identical. I adjusted the recommendation because the 'did you mean' step would rarely fire with a prefix-search endpoint, and because choosing a glyph by matching the reason string is fragile, so a backend reason code is proposed instead. Effort drops to S without the suggestion fetch. Severity stays low: the red chip is easy to spot, the tooltip does work, and nothing is ever blocked.

sources.surface: Unknown chips (.tag-check.unknown)
sources.observation: 'zzkx oc' and 'dreamy vibe' render as red-outlined '?' chips, easy to spot among 68 green ones. Why ('not found in Danbooru; generation is still allowed') is only in a native title. The backend's other reasons (deprecated, empty, created after the 2025-01-07 cutoff) look identical. The tray label gives no count, so on 4 rows you scan for red. You cannot get from an unknown chip to the nearest real tag without double-clicking and retyping.
sources.why_it_matters: 'Too new for this checkpoint' (a character the model never saw) and 'typo' need different fixes, and the advisory 'generation is still allowed' is hidden behind a slow native tooltip. The tray tells you something is wrong but not what to do.

findings.title: The Runs picker fills with single Generates and pushes grids off its 20-entry list
surfaces: Gallery head: Runs… dropdown
findings.recommendation: In loadRuns (web/panel.js:205-223), request limit 200. Put runs with images > 1 or jobs > 1 in an <optgroup label="Grids and batches">, labelled with their count and, where run.prompts > 1, 'N prompts'. Put at most 8 runs with images === 1 in a trailing <optgroup label="Single images">, each labelled with its seed or time to the second, because the clipped prompt makes consecutive singles identical. A 1-image run's sheet is one cell that the gallery's first card already shows, so dropping singles from the picker entirely is also acceptable.
findings.documented_rule: design-notes 'The morning after: runs and finished jobs': GET /api/runs groups by run_id and the UI reads it into the Runs picker (pick one: run:<id> search plus the sheet). run_id is derived from the run's cell keys (backend/grid.py:620), so every random-seed Generate is its own run. The picker follows the All models scope (panel.js:206-209).
findings.rule_tension: Compatible. Grouping and a larger limit change only the presentation. The run:<id> plus sheet on pick (app.js:220, showRun) and the scope parameter stay. The server already allows limit up to 200 (main.py:1216) and already returns images, prompts and jobs per run (schemas.py:741-765), so the grouping needs no backend change.
findings.smokes_affected: smoke.json:38 (options.length >= 2), :110/:114 (some option value === 'planted'; the planted run has 2 images so it lands in the grids group) and :160 (an option containing '(2 distinct)') all read els.runList.options, which includes options inside <optgroup>s. They should pass unchanged; re-run smoke.json. No other smoke references run-list.
findings.how_checked: Same 7919 fake. Submitted a 4-image steps grid, a 12-image prompt-variable grid and a 4-image batch through the page's fetch, then 16 single 1-image Generates. Called loadRuns() and logged every option of #run-list. Also fetched /api/runs?limit=200 to count singles and find where the grids sit.
findings.verifier_notes: Reproduced exactly as described. In an iteration session the picker becomes a list of identical single-Generate lines, and grids fall off after about 20 more Generates. Low is right: a grid stays reachable through its gallery card's sheet button or a run: search, and the morning-after banner's 'Show run' covers the latest job. Still, the one control meant for reopening a night's grid stops doing that job.

sources.surface: Gallery head: Runs… dropdown
sources.observation: After this walkthrough the picker held 20 entries, of which 13 were single 1-image Generates ('4 Oct, 03:39 pm · 1 img · portrait of an old fisherman, weathered fac…'). The three real grids/comparisons (4, 12 and 8 images) were entries 5-7. loadRuns asks for limit 20, so about 14 more ordinary Generates push last night's grid off the list. Several labels are identical apart from the minute.
sources.why_it_matters: The design note calls the picker the gallery's table of contents for night grids. In normal use it becomes a click log, and the run you want to reopen as a sheet (Task 5) is the one that falls off.

findings.title: The Refine dialog opens focused on its last control, so the first Tab leaves the dialog
surfaces: Refine dialog focus order
findings.recommendation: Move autofocus from #refine-run (index.html:628) to #refine-strength, and in openRefine call els.refineStrength.focus({preventScroll: true}); els.refineStrength.select() after showModal() (refine.js:157), so a typed value replaces the profile's strength. Keep the one-key run: add a keydown listener on els.refineDialog that calls runRefine() for a plain Enter (no Ctrl/Meta) whose target is an <input> (Strength, W, H, Seed). Exclude textareas, the Versions select and buttons. This works like a form's implicit submit, so 'open, Enter' still runs the pass and typing '0.3' then Enter runs it at 0.3. Keep the Refine title 'Run the pass (Ctrl+Enter)' and update the index.html:624-625 comment. Simply reordering the DOM so Refine comes earlier would break the visual order, so it is not recommended.
findings.documented_rule: index.html:624-628: 'autofocus: showModal() would otherwise focus the cross, the first control in the tree.' CLAUDE.md 'Frontend and CLI' (Refine dialog): 'Ctrl+Enter in the dialog runs the pass, not Generate'. Refine is aria-disabled with the reason as its title when refused, and a press says it in the dialog (refine.js:239, :361).
findings.rule_tension: Focusing Strength also avoids the cross, so the comment's purpose holds. Moving autofocus off Refine loses one thing the current focus gives: 'open, Enter' runs the pass at once (measured), the fast path for the defaults the dialog opens with. The compatible fix keeps that path by making Enter in the dialog's single-line inputs run the pass through the same runRefine(), which already refuses with the reason when Refine is aria-disabled. Ctrl+Enter is unchanged.
findings.smokes_affected: smoke-refine.json:25 (expects document.activeElement === els.refineRun on open) must expect els.refineStrength, and could also check selectionStart 0 / selectionEnd = value length. smoke-refine.json:103 dispatches a synthetic Ctrl+Enter keydown on els.refineStrength and is unaffected, because the new handler ignores Ctrl+Enter, which app.js:259-262 already routes. No other smoke reads the dialog's focus.
findings.how_checked: FLUX fake on 7921 at 2560x1305 (m108.json). I opened Refine by focusing a card's ⤢ and pressing a real Enter, then logged activeElement. I pressed Tab 16 times and Shift+Tab 7 times from Refine, logging each stop. I pressed Escape to check focus return. Then I reopened Refine by click and pressed a single Enter, counting gallery rows via /api/gallery before and after.
findings.verifier_notes: The observation reproduces exactly. I marked it adjusted because the finding's recommendation (autofocus Strength, rely on Ctrl+Enter) silently removes the measured open-then-Enter run. The dialog's design leans on that path: design-notes say a remembered strength is never a sweep 'or the next open would start one'. The Enter-in-inputs handler keeps it. Severity stays low: it costs keyboard users five Shift+Tabs per open and does not affect mouse users.

sources.surface: Refine dialog focus order
sources.observation: The dialog autofocuses Refine, its last control. The first Tab from there leaves the dialog (D1 = BODY headless; browser chrome in a real window). The next Tab reaches the ✕, and the first editable field, Strength, is the 11th Tab (D1-D11). The scale buttons expose 'times the source's size' names (good), but the user who opens Refine to change the strength must Shift+Tab back across Cancel, the Prompt and sampling fold, Seed and Versions.
sources.why_it_matters: Strength and scale are what a pass is opened to set. Starting on the last control makes keyboard use of the new dialog backwards.

findings.title: A lightbox delete gives no acknowledgement: the counter's numerator, the zoom and the crop stay where they were
surfaces: Lightbox after Delete
findings.recommendation: After forgetImages re-renders the lightbox, call `showError(`Deleted image ${id} (seed ${seed}).`, true)`. showError already mirrors into #lb-error, which is role=alert, so screen readers hear it too. Clear it on the next stepLightbox. Optionally run `els.lbImg.animate([{opacity: .25}, {opacity: 1}], {duration: 180})`, guarded by prefers-reduced-motion. Don't reset lbView.
findings.documented_rule: design-notes 'The lightbox zooms': lbView carries over between records of the same size, so the zoom is kept by design.
findings.rule_tension: A transient note and a short fade leave lbView alone, so the zoom carry-over is kept.
findings.smokes_affected: None. No smoke deletes from the lightbox or reads #lb-error after a delete.
findings.how_checked: Opened card 20 in the lightbox, zoomed with four '+' presses to 303%, then pressed Delete twice (confirm stubbed true). I logged lbCount, lbZoom, lbView, #lb-error, prompt and settings after each, and compared screenshots v2-lb-mid-zoomed.png and v2-lb-mid-after-del1.png. I did the same on fox seed 200.
findings.verifier_notes: 'No acknowledgement' overstates it: the counter's denominator drops, and the image, prompt and seed change. The real gap is that nothing names the delete, so on near-identical sweep images at a carried-over zoom the swap is easy to miss, and assistive tech gets nothing. Lowered to low polish; the fix is cheap and keeps the zoom rule.

sources.surface: Lightbox after Delete
sources.observation: Opened card 20, zoomed to 242% and pressed Delete three times. The counter went 20/82 → 20/81 → 20/80 → 20/79, the zoom stayed '242%' at x 0, y 0 (same size key), and #lb-error was empty after each. The only changes were the prompt line and the seed in the settings line (b01 vs b02). On the fox batch the prompt is shared, so only 'seed 201' → 'seed 202' changes.
sources.why_it_matters: On a sweep of near-identical images a delete looks as if nothing happened. A second Delete then removes the neighbour, whose confirm differs from the first by one digit (finding 2).

findings.title: After deletes, the Runs picker and the last-run banner still advertise deleted images and runs
surfaces: Runs picker in the gallery head; last-run banner
findings.recommendation: Call loadRuns() at the end of deleteImage (after forgetImages) and of deleteUnstarred (after resetGallery). That is one GET of 20 rows, the same thing generation.js:479-480 already does after a run. With G2.4's `deleted_count` on the job snapshot, announceLastRun (panel.js:168) writes '6 images (6/6 cells), 4 since deleted', or '..., all since deleted' with #last-run-show hidden when nothing is left.
findings.documented_rule: design-notes 'The morning after: runs and finished jobs': the Runs picker reads GET /api/runs (images, favourites, distinct prompts, jobs). The banner reads /api/jobs?include_finished=true, gated to one announcement per job per browser. design-notes 'The gallery is the running checkpoint's': the picker follows the All models scope.
findings.rule_tension: None for loadRuns(), which already reads the gallery's scope. The banner part depends on G2.4's server change, and should report the produced count plus a deleted count rather than lowering image_count (see G2.4's notes).
findings.smokes_affected: None. smoke.json:110, :114 and :160 read runList options ('planted' and '(2 distinct)') after generation and the All models toggle, not after deletes. No smoke reads the last-run banner text.
findings.how_checked: After the whole-gallery sweep in flow 1, I compared els.runList options with GET /api/runs. In a fresh page I read the last-run banner against the job's image_count after 4 of its 6 images were deleted. I then deleted one card via ⌦ and compared the picker with /api/runs again, and pressed the banner's Show run.
findings.verifier_notes: Reproduced. I didn't empty a run entirely in this pass, so I didn't see the 'Nothing matches' sheet. It follows directly from the run: search, given the stale banner and picker shown here. Low severity as filed.

sources.surface: Runs picker in the gallery head; last-run banner
sources.observation: After 8 of the teapot run's 9 images were deleted, the picker still read '4 Oct, 04:15 pm · 9 img · 1★ · a teapot on a windowsill…'. The fox run still read '4 img' after one of its images was deleted. After the whole-gallery sweep the picker still listed '1 img · a lighthouse on a cliff at dusk', whose only image was gone. With all 4 images of its run deleted, the banner still read 'Last run finished at 4 Oct, 04:23 pm: 4 images (4/4 cells).', and Show run opened a sheet saying 'Nothing matches. The filters above the sheet are the gallery search.' (e04).
sources.why_it_matters: The picker is the gallery's table of contents (design notes). Stale counts and emptied runs send the user to empty sheets and misreport what is left.

findings.title: Once any adapter is hidden, the LoRA help is replaced by a raw module path, the file name appears twice, and the default explanation is gone
surfaces: LoRA ? tip (#lora-tip)
findings.recommendation: In refreshLoras (status.js:257-270), start every state from the default and name the directory: `A LoRA adapter from ${body.directory}; Weight 0-2 scales its effect.` Then append a blank line and the hidden list: `Not shown, for another checkpoint: ${hidden.map(e => `${e.name} - ${e.detail.startsWith(e.name) ? e.detail.slice(e.name.length).trim() : e.detail}`).join('; ')}`. Give the tip class 'wide' (300px, pre-line) when it carries the list.
findings.documented_rule: CLAUDE.md, LoRA: a misfit is listed with its detail and hidden by the page. status.js:236-241 says the tooltip names a hidden file 'and says why'.
findings.rule_tension: The detail must stay reachable, and it does if it follows the default text instead of replacing it. Keep the 'Not shown, for another checkpoint: other-family.safetensors - ' phrase and '494 modules' somewhere in the tip, or update the smoke.
findings.smokes_affected: smoke-conditioning.json:14 uses startsWith('Not shown, for another checkpoint: other-family.safetensors - ') and includes('494 modules'). Change startsWith to includes; the stripped detail keeps '494 modules'.
findings.how_checked: Logged els.loraTip, the options and loraTipDefault on the klein fake, whose loras/ holds demo-style plus other-family. Hovered the LoRA ? badge with a real mouse move and measured the tip. Read backend/loras.py:176-187 to confirm the real detail also starts with the file name. I also removed demo-style from my scratch loras/ dir to see the 'every adapter' variant.
findings.verifier_notes: Reproduced; low severity is right. The only smoke change needed is startsWith becoming includes.

sources.surface: LoRA ? tip (#lora-tip)
sources.observation: With other-family.safetensors in loras/, the tip reads in full: 'Not shown, for another checkpoint: other-family.safetensors - other-family.safetensors attaches to 494 modules the fake's denoiser has not got, such as single_transformer_blocks.0.attn.to_k'. The default text 'A LoRA adapter from the loras/ directory, at a scale.' is gone, and nothing explains Weight or where to put a file. The real detail also starts with the name (backend/loras.py:183-186: f"{name} attaches to …"), so the duplication happens on the real server too. On hover the tip is a 240x98 px box of 11 px text that covers the select and the Seed row (k30-lora-tip.png). The select's option reads 'demo-style.safetensors (51.0 B)'.
sources.why_it_matters: The tip is the only explanation of the adapter controls, and with any stray file in the directory it becomes a debugging message. The user loses what Weight does and where adapters live, and reads 'single_transformer_blocks.0.attn.to_k' instead of 'made for a different model'.

findings.title: On SDXL the dialog's only size warning is FLUX's VRAM line, which fires at 2x though the SDXL pipeline was measured at 8.6 MP
surfaces: Refine dialog size line (#refine-size-hint)
findings.recommendation: Add a profile key such as refine_tight_pixels, passed in ModelStatus.defaults like refine_strength, with null meaning 'not measured: keep the 1600² default line'. Fill it only from verified.md rows: WAI v17 none within the guard (8.6 MP ran at 11,363 MiB card, 5.53/7.60 GiB), so no VRAM note; Z-Anime and FLUX.1 Krea dev about 2.4e6 (filled the card at 2.4 MP and spilled at 4.2). In refine.js:190, use w*h > (lastDefaults?.refine_tight_pixels ?? 1600*1600) only when the key is not explicitly 'none'. For the three unmeasured SDXL profiles, either keep the generic line or word it as borrowed: 'WAI v17, the same SDXL pipeline, ran 8.6 MP on 16GB; this checkpoint is unmeasured'. Keep the substring '16GB' in the FLUX wording. Add the key to tests/test_profiles.py and rewrite the design-notes sentence.
findings.documented_rule: design-notes 'The refine pass' > 'A pass has a size guard of its own': 'It is a typo guard, not a VRAM model … The dialog's size line says "may run tight on 16GB VRAM" past 1600x1600, as the panel's does; the time estimate, from passes already made at that size, is the honest per-checkpoint answer.' CLAUDE.md: 'A typo guard, not a VRAM model: what fits is the checkpoint's (docs/verified.md).' sizes.js:121-123.
findings.rule_tension: The generic line is a documented choice, so changing it means updating that design-notes paragraph. A per-profile figure is compatible with 'what fits is the checkpoint's' only if every value is quoted from verified.md and unmeasured checkpoints say so. Animagine, Kohaku and Illustrious are explicitly 'Not measured' (verified.md:395), so they cannot silently take WAI's 8.6 MP. The 8.4 MP guard stays separate and unchanged.
findings.smokes_affected: smoke-refine.json (FLUX fake, 7875): step 28 expects '2.3 MP — 1.5× the source' with no warn at 1344x1728 (2.32 MP, which stays under a 2.4e6 FLUX value). Step 31 expects '2× the source' and '16GB' at 1792x2304 (4.1 MP), so the FLUX wording must keep '16GB' or the step changes. Steps 52 and 57 (5.2 MP startsWith; the guard text) are unaffected. No SDXL smoke asserts the dialog's size line.
findings.how_checked: On the same Animagine fake at QHD, I clicked each scale button and read #refine-size-hint text and class. I compared the result with docs/verified.md's 'Past 4 MP' table and the design-notes paragraph that documents the line.
findings.verifier_notes: Reproduced exactly. I adjusted the recommendation because the original set Animagine, Kohaku and Illustrious to WAI's 8.6e6 'from the WAI row'. verified.md lists those three as not measured, and the task's own constraint says unmeasured checkpoints must be said to be unmeasured. The generic 1600² line is right for FLUX and Z-Anime at 2× and wrong only for SDXL, so this is copy-level, low severity. It shares a fix with the other reviewers' M9 (per-profile key), which is not in this list.

sources.surface: Refine dialog size line (#refine-size-hint)
sources.observation:
Animagine source 832×1216:
- 1.5× is 1248×1824 and reads '2.3 MP — 1.5× the source', neutral.
- 2× is 1664×2432 and reads '4.0 MP — 2× the source — may run tight on 16GB VRAM' in yellow, at both viewports.
The threshold is the hard-coded 1600² (sizes.js:123). For the same SDXL pipeline, verified.md records WAI 0.4 passes at 5.5 MP (4.61/5.98 GiB) and 8.6 MP (5.53/7.60 GiB, card 11.4 GB including the desktop), keeping character and composition at every size. So on SDXL the warning discourages a scale the card handles. Nothing marks 1.5x as the documented SDXL hires recipe (WAI's author's 1.5x at 0.35-0.5). The guide's own size word ('recommended' 0.98-1.05 MP), which the panel quotes for the same 1248×1824 ('above the 1.1 MP this checkpoint is recommended for'), is rightly absent from the dialog, because a pass keeps the source's composition.
sources.why_it_matters: M9 shows the same line understating the risk on FLUX. On SDXL it overstates it. One global number is wrong in both directions, and the dialog's one warning is not trustworthy on any checkpoint.

findings.title: The budget-stop message undercounts cells by one, the ETA ignores the budget, and the banner calls a budget stop 'cancelled'
surfaces: Done message in #error (note style), #cell-note ETA, #last-run banner
findings.recommendation: (1) generation.js:468: use `${data.run}/${data.total_runs}`. jobs.py sets job.run = index+1 only after the deadline check (jobs.py:503-509), so at a budget stop `run` is already the count of finished cells. (2) panel.js:182: put `last.stopped_by === 'budget' ? 'stopped at its time budget'` ahead of the 'was cancelled' branch; its `(run/total cells)` is already right for a budget stop. (3) ETA: when a status frame carries deadline, store budgetSeconds = deadline - (started_at ?? created_at), all server-clock values. In showCell, budgetLeft = budgetSeconds - data.elapsed. Show `~${humanTime(Math.min(eta, budgetLeft))} left`, plus ' (budget)' when the budget binds. The budget means 'start no cell after', so the true end is up to one cell later; the label can say 'stops starting cells in ~X'.
findings.documented_rule: design-notes 'Time budget': a budget stop returns through the cancel path, and the UI reads stopped_by to say the plan worked. 'waiting_on and the ETA': the ETA is elapsed*(1-f)/f on the server's clock, so the browser and server clocks need not agree. 'The morning after': the banner reads /api/jobs for 'why'.
findings.rule_tension: Keep the cancelled status and stopped_by as they are. The proposed ETA, `data.deadline - Date.now()/1000`, mixes the browser's clock with the server's, which the ETA note avoids on purpose. Use only server timestamps from the status frame.
findings.smokes_affected: None. No smoke asserts the budget message, the banner text or the ETA. smoke.json:157 checks #cell-note's 'Finished 6 images', which is unaffected.
findings.how_checked: Same fake (--step 0.3). Grid of 40 seeds, batch 2, 4 steps, budget 0.3 min (the payload takes floats; the UI box's min=1 is advisory). I read the cell note at 6 s and 12 s, the done message, /api/jobs?include_finished=true, and after a reload the morning-after banner. Then I read backend/jobs.py's loop.
findings.verifier_notes: Shot paths are relative to scratchpad/ux/verify-results-2/shots/. All three defects reproduce. Severity lowered to low: the budget is an occasional overnight feature, and Resume's arithmetic is the server's (storage.completed_cells), so no output is wrong; only the copy contradicts itself. It is still a real off-by-one and a cheap S fix. Side note: for an ordinary mid-cell cancel the banner's (run/total cells) counts the cancelled cell as reached, so 'cells' does not mean 'finished' there either.

sources.surface: Done message in #error (note style), #cell-note ETA, #last-run banner
sources.observation: A 60-cell grid with a 1-minute budget ended with 'Time budget reached after 34/60 cells — kept 35 images. Resume finishes the rest.' (batch 1). /api/jobs reported run 35 and image_count 35. jobs.py sets job.run = index+1 only after the deadline check (jobs.py:495-507), so `run` is already the number of finished cells, and generation.js:468's `data.run - 1` is off by one. The next morning-after banner for the same job read 'Last run was cancelled … 35 images (35/60 cells)', with a different count and calling a planned stop a cancel (panel.js:182). During the run the ETA read '~74s left' at 17 s, ignoring the budget that stopped it about 45 s later.
sources.why_it_matters: Two different cell counts for the same job, one inconsistent with its own image count, undermine trust in the Resume arithmetic that the budget feature is built around. The ETA promises a finish the budget will not allow.

findings.title: The time budget isn't reflected in the grid preview, even when it can't finish one seed
surfaces: Budget box and grid preview
findings.recommendation: In previewGrid (generation.js:333-338), only when els.gridBudget has a value and p.seconds is set: `const seeds = p.values.seed.length || +els.gridSeeds.value; const perSeed = p.seconds / seeds; const done = Math.floor(budget * 60 / perSeed);` Append ` · budget ${budget} min ≈ ${Math.min(done, seeds)} of ${seeds} seeds complete`, adding ' (the load counts too)' when status is not ready. Add the warn class when done === 0. Per-seed time is exact under the estimate because every seed runs the same cells; dividing by images is unnecessary. Skip the line under Resume (p.skipped > 0), where the seeds are no longer uniform.
findings.documented_rule: Design notes 'Time budget': budget_minutes is counted from submission, load included, and seeds are the outer loop so a night that ends early has complete seeds. 'Grid preview and the per-step estimate': no matching history, no estimate.
findings.rule_tension: Show the budget line only when p.seconds exists, as the per-step rule requires. Because the budget counts the load, the line must not promise completions when the model is not loaded. When the status is not 'ready', append 'plus the load'.
findings.smokes_affected: None. smoke.json line 154 (preview warn plus '2 would be identical') and smoke-conditioning.json line 66 (preview includes '3 images') run with Budget empty, so the appended text never appears.
findings.how_checked: Second fake on 8913 with --step 0.03, so the per-step estimate exists. I seeded 3 direct images and set Steps 6-40x2, CFG 1-5x0.5, Seeds 4 in the panel. I read the preview, typed '1' into Budget (focus + insertText) and read it again. I also POSTed /api/grid/preview with and without budget_minutes. Screenshot: m57-01-budget.png.
findings.verifier_notes: Severity lowered from medium to low. The preview already shows the total time, so a user can compare it with the budget; the gap is the per-seed arithmetic. Budget is an occasional overnight feature, and a budget stop is recoverable by Resume. In my run, 1 minute against about 3 min total for 4 seeds completes 1 seed. The 'cannot finish one seed' case depends on the rate, but the mechanism (budget ignored by the preview) is confirmed.

sources.surface: Budget box and grid preview
sources.observation: Steps 6-40x2 × CFG 1-5x0.5 × 4 seeds previewed '648 images · 18 steps x 9 CFG x 1 mu x 4 seeds · about 11 min · ~6.1 MB'. Typing Budget = 1 left the preview unchanged. At the preview's own rate (~1 s per image) 1 minute covers ~59 images, while one seed's comparison is 162 cells. The budget will stop before a single seed completes, though its help text promises 'what the night reached is a complete comparison for those seeds'.
sources.why_it_matters: The budget exists to bound an overnight run usefully. Without the estimate the user learns in the morning that the stop came mid-seed, with nothing usable, which is the case the design was meant to avoid.

findings.title: Compare names the versions but hides their text in tooltips, and 'Your version' is a 2,135 px one-line box
surfaces: Compare on the same seeds: #compare-options, #compare-own
findings.recommendation: Drop the card grid. The 'scroll up to read it' cost does not reproduce: at QHD the Rewrite textarea (y=652) and the Reordered textarea (y=880) are on screen with the labels (y=1071), and at 2048x1040 they are at 635/863 against 1053. On a tag checkpoint, Check's reordering is in the Order section on the same screen. The real cost is Your version: 2135 px wide at 12px, about 403 characters a line, so a 416-character prompt sits in 2 lines while you move a clause. M60's `.analysis-text { max-width: 120ch }` fixes this, since #compare-own has that class (index.html:124), giving 3-4 lines of about 140 characters. Optional, cheap link from name to text: give the critic and Order textareas `data-variant="rewrite|reordered"`, and on focus or hover of a compare checkbox add an outline class to the matching box (`.analysis-text.linked { border-color: var(--accent-2) }`). Leave the label text as it is.
findings.documented_rule: CLAUDE.md, Frontend and CLI: Compare 'takes Check's reordered as its Reordered row, else the critic's... drops a version identical to another'; 'its Your version box (yours) is the one way to test order on prose'; the comparison fields are autocomplete=off. design-notes.md, 'The prompt analyser': 'the page shows every version to be read before it is used'. The critic's Rewrite and Reordered textareas are where that reading happens.
findings.rule_tension: A width cap is CSS only and changes nothing about compareChoice, the identical-version drop, autocomplete=off or Original's disabled-checked box. The proposed card grid would print each version's text a second time, 190-420 px below where the critic's own boxes already show it, and would change the label textContent that nine smoke steps assert. Any version text must go outside the <label>.
findings.smokes_affected: None for the CSS cap or the hover link. If version text were put inside the labels (the original proposal), these would break: smoke-analysis.json:123, 149, 151, 154, 161 and smoke-animagine.json:111, 115, 134, 142, which compare label textContent with 'Original,Reordered,Rewrite' and similar.
findings.how_checked: Same FLUX fake runs at both viewports. Read each #compare-options label's textContent, title and rect. Measured #compare-own empty and after 'Start from the prompt' (size and characters a line), and compared the labels' y with the y of the critic's Rewrite and Reordered textareas. On Animagine, located Check's own reordering in the Order section.
findings.verifier_notes: The width part overlaps M60, because the same CSS rule fixes both, so they should be implemented together. The 'versions hidden in tooltips' half is mostly refuted at the target screen sizes. Kept as adjusted rather than duplicate because Your version is a separate editing surface, and the only way to test order on FLUX prose.

sources.surface: Compare on the same seeds: #compare-options, #compare-own
sources.observation: Compare lists versions as checkboxes: Original, Reordered, Rewrite, Your version. Each version's text is only in its label's title tooltip. The texts are shown in the Critic or Order section, 300-500 px above, so you scroll up to learn what 'Reordered' says. Your version is a 2135x38 px textarea (one line is about 350 characters). After 'Start from the prompt' it is 2135x55 holding the 416-character prompt in 2 lines, which is very hard to scan when moving one clause.
sources.why_it_matters: Your version is the only way to test word order on a prose prompt (CLAUDE.md), and the flow means picking versions, so you need to see what you are picking. Very long lines make the 'move this clause' job slow and error-prone.

findings.title: With the grid fold open, the run hint promises Runs passes that Run grid silently ignores
surfaces: Seed/Batch/Runs hint vs grid preview
findings.recommendation: In previewGrid (generation.js:331), when +els.runs.value > 1, append to the preview's first line: ' · Runs (N) does not apply to a grid: Seeds is its count', in the comparison's existing wording style. Add els.runs to the schedulePreview listener list (app.js:178-181). Runs is missing from it today, so the preview would not refresh when Runs changes. Also extend the fold's static hint (index.html:305-308) with 'Runs does not apply: the grid's Seeds box counts seeds.' That sentence is needed because the hint's 'A blank axis keeps the single value already in the panel' reads as if Runs carries over. syncRuns can stay as it is.
findings.documented_rule: generation.js:244-248 and design notes 'Runs, not batches': runs is not a grid axis, the seed count is, and the server refuses a grid that sets both, so gridPayload sends runs: 1. The comparison panel already says 'The main Batch and Runs settings do not apply' (index.html:140).
findings.rule_tension: None. The client keeps sending runs: 1, and this only adds copy. The run hint is still true for Generate, which honours Runs with the fold open, so its wording for Generate should stay and the grid's own count should carry the clause.
findings.smokes_affected: None break. smoke.json:154 and smoke-conditioning.json:66 use includes() on #grid-preview with Runs 1, where the clause does not appear. Optionally add a step to smoke.json: Runs 4 with the grid open, expect the preview to include 'Runs (4) does not apply'.
findings.how_checked: FLUX fake. Typed a prompt, Batch 2 and Runs 4 with real input, opened the Grid search summary with a real click, set the steps axis to 20,28, read #run-hint and #grid-preview, then ran the grid and counted the images saved.
findings.verifier_notes: Reproduced as described. The finding's recommendation is sound. Putting the clause in the grid preview is the better of its two options, since the run hint still describes Generate correctly. Also found: Runs is not in the preview's input-listener list.

sources.surface: Seed/Batch/Runs hint vs grid preview
sources.observation: Batch 2 and Runs 4 with the grid open: the line under the Seed row reads '8 images over 4 passes, seed +2 each, from a random start.' A few lines lower the grid preview reads '4 images · 2 steps x 1 CFG x 1 mu x 1 seed'. gridPayload forces runs: 1, and nothing tells the user that the Runs box doesn't apply to Run grid (m01).
sources.why_it_matters: Two counts for one panel, a few lines apart, disagree. A user who set Runs for more variety will get fewer images overnight than they expected.

findings.title: Every gallery card is 7 tab stops (about 1,000 for 144 images), with no arrow-key grid navigation
surfaces: Gallery grid keyboard order
findings.recommendation: Use a roving tabindex inside #gallery only. In card() (web/gallery.js:91), set the img's tabIndex to -1 and its tools' tabIndex to -1. Keep one `galleryCurrent` id: that card's img and tools get tabIndex 0. Set it to the first card in resetGallery/loadGallery when unset, keep it as pages append (gallery.js:57), and move it to a neighbour in forgetImages (gallery.js:244) when the current card is deleted. One keydown listener on els.gallery (lightbox closed, target is a .card img) handles: ArrowLeft/Right ±1; ArrowUp/Down ± `getComputedStyle(els.gallery).gridTemplateColumns.split(' ').length` (measured 12 = per-row at QHD); Home/End; preventDefault on each. ArrowDown on the last loaded row calls loadGallery() when galleryMore. Move focus with `focus()` and `scrollIntoView({block:'nearest'})`. Tab from the current image goes through its six tools and then leaves the grid. Optionally, on lightbox close, make the walked-to record's card current, which also helps M87's lost place.
findings.documented_rule: style.css:793-796: card tools are revealed by :focus-within (and on coarse pointers) because hover-only left invisible tab stops that could overwrite the prompt or delete an image. panel.js:281-300 (thumb): images are focusable with role=button, and Enter/Space opens the lightbox, so the lightbox is reachable without a mouse. app.js:255-268: arrow keys are read only while the lightbox is open.
findings.rule_tension: A roving tabindex is compatible with both rules. Focus-within still reveals the current card's tools, and there are fewer invisible tab stops, not more. Images keep role=button and Enter/Space. The arrows on a gallery image do not collide with the global handler, which returns early while the lightbox is closed. One care point: thumb() is shared by the results viewer, gallery cards and sheet cells, so put the roving logic in card()/loadGallery, never in thumb().
findings.smokes_affected: None found. No smoke step presses Tab through cards or asserts a card's tabIndex or focus (grep for activeElement/tabIndex near card, lb or gallery: no hits). smoke-conditioning.json:28,33 and smoke-refine.json:20 click card tool buttons via eval, and smoke.json:40 clicks `.card img` via eval; none depends on tabIndex.
findings.how_checked: On the same fake at QHD I counted focusable elements per card and in total, at the first load (96 cards) and after scrolling to 144 cards, plus those before #gallery. I pressed Tab 7 times from the first card's image, then ArrowRight and ArrowDown with a card image focused (lightbox closed). I grepped tools/smoke-*.json for Tab-order, tabIndex or focus assumptions on cards.
findings.verifier_notes: Reproduces exactly as stated (7 per card, 1,008 at 144 cards). The recommendation is sound and needs no rule change; the additions above are implementation care points (shared thumb(), paging, deletion), not corrections. Low severity: the app's user is primarily a mouse user, and keyboard access to every card still exists.

sources.surface: Gallery grid keyboard order
sources.observation: Each card has the image (tabIndex 0, role=button) plus six tool buttons, all in the tab order: 7 per card, 469 for 67 cards, about 1,008 for 144. Arrow keys don't move between cards; only the lightbox reads arrows.
sources.why_it_matters: Reaching the 30th image by keyboard takes about 200 Tab presses. Focus reveals the tools (good), but the order makes keyboard browsing impractical.

findings.title: 'Reuse settings' on a refined image opens the Refine dialog instead of filling the panel
surfaces: Card ↻ and lightbox 'Reuse settings' on a refined record
findings.recommendation: Pass rec.refine into syncReuseButton (lightbox.js:119 and reuseButton) and keep it in dataset. When it is not null, the lightbox label becomes 'Reuse pass…' ('⚠ Reuse pass…' on a model mismatch). The title becomes 'Open the Refine dialog on #4 with this pass's size, strength and seed', or the mismatch warning when that applies. The aria-label becomes 'Reuse this pass in the Refine dialog' (plus the warning). The card keeps ↻/⚠. Direct renders keep 'Reuse settings' / 'Load these settings into the panel'. Rewrite the stale sentences at docs/design-notes.md:716-724 ('Reuse does restore a refine pass ... clears the panel's source ... The card's and the lightbox's Refine share its field-filling (fillPanel) ...'). They describe the retired panel mode; refine.js does not call fillPanel.
findings.documented_rule: CLAUDE.md Frontend (Refine dialog bullet): 'reuse on a refined record, which first asks GET /api/images/{id} for its source' opens the dialog; 'A source gone at Reuse fills the panel instead, its size unchanged, with a note.' design-notes 'The refine pass' (~line 527): 'Reuse on a refined record asks GET /api/images/{id} for its source ... and opens the dialog on it.' syncReuseButton's mismatch warning ('Warn before the click') must remain.
findings.rule_tension: None: only the wording changes. syncReuseButton (gallery.js:162-178) needs the record's refine. Store it as button.dataset.reusePass so syncReuseButtons() can still re-sync after status. Keep the 'reuse-settings' class and the 'model-mismatch' variant.
findings.smokes_affected: None break. smoke-flux.json:40 checks lbReuse '⚠ Reuse settings' on a direct render (unchanged). smoke.json:115 checks '.card .reuse-settings.model-mismatch' (class kept). smoke-refine.json:118-123 calls reuse() directly; add an expect there for the new label on a refined record.
findings.how_checked: On port 7909 I opened pass 5 (a refine of 4) in the lightbox and read lbReuse's text, title and aria-label. I clicked it, then checked the lightbox and dialog state, the dialog title, size and strength, and that the panel's prompt and width were unchanged. I read the card ↻ attributes on the same pass. For the source-gone branch I relied on the code (gallery.js:409-419) and on smoke-refine.json:134-138, which asserts it. I read docs/design-notes.md 699-724 against web/refine.js.
findings.verifier_notes: Reproduced as stated. The label and tooltip promise the panel; the press opens a modal on a different image id. The source-gone fallback still fills the panel with an explanatory note, so 'Reuse pass…' remains truthful enough there. The design-notes contradiction is real: lines 716-724 contradict the later 'The refine pass' section (~527).

sources.surface: Card ↻ and lightbox 'Reuse settings' on a refined record
sources.observation: On pass 15 (refine of 14) the lightbox button reads 'Reuse settings' with the title 'Load these settings into the panel'. Pressing it closed the lightbox and opened 'Refine image 14' at 2528 wide, leaving the panel untouched (panel prompt unchanged). When the source has been deleted, the same button fills the panel instead and posts a note ('Image 3, the source this was refined from, is no longer in the gallery...'). The label and tooltip never change between these two behaviours. The design notes' 'Per-control defaults and Reuse' paragraph still describes the old panel mode ('Reuse does restore a refine pass ... clears the panel's source').
sources.why_it_matters: A button that does something other than its label says is a small surprise, but it lands in the compare-and-keep flow and teaches the user that the labels are unreliable.

findings.title: Reuse of a refined image opens a dialog titled for its source, and the reused pass is named only inside the closed fold
surfaces: Refine dialog opened by Reuse on a refined record
findings.recommendation:
In openRefine, when `pass` is given: - Set the title to `Refine image ${rec.id} as image ${pass.id} was made`, or the reviewer's `... again`; the ⤢ title stays unchanged. - Fill a new

inside .rf-source-text (hidden otherwise) with `Reusing image ${pass.id}: ${pass.width}×${pass.height} at strength ${pass.strength}, seed ${pass.seed}`. Add its id to the dialog's aria-describedby so a screen reader hears it. Related defect, same fix area: the card's ↻ title says 'Load these settings into the panel' (gallery.js:173), but on a refined record it opens the Refine dialog. Have reuseButton pass rec.refine != null into syncReuseButton and set the title to 'Open the Refine dialog with this pass's settings' for those records.
findings.documented_rule: CLAUDE.md, Frontend and CLI: 'reuse on a refined record, which first asks GET /api/images/{id} for its source - fills the dialog from the record'. design-notes 'The refine pass': 'Reuse on a refined record ... opens the dialog on it [its source]'. Opening on the source is deliberate and correct: the pass re-runs from the source's pixels.
findings.rule_tension: None. The dialog keeps opening on the source; only the copy changes. smoke-refine step 17 checks the title is exactly 'Refine image <id>' on a ⤢ open, so change the title only when `pass` is given. Step 20 checks the source line starts with '896×1152 · seed 5', so put the new text in a separate element, not in #refine-source-line.
findings.smokes_affected: smoke-refine.json step 17 (title on a ⤢ open; unaffected if the title changes only for `pass`) and step 20 (source-line prefix; unaffected if the new line is its own element). Reuse steps 109-110 and 116-117 and smoke-refine-unavailable steps 15-18 do not read the title.
findings.how_checked: Made a 7:9 1 MP source (image 3, seed 5) and a refine pass of it (image 4, strength 0.2, seed 9) on the 7911 fake. Clicked the pass card's own ↻ button (aria-label 'Reuse settings') and logged the title, the source line, the fold summary, the size, the strength and the seed, with an element screenshot. Repeated through the lightbox's 'Reuse settings' button.
findings.verifier_notes: Reproduced as described. The fold's summary note is visible while the fold is closed, but it describes only prompt and sampling, not the size, strength and seed that came from the pass. The misleading ↻ tooltip on refined cards is an extra fact from this check; it belongs with this fix.

sources.surface: Refine dialog opened by Reuse on a refined record
sources.observation: Reuse on image 15 (a refine of image 4 at 0.1) opens 'Refine image 4' with image 4's source line ('896×1152 · seed 5'). The only mention of 15 is the closed fold's summary note, 'as image 15 was made'. Size and strength are 15's, but nothing visible says the dialog holds a previous pass's settings.
sources.why_it_matters: The user clicked Reuse on one image and gets a dialog about another, which reads as a wrong target until they spot the fold note.

findings.title: A refused Refine press repeats the preview's sentence in red instead of focusing the field at fault
surfaces: Refine dialog: #refine-preview and #refine-error
findings.recommendation:
In runRefine's aria-disabled branch:
- If the reason is the preview's own line (refineProblem === els.refinePreview.textContent), clear the preview's text and remove its warn class, then call refineFailed(title). One line remains, red, with role=alert. The heights cancel (17px out, 18px in), so the dialog does not jump. The next refineChanged clears the error and the preview comes back. Also set aria-invalid="true" on Strength and focus it, since it is always visible. Do not open the fold to reach Steps.
- For a size refusal, keep #refine-error as it is. The amber size line sits about 520px above Refine when the fold is open, so the red line next to the button is not redundant there, and smoke step 59 expects it. Also set aria-invalid on W and focus it.
- For no capability, a busy critic or expansion, or an empty prompt: unchanged.
- Clear aria-invalid in refineChanged.
findings.documented_rule: CLAUDE.md, Frontend and CLI (Refine dialog): 'its refusal, a size past the guard or no capability makes Refine aria-disabled with the reason as its title, and a press says it in the dialog.' design-notes 'The refine pass' says the same. aria-disabled (not disabled) keeps the button focusable.
findings.rule_tension: The reviewer's fix (skip refineFailed when the reason is already shown) would leave a press with no visible response, against 'a press says it in the dialog', and the user may think the click did nothing. Their focus target for step refusals, Steps after opening #refine-more, adds the 136px fold jump of M91. The message says 'raise the strength or the steps', and Strength is always visible. Compatible fix: keep one copy and move it, so the press still says it in the dialog, once.
findings.smokes_affected: smoke-refine.json step 59 (size refusal shows #refine-error with 'past the 4448-pixel side'): unaffected if the size case keeps the error. Step 84 (preview warn text before the press): unaffected, since nothing changes until a press. smoke-refine-unavailable.json step 18 (#refine-error includes 'no refine pass'): unaffected. No smoke presses Refine during a preview refusal and then reads the preview.
findings.how_checked: On the FLUX fake: opened the fold, typed Steps 4 at strength 0.1, waited for the preview, then pressed the aria-disabled Refine. Logged both texts, the focused element, Steps' aria-invalid and the dialog rect, and took element screenshots. Repeated with a size past the guard (2688x3456). Read smoke-refine-unavailable for the no-capability path.
findings.verifier_notes: The duplicate is real: two identical sentences, 14px apart, in two colours. The reviewer's fix needed changes on two counts: it conflicts with the documented 'a press says it in the dialog', and opening the fold to focus Steps adds a 136px layout jump. Moving the one message instead of copying it keeps the rule and removes the duplicate and the jump.

sources.surface: Refine dialog: #refine-preview and #refine-error
sources.observation: With Steps 4 and strength 0.1, the preview shows in amber 'strength 0.1 of 4 steps is less than one step; raise the strength or the steps'. Pressing the aria-disabled Refine adds the identical sentence below it in red (#refine-error) and grows the dialog 32 px. The control concerned (Steps, in the fold) is not focused or marked.
sources.why_it_matters: The duplicate reads as two problems and adds height without information. A keyboard user still has to find which field to change.

findings.title: Range-syntax mistakes get misleading errors ('-' is only meaningful for mu)
surfaces: Steps/CFG/Mu axis boxes via the preview
findings.recommendation: Accept the spaced ranges instead of only rewording the error. _RANGE already allows `\s*` around '-' and 'x', but parse_axis splits on whitespace first, so those allowances never run. Before the split, do `text = re.sub(r"(?<=\d)\s*-\s*(?=\d)", "-", text)` and `text = re.sub(r"(?<=\d)\s*([x*/])\s*(?=\d)", r"\1", text)`. Then '2 - 5', '6-12 x2', '1-5 x 0.5' and '2 -5' parse as written, and mu '0.8 - 1.2' stops becoming three cells. For '..' and 'to', raise f"{label}: write a range as 6-12 (or 6-12x2)". Drop the proposed static hint line: the placeholders ('6-12x2', '0,0.5,1') and the ? tips already show the syntax, and the panel is already about 1550 px tall.
findings.documented_rule: Design notes 'Grid preview and the per-step estimate': the preview's message is the run's own (one server-side parser). grid.py NONE_TOKENS: '-' is a 'none' alias that only mu accepts. tests/test_grid.py:44-56 hold 'none' on CFG to 'only meaningful for mu', and '6..12' to an error starting 'steps:'.
findings.rule_tension: The fix stays in grid.py, the one parser, so the preview and the run still agree. Joining only digit-dash-digit and digit-x-digit keeps a standalone '-' as mu's none token ('none, -', '- 1.15'). It changes only text between two numbers, which today is either an error or a silent misread.
findings.smokes_affected: None in tools/smoke-*.json. tests/test_grid.py:44-47 ('none' on CFG must still say 'only meaningful for mu') and test_a_bad_axis_says_so ('6..12' must still raise with 'steps:') keep passing; add rows for the spaced forms.
findings.how_checked: I POSTed /api/grid/preview on 7913 with steps/cfg/mu specs: '2 - 5', '6 - 12', '6-12 x2', '6-12 x 2', '6..12', '6-12x', '6 to 12', '2 -5', '1-5 x 0.5', '1.1 - 1.3' and '0.8 - 1.2' on mu, and '6 8 10'. I read backend/grid.py parse_axis and _RANGE.
findings.verifier_notes: Real, and slightly worse than reported. Besides the misleading errors, a spaced range on Mu silently turns into a three-cell axis that includes a 'none' cell. The preview's resolved-axes line shows it, so severity stays low. I changed the recommendation from 'better error' to 'parse what the regex already meant to accept', which fixes both the copy and the mu misread in the one parser.

sources.surface: Steps/CFG/Mu axis boxes via the preview
sources.observation: Typing CFG '2 - 5' (a range with spaces) previews "CFG: '-' is only meaningful for mu", because '-' is one of NONE_TOKENS. Other natural attempts: '6-12 x2' → "steps: 'x2' is not a number"; '6..12' and '6-12x' → 'is not a number'. The syntax is taught only in the hover tips and by the input placeholders (rgb(117,117,117) on #1a1a21).
sources.why_it_matters: The first mistake a new user makes gets an error about mu, a field they did not touch, so the syntax is harder to learn without reading the docs.

findings.title: The comparison sheet labels rows with internal keys ('variant yours') and never shows each row's prompt
surfaces: Sheet row heads for var:variant
findings.recommendation: 1) In sheet.js, add a display map for VARIANT_AXIS values: {original:'Original', reordered:'Reordered', rewrite:'Rewrite', yours:'Your version'}. Unknown labels pass through. Use it at sheet.js:400 and :491 (export). Give the variant axis the label 'Version' in axesFor, so the row head reads 'Original' and the Rows/Columns pickers say 'Version' instead of 'variant'. 2) For non-original rows, append a `<span class="rowhead-diff">` with up to about 80 characters of the added text from promptChanges(originalPrompt, rowPrompt). promptChanges is global, in analysis.js:761. Do not use promptLabels: for a reorder it marks nearly every word position. Clamp it with `display:-webkit-box; -webkit-line-clamp:4; -webkit-box-orient:vertical; overflow:hidden`. The row head already wraps at max-width 170px (.rowhead.text, style.css:752), and rows are 390-518 px tall. 3) Set the row head's title to the full prompt. 4) analysis.js:1022: say 'version' instead of 'variant' in the compare preview.
findings.documented_rule: CLAUDE.md, Frontend and CLI: the sheet's layout contract lives in the client. A varying var:variant axis takes the rows (VARIANT_AXIS, held to grid.VARIANT by tests/test_grid.py). Each cell records variables={'variant': label}, which 'stats --by variant' reads. design-notes.md, 'Prompt labels on the sheet' and 'The contact sheet'.
findings.rule_tension: Change only the display: the stored label, the 'var:variant' key and stats --by variant stay. Leave the ambiguous case alone: when one label maps to several prompts, axesFor already keeps Prompt as an axis, so add the excerpt only when the label maps to one prompt. The export (sheet.js:491) must use the same mapping, because the sheet and its export draw the same labels.
findings.smokes_affected: smoke.json:97, :102 and smoke-analysis.json:135, :316 (rowhead textContent 'variant original,variant reordered,...'); 'variants' in the preview: smoke-analysis.json:127, 131, 154, 157, 294, 312 and smoke-comparison-batch.json:15.
findings.how_checked: On the FLUX fake, ran a four-version comparison (Original, critic Reordered, critic Rewrite, Your version) at both viewports and let it open its sheet. Read each .rowhead's text, title, rect and font size, the cell titles and aria-labels, the Rows/Columns pickers and the compare preview text. Read sheet.js axesFor, valueText, promptLabels and the export.
findings.verifier_notes: The core claim reproduces exactly. Two details in the source are off: each cell's aria-label is 'Open: ' plus the whole 416-character prompt, not 120 characters; and in this run the openings differ for Reordered ('shot on a 35mm...'), Rewrite ('Rewritten: ...') and Your version ('Soft pink...'). Also noticed, but outside this cluster: the comparison's sheet opens below the still-open, roughly 1,000 px prompt-check panel, so at QHD its first row head is at y=2224, about 900 px below the fold.

sources.surface: Sheet row heads for var:variant
sources.observation: The row heads read 'variant original', 'variant reordered', 'variant rewrite' and 'variant yours': 11 px, 90 px wide, with an empty title. In the panel the same things are called 'Original', 'Reordered', 'Rewrite' and 'Your version', and the preview line says '4 variants × 4 seeds'. Nothing on the sheet shows what differs in each row's 400-character prompt. Each image's aria-label is the first 120 characters of its prompt, and for these four versions that opening is identical.
sources.why_it_matters: A sheet gets read, starred and exported later, away from the panel. A row called 'yours' says nothing about which clause was moved.

findings.title: The prompt check's messages appear under Generate, 1,000+ px from what they explain
surfaces: #error (role=alert) in the settings column
findings.recommendation:
Add `

` inside #analysis-critic, directly after .critic-ask (index.html:99-104). That puts it between the Findings and the critic's answer, which these four messages are about. Add analysisMessage(text) to analysis.js: if the panel is shown and #analysis-critic is not hidden, unhide the slot, then write it (skip if the text is the same); otherwise call showError(text, true). Use it at analysis.js:286, 621, 636 and 644. Clear it in checkPrompt, askCritic's start and clearAnalysis. Keep 'Enter a prompt first.' and the 'Wait for...' refusals in #error. Also set the dead Use rewrite and Use reordered buttons' title to the reason ('The prompt changed since the critic answered; Check again'). Today they keep 'Replace the prompt with the rewrite, then check it' while disabled.
findings.documented_rule: state.js:318-329 showError: #error is role=alert, unhidden before it is written, and mirrored into lbError while the lightbox covers it. syncCritic's live-region rule: never rewrite with the same words. CLAUDE.md: a stale check is dimmed with every Use/Apply dead, and the badge says what changed.
findings.rule_tension: Whatever slot is used has to unhide before writing, as #error does, so a live region announces it. It must not rewrite identical text. It needs a fallback to showError when the critic section is hidden (--no-critic, or the panel closed). Putting the slot in .analysis-head, as proposed, would lose the message: at 2048x1040, scrolled to Compare, the head was at y=-953 while #error in the sticky settings column stayed on screen at y=774.
findings.smokes_affected: smoke-analysis.json:115 and :278, and smoke-animagine.json:242 read els.error.textContent for these messages. Point them at els.analysisStatus.
findings.how_checked: On the FLUX fake, asked the critic and edited the prompt 150 ms into the critique. Measured #error's rect, colour and size, the critic answer, the stale badge and the Use buttons' disabled state and titles at both viewports. Then clicked a finding after moving its words, to produce 'Those words are no longer where the check found them'.
findings.verifier_notes: The '1,000+ px' figure is overstated: the slot is about 390 px below and to the left of the answer's Use buttons, in the other column. It is about 1,000 px only from the middle of the answer's text. 'The panel looks broken' is also overstated, because the amber stale badge and Check again already mark the panel as out of date. What is missing is the specific reason, which shows only in grey 12px text in the other column. Stays low.

sources.surface: #error (role=alert) in the settings column
sources.observation: Editing the prompt while the critic ran produced a 4-line muted note at (35,985), 296x72 px, under Generate: 'The prompt, the negative prompt or the references changed while the critic ran: its answer is about the earlier text, so nothing from it can be applied. Check again for the current one.' The critic answer it describes was at x≥379, y=446-895. The other panel messages use the same slot: 'Those words are no longer where the check found them; Check again.' and 'The prompt check was replaced before the critic was asked...'. It is styled as .error.note in var(--muted).
sources.why_it_matters: These notes explain why a Use button is dead or why nothing was selected. Shown grey and in the other column, they are missed, and the panel looks broken instead.

findings.title: The critic's wait shows no elapsed time, and the first-use download shows no progress
surfaces: #critic-ask / #critic-line in flight
findings.recommendation: In index.html's .critic-ask (99-104), add `` after #critic-line. In askCritic (analysis.js:590), right after `critiquing = true`, record start = performance.now() and start a 1 s setInterval that writes `· ${Math.round((performance.now()-start)/1000)} s` and unhides the span. Clear the interval and hide the span in the finally. On first use, extend the downloading sentence to 'Downloading ... once - this can take a few minutes - then thinking…' (docs/verified.md measured 114.2 s for the first prepare() on Windows). No real download progress: prepare() exposes none, and adding it would be a backend change.
findings.documented_rule: syncCritic (analysis.js:561-588): '#critic-line is a live region: rewriting it with the same words would be read out again'. CLAUDE.md: the line promises the measured time and the GPU for the pinned pair only. The critic holds Generate, Run grid, Expand and Unload while it runs (design-notes, 'The prompt analyser').
findings.rule_tension: Keep the clock out of #critic-line. Make it an aria-hidden sibling so the live region is not re-announced every second and the smokes' exact-text checks on criticLine stay valid. An elapsed clock is a measurement, not a promise, so it can show for a configured override too. The hold on Generate, Expand and Unload stays.
findings.smokes_affected: smoke-analysis.json:83 (exact 'Downloading Qwen3-4B Q8_0 (about 4.0 GB) once, then thinking…') if the first-use sentence changes. :53, :55, :68, :77, :79, :81 and :86 read els.criticLine.textContent and stay valid only if the clock is outside #critic-line.
findings.how_checked: On the FLUX fake (first critique after a fresh start, then a later one), logged the button text, #critic-line text and aria-live, and Generate, Run grid and Run comparison aria-disabled, 120 ms into the critique. Grepped style.css for any animation. Read the measured first-use and critique times in docs/verified.md.
findings.verifier_notes: Reproduces as stated, and the recommendation is sound and respects the live-region rule. The only change is the first-use wording, now tied to the 114 s measured on this machine; the time depends on bandwidth.

sources.surface: #critic-ask / #critic-line in flight
sources.observation: While the critic runs, the button reads 'Thinking…' and the line holds one fixed sentence. On first use: 'Downloading llama.cpp b11206 and fake critic (about 4.5 GB) once, then thinking…'. After that: 'Thinking… about 15 seconds on the GPU.'. There is no elapsed time and no download progress. Generate, Run grid and Run comparison stay held (aria-disabled) the whole time.
sources.why_it_matters: A 4.5 GB first download can take many minutes, and with nothing moving the panel looks hung. The user can't tell 'slow' from 'stuck' while every generation button is blocked.

findings.title: 'Checking' and 'Danbooru unreachable' look identical, and the checking title says 'Lookup unavailable'
surfaces: Tag validation tray, pending vs unavailable states
findings.recommendation: (1) Give renderTagValidation an explicit state, 'pending' | 'checked' | 'offline', in place of overloading 'available'. Store it as els.tagValidation.dataset.state. For the pending render (tags.js:503), set the tray title to 'Checking Danbooru…', not the outage sentence at tags.js:464. (2) Offline: keep model tags green, as the backend already returns them, and use '–' as the mark for unchecked chips (tags.js:387), keeping '…' for pending only. Add '.tag-validation[data-state="offline"]::before { content: "Prompt tags · Danbooru unreachable, not checked"; color: #e0b050 }', amber, never red. (3) Respect the cap in validatePromptTags: send tags.slice(0, 64), and render the rest as { valid: null, reason: 'past the 64-item lookup cap' }. Add the label suffix '· first 64 of N checked', mirroring the analyser's categories_detail wording, so a 65-item prompt no longer greys out all 65 chips with a pydantic error.
