findings.documented_rule: CLAUDE.md: 'remote failure means unchecked, never invalid' and 'lookup failure stays advisory and never blocks'. design-notes.md: 'An unavailable API makes ordinary tags grey and unchecked, not invalid'. CLAUDE.md, Prompt analyser: tag lookups are 'capped at the chips' 64 items', and the analyser states what that cost in categories_detail.
findings.rule_tension: The offline state must not use red, so amber or neutral text is compatible. The 64-item cap is the documented limit of the chips. The fix is to respect it on the client, as the analyser already does ('the tag index was asked about the first 64 of 70 tags only'), not to raise it.
findings.smokes_affected: None found. No smoke reads #tag-validation's title, its ::before content, the '…' mark or the .unchecked class (grep of tools/smoke*.json). The 70-tag steps in smoke-animagine.json (lines 125-128) assert only analysis fields, not chip state, so validating the first 64 does not change them.
findings.how_checked: On the Animagine fake I captured the tray right after an input event (inside the 320 ms debounce) and again after validation. To simulate a Danbooru outage I wrapped window.fetch so /api/tags/validate answers exactly as backend unchecked_results does: available false, model tags kept valid, everything else valid:null, detail 'Danbooru did not answer: timed out after 8 s'. I hash-compared the pending and offline PNGs. I also sent 64 and then 65 comma items to see how the chips handle the request schema's 64-item cap.
findings.verifier_notes: The finding stands, with two corrections and one addition. Corrections: pending and offline look identical only for ordinary tags, because model tags turn green offline; and the 'Lookup unavailable' text in the pending state is rarely seen, since the chip's own title wins on hover and the window is short. Addition, which the source finding missed: a prompt longer than 64 comma items leaves every chip, model tags included, in the pending look indefinitely, with only a raw pydantic message in a native title. The other reviewer's 70-chip screenshot shows 68 green chips, which a stock fake cannot produce past the cap, so their 70-tag state was probably mocked. Severity stays low: Danbooru outages are occasional, and more than 64 tags is far past CLIP's 77-token budget on these checkpoints.

sources.surface: Tag validation tray, pending vs unavailable states
sources.observation: During the normal debounce the chips are dashed with '…', and the tray title reads 'Lookup unavailable; unchecked tags are not treated as invalid: Checking Danbooru…'. With the lookup failing ('Danbooru did not answer: timed out after 8 s') the chips are pixel-for-pixel the same, and only the titles differ. The label still reads 'Prompt tags · Danbooru'.
sources.why_it_matters: When the index is down (offline, rate-limited), users wait for ticks that will never come and cannot tell the chips are unchecked. The pending-state copy also claims an outage that isn't happening.

findings.title: A tag checkpoint's empty prompt shows a prose placeholder
surfaces: #prompt placeholder
findings.recommendation: In applyGuide (web/status.js, beside the tagHelper/examples update at lines 55-60): if tagHelper?.vocabulary === 'danbooru' && !tagHelper.hybrid_prompt && examples.length, set els.prompt.placeholder to the first example cut at the last comma at or before 60 characters plus ', …' (for example '1girl, green hair, sweater, looking at viewer, upper body, …'). Otherwise restore the default, stored once from index.html:59's attribute (e.g. in els.prompt.dataset.defaultPlaceholder). Among the catalogue's checkpoints only Animagine (the one guide with style expects 'tags') meets that condition.
findings.documented_rule: design-notes.md, 'The prompting guide': every profile's guide and examples are the authors' own words, never invented. CLAUDE.md: the Examples menu is built on open from the last status.
findings.rule_tension: Compatible. A placeholder taken from the first author example and cut at a comma boundary with an ellipsis uses the authors' words and invents nothing. Hybrid checkpoints (Kohaku, Illustrious, WAI: hybrid_prompt true) document prose as acceptable, so they keep the default placeholder.
findings.smokes_affected: None: no tools/smoke*.json step reads the prompt placeholder.
findings.how_checked: Fresh Animagine fake. I read els.prompt.placeholder and the guide's examples and hints from /api/status. Then I typed the placeholder's own text into the prompt and ran Check to see how the app judges it.
findings.verifier_notes: Reproduces exactly as stated, and the user cost is concrete: the app's own placeholder fails the app's own style check and tag validation on this checkpoint. It is visible only on an empty prompt (first visit, or after Reset), so it stays low.

sources.surface: #prompt placeholder
sources.observation: On Animagine the empty prompt's placeholder is the static 'a fox walking in the snow, overcast light' (index.html:59). The checkpoint's own guide, in the ? tip beside it, says 'Comma-separated Danbooru-style tags, not natural-language prose', and its Examples begin '1girl, green hair, sweater, …'. The placeholder never changes per checkpoint.
sources.why_it_matters: The first thing a new user sees in the box shows the wrong prompt style for this checkpoint.

findings.title: Escape from the Examples menu drops focus to <body>, and its role=menu has no arrow-key navigation
surfaces: Prompt toolbar: Examples menu
findings.recommendation: Make three changes in showExamples (app.js:19-56). (1) Return focus on close: when hiding, if els.examplesMenu contains document.activeElement, call els.examplesBtn.focus() after hiding. The global Escape handler (app.js:264) then lands on the button rather than <body>. (2) Close when focus leaves: add els.examples.addEventListener('focusout', e => { if (!els.examples.contains(e.relatedTarget)) showExamples(false); }). Today the menu stays open over the prompt after Tab moves into it. (3) Honour role=menu: make items tabIndex=-1 (roving). On the menu, handle ArrowDown/ArrowUp (wrapping), Home and End. On the button, ArrowDown opens the menu and focuses the first item. Tab out of an item closes the menu via (2). Apply (1) to showTagHelper (tags.js:695) too, since its role=dialog has the same Escape-to-BODY drop. The alternative from the finding (drop role=menu/menuitem and aria-haspopup='menu', and render a plain list of buttons) is equally valid, but it changes the li's into wrappers and breaks the smokes' children[n].click().
findings.documented_rule: CLAUDE.md 'Frontend and CLI': 'the Examples menu is built on open from the last status, and a pick tells the preview and the panel the way `choose` does'. Design-notes 'The prompting guide' says the same: 'The Examples menu builds on open'. Nothing documents the keyboard model or the menu role.
findings.rule_tension: None. The fix touches only focus and keys. pick() (app.js:40-50) keeps calling promptReplaced, schedulePreview, scheduleTagValidation(0), persistPanel and els.prompt.focus(). Keeping each item an <li role=menuitem> with its own onclick keeps the 7 smokes that call els.examplesMenu.children[n].click() working. Restructuring to buttons inside the li's would break them.
findings.smokes_affected: None with the roving-focus fix. smoke-anima.json:10-12, smoke-animagine.json:88-90, smoke-illustrious.json:33-35, smoke-kohaku.json:24-26, smoke-netayume.json:10-12, smoke-newbie.json:10-12 and smoke-flux.json:20 click els.examplesBtn and els.examplesMenu.children[n] directly. They keep passing as long as each child stays the clickable <li>, and would break if the items became <button>s inside <li>s.
findings.how_checked: FLUX fake on 7921 (m107.json) and an Animagine fake on 8921 for the Tags helper (m107b.json), at 2560x1305. I used real key events with key codes (Enter 13, Tab 9, ArrowDown 40, Escape 27, Shift+Tab) from a focused Examples button, logging activeElement, :focus-visible, the menu's hidden state and aria-expanded after each key. I also measured the open menu's rect against the prompt textarea after focus left the menu.
findings.verifier_notes: The core claim reproduces: Escape drops focus to BODY, and role=menu has no arrow keys. The stated consequence is overstated for the target browser, because Edge resumes Tab from the menu's position. The menu staying open over the prompt after keyboard focus leaves it is a stronger, related defect. A mouse click on the prompt does close it (app.js:151), so the overlap only hits keyboard users. Severity stays low.

sources.surface: Prompt toolbar: Examples menu
sources.observation: Enter on Examples opens the menu and focus stays on the button. ArrowDown does nothing (still on the button). Tab enters the first item. Escape there closes the menu and focus lands on BODY (c.out: 'after Escape: open=false BODY'). The list is role=menu with role=menuitem items, which tells assistive technology to expect arrow-key navigation, but items are only reachable with Tab.
sources.why_it_matters: A keyboard user who browses examples and backs out loses their place and must Tab from the top of the page (the first stop is Unload). The menu role promises arrow keys it does not support.

findings.title: During an outage every action says only 'Failed to fetch', and the message outlives the outage
surfaces: Panel #error for Generate, Check, Ask the critic and Load more while the server is unreachable; lightbox images
findings.recommendation: Implement with G1.3 as one 'server unreachable' state. In api() (state.js:293), catch the fetch rejection and throw `Object.assign(new Error('No answer from the Local Diffusion server — is it still running?'), { offline: true })`. Have showError remember whether the shown message was an offline one (callers pass err.offline, or showError(err) accepts an Error). Clear it on the first successful status poll. In renderLightbox (lightbox.js:95), set `els.lbImg.onerror = () => { els.lbError.hidden = false; els.lbError.textContent = 'This image could not be loaded — the server is not answering.'; }` and clear it in onload. Do not re-arm the Load more observer: the button stays the retry.
findings.documented_rule: gallery.js:79-89: after a failed page the Load more button is the retry, and the observer must not re-arm. state.js:303-314: readableDetail formats the server's own 4xx/5xx details.
findings.rule_tension: Compatible. Wrapping fetch's rejection in api() changes only the network-failure path. HTTP errors still go through readableDetail. Load more stays the retry and is not re-armed.
findings.smokes_affected: None. No smoke checks 'Failed to fetch' or a broken lightbox image. smoke-paging.json drives Load more only on a live server.
findings.how_checked: In the long-outage run: pressed Generate during 'reconnecting… (1)', pressed Check after the stream gave up, and opened a gallery card in the lightbox while the server was down. Then watched #error for about 18 s after the restarted server answered. Read state.js:293-301, gallery.js:60-89 and lightbox.js:88-97.
findings.verifier_notes: Reproduced. Load more was not re-tested: this gallery had fewer than a page of images. Severity lowered from medium to low. The outage is occasional, a watched job already shows 'reconnecting…', and once G1.3's offline state exists, most of this finding's cost (generic wording, a stale red message after recovery) is removed by the same flag. Kept separate from G1.3 because the surfaces differ (per-action messages, the lightbox image).

sources.surface: Panel #error for Generate, Check, Ask the critic and Load more while the server is unreachable; lightbox images
sources.observation: With the server dead, Generate (pressed while the stream was reconnecting) showed 'Failed to fetch' at (35,1061), 101 px under Generate, beneath a still-moving 'reconnecting… (1)' bar. 'Check again' produced the same text with no visible change. 'Ask the critic' replaced 'Lost the generation stream…' with 'Failed to fetch'. Scrolling to Load more did the same, and 48 cards stayed. Opening a gallery card showed a broken image (naturalWidth 0) with only its alt text at the top-left and an empty #lb-error (f3-10-lightbox-down.png). After the server came back (the topbar changed at T+52), the red 'Failed to fetch' stayed until the next Generate at T+62. It persists indefinitely if nothing is pressed.
sources.why_it_matters: 'Failed to fetch' is the browser's wording. It doesn't say the app's server is gone or what to do. Each action's message replaces the last, so the user can't tell which action failed or whether the problem is the prompt, the gallery or the server. A stale red error after recovery suggests something is still broken.

findings.title: After a lost stream, the blurred live preview of an unfinished cell stays in the viewer beside the real result
surfaces: #viewer after the SSE stream gives up
findings.recommendation: Call dropPreview() in source.onerror's give-up branch, just before setBusy(false) (generation.js:496-497). Keep it during the five reconnect attempts, where the stream may still resume. The 'lost' styling alternative is unnecessary.
findings.documented_rule: design-notes 'The live preview'. generation.js:387-388: the preview is one at the end of the strip and never a record. Results replace the viewer only when the job's first image lands.
findings.rule_tension: None. Dropping the preview when the stream is abandoned matches what the 'done' branch already does (generation.js:448). The preview is never a record, so nothing is lost.
findings.smokes_affected: smoke-preview.json:8 and :10 (preview present while busy, gone at done) are adjacent and unaffected by an onerror-only change.
findings.how_checked: In both crash runs, measured #viewer's images, their classes and titles, and viewerRecords after the stream gave up and again after the server came back. Read generation.js:387-500.
findings.verifier_notes: Reproduced. The leftover preview stayed through the outage, the restart and every later sample until the run ended. Severity lowered from medium to low. It is clearly blurred and a third of the finished image's size, and it misleads mainly together with G1.4's false 'carries on' copy. It is a one-line fix and could ship with G1.4.

sources.surface: #viewer after the SSE stream gives up
sources.observation: When the stream was lost mid-cell, #viewer held 2 images but viewerRecords held 1 (id 63). The second img is class 'preview', title 'live preview · step 13/28': a blurred 248 px gradient to the right of the 693 px finished image (f4-02-t16.png). It stayed through the outage, the restart and 26 more seconds (f3-12), until the next job's first image cleared the strip. onerror never calls dropPreview(); the done branch does (generation.js:448).
sources.why_it_matters: It looks like a second result, and its cell never finished, so the strip suggests 2 images were made when 1 was. Together with 'the run carries on', it reads as a job still in progress.

findings.title: Delete unstarred on a scope a running job is writing to fails every time at human speed, and after the 409 the page still shows the old count
surfaces: Delete unstarred while a job runs
findings.recommendation: (1) In deleteUnstarred (gallery.js:278), when `busy`, add before 'Type N to continue': 'A job is still running; if it adds an image here before you confirm, nothing is deleted.' (2) In the DELETE catch, when the 409 text matches /selection changed/, call resetGallery() and loadRuns() so the badge and grid show the server's new count. When busy, append ' A running job is still adding images here: press Delete unstarred again, or let it finish first.'
findings.documented_rule: design-notes 'Delete unstarred': '`expected` is compared under the write lock ... a sweep that lands more unstarred images while the dialog is open (the queue keeps running while one triages) is answered 409 with both numbers rather than swept up on a count confirmed for fewer.'
findings.rule_tension: Keep `expected`. Both changes are messaging and refresh only: a busy-aware line in the dialog, and a resetGallery() after the 409 so the page shows the count the server now has.
findings.smokes_affected: None. smoke.json:163-191 drives Delete unstarred with no job running and never meets a 409. Its expects ('Delete N unstarred images', 'keeping K starred', 'is not N', 'Deleted N images', 'free text') are untouched by a busy-only line.
findings.how_checked: At --step 0.3 I ran 6 runs at 10 steps (an image every 3 s) and set the search to run:<id> after the first image landed. I stubbed window.prompt to wait 4.5 s (blocking, like the native modal) and then type the shown count, and clicked Delete unstarred. I logged the error, badge, cards and the server's unstarred count. Then I retried immediately with no delay.
findings.verifier_notes: 'Fails every time at human speed' does not hold: it is the fake's 3 s cadence. A quick retry succeeded, and on the card images land every 10-43 s. What does reproduce: after the 409 the page still shows the stale count while the message says 'look again', with no refresh and no hint that the running job is the cause. Lowered to low.

sources.surface: Delete unstarred while a job runs
sources.observation: At --step 0.3 (10 steps a cell, 6 runs) the scope was run:5aaf2b0d036f: the gallery showed (1) and 1 card, while the viewer showed 3 images plus a preview. The dialog asked 'Delete 1 unstarred image matching "run:5aaf2b0d036f" (FLUX.1-Krea-dev only)…'. Answering 1 after 4.5 s got 'The selection changed: 3 unstarred images match now, not the 1 confirmed. Nothing was deleted; look again.' An immediate retry confirmed 4 and got '6 match now, not the 4 confirmed'. After the 409 the badge still read (1) with 1 card while the server counted 3 (e01). The message stayed put 3 s later.
sources.why_it_matters: The pin works and nothing is wrongly deleted. But the user can't tell why it failed or what to do: 'look again' points at a gallery still showing the stale 1, and every attempt during the run fails the same way.

findings.title: A LoRA weight sweep never names the adapter: not in the grid fold, its preview, the sheet's column heads or its export
surfaces: Grid fold LoRA weight, grid preview, sheet heads
findings.recommendation: 1) In generation.js:340-341, write `  ·  LoRA ${axisText(p.values.lora_scale)} (${els.lora.value.replace(/\.safetensors$/, '')})`. This keeps the asserted substring. 2) In syncConditioning, set els.gridLoraScale.placeholder to `${short}: 0-1x0.25` when an adapter is picked, else 'pick an adapter above'. 3) In renderSheet's head labels, when the axis is 'lora' and every shown record shares one rec.lora, label `LoRA ${short} ${v}`. The export takes the labels from the same heads/sheetLayout, so the PNG carries the name too.
findings.documented_rule: CLAUDE.md: GridRequest's LoRA weight is an axis only beside an adapter, and gridLoraScale is disabled without one. The sheet's layout contract lives in the client and the export draws sheetLayout. The LoRA axis reads lora_scale only (sheet.js:24-27).
findings.rule_tension: The adapter-only gating is unaffected. The original preview wording `LoRA ${name} @ 0, 0.5, 1` drops the substring 'LoRA 0, 0.5, 1' that smoke-conditioning.json:66 asserts, so put the name after the values instead.
findings.smokes_affected: smoke-conditioning.json:66 (preview includes 'LoRA 0, 0.5, 1'): kept by the adjusted wording. smoke-conditioning.json:75 checks only the axis key 'lora', so it is unaffected. No smoke asserts the LoRA head text.
findings.how_checked: Picked demo-style on klein, opened the grid fold and set Steps '4, 8' and LoRA weight '0, 0.5, 1'. Logged the preview, the tip, the placeholder and the box rects, ran the grid, opened its run as a sheet, and logged the heads.
findings.verifier_notes: Reproduced. I adjusted only the preview wording so it keeps the substring the smoke asserts; the substance of the recommendation stands.

sources.surface: Grid fold LoRA weight, grid preview, sheet heads
sources.observation: With demo-style picked, the grid fold's 'LoRA weight' box sits at y 1364, 570 px below the adapter select (y 794). Its tip says only 'Needs an adapter selected above'. The preview read '6 images · 2 steps x 1 CFG x 1 mu x 3 LoRA x 1 seed … steps 4, 8 · CFG 1 · mu none · LoRA 0, 0.5, 1'. The resulting sheet (columns 'LoRA 0', 'LoRA 0.5', 'LoRA 1'; rows 'Steps 4', 'Steps 8') shows the adapter nowhere, and so neither does Export PNG, which draws the same heads. The lightbox does name it ('LoRA demo-style.safetensors @ 0.5'), and Reuse restored demo-style @ 0.5 correctly.
sources.why_it_matters: A weight sweep is usually done for several adapters in turn. Sheets and exported PNGs labelled only 'LoRA 0.5' can't be told apart later, and the preview before the run doesn't confirm which adapter the night will use.

findings.title: The Size help tip opens over the scale buttons and silently swallows clicks on 1.25×, 1.5× and 2×
surfaces: Refine dialog > Size ? badge (#refine-size-tip) over #refine-scales and W
findings.recommendation: style.css:144: add pointer-events: none; to .tip. This was verified in-page to fix both the pinned and the hover case for every ? on the page. Optional: in the dialog, open the Size tip upward, `#refine-dialog .field > span .help .tip { top:auto; bottom:calc(100% + 7px) }`, so it covers the source line (not interactive) instead of the scale buttons. Do not do this for the Strength tip: 161 px upward would cover W/H instead. Polish seen in the same shot: `.tip.wide { white-space: pre-line }` (style.css:158) renders index.html's source line breaks inside the two dialog tips ('…a direct render / takes, to any 2 MP preset…', '…which is what a / direct render…'). Either write #refine-size-tip and #refine-strength-tip on one source line each, or give them a class without pre-line.
findings.documented_rule: style.css:131-158: the ? badge is 'an explicit hover target … a badge you can see and a panel we draw'. .help is tabindex=0 role=note and '.help:hover .tip, .help:focus .tip { display: block }' gives keyboard access. CLAUDE.md, Frontend: keep keyboard access; tips are CSS, not title=.
findings.rule_tension:
`.tip { pointer-events: none }` keeps every documented behavior: hover still shows the tip, keyboard focus still shows it, and a click still pins it until the next click elsewhere. Clicks simply reach the control underneath. The original's second rule, `.help:focus:not(:focus-visible) .tip { display:none }`, is unnecessary and removes click or tap to read (touch focus is never focus-visible). Drop it. Tips hold only text, and
, so nothing inside needs pointer events.
findings.smokes_affected: None. Smokes assert tip textContent only (promptTip, sizeTip, stepsTip, refineStrengthTip in smoke-conditioning, …), never display or hit-testing. Rejoining the two dialog tips' source lines does not change any substring the smokes check.
findings.how_checked: QHD, Animagine fake, fold closed. A real click on the Size badge centre at (1110,526): :focus with no :focus-visible, tip shown at [1098,539,300,130]. With the mouse moved away, elementFromPoint at 1.25×, 1.5×, 2× and W returns the tip. Real clicks on 2× and 1.25× left 1248x1824, and focus stayed on .help. Hover only, landing on the tip: a click on 1.5× was swallowed. Strength badge: its tip [1103,559,300,161] covers Strength, Versions and Seed. Then I injected '.tip { pointer-events: none }' in the page (not the repo) and repeated: the clicks go through (1664x2432, then 1040x1520) and the tip closes as focus moves to the button.
findings.verifier_notes: The finding is real, and the fix is a single CSS line that helps every ? on the page. I lowered severity to low. It takes a click on ? first, the tip visibly sits over the target, and the scale button's highlight and the size line show the result, so the wrong size is recoverable before Refine. I adjusted the recommendation: drop the :focus-visible rule, which would also hide tips on tap and on click-to-read.

sources.surface: Refine dialog > Size ? badge (#refine-size-tip) over #refine-scales and W
sources.observation: Clicking the Size '?' (a natural way to read it) focuses .help, and the .tip.wide (300x130 px at [1098,539]) stays displayed through :focus. document.elementFromPoint at the centres of 1.25×, 1.5× and 2× and on the W box returns the tip; only 1× is reachable. Real clicks on 2× and then 1.25× left the size at 1248×1824, with the tip still open. The tip is part of .help, so clicking it keeps focus there. Hover alone does the same: in my first run the pointer moved from the badge onto the tip, the tip stayed open, and my click on 1.5× hit it. The sweep I meant for 1.5x ran at 1664×2432, 4.0 MP (rows 6-8 in the gallery DB are 1664x2432). The Strength tip likewise covers the Strength box (M71). This is not SDXL-specific, but it was not in the merged list.
sources.why_it_matters: The scale buttons are the dialog's main control. A dropped click leaves a 4 MP pass where 2.3 MP was intended. Per verified.md that is 1.6x the time on SDXL, and on FLUX it spills past the card. The only sign is a yellow size line the user may not reread.

findings.title: A critic failure leaves the critic block as if it was never asked, and leads with the exception class
surfaces: Prompt check's Critic block after a 502 or 503 from /api/prompt/critique
findings.recommendation: Keep showError. Wrap only the /api/prompt/critique call (analysis.js:629-633) in its own try, and on failure set a separate `critiqueFailure = err.message`; do not set it in the outer catch, which also receives pre-check failures such as smoke-analysis's 'check boom'. renderCritic draws one muted row in #critic-result from critiqueFailure, e.g. 'The critic did not answer — llama-server stopped before it was ready. Ask again, or check the server log.' Clear critiqueFailure on the next ask, on clearAnalysis and when a check replaces the text. Move focus to #critic-result for the failure row under the same 'focus still on the button' rule as an answer. Server: in main._prompt_failure (main.py:814-831), drop the 'CriticError: ' and 'CriticUnavailable: ' prefix from the HTTP detail for those two classes, and keep short_error(exc) in the log line.
findings.documented_rule: CLAUDE.md the critique route: CriticUnavailable is 503, CriticError 502. Frontend: Ask the critic is aria-disabled, never disabled; an answer takes focus (#critic-result, tabindex=-1) while focus is still on the button. The task's constraint: a failed critique must not leave a critiqueResult that Use or Apply could act on.
findings.rule_tension: The original recommendation sets critiqueResult = { failed }. That conflicts with every reader of critiqueResult.body (renderCritic, renderCompare, the Use/Apply paths) and with smoke steps that expect critiqueResult === null. Keep the failure in a separate variable, so nothing can be applied from it. Status codes stay as documented.
findings.smokes_affected: smoke-analysis.json:98, 278, 281 (expect critiqueResult === null; storing the failure there would break them); smoke-analysis.json:286 (expects els.error === 'check boom' after a pre-check rejection; the failure row must be scoped to the critique request). pytest tests/test_api_analysis.py:1017-1028 asserts the 'CriticError: …' and 'CriticUnavailable: …' details and must change with the prefix.
findings.how_checked: On 7971 at QHD: typed a prompt, pressed Check, then focused and pressed Ask the critic with the scratch critic flag set to error (CriticError), then prepare-error (502 download), then prepare-unavailable (503). Measured the Ask button, #critic-result, #critic-line, focus, #error and critiqueResult. Read analysis.js:590-660 and main.py:814-831, and grepped the smokes and tests that read critiqueResult and the critique's error detail.
findings.verifier_notes: Reproduced. After the failure, the line under the button reads the same idle timing line, and nothing in the Critic block shows a failure. Adjusted because the original recommendation overloads critiqueResult, which smoke-analysis and the Use/Apply code read as 'answered'. Severity low stands. The error's distance from Ask (Ask's bottom at y=396, the error at y=1003) is M99's placement finding, not this one.

sources.surface: Prompt check's Critic block after a 502 or 503 from /api/prompt/critique
sources.observation: Ask the critic with CriticError injected: 'CriticError: llama-server exited with code 1 before it was ready' appeared in the panel's #error at (35,1003), 754 px from the Ask button at (379,332). M99 already covers this placement. New here: the Critic block itself showed no failed state. #critic-result stayed empty, focus stayed on the button, and the line under it read 'Local fake critic on the GPU, about 15 seconds; waits for image jobs.', the same as before asking (f5-01-critic-error.png). 503s from prepare() do carry a remedy ('install it with: sudo apt install libgomp1'), which is good. '6+' : found.models.length} checkpoints (${found.models.map((m) => m.split('/').pop()).join(', ')})``. findings.documented_rule: design-notes 'Delete unstarred': 'a sweep goes wrong by taking the wrong *scope* ... the dialog shows them, and asks for the number of images to be typed back'. gallery.js:290-293: 'The checkpoint scope is part of what is confirmed ... the dialog says so by the server's own name for it.'
findings.rule_tension: None. The fix names the scope from the server's own `models` list, as the narrow case already does, and keeps the typed count as the gate. matching_preview's distinct('model_id', 6) caps the list at 6, so the copy needs an 'and more' at 6.

findings.verifier_notes: Reproduced as stated. The wider, cross-checkpoint sweep differs from the narrow one by a single count here (199 against 200) and names no checkpoint. Low and rare, as filed.

sources.surface: Delete unstarred prompt()
sources.observation: With All models off: 'Delete 67 unstarred images in the gallery (FLUX.1-Krea-dev only), keeping 5 starred?' With it on: 'Delete 68 unstarred images in the gallery, keeping 6 starred?', although the preview returned models ['black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-Krea-dev', 'krea/Krea-2-Turbo']. set_aside.title: Check's tag-order fix and Use reordered can only change the panel's prompt; a pass's prompt can't be checked or fixed
surfaces: Prompt check (panel) vs Refine dialog; Reuse on a refined image
set_aside.recommendation: Merge into G4.1. That dialog check line lists rule findings carrying a whole-field suggestion, each with an Apply that calls replaceBoxText(els.refinePrompt, f.suggestion); the existing input listener runs refineChanged(). Optional and separate: a ghost tiny 'From panel' button in the fold's Prompt caption, disabled while the two texts are equal. It copies els.prompt into els.refinePrompt, and els.negative unless that box is disabled, through replaceBoxText. This lets the critic's rewrite or a comparison winner reach a pass by an explicit click.
set_aside.documented_rule: CLAUDE.md, Frontend: the prompt check 'describes one text: the prompt and negative prompt as collect() sent them'. collect() sends refine: null and the panel never refines. design-notes 'A dialog, not a mode of the panel': the dialog starts from the record. CLAUDE.md: Use and Apply write through replaceBoxText (so Ctrl+Z restores).
set_aside.rule_tension: Check describing the panel's text after a Reuse is the documented behavior, not a defect. The real gap, that a pass prompt cannot be checked or fixed, is the same missing dialog-side check as G4.1. replaceBoxText(el, text) is element-generic (analysis.js:315), so Apply can target els.refinePrompt with the same undo behavior. An optional 'From panel' button is compatible only as an explicit click, never automatic.
set_aside.smokes_affected: None. A new dialog Apply would want a step in smoke-animagine.json. No existing smoke asserts the dialog's button list.
set_aside.how_checked: Code reading plus the analyze call from G4.1. Read usePromptText (analysis.js:326-339): Use reordered and Apply write els.prompt only, through replaceBoxText. openRefine (refine.js:126-128) fills the dialog from the record's prompt. Listed the dialog's controls: no check, no apply, no 'from panel'. Took the reordered text /api/prompt/analyze returns for the pass prompt and counted it with the real CLIP tokenizer.
set_aside.verifier_notes: This duplicates G4.1: both say the dialog has no prompt check, and the fix is one dialog-side analyze call. The original's 'the order fix matters most here' does not hold on its own example. The documented order puts an added detail tag just before the quality suffix, which is still past the 77-token cut on a 41-tag prompt. The cut warning, not the order Apply, is what helps that user.

sources.surface: Prompt check (panel) vs Refine dialog; Reuse on a refined image
sources.observation: I pressed Reuse on refined image 10. It opens the modal dialog (by design, M89), so the panel's Check is inert behind it. After Escape, Check described the panel's own prompt ('11 words, a tag list · no warnings'), not the pass's. Workaround: I fetched pass 6's prompt and pasted it into the panel. Check then found the 124/75 cut, '"masterpiece" (Quality) comes before "smirk"' with Apply, and 'In that order: … Use reordered'. Use reordered rewrote els.prompt only. Reopening the pass, by Reuse on image 6 or ⤢ on its source image 5, filled the dialog with the record's own prompt (refinePrompt === panel prompt: false). The reordered text reaches a pass only by hand copy into the 3-row box. Compare on the same seeds would also run direct 832x1216 renders, not passes, and the panel Check reported 'No negative prompt runs', which is the panel's empty negative and not the pass's.
sources.why_it_matters: The analyser's order rule matters most on these tag checkpoints. Order is documented for Animagine, and the 77-token cut makes order decide what is read. Today its fixes reach direct renders only. To act on a finding for a pass, the user has to copy text between two boxes, one of them modal, and that is the clunkiness the user named.

visual: Muted secondary text is readable: --muted #8b8b9a measures 5.52:1 on the panel and 5.86:1 on the page, and the deliberate #a2a2b0 for explanatory notes is 7.35:1. Contrast was clearly thought about where it was looked at.

The lightbox uses the wide screen well. The image fills a 2211x1269 stage (fit 124% for a 1024px image), with a fixed 280px side column whose Favourite/Reuse/Refine/Delete stay in place from one image to the next.

Tooltips are drawn by CSS (.help/.tip) rather than relying on title=, and the panel's z-index stacking context was fixed so they paint above the cards. This is the right base to reuse for icon labels.
Greyed-not-hidden controls (True CFG, Reference images, LoRA) keep the panel the same shape across checkpoints, so the user's spatial memory survives a model switch.
There is already a QHD rule (.viewer.many at >=2000px), so wide screens have been considered. The fix is to tune it, not to add the idea.
The Refine dialog's own controls match each other: styled select, 41px inputs, a folded 'Prompt and sampling' section, and a dimmed rather than black backdrop that keeps the page as context.
Card favourites (amber ring plus a dark badge with a star) are easy to spot across a 12-wide grid at 171px.
Encoder bars in the prompt check are a compact, readable way to show the token budget and the cut-off point.
panel: The ? tooltips come from the server's profile for each checkpoint and contain real guidance, not generic definitions. Mu on Turbo: '1.15 is Turbo's trained value; higher spends more steps at high noise'. The prompt tip carries the authors' guide (h-mu-crop.png, h-prompt-crop.png).

Dead controls are greyed with a reason instead of disappearing: True CFG on Turbo says 'Not a separate knob on this checkpoint', and the negative note names the box that switches it on. The panel keeps its shape across checkpoints.

The run hint turns Batch/Runs into plain arithmetic ('3 images over 3 passes, seed +1 each, from a random start'), and the grid preview is the server's own expansion: image count, resolved prompts, ETA, disk size and duplicate warnings before anything is queued.

The size line quotes the guide's own wording and adds the VRAM caveat ('4.2 MP — above the 1.6 MP this checkpoint is recommended for — may run tight on 16GB VRAM'), and portrait/landscape inverses share one segmented box.

Generate stays live while a job runs and becomes 'Generate (queue)', using aria-disabled rather than disabled, so a keyboard user doesn't lose their place. Pause and Cancel say what they do in their titles.

Examples are the authors' own prompts and are built when the menu opens, so the list is never stale. Panel persistence remembers per-control ownership and never restores Resume, so a remembered panel can't silently skip cells.
results: Queueing never blocks: while a job runs Generate becomes 'Generate (queue)', the POST is the only held moment (aria-disabled), and watchNext() attaches to the next job by itself ('next in the queue…').
A reload mid-run reattaches cleanly: 0.6 s after navigation the viewer held the job's finished image plus the live preview, with 'run 2/3' and the ETA restored (g03-reattach.png).
The ETA is the job's own pace (elapsed over the fraction done), and grid cells name themselves ('cell 2/60 · 4 steps, CFG 3.5, mu off'), which says exactly what is running in a sweep.

Cancel is quick and its outcome is calm and specific ('Cancelled — kept 1 image.' in muted note style, not red), and the done summary reports duration and a distinct count ('Finished 8 images in 10s.').
waiting_on separates 'loading weights…' from 'waiting for the job ahead…', so a queued job explains its wait rather than looking stuck.
The 8-column many tier at >=2000 px fits QHD exactly (8 x 256-258 px tiles in a 2161 px viewer), and VIEWER_MAX keeps a long night's DOM bounded.
At 2560x1305 (100%) the sticky panel keeps Generate, the bars, Pause and Cancel on screen while the gallery is scrolled.
The live preview appears from the first step and is visibly provisional (dashed border, 0.85 opacity).
gallery: The lightbox view carries across same-size records: zoom and pan stay put while arrowing down a steps or CFG sweep, which is exactly right for comparing cells. The wheel zooms about the pointer, layout uses real width/height (no transform blur), and 1:1 divides by devicePixelRatio.

Strong lightbox keyboard support: ←/→ walk, F toggles favourite (verified), Delete, + / - / 0 / 1, and Escape. It is a real <dialog> with a focus trap and focus restore, and autofocus on × keeps the first Tab sensible.
The lightbox walks off the end of the loaded page into the next one, and the IntersectionObserver auto-paging loaded all 143 images by scrolling alone, with no clicks.

Delete unstarred's gate is well designed: the typed-back count, the scope stated with the checkpoint ('matching "steps:20" (FLUX.1-Krea-dev only), keeping 1 starred'), sample prompts, and the expected count enforced server-side. The per-card confirm names the seed and the prompt.
The Re-render button states its scope and size ('↻ Re-render 19 at 1024×1024'), and All models shows what it would add ('(+8)').
The model-mismatch Reuse warning (⚠ glyph and aria-label naming both checkpoints) appears before the click.
Starred cards stand out at a glance: an amber ring plus a dark-backed ★ that reads on any image.
The Runs picker opening a run as a sheet in one gesture is a good 'morning after' entry point.
Thumbnails are 384px lazy webp: the 143-card grid scrolled smoothly, and the 384px source would allow larger cards without new server work.
refine-flow: The dialog keeps the panel untouched: the panel's prompt, seed and size stay as they were after a pass (verified: prompt 'a fox in the snow' and seed kept), which fixes the old mode-of-the-panel confusion.

Every change asks the server's own preview, so mistakes are refused in the dialog in the server's words before submit: a mistyped sweep gave "strength: '0.10.05' is not a number" with Refine aria-disabled and the reason in its title.

Clear, honest status lines: '2.3 MP — 1.5× the source', 'seed 31, from the source's', '1 image · strength 0.1 · about 3 of 28 steps run', and scale buttons that disable themselves with the size in the title when a pass would pass the guard (refining a refined image offered only 1× and 1.25×).

A strength sweep runs as one job and opens its sheet with Strength as the column axis by itself, with no extra navigation, and the lightbox carries the zoom across sweep cells because they share dimensions.
Refine autofocuses, Ctrl+Enter runs the pass from anywhere in the dialog, and a pass submitted while a job runs queues ('Refine (queue)', '1 more job queued behind this one').
Another checkpoint's image opens with the 'Prompt and sampling' fold already open and the note 'made on Krea-2-Turbo: steps, CFG and mu are FLUX.1-Krea-dev's', so the substitution is visible.
Reuse on a refined record reopens the pass as it ran (size, strength, seed), and a pass whose source has gone falls back to the panel with a clear explanation.
The live preview and step progress ('19/60', '1s elapsed · ~3s left') work for passes too, counted over the steps that actually run.
refine-dialog: Refine is cleanly separate from the panel. The dialog opens with the source's own prompt, seed and sampling, and the panel stays untouched: its prompt and Seed were unchanged after each pass I ran. This fixes the old 'mode of the panel' confusion that the design notes describe.

The preview is validated by the server and shown before submitting. A strength that leaves no step ('strength 0.1 of 4 steps is less than one step; raise the strength or the steps'), a size past the guard, an empty prompt and a deleted source are all refused in the dialog, and Refine goes aria-disabled with the reason.
'about 3 of 28 steps run' turns an abstract strength into concrete work, and 'about 1s' appears once a pass at that size exists.
The fast path is short. Focus opens on Refine, so ⤢ then Enter (or Ctrl+Enter from any box) runs it. Escape returns focus to the ⤢ that opened it, and the Refine button shows a clear focus ring.
Scale buttons disable themselves past the guard, and the opening size falls back to the largest factor that fits: a 4 MP source opened at 1.25x with 1.5x and 2x greyed.
A sweep works well once typed: '3 images · strength 0.05, 0.1, 0.15 / Opens as a sheet when it is done', and the seed hint adds 'at every strength'.

The fold follows the panel's rules: the negative prompt is greyed with '(needs True CFG > 1)', Mu and True CFG follow the checkpoint, and the fold opens itself to explain substitutions for another checkpoint's image.
The seed hint spells out consecutive seeds per version ('seeds 5-6, from the source's').
It fits the secondary target: at 2048x1040 and 125%, the dialog with the fold open is 833 px tall and needs no scrolling.
grid: The grid preview is the server's own expansion. It shows the count, the resolved values of each axis ('steps 6, 8, 10, 12 · CFG 2, 3.5, 5'), the first resolved prompts, a time estimate from this checkpoint's history and a disk estimate, all debounced at 250 ms, and a bad axis shows the error the run itself would give, in the warn colour.
The running-grid readout is clear: 'cell 6/24 · 8 steps, CFG 5, mu off · 2s elapsed · ~7s left' under two bars (run and step), with Run grid relabelled 'Run grid (queue)'.
Run grid writes a random base seed back into the Seed box (8526501783048556 here), and the panel persists the grid spec and fold state, so a same-browser Resume works.
Resume's preview says exactly what it will skip ('0 images … 24 already done'), and Run grid refuses with 'every cell is already rendered' instead of queueing nothing.

The sheet picks axes well: steps×CFG became Columns=Steps, Rows=CFG with the seed pinned; a variable run labels by variable name in declared order ('size big | size small | size none', 'ground grass | ground snow'); a 10×6 run at 207 px cells nearly fits QHD.
Opening a cell from the sheet walks the lightbox in sheet reading order ('1/6'), F stars it, and the cell's mark updates in place without a re-render.
Export burns in 14 px white labels and a caption naming the search, the pins, the model, the size, the run and the time. It is more legible than the on-screen sheet.
The Runs picker gives a compact table of contents: date, image count, distinct count, stars and prompt.
The help tips are thorough and example-led ('6-12x2 — start-stop, step after the x, both ends included'; 'none is a value too').
analysis: Every finding names its basis (GUIDE / AUTHORS / ENCODER / HEURISTIC) and links the authors' page, and the critic's issues carry numbered cites (G1 · Guide) and a note saying whose words they are. That traceability is rare and worth keeping.

The stale state is clear and safe: an amber 'PROMPT CHANGED SINCE' badge and 'Check again' in the head, the body dimmed but readable, every Use, Apply and Run comparison dead, and 'references changed since' when only references moved.
Check is instant and cold: it runs on the CPU with no model load, and the heading takes focus on a two-column page (measured: focus on H2 after Check, on #critic-result after the critic answered).
The encoder bars show the cut directly: the red or amber tail is what the pipeline never reads, and the 'stops reading at "..."' link selects exactly that tail.
The rewrite diff is exact (ins/del text nodes, character counts) and survives escape-only and Unicode edits.

The comparison preview gives the cost before anything runs ('16 images · 4 variants × 4 seeds · batch 1 · about 2s'), the seeds are paired across versions, and the sheet puts versions in rows in the order given.

The server says what it set aside and why ('The critic's reordered version was left out: in it, "best quality" (Quality) comes before "green hair"...'), so a missing suggestion is explained rather than silently absent.
Use and Apply write through replaceBoxText, so the browser's undo history survives a replacement.
tags: The chips edit the prompt itself. Drop, ×, the inline editor and the helper all serialize through writePromptTags, so the textarea, chips, preview and saved panel never disagreed in any flow I ran.

In-place edit is well built. Double-click or Enter opens the chip's text selected, and suggestions wait for the first keystroke, so Enter on an untouched edit keeps the tag. Escape returns focus to the same chip (verified: activeElement back on chip 1).

Right-click insertion is precise. tagInsertionIndexAtPoint picked the correct boundary in a gap (index 5) and the start on the label (index 0). The inline editor has its own autocomplete with category and post counts.
Readable chips at QHD. 12px light text on charcoal, 26px tall, average 103px wide. 70 tags wrap into 4 rows (144px) with no nested scrollbar, and the two red unknowns stand out at a glance.
Unknown is advisory and never blocks, as the guide intends. The red '?' with neutral text stays legible, not colour-on-colour.

The Tags helper is guide data, not a hard-coded tag cloud. Active tags show teal and toggle off, exclusive groups replace in place, and 'Finish with masterpiece, high score, great score, absurdres' moves the suffix to the end.

Size guidance is accurate and specific. Aspect presets go green only when aspect and tier both match the card (16:9 and 3:4 stay neutral), titles say 'a recommended aspect and size for this checkpoint', and the line warns '4.2 MP — above the 1.1 MP this checkpoint is recommended for'.
Autocomplete rows show category and humanized post counts (e.g. 'GENERAL green hair 590k'), the information you need to pick between near-duplicates.
walkthrough: Ctrl+Enter generates from anywhere, including the prompt box, and runs the pass inside the Refine dialog. That made iterating 1 click/keystroke per edit (Task 2).

Feedback during a run is good: live latent preview, 'Generate (queue)' relabelling, '2s elapsed · ~2s left' ETA, the cell label for grid cells, and a 'Finished N images in Xs' summary with a distinct-count warning ('Only 4 distinct').

The Refine dialog is a clear improvement over a panel mode. From the lightbox it is 3 clicks to a 2x pass. It opens on the image's own prompt and seed with the checkpoint's strength (0.1 on FLUX), and its preview line ('1 image · strength 0.1 · about 3 of 28 steps run') and VRAM warning ('4.2 MP — 2× the source — may run tight on 16GB VRAM') say exactly what will happen.
The lightbox's keyboard model (←/→, F, 1, 0, Escape), its controls pinned to the bottom of a side column, and arrows that walk a sheet in reading order made star-and-step reviews fast.

The grid preview ('12 images · 3 steps x 1 CFG x 1 mu x 4 seeds · about 23s · ~129.3 KB' plus the resolved axes) catches a mistyped axis before anything runs. In my run it showed '1 steps' when my Steps click had missed.
Use rewrite/Apply write through replaceBoxText: Ctrl+Z after Use rewrite restored the original prompt exactly. This is the model the Reuse path should follow.
A comparison's sheet has the right shape: one row per version, seeds across, opened on its own job with Favorites unticked.
Search plus the card's ⊞ and the Runs picker make any run reopenable as a sheet without retyping anything; key:value search found the right images in one step.
copy-a11y: The muted colour is chosen for contrast, not opacity: #8b8b9a measures 5.52:1 on the panel and 5.16:1 on inputs, and the field notes' #a2a2b0 is 7.35:1. The CSS comment explains why opacity was dropped (style.css:98-101).

Submit buttons use aria-disabled, so they keep focus. A refused Refine says why: its title and the dialog's error carry the server's reason ('strength 0.1 of 4 steps is less than one step; raise the strength or the steps').

Focus return works where it matters. Escape from a Refine dialog opened by a card's ⤢ returns to that ⤢. Refine opened from the lightbox returns to the image that opened the lightbox. Check moves focus to the panel heading on a two-column page, and the critic's answer takes focus.

Images in the viewer, gallery and sheet are focusable role=button elements named 'Open: <prompt>', with a 2px inset accent-2 ring (10.4:1). Card tools have aria-label equal to their title (gallery.js:146-149).

Error and status copy is specific and actionable: 'Enter a prompt first.', 'Cancelled before anything finished.', 'Time budget reached after N/M cells — kept K images. Resume finishes the rest.', the queue line '1 more job queued behind this one.' with its own Cancel queued.
Live regions are deliberate: #error is role=alert and unhidden before writing; progress text is role=status; the critic line and the zoom readout are aria-live.
The Refine dialog's own lines state the cost before you run: '2.4 MP — 1.5× the source', 'seed 31, from the source's', '1 image · strength 0.1 · about 3 of 28 steps run'.
Prompt-check findings cite their source with a Guide badge whose tooltip holds the cited sentence, and say what the app checks itself (Heuristic) versus what the authors wrote.

coverage.critic:
Coverage of the happy paths at QHD is good: 11 areas reached the panel, results, gallery, lightbox, Refine (twice, on FLUX), grid and sheet, the prompt check and critic, the tag chips (Animagine), copy/a11y and a walkthrough. Most also ran at 2048x1040 @1.25. The 108 merged findings are well grounded. Four kinds of state stand out as never reached, and every area lists some of them as not covered:

1. **Failure and recovery.** No load failure, no failing cell or job, no server stopped mid-session, no critic error. The fake can't fail on its own; the scratch wrapper pattern in find-results/slowload_server.py can make it.
2. **Destructive actions.** Every delete was stubbed to capture its confirm text. Nothing was actually deleted, so no one has seen what the page leaves behind.
3. **klein's references and LoRA.** The only conditioning workflow in the catalogue. No one used it beyond the ⤢ refusal.
4. **Refine on an SDXL tag checkpoint.** The user named Refine, but both Refine reviews ran only on FLUX.1 Krea [dev]. Animagine, Kohaku, Illustrious and WAI all take a pass at 0.4, and with a tag prompt the dialog's 3-row plain textarea (index.html, refine-prompt) has none of the panel's chips, autocomplete or Check.

Lower-value gaps I am not briefing:
- ERNIE's Expand and translation field: the fake's expander returns 'Expanded: <prompt> (WxH)' instantly (tests/fakes.py:71), so a wrapper would be needed to judge it.
- Other guides: NewBie's XML in the 296 px prompt box, Z-Anime, Anima's artist note.
- The under-901 px layout, which is not the target.
- Real screen readers, and two tabs on one server.
- Whether the layout proposals compose when applied together (M3, M14, M16, M24, M35, M43). None was tested together with the others.

gaps.brief:
No reviewer has seen a single failure state. Drive them on the default checkpoint, at 2560x1305 and then 2048x1040 @1.25. Use the port-safe driver scratchpad/ux/find-analysis/drive.mjs.

SETUP. Copy the pattern of scratchpad/ux/find-results/slowload_server.py into your own scratch directory: environment set first, scratch paths asserted, no bytecode. Patch in memory:
(a) FakeBackend.load raises while a flag file <dir>/fail-load exists. Use huggingface_hub's gated-repo text: "403 Client Error. Cannot access gated repo for url https://huggingface.co/black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-Krea-dev/resolve/main/model_index.json. Access to model black-forest-labs/FLUX.1-Krea-dev is restricted. You must have access to it and be authenticated to access it. Please log in." FLUX.1 Krea [dev] is click-through gated (CLAUDE.md), so this is a new user's first Generate.
(b) Wrap FakeBackend.__init__ to set self.fail_on from env FAIL_ON. The numbers are 1-based generate() calls over the server's life (tests/fakes.py:118).
(c) Patch the FakeCritic instance's fail / prepare_fail from env (tests/fakes.py:220-277).

FLOWS.
1. Fresh page with the flag present.
   - Press Generate, then watch the topbar and the panel.
   - status.js:213-219: the 'load failed' text, the Load button, and showError(s.detail) re-run on every 3 s poll. Does the detail clobber other messages, and does it reappear after you dismiss or replace it?
   - Remove the flag, then press Load and Generate. Is the retry obvious?
2. Grid of 12 cells with FAIL_ON set so one cell fails. Then a second grid with three consecutive failures, which stops the job (jobs.py:418-419).
   - Capture the red #error line, the cell line and the last-run banner on the next reload.
   - Does the page say which cells failed and how to retry them? Can Resume pick them up?
3. Server killed mid-run, with --step 0.3 and a Runs 4 job going.
   - Start a background shell command that sleeps about 6 s and then stops the process listening on your port: PowerShell `Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort <port> -State Listen | % { Stop-Process -Id $_.OwningProcess }`.
   - Have the steps file shoot every 4 s for 30 s.
   - Expect status.js:230 to swallow poll failures, so the topbar may stay green with the model name. Expect the progress text to show 'reconnecting… (n)', then generation.js:498, 'Lost the generation stream. The run carries on — reload to pick it up', which is false when the server died.
   - While it is down: press Generate ('Failed to fetch'?), Check, Ask the critic, open the lightbox, and scroll for Load more.
4. Restart the same command (same --data, no --fresh) without reloading the page.
   - Does the page notice? Does Generate work?
   - A reattached stream for the old job id gets a 404 (main.py:1262), so EventSource closes at once. What does the panel say?
   - Do the dead job's finished images show up?
5. Critic errors: CriticError (502), CriticUnavailable (503), and a run with --no-critic. Where does the message land relative to the check panel?

FOR EACH STATE, RECORD:
- whether the message says what happened and what to do
- where it appears (panel #error vs the viewer or topbar), in px from the action that caused it
- whether it persists, or is overwritten or stale
- whether the topbar tells the truth
- whether the recovery is one obvious click

Respect the deliberate rules: aria-disabled, the budget stop returning through the cancel path, and the 'three in a row' rule. Stop every server you start, including restarted ones.
gaps.why: Every area's not_covered list names error, load-failure or lost-stream states, and none were reached. The default checkpoint is gated, so a 403 on first load is the likeliest first experience for a new user. Reading the code also suggests two misleading states: a topbar that stays 'ready' when the server is gone, and 'The run carries on' after a server death. That makes this the highest-severity unreviewed area.

gaps.brief:
Nobody actually deleted anything. Every confirm was stubbed and cancelled, so no one has seen forgetImages (gallery.js:244-268) and resetGallery acting on a real page.

SETUP.
- Build a FLUX.1 Krea [dev] gallery of about 80 images with --step 0. Include a single image, a batch of 4, a 3x3 steps x CFG grid, a refine pass and its source, and 4 starred images.
- Then restart the same --data with --step 0.3 (no --fresh) for the run-concurrency cases.
- Use scratchpad/ux/find-analysis/drive.mjs at 2560x1305.
- Neither driver handles JS dialogs, so first eval: window.__msgs=[]; window.confirm=(m)=>{__msgs.push(m);return true}; window.prompt=(m)=>{__msgs.push(m);return window.__typed ?? ''}. Log __msgs after each delete.

WALK.
(a) Card ⌦, by real click on the hover tool, on the image currently shown alone in the viewer. Then on one tile of a 4-image batch in the viewer.
- Shoot the viewer afterwards. Does it go blank with no placeholder? Do the multi/many classes fit?
- Check the gallery reflow, the count badge, and where keyboard focus lands.
(b) Lightbox from card 20.
- Press Delete three times. Which image follows, does the counter change, and does the zoom survive?
- Delete the last image of lbList.
- Delete from a lightbox opened on a sheet cell, and shoot the sheet afterwards. Is there a hole? Does an axis value vanish? Does the scroll jump?
(c) Delete a refine pass's source, then open the pass in the lightbox ('refine of N' now names a deleted id). Try Refine and Reuse on it.
(d) Delete unstarred, in four cases:
- Empty search over the whole gallery. Measure the prompt() text.
- A run:<id> scope from the Runs picker.
- A mistyped count.
- A running --step 0.3 job that lands an image between the count GET and the DELETE (set __typed to the old count). This should give a 409 on the 'expected' guard.
Shoot after each case. Note:
- where the outcome message lands (panel #error vs the button at the gallery head's right)
- the scroll position after resetGallery
- whether the sheet, Favorites or All models views change what is offered
(e) Check that Delete pressed on a focused gallery card or in the sheet does nothing destructive. The lightbox binds Delete at app.js:276.

LOOK FOR:
- any leftover pointing at a deleted id: a viewer tile, the refine dialog source, a sheet cell, the last-run banner's Show run, the Runs picker
- a count badge that disagrees with the grid
- lost gallery position
- whether the irreversibility is stated before the click, given that files are removed from disk and there is no trash or undo
- how close ⌦ is to ☆ and F, in both px and keystrokes

Keep the deliberate design: typing the count back, and the expected pin under the write lock.
gaps.why: Deletion is the one place this app can destroy work: files are removed from disk with no undo. All four reviewers who touched it (gallery, visual, walkthrough, copy-a11y) only captured confirm text. The aftermath (viewer, sheet, lightbox strip, lineage, counts, scroll) and Delete unstarred racing a running job are unobserved, and those are where lost-work and wrong-scope errors would show.

gaps.brief:
Walk the conditioning workflow on a klein fake. It lists demo-style.safetensors and hides other-family.safetensors with a reason (tools/fake_server.py:62-76, tools/smoke-conditioning.json). Use the port-safe driver at 2560x1305, then 2048x1040 @1.25.

FLOWS.
1. Make 8 images, then add references only by real clicks on the gallery card's ❐ hover tool (gallery.js:108-122). This is the only way to add one: the lightbox and the viewer have none, and there is no upload route.
   - After each add, shoot both the card and the panel's Reference field (sizes.js:198-230). Is there any feedback near the card? How far apart are the ❐ and the chips, in px?
   - Are the chip thumbnails large enough to tell images apart? Note the chip size.
   - The note '(n, each lengthening the sequence)'.
   - A 5th add: the refusal lands in panel #error.
   - Removing a chip with ×.
   - Whether the order can be changed. klein's guide asks what each reference is for.
2. Generate with 2 references.
   - How does the result say which references it used? The lightbox shows 'ref 3+7' as bare ids (lightbox.js:110).
   - Reuse that record: are the chips restored?
   - Reuse a record whose reference was deleted.
   - All models, with its ⚠ mismatch.
3. Prompt check with references.
   - klein's references rule.
   - The stale badge 'references changed since' after adding or removing a chip (analysis.js:207).
   - Check again, and Ask the critic.
4. LoRA.
   - Pick demo-style. Weight becomes enabled; read the tip text from the DOM, including other-family's reason.
   - In the grid fold, a LoRA weight axis '0,0.5,1' against a steps axis. Run it and shoot the sheet: weight as an axis, and the labels.
   - The lightbox settings line showing the adapter and weight.
   - Reuse restoring the adapter.
5. The missing-capability question. A klein user who wants to edit their own photo or sketch has no way in: references and refine sources are gallery ids only (CLAUDE.md 'Reference images are gallery ids, never paths'; no upload route in backend/main.py). Report the UX cost. If you recommend something, keep the rule: for example an upload or drop target that stores the file as a gallery row and so gets an id.

Measure the field sizes and px distances, and quote the copy exactly.
gaps.why: klein is the catalogue's only reference-conditioning checkpoint and its main editing workflow. Four reviewers listed references, chips and a selected LoRA with a weight axis as not covered, and the only klein run checked the ⤢ refusal. Reading the code suggests friction no finding covers: references can be added only from a 23 px gallery hover tool far from the chips; there is no way to bring in an outside image; and lineage is shown as bare ids.

gaps.brief:
The user named Refine as the clunkiest feature, but both Refine reviews ran on FLUX.1 only, at strength 0.1. Run the same dialog on an SDXL tag checkpoint, where the profile's strength is 0.4 (model_defaults.py, the animagine-xl profile). Use the port-safe driver at 2560x1305, then 2048x1040 @1.25.

SETUP.
- Use the panel's chips and autocomplete to make three 832x1216 Animagine images from a 35-45 tag prompt and the recommended negative from the Tags helper.
- The fake tag index knows only a few tags. As the tags reviewer did, stub fetch for /api/tags/validate and /api/tags/suggest in the page if you need a realistic vocabulary.

FLOWS.
1. Open Refine from the card ⤢ and from the lightbox.
   - Open 'Prompt and sampling'. refine-prompt is a 3-row plain textarea and refine-negative is 2 rows (index.html:600-612). Neither has chips, autocomplete, validation or Check (no refine references in tags.js or analysis.js).
   - Measure the visible share of the tag prompt and the negative.
   - Edit a tag there by real typing ('smile' to 'open mouth', and a typo like 'smlie'). Note what feedback you get compared with the panel.
2. Strength and size.
   - Default 0.4, the placeholder, and the tip's sweep examples. On FLUX these contradicted the checkpoint (M29); check whether they fit SDXL.
   - 1.5x (1248x1824) and 2x (1664x2432, about 4 MP) against Animagine's documented pixel range. Does the dialog quote the guide's size word, as the panel's size line does? What warns?
   - Run a sweep '0.3,0.4,0.5' and shoot its sheet.
3. Run a pass.
   - Real SDXL sends no live-preview frames (docs/verified.md:176 and :343: no fitted map for the 4-channel VAE). The fake does send frames, so judge the wait by also blanking them: in an eval, drop previewEl, or override EventSource handling of type 'preview'.
   - Where is progress shown once the dialog closes, and what does the viewer show meanwhile?
4. Reuse the pass and open Check on the pass's prompt. Can its tag-order finding be acted on for the pass, or only for a direct render?

Compare with the FLUX findings already merged (M6, M9, M29, M51, M52, M92, M95). Report only what differs or is new on SDXL. Respect the Refine dialog's contract: the panel never refines, collect() sends refine: null, and Ctrl+Enter in the dialog runs the pass.
gaps.why: Refine is the user's named pain point. It is supported on four SDXL checkpoints (Animagine, Kohaku, Illustrious, WAI), all with tag prompts and 0.4 strength. Every Refine observation so far is FLUX-only, and the refine-flow reviewer listed SDXL strengths and tips as not covered. Editing a tag prompt inside the dialog's plain 3-row box, with none of the panel's tag tools, and waiting on a pass with no preview are new surfaces no one has seen.

directions.name: Same bones, real scale
directions.thesis: The page's structure is right; what's wrong at QHD is that it was sized for about 1400 px and then stretched. At 2560x1305 the 330 px panel is 12.9% of the width. Its text is 10-12 px: field labels 11 px, the Examples/Check/Reset buttons 10 px on 19 px targets, presets 11 px. Control borders measure 1.24:1. The gallery packs 12 columns of 171 px. Refine shows the image you are refining as a 72 px thumbnail in a 460 px dialog. Opening the prompt check pushes the image you just made down to y=634 and the gallery off the screen (head at y=1604). The fix is a token system: type, space, control height, colour and layout widths, with a wide tier from 1800 px wide and a short-window tier, so 2560x1305 and 2048x1040 (125%) each get real scale. Spend the spare width where the user works: a 460 px panel; the prompt check docked beside the viewer instead of above it; the just-made image with its actions beside it; Refine as a two-pane dialog showing the source large with the kept region framed. It is mostly CSS. The DOM additions are two headings, a fold, a viewer side column and a crop frame. Every rule is scoped to min-width 1800 px, so the 1400x900 smokes render exactly as they do today.
principles: Scale through tokens: one type scale (12.5/13.5/15.5/17/19 px at 2560, fluid down to 11.5/12.5/14/15/17 at 1800), a 4 px spacing ladder and four control heights replace about 20 one-off sizes. At 1400 the tokens hold today's values, so nothing moves there.

Two label levels, not three. Field labels are 13.5 px, weight 600, sentence case, #c4c4d0. Group headings and fold summaries are 12.5 px uppercase muted with a divider. The current mix of 12 px uppercase captions and 11 px sentence-case labels goes.
Only the selection and the primary action carry the accent. 'Recommended' becomes a quiet zero-width underline, red hover is reserved for destructive buttons, and control borders reach 3:1.
Dead controls collapse to their label and the reason, never vanish: the caption, the ? badge and the note stay, and only the empty body shrinks.

Spend QHD width beside things, not above them. The prompt check docks to the right of the viewer and the just-made image gets an info and actions column, so nothing pushes the image or the gallery down.
Show the object being worked on at real size. Refine shows its source large with the kept region framed, instead of a 72 px thumbnail.
Whatever the window height, Generate stays above the fold at load. The panel's sticky top is measured, not guessed.
directions.layout:
At 2560x1305 (DPR 1):
- Topbar: 56 px.
- Grid: panel clamp(400px,18vw,480px) = 461 px, then the stage at 2012 px, with 24 px gutters.
- Panel, top to bottom: Prompt (7 lines to start, growing to 16 with field-sizing:content), Negative, Size, then three groups: SAMPLING (Steps/CFG/Mu/True CFG), a CONDITIONING fold (LoRA and references, with a one-line state summary), and OUTPUT (Seed/Batch/Runs/dice). Then Generate (46 px, y=993, with a Ctrl+Enter chip), status, and the GRID SEARCH fold.
- Panel height is 1189 px with the last-run banner showing, inside the 1201 px available. Its sticky top is computed from its measured height, so an open grid fold sticks by its bottom.
- Stage: an idle viewer is one line. With one finished image the viewer is 791 px tall: the image at 58vh (757 px) plus a 340 px column with the prompt, size, seed, steps and CFG, Star, Refine… and Reuse settings.
- Gallery head at y=903. Then 8 columns of 241 px cards (they were 12 of 171), the first row ending at y=1206, above the fold. Cards are letterboxed and their tools are 32 px with word labels on hover/focus.
- With the prompt check open, the stage becomes a two-column grid: chips and viewer in a 1297 px column, the check docked at clamp(520px,27vw,700px) = 691 px and exactly the viewer's height (791 px), scrolling inside itself. The gallery head stays at y=903 (it is at y=1604 today).
- Refine is a modal of 1400x820: an 888 px source pane with the full PNG contained (818x818) and a kept-region frame, plus a 461 px controls column matching the panel's width.
- Lightbox side column: 380 px, prompt at 15.5 px.

At 2048x1040 (DPR 1.25, QHD at 125%):
- Tokens interpolate: body 14.5 px, labels 12.8 px.
- Panel 400 px; stage 1573 px; gallery 7 columns of 214 px, first row 795-1009 inside 1040.
- A max-height:1150px density tier (inputs 34, small controls 30, primary 42, gutter 20, panel gap 12) keeps Generate at y=878 (bottom 922). Without that tier the panel measured 1252 px and Generate sat at y=1057, below the fold.
- The prompt check docks at 553 px, the Refine source pane is about 690 px tall, and the idle page shows 3 gallery rows.

At 1400x900 (every smoke):
- No wide-tier rule applies: the panel stays 330 px and body 14 px.
- The only visible change is from the DOM additions: the two group headings take today's 12 px uppercase caption style, and LoRA and references sit in the closed Conditioning fold.

changes.change: Introduce the tokens above. Base values equal today's literals; the >=1800px tier overrides them. Replace literal font sizes, paddings and heights with var() references.
grid-template-columns: var(--panel-w) minmax(0,1fr), with the gutter from the token. Measured: 330 -> 461 px at 2560, 400 px at 2048, stage 2012 / 1573 px.

One field-label style (.field > span, .sub i): fs-sm, weight 600, --text-2, sentence case. Add two <h3 class="group-head"> elements ('Sampling' above the Steps row, 'Output' above the Seed row) styled like the fold summaries: fs-xs uppercase muted with a top divider.

Wrap #lora-field and #reference-field in a <details class="section">. Its summary carries a state note ('no LoRA · references n/a here' / 'LoRA x × 0.8 · 2 references'), written by sizes.js syncConditioning. It opens whenever a LoRA is selected or references are set. Panel height drops about 90 px on FLUX.

Inputs/selects: height --h-md, --field fill, --line-strong border, ::placeholder muted at opacity 1, and a 3 px accent focus halo. Buttons: .ghost uses min-height --h-md, .small --h-sm, .tiny --h-xs (today 19 px). Generate is 46 px on --accent-strong. Add color-scheme:dark and accent-color, so the LoRA select and the checkboxes stop rendering as white native controls. Add an explicit 2px --accent-2 :focus-visible ring on button, checkbox, summary and .help; color-scheme:dark otherwise turns Chromium's outline:auto ring near-black, as observed on Check in iteration 1. Disabled panel inputs drop to 0.45 opacity with cursor:not-allowed.

All pills neutral. Recommended is box-shadow: inset 0 -2px 0 rgba(74,222,128,.7), which takes no width. An earlier dot marker wrapped the presets to 3 rows at 2048. Active pills are --accent-soft fill with an accent border. Pills are 32 px tall at 13.5 px. The Orientation button loses its min-width.
#negative-field.disabled textarea collapses to one --h-md line (label and note kept). #reference-field.disabled .chips is hidden (caption, badge and note kept).
#prompt starts at calc(min(7lh,12vh)+22px) and grows with field-sizing:content up to 16 lines (Chromium; elsewhere rows=5 plus the min-height).

About 10 lines in app.js: a ResizeObserver sets --panel-top to the gutter while the panel fits, and to innerHeight - height - gutter while it does not. Generate and Run grid stay reachable with the grid fold open; this replaces the dead max-height:900px guess.
::after shortcut chip, content: "Ctrl+Enter" / "" (empty alt, so the accessible name stays 'Generate'), plus aria-keyshortcuts in markup.
.ghost.small hovers neutral. Red hover is kept only on #btn-cancel, #btn-cancel-queued, #btn-delete-unstarred and #lb-delete.

An idle viewer (.viewer:has(> .placeholder:only-child)) is one 50 px line instead of a 380 px box. A single image is capped at 58vh (757 px at 1305). panel.js appendResult builds a .result-side column when the strip holds exactly one image: the prompt (6-line clamp), WxH · seed · steps · CFG, and Star / Refine… / Reuse settings, all built from gallery.js's own setFavorite, openRefine and reuseButton. The column is removed when a second image lands.

Columns use minmax(var(--thumb-min),1fr): 12 columns of 171 become 8 of 241 at 2560, and 9 of 174 become 7 of 214 at 2048. Images use object-fit:contain on near-black. Tools are 32 px; tool() takes a short label rendered as an instant ::after word above the row on :hover and :focus-visible ('Refine…', 'Use as reference', 'Delete'). All six tools fit inside a 241 px card. The search box gets max-width 560 px.

CSS only, with no change to placeTagValidation. .stage:has(#prompt-analysis:not([hidden])) becomes a grid: minmax(0,1fr) var(--dock-w), explicit rows for chips / viewer / note, and margins instead of row-gap. #prompt-analysis takes column 2, rows 1-3, with height:0 and min-height:calc(100% - gutter) plus overflow:auto, so it fills the viewer's height and never moves the gallery. Sections stack in one column inside the dock. Measured: dock 691x791 beside a 1297 px viewer; gallery head unchanged at y=903 (today 1604).
Body fs-sm (13.5), titles fs-lg, h3 fs-xs, buttons --h-sm at 13.5 px, source badges fs-xs, marks 18 px.
Two panes; see refine_redesign. 72 px thumbnail -> 818 px source; 11 px outcome line -> a 13.5 px summary box; scale buttons show the size they give; the dialog grows downward from a fixed top.
380 px column, prompt at fs-md (15.5), settings at fs-sm in --text-2, 52 px nav circles, buttons --h-md.
Row and column headers at fs-sm in --text-2 (today 11 px muted); the favourite star at 16 px.
18 px badges with --line-strong border. Tips 340/400 px wide at fs-sm with line-height 1.5 (today 240/300 px at 11 px).

directions.refine_redesign:
Refine becomes a two-pane working surface instead of a narrow form. The modal is min(1400px, 100vw-64px) wide and at least min(820px, 100vh-64px) tall, anchored at max(32px, 6vh) from the top so it grows downward instead of re-centring on every height change (M91).

The left pane, about 888 px at QHD, shows the source from the full PNG (rec.url instead of the 384 px thumb_url, wide tier only), contained on black at up to 818x818. A dashed frame shows the region the pass keeps. It is computed with refine.fitted's own cover-and-centre-crop math: s = max(w/sw, h/sh), kept = (w/s/sw, h/s/sh). Everything outside the frame is dimmed. When the shape crops, the frame turns amber and is labelled, e.g. 'kept: 56% of the source' for 1536x864 from a square. A caption along the bottom reads 'Source 1024×1024 → 1536×864 (1.3 MP)'. Today the only signal is the text 'the source cropped to this shape' (M51, M6).

The right pane is the existing controls at the panel's width (--panel-w, 461 px), so the dialog and the panel read as one system:
- Title, then the source line and its prompt clamped to 2 lines.
- Size as a 4-cell segmented control, 52 px tall, each cell showing its factor and the output size it gives (CSS attr(title), so 'too large' on a disabled cell) (M92).
- W/H, then Strength / Versions / Seed at 38 px.
- The 'Prompt and sampling' fold.
- The server's outcome ('1 image · strength 0.1 · about 3 of 28 steps run') promoted from an 11 px hint to a 13.5 px summary box above the actions, turning amber on a refusal.
- Cancel and a 46x200 Refine button with its Ctrl+Enter chip, pinned to the bottom.

Refine is also reachable from where the image is shown: the viewer's result column has 'Refine…' beside the just-made image. That was verified on the page: it opens 'Refine image 20' on the new heron. Today that needs a gallery card's ⤢ or a lightbox round trip.

Nothing in the dialog's contract changes: openRefine still fills it from the record; aria-disabled with the reason as title; Escape; the remembered scale, versions and strength; the sweep's sheet; Ctrl+Enter running the pass. At 2048x1040 the same layout gives a source pane about 690 px tall.

Out of scope for this direction, but compatible with it and left to other findings: M9 (opening size), M28 (keeping a draft on close), M29 (strength placeholder), M52 (closing only after accept), M108 (initial focus).

AFTER, same state. Panel 461 px; body 15.5 / labels 13.5 px; Sampling, Conditioning (folded, with summary) and Output groups; presets neutral with only 1:1 and 1 MP lit; Generate 46 px with Ctrl+Enter chip at y=993. The image (757 px) has its prompt, facts and Star / Refine… / Reuse beside it. Gallery: 8 columns of 241 px from y=965, first row fully above the fold.

BEFORE lightbox: 280 px side column, prompt 13 px.
AFTER lightbox: 380 px side column, prompt 15.5 px, bordered buttons, visible focus ring on the close cross.
AFTER, the contact sheet for a 4-seed batch: headers at 13.5 px in --text-2; controls at panel scale.

BEFORE 2048x1040 at DPR 1.25: panel 330 px, Generate y=915, gallery 9 columns of 174 px with the first row cut off at the fold (925-1099).
